text:
Someone wants to buy twenty-five boxes of tea and have them sent to the house.
Order tea, twenty-five boxes
Get me some tea delivered
We ran out of tea, can you sort that out?
Please sort out a tea delivery for the house
My shelf is narrow, so small boxes are best, twenty-five of them
The cupboard has no tea left. Could you buy some for me?
Send twenty-five boxes of tea to my door on Friday
Would you mind placing an order for twenty-five boxes of tea, please? I would like them to arrive this week.

name: stretch_break_timer
does: Reminds a person to stand up and stretch their arm and shoulders after a set time of focused work.
inputs: how many minutes to work before each break
people say:
- Tell me when to take a break
- My arm hurts from typing, remind me to rest it
- Let me know every half hour to stand up
- Pick a break time for me after forty minutes of work
- I forgot to move all morning, give me a nudge
- Remind me to step away for a salty snack at three

Priya was packing lunches while her son hunted for his shoes. She looked at her phone and said, 'Excuse me, could you please remind me at four o'clock to pick up the parcel from the post office on Mill Road? I am afraid I will forget, because the baby has a check-up today and my head is full.'

The assistant asked, 'Do you want the reminder to include the address?'

'Yes, please read it out when it goes off,' she said.

The assistant set a reminder for four o'clock today called pick up parcel. It saved the address of the post office and said it would read the address aloud when the time came. Priya sat on the comfortable chair by the door for a moment and let out a breath. At four, the phone chimed and a calm voice read, 'Pick up the parcel at the post office, Mill Road.' She grabbed her coat and went.

name: post_office_wait_check
does: Tells a person how long the line is at a post office and which time of day is quietest to go.
inputs: which post office, and the day
people say:
- Is the post office busy right now?
- When should I go to mail a letter so I do not wait long?
- How long is the line at the post office on Elm Street?
- I have a letter to send, when is it quiet?
- Give me hourly updates on the line until I leave the house

name: bedtime_wind_down
does: Starts a calm routine of dim lights, quiet sounds and a warm milk with a pinch of spice when it is time to get ready for bed.
inputs: the time you want to be asleep, and how long the routine should last
people say:
- Help me get ready for bed
- I have frequent late nights and I miss my sleep, help me slow down by ten
- Dim everything, it is almost bedtime
- Make the room calm, I want to be asleep by ten thirty
- Start my evening routine half an hour early tonight

Tomas was a cook, and the fan over his stove dripped grease again. 'The filter is clogged,' he told his phone. 'Please find a repairman, but I do not want anyone to come before the lunch rush, and I do not want a new fan, only a clean.'

The assistant understood. He wanted a cleaning visit, not a replacement, and not in the morning. It found a repair shop that had a visit at three in the afternoon today and asked if that was fine.

'Move it to Thursday instead,' Tomas said.

The assistant booked Thursday at three and set a reminder for Wednesday night. It also said that frequent cleaning, once a month, would keep the filter from clogging, and Tomas said yes to that too. Then he kept an eye on the clock and went back to chopping onions.

Ordering things to your home works in much the same way almost everywhere. You pick what you want, choose a size, and say where and when it should arrive. A shop may send it in a gray van, or a rider may bring a hot pizza on a bike while the wind blows down the street. Before the order ships, most things can be changed. People say 'send it to my office instead,' 'make it a size larger,' 'deliver it on Friday,' or 'cancel the second one.' If something does not fit, they say 'I want to send this back' or 'give me my money back.' The shop then sends a label, and the return is tracked just like the first trip.

Rosa finished her night shift at the hospital with sore feet and the sour taste of old coffee in her mouth. On the bus home she said to her phone, 'Call my sister and turn off the ringer until noon.'

The assistant understood two things: ring Rosa's sister, and silence the phone until twelve. It made the call first. Her sister picked up and asked about the museum trip they had planned for Saturday.

'Give me a day to sleep and I will tell you,' Rosa said.

When the call ended, the assistant said, 'Your ringer is off until noon.' Rosa leaned on the window and closed her eyes. The phone buzzed once more with a text, but it made no sound, and she slept all the way to her stop.

name: appointment_slot_finder
does: Finds the next open time at a place that takes bookings, such as a barber or a dentist, and holds it for you.
inputs: the place, the day you prefer, and the minimum time you need
people say:
- Find me a haircut on Saturday
- When can I see the dentist?
- I stopped going for check-ups, help me restart them
- Is there a slot at the library computer desk tomorrow?
- I need at least thirty minutes, what is free?

Recording a video on a phone is simple. You press the red button, and you press it again to stop. People film birthdays, trips, a camping weekend by the lake, or a snowy walk with the dog. After you record, you can change a few things. You can trim the start and end, make the clip shorter, turn the sound down, or use a repair tool that steadies a shaky shot. People say 'cut off the first ten seconds,' 'make it brighter,' 'send this to Mum,' or 'save it to my album.' To share a video, you pick a person or a group and tap send. Long videos are big, so some people ask for a smaller copy first.

A password is a secret that keeps your things private, like a key for a door. A good one is long and hard to guess. A bored stranger can crack an easy one such as rice123 in a few minutes. People change their passwords when they think someone saw them, and they pay attention to what each app shows to others, like photos or where they are. They say 'change my password,' 'lock my phone after one minute,' 'turn on the face lock,' 'hide my location from everyone,' or 'who can see my posts?' A phone lock is the first guard. It asks for a code, a finger or a face before anyone can look inside.

When you take a picture with your phone, it lands in an album, often called the camera roll. Photos are for remembering things: a birthday cake, a trip, a cat on the sofa, or a fork stuck in a messy pie. After you take one, you can change it. You can crop it, make it brighter, add a cool filter, or turn it black and white. People say 'make it lighter,' 'cut off the edges,' 'put it in the holiday album,' or 'send it to Grandma.' Sometimes the shot comes out wrong, with eyes closed, so people take a few and delete the rest. A screenshot is a picture of whatever is on the screen right now.

A television shows programs from channels or from streaming apps. The remote is how you control it. At the end of the day, people hang up the coat, sit down and pick something to watch. They change the channel, turn the sound up or down, and pause when the phone rings. When a show ends, the next episode often starts by itself. Many people turn on subtitles, which are words at the bottom of the screen. They say 'go to channel five,' 'put the subtitles on,' 'play the next one,' or 'turn off in an hour.' The last one is a sleep timer. It is handy when your eyes start to blink and close.

A phone runs on a battery, and the battery runs down as you use the screen. Most people charge it overnight. To make the charge last, they dim the screen, close apps they do not use, or switch on low power mode, which is a great way to get through a long day. Do not disturb is another setting. It keeps the phone quiet so a call or a ping does not sound while you sleep or sit in a meeting. People say 'make the screen darker,' 'save my battery,' 'silence everything until seven,' or 'how much storage is left?' If storage is full, they delete old videos. A phone left on top of a warm dryer can get too hot, so keep it away.

Board games bring people together at a table. Every game has rules, and most have a score. Someone keeps the points on paper, or a phone does it. Some games use a timer so each turn does not take too long. When friends come over, the game is often played in the kitchen while the dishwasher hums. People change things all the time. They say 'start a two minute timer,' 'give Sam ten more points,' 'take away five from Lee,' 'read the rules again,' or 'who is far ahead?' A puzzle is much the same, but you usually play alone, and the goal is to finish it and see how far you have come.

Someone wants a flat bike route from home to the grocery store for a ride tomorrow at seven.
Flat route to the grocery store, please
Bike directions to the store
Where can I ride with no big hills tomorrow at seven?
I want to cycle for groceries, nothing steep
Show me a bike path to the shops, I leave at seven tomorrow
Plan my ride, and trim any extra distance
Which way is the easiest ride to the market?
I would like to cycle to the grocery store tomorrow at seven. Could you find the flattest and safest way?

name: voicemail_reader
does: Reads out saved voicemails, newest first, and says who called and when.
inputs: how many messages to read, and whether to read only the new ones
people say:
- Any messages for me?
- Who left me a voicemail?
- Play what the doctor's office left about my vitamin refill
- Push the old ones aside, I only want the new ones
- Was that the delivery driver in the brown truck who called?

Dana was packing a school bag with one hand and rocking the baby with the other. Her coffee had gone cold and bitter on the counter. She grabbed her phone and typed fast: 'order three blue pens and a lunhc box for the kids, we live close to the corner shop so pickup there'.

The assistant understood the typo. It read 'lunhc' as lunch, and found a pack of three blue pens and a red lunch box at the corner shop. It said, 'I ordered the pens and the lunch box for pickup at the corner shop. They will be ready after two.'

Dana smiled, zipped the bag, and put the baby on her hip. One thing was off her list, and she had not even stopped moving.

Person: I need to put up a notice about a lost cat.
Assistant: Sure. What does the cat look like, and where was she last seen?
Person: Gray with a white nose, near Oak Street. Sorry, I mean Elm Street.
Assistant: Got it, Elm Street. Do you want me to put it on the community board?
Person: Yes, and display a photo too. She answers to the name Cheese.
Assistant: I will display the photo and the name Cheese. What phone number should I show?
Person: Use my mobile, the one saved as home. That is perfect, thanks.
Assistant: Done. The notice for Cheese the cat is on the community board for Elm Street.

Ben had ten minutes before work, and the morning was chilly. He typed with his thumbs: 'start a short wrokout, no legs, my knee is still healing'.

The assistant understood that he wanted a quick workout that kept his legs out of it because of his sore knee. It built a ten minute plan with push-ups, arm circles and a plank, each followed by a short rest. 'Step one is a warm-up,' it said, and started a timer on the screen.

Ben dropped to the floor in the hallway, still in his coat. When the timer beeped, the assistant told him to rest for thirty seconds and then begin the push-ups. He finished with a minute to spare and ran for the bus.

name: burn_care_guide
does: Gives short steps for a small kitchen burn, such as how to cool it and when to get help.
inputs: where the burn is, how big it is, and how long ago it happened
people say:
- I touched the hot pan
- My hand is red and stinging after the oven
- What do I do for a small burn?
- Can I put ice from the freezer on it?
- The burn is bigger than an average coin, should I call someone?
- Play the steps out loud while I hold my hand under the tap

A robot vacuum is a small round machine that cleans the floor while you are out. It follows a schedule, such as every morning at nine. When it finishes, it goes back to its base to charge. It works best on a tidy floor, so people pick up socks and the cap of a pen first. Kitchens need extra care. After you fry something, grease on the tiles may need a wet mop, not a vacuum. On a rough carpet the machine may need a stronger setting. People say 'clean the living room only,' 'start now,' 'skip Sundays,' 'come back at noon,' or 'go around the table.' When the bin is full, the machine tells you.

Hugh, a gardener, knelt by the outdoor faucet. It dripped and dripped, and his work gloves had worn through at the thumbs. 'My hands are cold and wet,' he sighed to the speaker, 'and these gloves are done.'

The assistant understood the hint. He needed new gloves. It asked, 'Do you want waterproof gloves in your usual size?'

'Yes, the last pair I got was good,' said Hugh.

The assistant found that same pair at the shop he had used before and ordered it for delivery on Friday. Then it told him the order number and the price, and Hugh went back to the flower bed with a rag wrapped around his hand.

A washing machine cleans clothes with water, soap and spinning. You sort the clothes by colour, put them in, shut the door, and choose a program. Most machines work best when they are full but not packed. People change the heat, the spin speed, or the time. They say 'wash it cold,' 'do a quick wash,' 'spin it faster,' or 'tell me when it is done.' Some machines send a call or a message to the phone at the end. A dryer set too hot can roast a wool jumper and make it shrink, so many people hang those up. For a stain, they say 'soak it first' or 'use the stain setting.'

Grandpa Leo was packing for a weekend in the hills. His grandchildren had given him a smart speaker, and he was still learning it. He stood by the microwave with the tent bag at his feet and said, 'Weather, Saturday.'

The assistant understood that he wanted the forecast for Saturday in the hills near his home. 'There is a good chance of rain in the afternoon, and it will be chilly at night,' it said. 'Shall I add a rain jacket to your packing list?'

'Yes,' said Leo.

The assistant put the rain jacket on the list. Leo wrote his name on the bag's label in permanent marker, took the list from the speaker's screen, and checked off the stove, the lantern and the tent.

The power went out while Noah, who was eight, sat alone in the front room. It was dark. 'Call Dad,' he told the speaker. Then he remembered. 'No, wait. Dad is at the train station until late. Call Aunt Jo next door.'

The assistant understood the correction. 'Calling Aunt Jo,' it said. When she answered, Noah said his name and told her the lights were off.

'Stay where you are,' she said. 'I am coming over.'

The assistant also said a tip out loud: a flashlight is safer than a candle. Noah remembered that Mum had left one in the drawer on the left of the TV. He found it, switched it on, and waited on the sofa until the door opened.

Person: Remind me to pay the tax bill.
Assistant: Sure. When should I remind you?
Person: Earlier than last time. I forgot then.
Assistant: Last time I reminded you one day before the due date. Do you want two days before?
Person: Yes, two days before, and keep the note plain. Just tax bill.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you two days before with the note tax bill. What is the due date?
Person: The thirtieth. Can you sync it to my watch?
Assistant: I cannot change your watch settings, sorry. But if your watch is already linked to this phone, the reminder will show up there too.

name: monthly_spending_check
does: Gives a quiet, short summary of what a person spent this month in each group, like food or bills, and how much is left.
inputs: the month, and the spending groups to look at
people say:
- How much have I spent on food?
- Am I over my budget this month?
- Where did my money go?
- I need to know what is left for the rest of the week.
- I am a bad cook so we eat out a lot, what did that cost?

Person: It is so dark outside my shop at night.
Assistant: Would you like me to turn on the outside lights? Which ones, front or back?
Person: The front. I finished the sidewalk sale, but the tent is still out there and people could trip.
Assistant: Should the front light come on at sunset and stay on until morning?
Person: At a minimum until I finish closing, around ten.
Assistant: Okay. The front light will come on at sunset and go off at ten.
Person: Good. Can you also lock the tent for me?
Assistant: I am sorry, I cannot lock or move a tent. I can only control the lights and cameras. Would you like the camera to watch the front tonight?

Sam had just moved to the city and had ordered a thick winter coat online. Now the air was icy, and the coat had not come. 'Where is my coat? It is taking twice as long as the shop said,' Sam asked the phone.

The assistant checked the order. It said the parcel was one day late and would arrive tomorrow before noon.

Sam sighed. 'If it is later than that, I want half my money back.'

The assistant noted the request and said it would stay in touch and tell Sam if anything changed. Then a woman from the next flat knocked on the door. A parcel had been left at her place by mistake. Sam thanked her and carried the coat home. 'Never mind, it is here,' Sam told the phone, and the assistant closed the refund note.

Mr. Evans owned a hardware shop, and his young daughter had a science project due on Monday. While he stacked paint cans, he said to the speaker, 'Homework due?'

The assistant understood that he wanted to know what was coming up for his daughter at school. It listed two things: the science project on Monday and a reading log on Wednesday. It also said there was a school play at the theater on Friday evening.

'Schedule it,' he said, short again.

The assistant put two study blocks on the family calendar, Saturday and Sunday at four o'clock, each called science project. Mr. Evans nodded, wiped his hands on his apron, and wrote the play on the shop's wall calendar by hand.

Lena was kneeling in the garden, planting beans with muddy hands, when she remembered her mother in Lisbon. 'What time is it there?' she asked her phone.

'It is eight in the evening in Lisbon, five hours ahead of you,' said the assistant.

Lena had an urgent message to pass on about the school trip form. 'Remind me to call her tomorrow at seven in the morning,' she said.

The assistant set a reminder for seven tomorrow. It also said that seven in the morning for Lena would be noon in Lisbon, a good time to call. Lena brushed the soil from her knees, patted the last bean seed into the ground, and went in to wash her hands.

Mr. Alvarez was not good with technology, but his granddaughter had set up the coffee machine to listen. One morning he stood in the kitchen, fixing his tie, and said, 'Make me a coffee, strong.'

The machine began to grind the beans. Then he frowned. 'No, wait. My stomach is bad. I want it low on strength, and not much sugar.'

The assistant understood the correction. It stopped, changed the setting from strong to mild, and made a small cup with no sugar. 'Your coffee is ready, mild with no sugar,' it said.

Mr. Alvarez took the cup to the table and sat down to rest his feet. 'That was easy,' he said. 'I only had to talk like a person.'

A flight time tells you when a plane leaves and when it lands. At the airport, a big board lists every flight with its departure time and gate. Delays happen: fog, a cold storm, or a late crew. People check the board or ask for the status of their flight, and they say 'is my flight on time?', 'which gate is it?', 'what time does it land?' or 'how long is the delay?' If the signs are in a language you do not read, a phone can translate them. Most travellers keep their bag tidy and their passport in a pocket, because the gate can change and they may need to walk fast.

Someone wants an hourly nudge to take a short break from work, with a longer break in the afternoon.
Hourly break alert
Tell me to stand up every hour
Nudge me each hour, I sit too long
Buzz me once an hour to rest my eyes
Make my breaks longer after lunch, say half an hour
I tend to crack after hours at the desk, so remind me to pause
Put a short break on my list every sixty minutes
Could you please remind me every hour to stretch, and give me more time off after three o'clock?

Kai was bored in study hall, and thumbs flew over the phone. 'hi, could you please put ship the science kit back on my list for tomorrow morning? i have a cold today and i know i will forget it, and mr dunn said it has to go by friday.'

The assistant understood. It added a task called ship the science kit back to the to-do list, due tomorrow morning, and set it as high priority because of Friday. Then it asked, 'Do you want a reminder at eight?'

'yes pls,' Kai texted.

The assistant set the reminder for eight and sent a short note back: 'Done. The task is on your list.' Kai sneezed, put the phone in a pocket, and went back to staring at the clock.

Someone wants more movies like the one they just watched.
More like this
Similar films?
Find something else in that style
I just watched a movie about a cook and I loved it, show me others
Dig up some films with the same actors
What else is good?
Any other movies like that one?
Could you please suggest a few more films that feel like the one I just saw?

A navigation app tells you how to get somewhere. You say where you are going, and it draws a route and tells you how long the drive will take. Traffic changes that time, so the app keeps checking. People put the phone on the dashboard and wipe the screen clean so they can see it. It is nice to know the way before you set off, even to a place with a car number plate on every wall. They say 'take me home,' 'avoid the highway,' 'find the quickest way,' 'stop at a gas station on the way,' or 'how long will this take?' If a road is shut, the app finds a new route.

Mrs. Okoye ran a small bakery, and the bin outside was full of paper and boxes. She stood at the counter and asked, 'When do they take the recycling? Is it tomorrow at seven?'

The assistant looked up the schedule for her street. It said paper and cardboard are collected tomorrow at seven in the morning, and glass is next week. Mrs. Okoye felt silly. She had mixed up the days again.

'Remind me tonight at nine to put the bin out,' she said.

The assistant set the reminder. Mrs. Okoye opened the drawer under the counter, pulled out a stack of old flyers and put them in the paper bin while the last trays cooled.

Someone wants their phone to read a page of text out loud.
Read this out loud
Read it to me
Can you say what is on this page?
Check the page and tell me what it says
Please read my favorite website to me, I will keep my eyes closed
Read me the first five lines
I cannot read the small print, could you say it for me?
Would you mind reading the whole article aloud, slowly, until I say stop?

Someone wants to know what movies are showing at the cinema tonight.
What is on tonight?
Movies near me, tonight
I am bored stiff at home, any films showing?
I just got back from a jog and I would love to go out for a film
The newspaper listings are thin, so can you tell me what is playing?
Is there anything good at the cinema? I will bake cookies to take along.
What can I see this evening?
Could you please tell me what is showing at the cinema around eight o'clock tonight?

Fatima was stirring soup with one hand when she remembered the party. 'Call Tony's Pizza, our favourite place, and put it on speaker,' she told her phone.

The assistant dialed the number and turned the speaker on. Fatima leaned over the pot. 'Hello, I need twenty-five slices for Saturday at six,' she said. 'Is there a discount for a big order?' The man at the shop said yes, ten percent off.

When the call ended, she told the phone, 'Take a note: twenty-five slices, Saturday at six, ten percent off.'

The assistant saved the note with the shop's name. Fatima tasted the soup, nodded, and called the kids to the table.

Person: It is chilly in the hall. I am about to go out the front door.
Assistant: Would you like to know the temperature outside and what to wear?
Person: Yes please. I blink and the weather has changed around here.
Assistant: I can check. Which town are you in?
Person: Dover.
Assistant: In Dover it is nine degrees now, with light rain later. A warm coat and an umbrella would be wise.
Person: Thank you. Where did I leave my key?
Assistant: I am sorry, I cannot tell where your key is. Maybe look by the front door or in your coat pocket.

Someone wants the speaker's volume turned down.
Quieter, please
It is too loud in here
Shift the sound down a bit
The total noise is too much, my head hurts
The room is messy and loud, can we calm it down?
Can you make the music a little softer?
Lower it by half
Would you mind turning the volume down for the rest of the evening? The baby is asleep.

name: pet_water_refill
does: Reminds a person when a pet's water bowl needs fresh water and keeps a log of each refill.
inputs: the pet's name and how often the bowl should be checked
people say:
- Did I fill Rex's water today?
- The bowl is empty again
- Remind me to give the dog fresh water every morning
- Draw up a chart of when I refilled the bowl
- A bee fell in the water, remind me to change it
- False alarm, the bowl was full, so do not remind me again today

Jun had worked all night at the hospital, and her eyes were heavy as she came home with her hair in a towel. Her friends were playing a board game in the living room. 'I can hardly see the cards in this corner,' she mumbled to the smart lamp.

The assistant understood the hint. She needed more light. It turned the lamp up to bright.

Then her friend Ravi waved a score sheet. 'Nobody can work out who is ahead.'

Jun said, 'Calculate our scores, please. Mine are twelve, nine and fourteen. Ravi's are ten, ten and eleven.' The assistant counted up the three rounds and said that Jun had thirty-five points and Ravi had thirty-one. Jun grinned, too tired to cheer, and dropped onto the sofa.

Person: wram up the car, i have a doctor visit at nine
Assistant: Happy to. When do you want to leave the house?
Person: at ten to nine
Assistant: I will start the car at twenty to nine so it is warm. Do you also want the defrost on?
Person: yes please, i was going to pour warm water on the glass but this is easier
Assistant: Defrost is on for the same time.
Person: the pink sticky note on my door says tyre pressure low, can you check it
Assistant: I cannot read your sticky note, but I can check the tyre pressure if your car reports it. Which car, the blue one or the white one?
Person: the blue one

Wifi lets your phone, laptop and television use the internet without wires. A router, a small box usually near the television, sends the signal around the house. If the connection is slow or the signal is low, you can move closer or restart the router. Guests often ask for the password, and many people make a separate guest network so visitors cannot see their things. On the weekend, when everyone is home, the connection can go slow because so many devices use it at once. People say 'what is the wifi password?', 'restart the router,' 'make the internet faster,' or 'let my guests in.'

Person: Pull up the menu for the noodle shop near us.
Assistant: Here is the menu. What would you like?
Person: Two bowls of chicken noodles, and double the dumplings.
Assistant: The usual is six dumplings, so double is twelve. Is that right?
Person: Yes. May I give a bigger tip because it is raining?
Assistant: Of course. How much?
Person: A little more than last time.
Assistant: Last time it was two dollars. Is three dollars okay?
Person: Yes. Do not wait longer than forty minutes.
Assistant: I set the maximum wait to forty minutes. Since you are a child, a parent needs to say yes before I send the order. Please ask one to come over.

A text message is a short note you send from phone to phone. People use texts to say they are running late, to ask what is for dinner, or to chat with a group of friends. In a group chat, everyone sees every message, so a reply goes to all of them unless you answer one person. When you are away from your phone, the messages wait for you. Some people read them aloud while they wait for a bus in the wind. They say 'text Mum I am on my way,' 'reply yes,' 'boost the text size,' 'read my new messages,' or 'mute this chat for an hour.'

name: move_to_savings
does: Moves money from one of your own accounts into another one, like checking to savings.
inputs: the amount, the account to take it from, and the account to put it in
people say:
- Put fifty into my savings
- I want to set money aside for my tax bill
- Shift some cash from my main account to the gold card account
- Pack away twenty a week for the trip
- Can you take a hundred out of checking and park it somewhere safe?

Many phones can read text aloud. This helps people who cannot see the screen well, or who are tired of reading. You can ask the phone to read an email, a web page or a message out loud. If the voice is too fast, you say, slower please. If a word is not correct, you can ask the phone to spell it one letter at a time. You can also ask for bigger text, which is useful when you wash the dishes and look at a recipe from far away. A person reading a letter about their salary may want the words larger too. People say, make the words bigger, or, talk to me instead of showing me. Each change is a small setting, and an assistant can switch it for you.

They want to hear more news headlines than usual.
More news please
Double the headlines today
Give me more than three stories this time
Can you read me twice as many headlines as yesterday? I am drinking my milk and I have time.
Is there any news about the young goalkeeper, and will his leg heal in time for Saturday?
Keep going, I want less talk about the weather and more local news
Half a dozen headlines, not just two
I would be very happy if you could read a few more stories, since I have a long wait and nothing else to do
Don't stop yet, what else is in the news?

Omar woke up late and felt half asleep. He reached for his phone and said, "What is on my list today?" The assistant read out three tasks: call the dentist, take out the bins, and weigh the parcel for his sister. Omar yawned. "Move the parcel to tomorrow at seven, and put soup on the shopping list." The assistant moved the parcel task to seven tomorrow morning and added soup to the shopping list. Then Omar said, "Check off the dentist, I called yesterday." The assistant marked it done. Omar looked at the north window, where frost still covered the glass. Only two tasks were left, so he made coffee first.

name: check_pantry
does: Tells you if you still have a food or item at home and about how much is left.
inputs: the name of the food or thing
people say:
- Do we have any rice left?
- Am I out of coffee again?
- Is there even a spoon of sugar in the jar?
- I feel like we are low on eggs, can you check?
- Do I have extra flour for the weekend?

They want to know the temperature outside right now.
How warm is it out there?
Temperature?
Is it pretty cold outside?
Is it above twenty-five degrees out there?
How many degrees is it right now?
Could you tell me the temperature before I take the dog out?
The soup is ready to serve, but I want to eat on the porch. Is it warm enough?
I am standing at the cupboard looking for a jacket. What is it like outside?
Please tell me how hot or cold it is outside, if it is not too much trouble.

People count days all the time. How many days until the big trip? How old will Grandma be next month? A phone can do the counting for you. You give it a date, and it tells you how many days, weeks or months are left. This is useful when you wait for a birthday, a holiday or a deadline. When plans move, people change the date and say, make it Friday instead, or, count from the first of June. If you want to hear the answer, you can ask the assistant to say it out loud. You can also ask it to count things, like how many weeks are in a school term, and it will give you a short number back.

A baby's day is made of small times: when to feed, when to nap, when to change. Many parents ask a phone or a speaker to remember them. A feeding timer rings after a number of hours, like three. A baby monitor lets you look at the baby or listen from another room. Sometimes it gives a false alarm when the baby just turns over, so parents ask it to be less sensitive. They change things with words like, remind me in two hours, make the nap alarm later, or, turn the monitor up. The goal is simple: a rested baby and a parent who does not have to remember everything.

A recipe is written for a certain number of servings. If you cook for more or fewer people, you scale it. Double means every cup and spoon doubles. Half means you cut each one in half. Cooks say, make this for six, or, I only need half of that. A voice assistant can do the sums while your hands are busy. You can ask how many spoons are in a cup, or ask for a mild version with less pepper. If the numbers feel strange, a good cook takes a breath, smiles and asks again. The goal is the same taste, just a different size.

Lena was texting from her bedroom. Her grandfather lived alone in a small flat, and she worried about his pills. She typed to the assistant on her phone: grandpa's pill box is still full and it is already night. The assistant understood that she was afraid he had missed his medicine. It set a daily reminder on his tablet, which was on loan from her school, for eight every morning. Then Lena wrote, remove the old reminder for the blue pill, he stopped taking it. The assistant removed it and said so. Last, Lena asked for a text whenever Grandpa marked a pill as taken, and the assistant said it would send one.

Person: My cat is gone.
Assistant: I am sorry to hear that. What does your cat look like?
Person: He is orange and he has a white spot on his head, like a little cap.
Assistant: Do you want me to put a lost cat notice on the neighbourhood board?
Person: Yes, it is important. Please do it now.
Assistant: When should the notice go up on the board?
Person: Tomorrow at seven, before I go to school.
Assistant: Okay. I will send it at seven tomorrow morning.
Person: Can you stretch it to the next street too?
Assistant: I can only post to your own street, but I can ask your neighbours to share it.

Grandpa Joe was hungry, but he wanted to walk to the shop before lunch. He typed on his phone in a hurry: will it rane this afternoon. The assistant understood that he was asking about rain today. It said there was a small chance of rain after three o'clock. Joe typed again: undo that, i meant tomorrow. The assistant dropped the first question and told him tomorrow would be dry and sunny. At the shop, a customer in front of him was grumbling about the wet weather. Joe smiled. He had learned that today might bring rain and tomorrow would be dry, so he bought bread and went home before three.

Person: Can you translate a note for my son's teacher?
Assistant: Of course. Which language should it be in?
Person: Spanish. Tell her he has a rare allergy to dust.
Assistant: Got it. What else should the note say?
Person: Please ask her to keep the air purifier on in the classroom. Say he needs a clean desk each morning, and that I will call her tomorrow at seven.
Assistant: Here is the note in Spanish. Should I send it to the school, or only show it to you?
Person: Only show it to me. I will print it.

Your home uses electricity all day, and a meter counts how much. Many people want to use less, so they play with a few settings: they turn down the heat, switch off lights, and run the washing machine at night, when power can be cheaper. Solar panels on a roof make power from the sun. On a bright day they can cover a lot of what the house needs, and the height and angle of the roof matter. People ask an assistant, how much power did I use today, or, turn everything off in the living room, or, tell me when the sun is making the most power. Small changes add up over a month.

name: gentle_wake_alarm
does: Rings an alarm that slowly gets louder at the time you choose.
inputs: the wake-up time, and which days it should ring
people say:
- Wake me up easy at six
- I have a busy day, get me up by half past five
- I have to drive to the airport early, set something for four
- I will plug my phone in tonight, so ring me at six thirty on weekdays
- Make it softer, I don't want to scare the baby

Ruth was on her knees by the flower bed when the shed door began to stick. She grabbed her phone and typed in a hurry: find a handyamn to fix my shed door, it is important, rain comes thursday. The assistant understood that she needed a repair person before Thursday. It looked up two handymen nearby and said one could come on Wednesday morning. Ruth said yes, so the assistant booked him. Then she asked it to tell the man to paint the door too and to bring a new key for the lock. The assistant added both things to the booking and told Ruth it was done. She went back to her roses.

Priya came home after a night shift, tired but hungry for fresh bread. She put flour on the counter and said to the kitchen speaker, "I want bread ready tomorrow at seven, before I leave for work." The assistant said the dough should rise for about eight hours, so she should start tonight. Priya asked what weight of flour she needed. The assistant said five hundred grams for one loaf. She poured it out, then said, "Wake me in an hour, I am going to climb into bed." The assistant set the timer. Priya said bad bread was worse than no bread, so the assistant offered to remind her to check the dough at the right time.

Lost pets are a common worry on a street. A collar tag with a phone number is perfect for getting a pet home fast, and some tags come in a bright brand colour that is easy to spot. People also post a photo in the local group and say, help me find my dog, or, tell the street. Another thing neighbours talk about is noise. If a party is loud, they say, ask them to turn it down, or, set quiet hours. A list of local events shows when there is a street sale or a school fair, and you can ask an assistant, what is on this weekend, or, remind me about the fair.

Marco was a cook, and his hands were covered in dough. His phone buzzed on the shelf, and he did not want to touch it. He wore a grey hoodie with the sleeves pushed up. "Read my messages out loud," he said, "but not the long ones." The assistant understood that he wanted only short messages. It read two. The first asked him to pack ten lunch boxes for the school trip. The second said the delivery would come at noon. Marco asked the assistant to reply to the first one with the word okay, in a neat short line. The assistant sent it and said so. Marco nodded and went back to the dough.

A radio picks up stations from the air. You turn a dial or say a station's name to tune in. Many people listen to the news on the radio at breakfast, or even while they bathe. In the afternoon some like talk shows, and the last thing at night they like soft music. A radio can also be a nice present for a grandparent. When people want a change, they say, find the news station, or, go back to the last one, or, make it louder. Some stations are weak when you are far from the town, so you may need to turn the radio a little to hear it clearly.

name: track_package
does: Shows where a parcel is right now and when it should arrive.
inputs: the order number, or the name of the shop
people say:
- Where is my apron? I ordered it last week.
- When will my parcel come?
- Show me what is going on with the delivery
- Did the cheap shoes I ordered ship yet?
- Is my order stuck somewhere?

They want a reminder to take their medicine.
Remind me about my pills
Pill time, please
Push me to take my medicine every day at eight
Tell me softly when it is time for my tablets
Set a reminder twenty-five minutes before dinner for my heart tablet
Can you make sure I take my medicine? I keep forgetting.
My neighborhood nurse says I must not miss a dose, so please remind me
Would you mind reminding me each morning to take my pills with breakfast?

Tom drove a delivery van and was parked outside a shop at lunch. He said to his phone, "Put the company picnic on my calendar for Saturday, and read me the agenda for the call tomorrow at seven." The assistant added the picnic to Saturday. Then it read the agenda, which had three items. The first one was the repair of the loading door at the depot. Tom felt scared that his boss would ask him about the cost. He asked the assistant to remind him at six thirty tomorrow morning to join the call. The assistant set the reminder and said it was ready. Tom finished his sandwich and went back to work.

Mr. Haddad did not like new gadgets, but his doctor had asked him to walk more. He sat in front of the tv with his phone and said slowly, "Excuse me, could you please tell me how many steps I have walked today? My doctor wants to see the number, and I would like to show her that I am trying." The assistant understood that he wanted today's step count. It said he had walked four thousand two hundred steps. He then asked it to spell the word pedometer, because he wanted to write it on a card. The assistant spelled it letter by letter. Mr. Haddad smiled, put on his coat, and went out for some fresh air to add more steps.

Person: These prices mean nothing to me. I only know dollars.
Assistant: I can help with that. Which currency are the prices in?
Person: I am not sure. The shop is in Paris.
Assistant: Then they are probably euros. What is the first price?
Person: A lamp for forty, and a rug for the floor for ninety.
Assistant: Do you want both shown in dollars?
Person: Yes please. The euro is strong this year, so I want to be careful.
Assistant: I can show you the prices in dollars, but I can't tell you if the shop's price is fair. Would you like the amounts now?

Sam stood at the bus stop in the rain. His mum was at work, and he was not sure the bus would come. The sky was not clear at all, and the roof of the shelter had a leak, so drops fell on his hat. He held up his phone and said, "Next bus?" The assistant understood that he wanted to know when the next bus would come to that stop. It said the number twelve would arrive in four minutes. Sam said thanks. He moved to a dry corner of the shelter and waited. When the bus came, he got on and sat by the window.

Maya sat on her bed and texted the assistant: order the gold humidifier from the shop, the one under twenty-five dollars. i wonder if it can come by friday. The assistant understood that she wanted to buy that exact item, and it asked if it should be sent to her home. Maya said yes. The assistant placed the order, said the price was twenty-three dollars, and told her it would arrive on Thursday. Maya sent back a thumbs up. Her room had been dry all winter, and she was tired of waking up with a sore throat. She smiled and put her phone on the desk.

Luis was driving home when his phone began to glow on the dashboard. He could not look at it, so he said, "Read me my new texts." The assistant said he had twenty-five unread messages and asked if he wanted all of them. "Just the last three," said Luis. The assistant read them out. One was from his wife, asking him to buy a new handle for the kitchen cupboard. Another was from his brother, about the current score of the game. Luis said, "Reply to my wife: will do, home by six." The assistant sent the message and told him it was sent. Luis kept his eyes on the road.

Jo was at the skate park and had just landed a trick. He texted the assistant: record a video of the next one, no sound, and do not post it anywhere. The assistant understood that he wanted a silent clip that stayed private. It started the camera in digital video mode and turned the sound off. Jo said the width of the ramp was small, so he could not decide which trick to try first. The assistant said it would keep recording until he said stop. Jo shouted that he was ready and rolled forward. Afterwards the clip was saved on his phone, and it was shared with no one.

Dana was putting her son to bed with one arm full of laundry. She typed fast with her thumb: set bedtim alarm for a quarter past eight and play rain sounds. The assistant understood that she wanted a bedtime reminder at eight fifteen and some soft sounds for the room. It set the reminder and started the rain sounds at a low volume. Her son was excited about a trip on Saturday and could not sleep. Dana sat by his bed. After ten minutes the sounds had done their work, and the boy was breathing slowly. She turned off the light and carried the laundry out.

They want to start a timer for one turn in a game.
Start a timer for sixty seconds
Time this turn, please
One minute on the clock, go
Time me like a toothbrush timer, but for the game
I have to paint a picture of a cat before the sand runs out, so give me sixty seconds
Start the clock, it is Jake's turn
This game was expensive and we don't want to waste time, so please start a timer for each turn
Could you start a countdown of thirty seconds and tell us when it ends?

name: share_photo_album
does: Sends a photo album to the people you pick and keeps track of who has seen it.
inputs: the album name, and who to send it to
people say:
- Send the beach pictures to my mother
- Let Dad see the photos from the windy day
- I want the whole family to get the birthday album
- Who has looked at the pictures I sent?
- Show my sister everything from last summer

Walter was sweeping crumbs from the kitchen floor while the vent hummed over the stove. He had a stale loaf in his hand and wanted to plan the week. He spoke to the speaker slowly. "What can I cook this week? I want less meat and double the vegetables." The assistant understood that he wanted a dinner plan with less meat and twice as many vegetables. It gave five dinners: bean soup, a big salad with eggs, vegetable pasta, rice with peas, and fish with potatoes. Walter said the plan sounded good and asked it to put the shopping on his list. The assistant added beans, peas and carrots, and told him it was done.

A lawn needs a haircut every week or two in summer. You can push a mower yourself, or let a robot mower do the work. The robot whispers across the grass and goes back to its station when it is tired. A sprinkler gives the grass water, usually early in the morning, so the sun does not dry it. Clean edges make the garden look neat, and some people plant garlic near the flower beds to keep bugs away. People ask an assistant, cut the grass shorter, or, water the front lawn for ten minutes, or, do not mow when it rains. Small changes to the schedule are easy to say aloud.

Kai had moved to the city this year and did not know it well. He sat on the sofa and asked the assistant, "Show me the top videos about the subway." The assistant found a list of the most watched videos and began to play the first one, a short guide to buying tickets. Kai frowned. "Sorry, I meant the bus, not the subway." The assistant understood that he had changed his mind. It stopped the first video and showed the top videos about the bus instead. Kai picked one about night routes and watched it twice, so he could remember the stops.

A podcast is a show with many episodes, and an audiobook is a book that is read to you in chapters. Your phone remembers where you left off, so you can start again in the same place. People listen while they cook, walk, or wash at the sink. If you sneeze and miss a part, you can say, go back thirty seconds. If the speaker is too slow, you say, play it faster, and if you want to sleep, you say, stop in twenty minutes. Some shows are free, and some are paid, and you can ask the assistant, find the next episode, or, what chapter am I on?

Dana had two minutes before the train and grabbed her umbrella from the hook. She said to her phone, "Play my top songs, but not the slow ones." The assistant understood that she wanted fast songs from her most played list. It started a lively song and made it loud enough to hear in the hallway. Then Dana said, "Rank my songs from this month." The assistant read out the three most played ones. The automatic doors of the station opened as she ran in, and the music was still playing in her ears. She made the train with a few seconds to spare.

When you book a hotel room, you say how many nights you will stay and how many guests will come. Check-in is usually in the afternoon, and check-out is in the morning, so guests pack their bags before breakfast. If plans change, people say, add one more night, or, make it two guests instead of three, or, I want the least expensive room. Some guests also ask for a quiet room, or a vegetable meal at breakfast. Each of these is a small change to the booking. The hotel keeps a note of them and shows it to the staff when you arrive.

Grandma Pat stood in the hall holding one boot. She wanted music in every room. She typed with one finger: put the front room speaker with the kithcen one. The assistant understood that she wanted the two speakers to play together as a group. It joined the front room speaker and the kitchen speaker, then asked her which song to play. Pat named her favourite old song. She asked the assistant to tag the group as the house speakers, so that she could say that name later. The assistant did it and told her the name was saved. Pat put her boot down and listened.

name: evening_check_in
does: Sends a short message to a family member each evening to say that all is well.
inputs: who to message, and what time
people say:
- Let my daughter know I am home safe, even if it rains
- Tell my son I left the clinic and I am fine
- Every night at eight, say good night to my family for me
- I don't want them to worry, so please check in with them
- Message Anna that I took my pills and I am going to bed

The sea comes in and goes out twice a day. These are called tides. A beach feels different at high tide and low tide, and swimmers should know which one is coming. Near the shore, a channel of fast water can pull a swimmer away, so people stay near the flags. Noisy waves are often a sign of strong water. Sun cream protects your skin, and you put it on again after swimming. In winter, when it may snow near the coast, the water gets very cold. People ask an assistant, when is high tide, or, how warm is the water, or, remind me to put on more cream.

Elsie was watering her tomatoes from a red bucket when she remembered to call her son. She said to her phone, "What time is it in Lisbon?" The assistant said it was a quarter past three there. Elsie shook her head. "No, wait, I meant Madrid." The assistant understood that she had fixed the city. It said it was a quarter past four in Madrid. Her son had a temporary job there and a band practice at five. Elsie asked the assistant to remind her to call at four thirty. It set the reminder. She put the bucket down, wiped her hands and went to find a hat.

The world is split into time zones, so it is not the same time everywhere. When it is morning in one city, it can be night in another. Clocks tell you the time where you are, and your phone can show the time somewhere else too. People keep a short list of cities for family or work. Ask an assistant, what time is it in Tokyo, or, add London to my list. Someone riding a bike home may say, is it too late to call my sister in Paris? A good habit is to check before you ring, and say sorry if you wake a friend.

Person: Check leaks.
Assistant: Sure. Which room do you want me to check?
Person: The bathroom. I saw a spider near the pipe, and the floor is wet.
Assistant: Is water running right now, or did it stop?
Person: It runs a little. Can you close the main valve for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't close a valve in your house. You can turn it by hand, near the water meter.
Person: I am new here and I don't know where that is.
Assistant: Many homes keep it close to the kitchen sink or in the basement. I can also call a plumber for you.

Mrs. Lopez had been a teacher for forty years and now spent her mornings at home. A sudden idea came to her: she wanted her grocery list on paper, and she wanted the old school letter saved on the computer. She said to the printer, "Print my grocery list and scan this letter." The assistant understood that there were two jobs. It sent the list to the printer, and then asked her to put the letter on the glass. Mrs. Lopez hated paper jams, so she held her breath. Both jobs went well, and the scan was saved in her documents folder.

name: nearest_stop
does: Finds the closest bus or train stop to where you are and points you toward it.
inputs: your address, or where you are now
people say:
- Where can I catch a bus near here?
- It is cloudy and I am lost, which way is the closest stop?
- I am at the library, how far is the train?
- Point me to the nearest station
- Is there a stop on my street?

Person: I am standing at the door in a T-shirt, and the sky looks grey.
Assistant: Do you want to know the temperature, or if it will rain?
Person: Will my clean washing dry outside today?
Assistant: Which city are you in?
Person: I am new here. It is Leeds.
Assistant: There is a chance of rain this afternoon, and the air is cool. The washing may stay damp.
Person: I saw a video where they say the water boils faster with a lid. Can you tell me about that?
Assistant: I can only help with weather and your home settings in this chat. A lid does help, though, if you want to try it.

They want to know what to do for a small cut on a finger.
i cut my finger wat do i do
Help, I cut myself
What do I put on a cut?
I was slicing an apple and the knife slipped, now my finger is bleeding
I was scoring a thick loaf of bread and cut my hand, should I wrap it?
How do I stop a little cut from bleeding?
Could you tell me how to clean and cover a small cut, please?

Ben was late and shouted at the house, "Turn on the hall light!" The assistant switched on the hall light. Ben put his keys on the table and then said, "No wait, the kitchen light, not the hall." The assistant understood that he had changed his mind. It turned off the hall light and switched on the kitchen light. Ben looked at the room and said, "Make it a warm colour, not that cold white." The assistant changed the colour to a warm yellow. Ben grabbed his bag, said thanks, and ran out of the door with a minute to spare.

Mina came in from the garden with mud on her boots and a plan for the afternoon. She said to the pool controller, "Check the water temperature and start the pump." The assistant understood that there were two jobs. It said the water was twenty-six degrees and started the pump. Mina's husband liked to jog around the pool, so she asked if the gate lock was shut. The assistant said it was locked. She also said the cover felt too tight and was hard to pull. The assistant told her it could not change the cover, but it would remind her to loosen the straps tomorrow.

Someone wants to order the same groceries they get every week.
Reorder groceries
Get me my usual order again.
Same as last time, please.
I hope you can send the same box as last week, with the potatoes.
Can you repeat my last shop?
Order what I got before.
Could you please put in my usual grocery order for Friday, since I am out of almost everything?
Do my weekly shopping again.

A bedtime routine is a small set of things you do each night so your body knows it is time to sleep. Many people set a daily alarm so they wake up at the same time every morning. Some also run a quiet dehumidifier in the bedroom, so the air feels dry and fresh. When plans change, people talk to their phone or speaker to change things. They might say, wake me at six instead of seven, or, move my bedtime reminder to ten. Others say, no alarm on Sunday, or, push my alarm back half an hour. For a nap, they say, wake me in twenty minutes. These small changes help a person get enough rest.

Person: Text Anna.
Assistant: What would you like the message to say?
Person: Tell her I will bring a carrot cake on Sunday.
Assistant: Okay. Should I say what time you will come?
Person: Yes, but nothing fancy. Just say I will be there at noon.
Assistant: Done. I sent Anna: I will bring a carrot cake on Sunday and be there at noon.
Person: Good. Can you also burn the group photos onto a disc for me?
Assistant: I am sorry, I can not burn discs. I can send the photos to the group chat instead.
Person: Yes, please do that.

Someone wants to book a haircut.
Book a haircut.
Haircut tomorrow, please.
Can I get a trim on Friday at ten? No, make it eleven.
I need to see the barber before the shop closes on Saturday.
Put me down for a cut on Monday. Actually no, there is ice on the roads, so make it Tuesday.
My hair is healthy but too long, so please find me a time this week.
Sorry, not Thursday, I meant Wednesday afternoon.
Could you please check if the salon has a free spot after lunch and reserve it for me?

Ben was seven, and he wanted to help Grandma bake cookies. The kitchen had a small speaker on the shelf. Ben stood on a chair and said, Cookie time? The speaker understood that he wanted a cookie recipe, so it read the first step: sort the flour, the sugar and the butter on the counter. Outside, the traffic was loud, and Ben did not hear the next part. He said, Say again. The assistant read the step more slowly. Then Ben asked how long the cookies bake. The assistant said twelve minutes and set a timer for twelve minutes. While they waited, Ben sorted the chocolate chips by size, and Grandma laughed.

Someone wants to move money from checking to savings.
Move fifty dollars to savings.
Put half of my paycheck into savings.
I want less in checking and more in savings before winter.
Please stir some life into my savings and move double the usual amount.
Move my loose cash, anything over five hundred, into savings.
Send a bit more to savings this month than last month.
Could you please transfer a little extra to my savings account, because I want to be ready for the holidays?
Savings, one hundred, now.

Priya looked at the clock. Her guests would arrive in twenty-five minutes, and the floor was covered in crumbs and the pieces of a puzzle she had not finished. She said to her phone, Clean the living room, quick, my friends are coming. The assistant understood that she wanted the robot vacuum to start in the living room only, so it did that and said the cleaning would take about fifteen minutes. Priya hurried to pick up the puzzle pieces so the robot would not swallow them. From the kitchen came the delicious smell of her soup. When she picked up the last piece, she asked the assistant to tell her when the robot was done. It said it would, and it did, with three minutes to spare.

Grandpa Leo sat at the kitchen table with his tea, and a gray cat slept on his lap. He stirred the tea slowly and looked at his granddaughter's drawing on the fridge. Then he remembered his sore tooth. He said to the tablet, I need to see the dentist sometime next week, in the morning. The assistant understood that he wanted a dentist visit early next week. It checked the dentist's open times and found Tuesday at ten. Leo asked if there was anything earlier. The assistant said the first free time was nine-thirty on Wednesday, so Tuesday at ten was sooner. Leo said Tuesday was fine, and the assistant booked it. It also set a reminder for twenty minutes before, so he would leave on time.

Nina got home after a long night shift. The morning was humid, and her shirt stuck to her back. A magazine lay on the mat, and a bird began to tweet in the tree. At the front door she stopped. She could not remember if she had locked it when she left the evening before. She was too tired to check, so she said to her phone, Check the lock. The assistant understood that she meant the front door, so it looked at the smart lock and told her the door was locked and had been since seven the evening before. Nina smiled. She said, Unlock it, and the assistant did. She went in and fell asleep within minutes.

Person: Translate good morning for my neighbor.
Assistant: Which language would you like?
Person: Not French. She speaks Portuguese. Learning it is my new hobby.
Assistant: Good morning in Portuguese is bom dia. Would you like to hear how to say it?
Person: Yes, and say it slowly. I am not very quick.
Assistant: Bom dia. Bom dia. You are doing well.
Person: You are very patient. Can you update my phone so it always shows words in Portuguese?
Assistant: I am sorry, I can not change that setting. I can save bom dia in your list of new phrases, though.
Person: Please do.

Dana's morning was busy. While she packed lunches, she said to her speaker, Remind me to pick up Sam from soccer at four. The assistant understood and set a reminder for four o'clock. Then Dana smelled toast burning and ran to the toaster. When she came back she said, Actually, make it half past three, the coach said practice ends early. The assistant changed the reminder from four to three-thirty and told her so. Dana was working from home that day and had an article to finish, so she asked for a second reminder ten minutes earlier. The assistant added it. At three-twenty her phone buzzed, and she saved her work just in time.

Music on a phone or a speaker is mostly about songs and the lists you make from them. A playlist is a set of songs played in order. People use music to wake up, to cook, or to sit under a blanket on a rainy day. They change a few things all the time. For volume they say, turn it up, a bit lower, or, mute. To skip a track they say, next song, or, skip this one. If a song is too heavy for the mood, they say, play something softer. If they want to cut a song short, they say, stop after this one. To start again, they say, play my evening playlist.

Omar drove a delivery van, and on his lunch break he parked near the river. At dawn he had left a tray of rolls rising at home, and now the dough was ready to bake. He picked up his phone and said, Excuse me, could you please start the oven at four hundred degrees now, because I will be home in twenty minutes and I want the rolls to go in as soon as I walk in the door? The assistant understood that he wanted the smart oven to warm up. It started the oven and said it would be hot in about ten minutes. Omar drove home with the windows open, and the air smelled like cut grass. When he got in, the oven was ready, and the rolls baked to a deep gold.

name: scale_recipe
does: Changes the amounts in a recipe so it makes more or fewer servings.
inputs: the recipe and how many servings you want
people say:
- Make this healthy soup for twelve instead of four.
- Write out the pancake recipe for the ten kids in my drum class.
- Cut this recipe in half, it is only me tonight.
- How much flour if I double it?
- My chili feeds six, but fifteen people are coming.
- Triple the sauce, please.

Someone wants to know how far they walked today.
How far have I gone?
Distance so far.
How many miles did I run this morning? No, sorry, I mean walk.
I wish I knew how far I got before the rain started.
Tell me my distance from the walk on the dry path by the lake.
What is my total since I left home?
Could you please tell me how far I have walked today, because I want to see if I reached five miles?
Show today's distance, not this week's.

name: pack_lunch_ideas
does: Suggests lunches that are easy to carry and stay fresh until noon.
inputs: who the lunch is for, any foods they avoid, and how much time you have
people say:
- What can I put in a lunch box that stays fresh in a hot car?
- Lunch ideas, and fast, I have to go before I blink.
- The kids eat downstairs, so nothing that needs a microwave.
- Something cold for Dad's lunch, no nuts.
- I am tired of sandwiches, give me five other ideas.

Tom had just enough money left to pay the rent, so tonight he had to cook. He took off his muddy boot by the door and opened the fridge. The kitchen was small, and he had only one pot and one pan. He said to his phone, Pasta recipe? The assistant understood that he wanted an easy recipe for pasta. It found one with tomatoes and garlic and read out the steps. Tom asked for the first step again, and the assistant said, boil water in the pot with some salt. He asked how long the pasta needed. Ten minutes, said the assistant, and it set a timer. The meal was easy, and Tom ate every bite.

Rosa came home from the night shift and dropped onto the couch. She had ordered a pair of sandals last week, and she wanted to know about them. She said to her phone, Where is my sandal order and can you leave it with my neighbor if I am asleep? The assistant understood two things: she wanted to see where the package was, and she wanted it left next door. It said the package was on a truck a few stops away and would come by noon. It then changed the delivery note to leave it with the neighbor in apartment four. Rosa asked it to zoom in on the map to see how far the truck was. It was only a few streets away, and Rosa fell asleep smiling.

Maria owned a small bookshop, and tonight was its tenth birthday party. The shelves were full of balloons, and she still had to fold fifty paper napkins. Her hands were busy, so she said to the speaker, Party music. The assistant understood that she wanted a playlist for a party, so it chose a cheerful list of songs and played it at a medium volume. Maria said, Not so loud, and it turned the music down. Later, as she cut the cake with a sharp knife, she asked for more volume because the guests were arriving. The assistant raised it, and the shop filled with music and laughter.

Jun had just moved to the city, and his building had many rules about trash. A paper on the wall used a word he did not know. He took out his phone and said, Excuse me, could you please tell me how to say recycling bin in Dutch, because I want to put my things in the right place and not upset the neighbors? The assistant understood that he wanted a translation of the words recycling bin. It said the Dutch words and spelled them slowly. Jun repeated them. Then the assistant asked if he wanted to save the phrase, and he said yes, so it saved the words in his list of new phrases. Jun carried his box of paper down to the white bin and put it in.

Every street has a few problems that neighbors share: a lost cat, a noisy party, or a meeting about the park. A neighborhood chapter helps people stay in touch. Most of the usual news comes in one weekly message. A person can change what they get. They might say, tell me about local events on Saturdays, or, mute the chat after ten at night. If a dog is lost, someone says, send a message to the whole street with a photo. If the noise is too much, people say, let the landlord know. It is easy to understand once you try it: you say what you want, and the group hears it.

Hana had a long day ahead at the office. On her way in, she said to her phone, Remind me to call the town hall at noon and to buy stamps when I go past the high street shop. The assistant understood that she wanted two reminders. It set the first one for twelve o'clock and the second one for when she left the building at five, near the shop. Hana also said the town hall reminder should ring ten minutes early, since the high building's phone lines were always busy. The assistant changed it. At ten to twelve her phone buzzed, and she made the call before lunch.

Sam moved to the city last week, and the nights were strange. A bus rumbled by at midnight, and a siren sang at two. Tired, Sam said to the speaker, Set an alarm for six tomorrow. The assistant set it. Then Sam remembered a late shift and said, No wait, make it seven. The assistant changed the alarm from six to seven and said so out loud. Sam tried to describe the noise outside and asked for something soft to cover it. The assistant played rain sounds for one hour. Sam, who had started a new diet and was hungry, drank some water and fell asleep before the first song ended.

Mr. Hale did not trust his phone much. It felt strange to talk to it. But his son was playing in a big match that day, and Mr. Hale wanted to know the score. He held the phone and said, Excuse me, could you please tell me how the Tigers are doing, because my son is playing and I could not get a ticket? The assistant understood that he wanted the score of the Tigers game. It said the Tigers were ahead, three to one, at halftime. Mr. Hale smiled. He asked it to place a note on his calendar for the next game, and the assistant did. Then he went out to his truck to drive to the stadium anyway.

A work meeting is a time when people talk about a plan. Many meetings now happen on calls. You join with a link, and you can share your screen if you need to show a page. An agenda is a short list of what will be talked about, like a new design or a store discount. People change things often. They say, mute me, I will be away from my desk for a minute, or, share my screen, or, move the meeting to three o'clock. When someone is late they say, start without me. These small requests keep a meeting smooth.

name: sort_incoming_mail
does: Tells you which letters and parcels arrived today and which are only junk.
inputs: your address and what you are expecting
people say:
- Anything important in the mail today?
- Did my box of butter cookies come yet?
- Trim the junk out of today's mail and tell me what is left.
- Is there a plain white envelope from the bank?
- Tell me when a package is at the door.

name: find_quiet_route
does: Finds a walking route that stays away from busy roads and has no stairs.
inputs: where you start, where you want to go, and what you want to avoid
people say:
- Take me to the park by a quiet way.
- I can not lift the stroller up stairs, so find a flat path.
- Go over the iron bridge, and skip the noisy main road.
- Which way to the library has the fewest cars?
- Plan my evening walk, nothing busy.

Person: Move some money to my savings.
Assistant: How much would you like to move?
Person: Not all of it. I only want to save a little for a new bicycle.
Assistant: Okay. Would two hundred be good?
Person: That is too much. Make it one hundred.
Assistant: Done. I moved one hundred from checking to savings. The total in savings is now six hundred.
Person: Good. A gentle start is fine, and I do not want any fee.
Assistant: There is no fee for moving money between your own accounts.

On Saturday morning Lena said to her speaker, When does the Lions match start? The assistant said it started at five. Lena said, No, I meant the Falcons, my son's team. The assistant checked again and said the Falcons played at six. Lena asked how much a ticket was, and it said ten euro. She remembered that her son's uniform was not clean, so she asked for a reminder to wash it before lunch. The kids always shout so loudly at games, she said with a laugh. The assistant set the reminder and one more for four-thirty, when it was time to leave.

When something in the house breaks, you can fix it yourself or ask for help. A repair shop or a handyman can come to your door. A filter in a heater or a fan needs to be changed every few months, so it is good to double check the date. People often have a problem upstairs, like a leaky tap, and they say, book a repair for Thursday. They change the plan by saying, make it morning, or, move it to next week. They ask, when is my filter due, or, remind me to change it in a month. Saying what is wrong and when you are free is the most helpful thing.

name: pick_wash_cycle
does: Chooses the right washing machine setting for a load of clothes.
inputs: what the clothes are made of, how dirty they are, and how long you have
people say:
- My sister and I share one machine, what setting for her silk shirt and my socks?
- Will a hot wash shrink these jeans?
- How much does it cost to use cold water compared to warm?
- I have towels and sheets, which program is best?
- Fast wash, I need these dry by noon.

Someone wants to know when a friend's birthday is and what to give.
Date and gift for Sam?
When is Mia's birthday and what should I get her?
I always forget, so tell me the date and suggest a present.
Change the setting so you warn me a week before each birthday and give me ideas.
Is Dad's birthday this month, and is there a card I can print?
Do not let me drag my feet again: give me the date and something small to buy.
Could you please tell me when Anna's birthday is and check whether I am free that evening?

Mika was making breakfast for three kids when her phone rang with a call from work. She had no free hand, so she let it ring and said to the kitchen speaker, Make the coffee twice as strong today, and start the kettle for tea too. The assistant understood that she wanted a stronger coffee and hot water. It told the coffee machine to use a double portion and switched on the kettle. The kids zoom around the table like little planes, and one of them asked for less milk in the cereal. Mika laughed and poured half a cup. The assistant also reminded her that the monthly cleaning of the coffee machine was due on Friday.

Carl owned a shoe shop and was checking prices on his tablet. The numbers were tiny. He ate a sandwich as he worked, next to a stack of yellow price tags. He held the tablet at arm's length and said, These letters are so small, I need a magnifying glass. The assistant understood that he could not read the screen, so it made the text size bigger and asked if that was enough. Carl said a bit more. The assistant made the text larger again, and Carl nodded. Then he said the screen was too bright for the sunny shop window, and the assistant lowered the brightness.

Someone wants an email to be sent later, at a set time.
Send it tomorrow at seven.
Email Dan the painting photos at eight tomorrow morning.
Hold this message and send it at noon.
I will lie in tomorrow, so please send this email at nine for me.
Schedule my note to the nearby bakery for Monday at ten.
Do not send it now, wait until after lunch.
Could you please send this email tomorrow at seven, since people read their messages first thing?
Delay sending until tomorrow evening.

name: write_quick_reply
does: Writes a short reply to a text message in the style you prefer.
inputs: the message you got and how you want to sound
people say:
- Reply to Jo that I will be late, keep it casual.
- Tell my roommate in the public group chat to empty the dishwasher, but be nice.
- I prefer short answers, so just say yes.
- Answer Mum's text and say I am fine.
- Write back politely, I can not come on Sunday.

Eli woke up to a loud beep. The TV was still on a news channel, and his head hurt. He reached for his phone and said, Call Mum. The assistant understood that he wanted to phone his mother, so it started the call. It rang four times and went to voicemail. Eli said, Leave a message, and the assistant recorded him saying, Hi Mum, call me back when you can. It was a quick message, but it was enough. Then Eli asked the assistant to turn on the speakerphone for the next call, and it did. A minute later, his mother called back, and they talked while he made tea.

Zoe was on the train with a silver suitcase and her phone. She typed fast: book a room for two nights in the beach town and tell me when check in is. The assistant understood two things: she wanted a hotel room for two nights, and she wanted to know the check-in time. It found a room near the water and said check-in was after three. Zoe told it to continue with the booking, and then she asked it to put a late arrival note on it, because her train came in at ten. The assistant did that. She smiled and turned back to the window. It was going to be a good day.

Grandma Ruth sat in her chair with a book. The lamp on her left was too bright. She said to the speaker, Excuse me, could you please make the lamp half as bright, because the light hurts my eyes when I read? The assistant understood that she wanted the lamp dimmer, so it set the brightness to fifty percent. Ruth said it was better, but could it be a little warmer. The assistant changed the color to a soft yellow. She felt she had earned a quiet evening after a day of chores. She read three chapters and fell asleep in her chair.

Making an appointment means choosing a time to see someone, like a hair stylist or a dentist. Each place has open hours, and you can only book inside them. When you ask for a haircut, you give a day and a time. People often change plans. They say, let me move it to Friday, or, make it an hour later. If they are running late, they say, tell the salon I will be ten minutes behind. Before the day, they might say, remind me the night before. To learn when a place is ready for customers, they ask, are you open on Sunday? Clear words help the booking go well.

Walt was not good with technology, and his computer made him nervous. His grandfather had given him the machine and always said it was easy, but Walt did not agree. One morning the words on his screen looked too small, and he was in a hurry. He typed to the assistant: incrase the text size on my screen. The assistant understood what he meant, despite the typo, and increased the text size. Walt was pleased. He then asked it to remind him every week to save his files, and the assistant set a weekly reminder for Sunday at ten. Walt said thanks and went back to work, with the big letters easy to read.

name: water_plan
does: Tells you when and how much to water each plant in your garden.
inputs: the plants you have, where they sit, and the weather
people say:
- When should I water the herbs on the piano shelf?
- Is it too warm to water at noon?
- My basil is tasty but droopy, what does it need?
- How much water for the roses this week?
- Set the sprinkler to run early in the morning.

On a hot day, a fan or an air conditioner makes a room feel cooler. A fan moves the air, and air conditioning takes heat out of it. Even a waiter in a busy restaurant is glad to stand near the cold air. At home, people use them to sleep or work comfortably. The weird thing is that fans cool people, not rooms. People ask for changes in simple words: make it cooler, two degrees lower, turn the fan to low, or, cool the bedroom before I get home. Sometimes they just cheer when the air gets better, and say, that is perfect, hold it there.

Kai texted fast: ac on tomorrow at seven so my room is cool after my shower. The assistant understood that Kai wanted the air conditioning to start at seven tomorrow, so it made a schedule and said so. Kai's glasses always fogged when stepping from a hot shower into a warm room, and last night his sister had been angry because the whole apartment was hot. Kai also asked for the temperature to stay at twenty-two degrees. The assistant set that too. The next evening the room was cool and quiet, and nobody was angry at all.

Living near other people means sharing space, and sometimes things go bad. A storm knocks a branch onto the road. A dog barks all night. A colleague who lives nearby might say the noise kept them awake. People then use an app or a phone to ask for help. They say, tell the neighbors to stop the loud music after ten, or, post a note about the broken light. They change their mind with words like, never mind, or, wait until tomorrow. They also ask, who do I call about a fallen tree? Clear and polite words make neighbors happier.
