Assistant: I can't read messages from the doctor's office, but I can show you your missed calls. Would you like that?
Person: Yes, please.

Hana was in her humid kitchen, stirring a stew, when she remembered the delivery. "Track order," she said. The assistant checked and said her new pan was out for delivery, due by five o'clock. A cooking stream was playing on the tablet, and the assistant turned it down so she could hear. Hana added, "Tell the driver to ring twice." The assistant put the note on her order. It also said the driver would need the key code for the building gate, and asked if it should send it. Hana said yes, and the assistant sent the code to the driver.

A baby monitor lets parents hear or see a baby who is asleep in another room. It is for knowing when the baby wakes, and for keeping feeding times and nap times in order. Parents change the volume, switch on night mode and set reminders. They say, turn the monitor louder, remind me to feed her at six, or, wake me if she cries. Many keep personal notes on what the baby ate, like pieces of fruit that were peeled and mashed. A baby with little hair may still need a hat when it is cold. Parents also say, how long did she sleep, or, start the nap timer.

Tara was lying under the bathroom sink, fixing a faucet, when her little son called out a homework question. She spoke to her phone. "What is forty-eight divided by six?" The assistant understood it as a division and said eight. "And what is half of that?" she asked. The assistant said four. Tara said her son's next question was twice as hard, so she asked, "What is seven times nine?" The assistant answered sixty-three. Then she asked it to create a note: buy twice as many pencils. The assistant made the note and put it at the top of her shopping list.

name: days_until
does: Counts how many days are left until a date, or since a date, and can rank several dates by which comes first.
inputs: a date or the name of an event, and optionally a list of other dates
people say:
- how long until my birthday
- how many sleeps till the holiday
- which comes first, the party or the trip
- countdown to Friday
- how many days until my next lesson, it feels weird to lose count

They want to restart a frozen computer without losing their files.
Restart my computer but keep my files.
reboot, don't delete anything
The screen is stuck. Please restart it, but don't wipe anything.
Turn it off and on again, nothing else.
I don't understand why it froze, so just restart it and leave my folders alone.
The screen has been acting rough all day, so could you please restart the computer so the printer connects again? I do not want to erase or move any of my files.

Buses and trains run on timetables, which say when each one leaves each stop. A timetable is for planning a trip so you do not wait too long. When a bus or train is late, that is called a delay. People change the stop they leave from, the time they want to go and which line they take. They say, when is the next train to the ocean, is the number nine bus late, or, find a station with a lift. On a bitter cold morning, many people ask, are the trains running, before they leave the house.

They want an idea for a birthday gift for their mother.
Gift ideas for mom?
What should I get my mom?
I need a present for my mother, nothing boring.
Suggest something for her birthday that isn't flowers.
Help me pick a gift, something she can touch and use, not just a card.
She is hard to shop for, and I'm a hundred percent sure she does not want a candle.
Her constant complaint is that she has too much stuff, so please give me ideas that are not scarves or mugs.

Jay was on the bus heading east, texting his phone fast. He was planning a party and wanted to invite twelve friends, with seven pieces of candy for each. He typed: "how mcuh is 12 times 7". The assistant understood it as the question how much is twelve times seven, and it answered eighty-four. Jay then wrote "ok thats a lot of candy," and asked for half of that. The assistant said forty-two. Jay decided to buy forty-two pieces and tell his friends to bring their own.

They want a reminder about a friend's birthday.
Remind me about Sam's birthday.
Don't let me forget Sam's birthday on Friday.
Ping me tomorrow at seven about the party.
I want a reminder before my journey on Saturday, so I can buy Sam a card first.
Set a bright alert on my screen for Sam's birthday.
Could you tell me tomorrow at seven that Sam's birthday is this week?
Would you please nudge me the day before, since I want to bring a gift?

A ticket is your proof that you can ride a bus or train. It is for paying the fare, and some tickets are good for one trip and some for a whole day. Young children often ride free or pay half, and older people may have a cheaper fare too. People change the kind of ticket, how many people it is for and the day it starts. They say, buy a day pass, two tickets for tomorrow, or, a ticket for my daughter. The stop for the museum lies two blocks past the library, and the app keeps a record of your trips so you can see what you paid.

Ben, a student, was doing his fraction homework with the radio on low. The song that came on was not one he cared for. "Change station," he said to his speaker. The assistant understood he wanted a different radio station and switched to the news station he usually listens to. The news was about the weather, which was fine. After a minute Ben said, "Volume up," and the assistant made the sound a little louder. Then he got back to his fractions, with the usual voice of the news reader in the background.

They want the robot mower to start cutting the grass now.
Start mowing.
Mow the lawn.
Can the robot cut the grass now?
Get the mower going, it's an easy job.
I'd like the lawn cut before the rain comes, so please send the mower out.
Let the robot out for a run, I don't want to touch a button.
Check the battery balance on the mower and then get it going on the front lawn.

Person: when does my flight leave
Assistant: Which flight is it? Can you tell me the flight number, or the city you are going to?
Person: the one to lisbn tomorrow
Assistant: Thank you. Your flight to Lisbon leaves tomorrow at 7:40 in the morning from gate 12, which is in the green zone of the terminal.
Person: ok, i'll scroll through my email to find the check-in time. i only packed lettuce wraps for lunch lol
Assistant: Check-in opens about three hours before the flight. Would you like a reminder for tomorrow at 4:30?
Person: yes please

Luca was a teenager who worked on weekends at a shop that sells boots. His phone buzzed: the staff call was about to start. He texted his assistant, "Could you please open the meeting link for the staff call and share my screen with the sales sheet? I'm a little late, and my manager said she would wait for me." The assistant opened the link from his calendar and joined the call. Then it shared his screen with the sales sheet, as he asked. It told him it had joined with the camera off and his microphone muted, and Luca said that was fine.

Nina ran for the door with a cookie in her hand. "Make a note," she said to her phone. "Get double the milk this week, and half the sugar." The assistant answered in a polite voice that it understood. It wrote one note that said buy twice as much milk and half as much sugar as last time, and it saved the note to her shopping list. Nina also asked for one more pair of socks to be put on the list, and the assistant did that too. Then she shut the door and went to work.

Person: Set a timer for the stew. Keep it short, I'm driving.
Assistant: How many minutes should the timer run?
Person: I want the stew ready tomorrow at seven. I need to see the recipe when I park.
Assistant: The recipe says the stew needs three hours of cooking. I can't start your oven from here, but I can remind you at four tomorrow to put the pot on.
Person: Good. Is the oven temperature the same as the one in the book? I just want to be comfortable with it.
Assistant: Yes, it is 160 degrees. Please bring a big wooden spoon too. I will show you the recipe when you stop.

Coffee, tea and smoothies can all be made weaker or stronger, sweeter or less sweet. A drink is for waking up, cooling down or just enjoying a break. People change how strong it is, how much sugar goes in and how big the cup is. They say, make it stronger, no sugar please, or, a small soft drink with ice. A smoothie maker can draw a little fruit skin into the cup, so some people ask for the skin to be left out. A good tea takes three minutes, and people tell the assistant, set a timer for three minutes.

A package is a box or an envelope that is sent to your home. People use packages to get things they ordered, like a new humidifier, without going to a shop. A tracking number shows where the box is. People change the day it comes, where it is left and who signs for it. They say, where is my parcel, leave it with the neighbor, or, deliver it on Saturday. If a box shows up at a weird time, or a weird place, they ask the assistant to check it. The box may also say how to install the thing inside it.

It was Monday, and Ken was late for work. He ran to the car with his coffee and shouted at his phone, "Traffic news." The assistant understood he wanted a traffic report from the radio and tuned in to the local traffic station. The voice on the radio said there was a crash on the highway and told drivers to look for a different road. Ken said, "Great," which was not what he meant, and then said, "Another route." The assistant opened the map and showed him a way through the town that was ten minutes slower.

name: check_balance
does: Tells you how much money is in one of your own accounts right now, so you feel sure before you spend.
inputs: which account, like checking or savings
people say:
- how much do I have in savings
- can I afford a new tv this month
- take a quick look at my account
- what's left in checking
- tell me my balance

A flight board shows when planes leave and land, and which gate each one uses. It is for knowing where to be and when. If a plane is late, the board shows a delay and a new time. People change the flight they follow, the airport and how they want to hear about changes. They say, when does my flight leave, which gate is it, or, tell me if it is late. My dad always checks the board before he leaves home. If a flight number is lost, people dig through their email to find it. A dry, clear day usually means few delays.

Hugo was in the garden with a cup of creamy coffee on the bench. The hose began to drip onto the tomatoes, but he left it. He had a different job: his phone's password was too old. "Make my phone lock sooner," he said, "after one minute, not five." The assistant understood that he wanted the screen to lock after one minute, which is less time than before. It changed the setting, and then it asked Hugo to press the button on the side of the phone to check the lock. He pressed it, the screen went dark, and the assistant said the change was saved.

They want to lock their phone right now.
Lock my phone.
Lock it now.
Phone locked, please.
I'm getting in the bath, so please lock my phone.
Tidy up my screen and lock it.
Could you lock the phone before I walk into the local cafe?
Keep people out of my phone, lock it for now.

name: share_clip
does: Turns a saved video clip into a link that friends can open online, and measures the clip first to tell you if it is too big.
inputs: which clip, and who to send it to
people say:
- send my video to Mia
- put my dance video online
- get a link for the beach clip
- let grandma watch the video of me trying on my jeans
- how big is this clip

They want to know where their parcel is and when it will come.
Where's my parcel and when is it coming?
Track my package and tell me the date.
Can you check the parcel and say if it will come today?
I ordered a garlic press, so is it on its way and when does it land?
The tracking page is not working, so find my order and tell me when it comes.
I need the new iron before I iron shirts for the week, so where is the parcel and what day does it get here?

A playlist is a list of songs that you put together and play in order. People use playlists for a workout, a party or a quiet night. They design a playlist by picking songs, artists or a mood. They also change the volume, which works like a thermostat for sound: up when the room is loud, down when it is late. They say, play my running playlist, skip this song, turn it down, or, play something by that singer again. A salty sea song might go on a beach list. When people are done, they say, stop the music.

Person: record the front of the shop for an hour
Assistant: Sure. Which camera should I use, the door camera or the one by the till?
Person: the door one. i want to show the new bush plants we sell
Assistant: Good. The door camera will record for one hour, starting now.
Person: thats cool. can you post it on my shop page when it's done
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't post to your shop page. I can save the video and tell you when it is ready, if you like.
Person: ok save it

Mia's taxi was waiting by the park, and she was late. She ran to the door and typed to the home app: "turn on the alram and set the cameras to medium." The assistant understood that she wanted the alarm on and the cameras at medium sensitivity, and it did both. Mia then typed, "list open windows." The assistant checked the sensors and said the kitchen window was still open. Mia ran back, shut it, and the assistant told her the house was safe. She jumped into the taxi.

Person: Please turn on the porch camera and tell me if anyone rang the bell today.
Assistant: Sure. Which camera do you mean, the front porch or the back door?
Person: The front porch. I'm in the laundry room and the washer is so loud I can't hear a thing.
Assistant: Got it. The front porch camera is on and it works well. The bell rang twice today, once at nine and once at noon.
Person: Good. Lock the back door and set the alarm too.
Assistant: The back door is locked. What time should the alarm start tonight?
Person: Ten o'clock, please.

A phrase app helps you say simple things in another language, like asking where the park is or how much a ticket costs. People use it when they travel, or when they are tired of looking up words one at a time. You can change the language, slow the voice down, or save a phrase to a list. You might say, "say it again slower," or "switch to Spanish," or "what does this word mean?" Learning a language is a bit like making soup: you stir in a few new words every day, and slowly they mix together. Spelling help works the same way. Ask how to spell a word and the assistant says it letter by letter.

Sam woke up bored and slow. A bird sat on the fence outside, singing at nothing. His phone was on the pillow, so he picked it up and mumbled, "Show tasks." The assistant understood that he wanted his to-do list for today and read it out: pay the water bill, call Aunt Rosa, and fix the shelf. Sam yawned. "Bill's paid." The assistant understood that the water bill was already done, so it checked that task off the list. Then Sam said, "Count what's left," and the assistant told him two tasks were left. Sam smiled, because two tasks felt easy, and he got out of bed.

Priya woke up to her phone buzzing again and again. Every few seconds it showed a new like on her photo of the cake she baked. She rubbed her eyes and said, "Stop telling me about every like, but don't turn off messages from my sister." The assistant understood that she did not want like alerts, but she did want to keep messages from her sister. It turned off the like notifications and left the sister messages on. A minute later the phone was quiet. Then a friend's post, written in big capital letters, seemed to shout about cheap concert tickets. Priya smiled and saved the post for later, since she was finally awake.

An automatic pet feeder gives your cat or dog food at the same times every day. It is useful when you are at work or away for the weekend. People often change how much food comes out, or when the meal happens. They might say, "give him a bit less at night," or "feed her at seven instead of eight." The feeder can also record each meal, so you can check later that the bowl was filled. Some people put the bowl on a rug so the floor stays clean. If a pet seems too full or too hungry, you can ask for a smaller or bigger portion.

Mia was lying on a towel at the beach with her phone. She typed, "ugh the sun is so strong and my nose is already pink." The assistant understood that she was getting sunburnt and needed sun cream. It said it could set a reminder to put on more every two hours, and Mia said yes. It also told her the tide would fall in about an hour, so there would be a pretty strip of sand to walk on. Mia found her missing sock under the towel and laughed. When the reminder buzzed two hours later, she put on more sun cream and moved under the umbrella.

Ben sat at his desk with a messy pile of papers and a cold coffee. He said to his phone, "Read me the top headlines and tell me the score of last night's game." The assistant understood that he wanted two things, so it did both. First it read three headlines: one about a new bridge, one about an artist who would paint a big picture of the ocean on a school wall, and one about the weather. Then it said the home team had won by two points. Ben nodded, thanked the assistant, and went back to sorting his papers while it read the next headline.

Lena woke up in a humid bedroom on a slow afternoon. The fan was not helping. She grabbed her phone and typed fast, in lowercase: "open my book and go to the bookmrak." The assistant understood that bookmrak meant bookmark. It opened her book on the page she had saved, chapter nine. Lena then asked it to call her a good time to stop reading, and the assistant said she usually read for thirty minutes, so it set a gentle timer. Lena lay back with the book, and when the timer rang she put the bookmark back in and went to find a cold drink.

Person: Did my package come today? I'm so tired after work.
Assistant: I can check. Which package do you mean?
Person: The blue one. Wait, no, the one from the shoe website.
Assistant: Okay, the shoe website order. It says it was delivered at ten this morning and left by the front door.
Person: Good. I paid for express shipping, so I'm glad it came quickly.
Assistant: Yes, it came a day early. The porch light flashed when the driver left it there.
Person: Thanks. Can you sign for the next one for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't sign for packages. But I can tell you when one arrives.

Tom was eight and he was going camping on Saturday. He had a little cough, so his mom let him ask the speaker for help. "Tell me what to pack for the tent and what the weather will be on the hill," he said. The assistant understood that he wanted two things. It read a short packing list: a warm jacket, a sleeping bag, a flashlight, and a water bottle. Because of the cough, it said to pack an extra scarf. Then it said the hill would be cool and dry on Saturday. Tom packed his gold flashlight first. He wanted to celebrate the trip with a big marshmallow.

Person: Please lock the door.
Assistant: Of course. Which door do you mean, the front door, the back door, or the garage?
Person: The garage. No wait, the front door. I took the trash out and left it open.
Assistant: The front door is locked now.
Person: Thank you. It was rude of me to leave it open when the neighbor came by.
Assistant: Don't worry. Do you want me to shut the garage door as well?
Person: Yes, please shut it.
Assistant: The garage door is shut.

Carlos was driving to work when he said, "Put on the news station." The assistant understood that he wanted the news on the radio and tuned in to the news channel. Carlos was a bit nervous about being late. A hammer rattled in the toolbox in the back seat, and he tried to ignore it. After a minute he said, "No, wait, the sports channel instead." The assistant understood that he had changed his mind, so it switched to the sports station. Carlos listened to the match talk, spot on time to hear the score. When he parked, he was happy to spot an empty space right by the door.

They want to know if this month's electricity bill is higher than last month's.
Is my bill more than last month?
Did the power bill go up?
How much more did I pay this time?
Text me the amount for this month and last month.
I think my hair dryer may have doubled the bill. Is it twice what it was?
Is the bill half of what it was in winter, or about the same?
Could you tell me if this month's electricity cost is less or more than before?
I'd like a fancy little chart that shows how much more I spent this month, if you don't mind.
Would you please compare this month's bill with last month's and tell me which one is bigger?

They want to find the note about their shopping list.
Shopping list.
Find my list.
Open shopping note.
Where is the note I made for groceries?
Show me what I wrote about the store.
The voice note I made when my phone beeped, the one with the milk and eggs.
I wrote something on a cloudy Monday about what to buy and what's in my purse. Can you find it?
Could you please look through my notes and open the one about groceries?

Dana was folding clothes with one hand and holding a spoon with the other. She called out, "Start the dryer and send me a message when it's done." The assistant understood that she wanted two things, so it started the dryer and said it would send a message when the cycle ended. Her son was watching an episode of his favorite show, and he opened his eyes wide when the dryer began to hum. Forty minutes later the phone buzzed with a message that the dryer was done. Dana put the spoon down, took out the warm clothes, and filled the wide basket again.

Grandpa Joe did not know much about his new gadgets. The little box by his bed was one of them. Last night he had woken up too early, so he said to it, "I want to sleep longer. Make my alarm half an hour later." The assistant understood that he wanted the alarm moved from seven to seven thirty, and it said so. Joe was glad. "And I'd like more deep sleep," he said. The assistant explained that it could not change how he slept, but it could remind him to go to bed earlier. Joe agreed. The next morning he slept until seven thirty and felt much better.

Nora had just finished a long night shift at the hospital. On the bus home she said to her phone, "Find out if the Thai place is open and book a table for two at seven." The assistant understood that she wanted two things. It checked the opening hours and found the restaurant was open until ten. Then it booked a table for two at seven. It also warned her that the place gets busy on weekends, so she should arrive a little early. Nora has a vegetarian diet, so she asked for the menu, and the assistant said there were many dishes she could eat. For dessert she wanted frozen yogurt. She smiled and closed her eyes.

Harold did not trust his phone much, but his hair was getting long. He was cutting bread with a knife in the kitchen when he said, "Book haircut." The assistant understood that he wanted an appointment at the barber. It asked, "Which day would you like?" Harold said, "Saturday morning." The assistant booked ten o'clock on Saturday and said the barber would welcome him at the shop on Elm Street. It also said the wait is usually short, with a maximum of fifteen minutes. Harold thanked it and finished his sandwich. On Saturday he walked in at ten, and the barber was ready for him.

Lily was nine and she lived a mile from the park. Her tomatoes were the thing she cared about most. Before school she told the speaker, "Water the plants tomorrow at seven." The assistant understood that she wanted the garden sprinkler to run at seven o'clock the next morning, and it said it had set that up. Lily also wanted to paint the fence blue, but she knew the paint needed to dry, so she asked the assistant if it would rain. It said no rain was coming. The next morning the sprinkler turned on at seven, and the tomatoes got a long drink while Lily ate breakfast.

Omar woke up and checked his phone before his eyes were fully open. "Where's my parcel?" he asked. The assistant understood that he wanted the tracking for his latest online order and told him the driver was about twenty-five minutes away. Omar said, "Forward that to my brother." The assistant sent the tracking message to his brother. The parcel was a pair of cinema tickets in a small envelope, a gift for his mom. The assistant said there might be a short delay on the road, but it would still come before noon. Omar got up, made tea, and waited by the door.

Person: Could you please set a timer for my card game? My grandchildren are coming on Friday, and I want every turn to be short so nobody gets bored.
Assistant: Happy to. How long should each turn be?
Person: Oh, I don't know. What do you think?
Assistant: Two minutes is a good start. Should I set it for two minutes?
Person: Yes. And can you tell me the current score?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't see your cards, so I don't know the score. If you tell me the points, I can keep them.
Person: Good idea. Please wipe the old score first.
Assistant: Done. The score is zero to zero.

Aisha got home from the hospital at dawn, tired and hungry. She was on a diet, so she poured a bowl of plain oats and sat in the dim kitchen. Then she remembered the old camera by the door and typed fast, in lowercase: "turn on the hallway camra." The assistant understood that she meant the hallway camera. It turned the camera on and said it was recording. She asked if a second one could be installed by the back door. The assistant said it could not install a camera by itself, but it could find a local shop and book a visit. Aisha said yes, and then she went to sleep.

Mark came home after a long day at the office and said, "Play some jazz on the kitchen speaker." The assistant understood that he wanted jazz in the kitchen and started a soft playlist there. A minute later Mark said, "Actually, the living room one." The assistant understood that he had changed his mind, so it stopped the music in the kitchen and moved it to the living room speaker. The room was dark, so Mark asked for the lamp to be turned on, and the assistant did that. On the other hand, he did not want it too loud, since he had invited a friend to talk. He asked for the volume to be lower, and the assistant lowered it.

They want the pool pump turned on.
Pump on.
Start the pool pump.
The water looks dim and cloudy. Can you get the pump going?
Switch the pool cleaner on, please.
I'd like the pump running before lunch.
My kids have swim practice in an hour. Can you start the pool pump?
Could you please turn on the pump now? We have a birthday party at the pool this afternoon, and I want the water to be clear before we bring out the cake.
Would you mind starting the pump so the water is clean and ready for our guests?

Jin ran out the door with a bag in one hand and his phone in the other. The assistant could hear him breathing fast. "Days left?" he asked. The assistant was not sure what he meant, so it said, "Days left until what?" Jin said, "My trip." The assistant knew his trip was on the calendar for next Tuesday. It answered that there were six days left. Jin said, "Message Dad." The assistant sent a text to his dad saying Jin would be there in six days. Jin read it online later on the train and was glad it had gone through.

Grace owns a small shop on a busy road. One morning she walked in and sniffed. "It smells dusty in here, and the air feels heavy," she said to the smart speaker. The assistant understood that she thought the air filter was old and needed a change. It asked if she wanted a repair visit, and Grace said yes. It found a digital booking page and set a visit for Thursday at nine. Grace wanted to know the price. The assistant told her the filter was forty dollars. She asked it to subtract the price from this week's repair budget, and the assistant told her what was left. Grace nodded and opened the shop.

A digital door lock works with a code, a phone, or a small card instead of a key. It is for people who forget keys, or who want to let a guest in while they are away. At a theater or an office, the same kind of lock lets only some people turn the handle and walk in. At home, people change the code, add a guest code for a day, or lock the door from far away. They might say, "lock the front door," "let my sister in," or "change the code to a new one." The lock can also tell you when the door was last opened.

They want to know the weather in the hills tonight.
Is it going to be chilly up there?
Will it get cold tonight in the hills?
How low will it go tonight?
Will it drop below ten degrees?
Should I bring a thick jacket for the hill camp?
I want to cook outside tonight. Will the wind be too strong?
Is it too chilly to put the carpet down in the tent and sleep?
Could you please tell me what the night weather will be like on the hill, so I know how many blankets to pack?

Rosa came in from walking the dog and hung the leash on the hook. The house felt dry and smelled of salty soup from last night. She said, "Turn on the air purifier and make the room a little less dry." The assistant understood that she wanted two things, so it switched on the purifier and started the humidifier. It said the air would feel better in about an hour. Her son said, "I like the humidifier, it sounds like rain." Rosa laughed. Then she asked the assistant to open the window in the kitchen for a few minutes, to let in fresh air. The assistant said it could not open windows, but it could remind her to do it.

Many board games and puzzles keep score or use a timer. A timer helps everyone know when a turn will end, and a score keeper helps players remember the points. Sometimes the rules seem weird, so people ask for them to be read out loud. They might say, "start a three minute timer," "give me ten more seconds," or "add five points to Sam." Some people also ask, "who is winning?" or "reset the score." An empty can or a plastic cup can hold game pieces, and a small bell can mark the end of a round. The fun part is that everyone agrees on the rules before they begin.

Grandpa Arthur stood at the bottom of the hill with his bike. His homework from the doctor was to ride a little every day, but his legs felt tired just looking at the hill. He told the speaker, "That hill looks like a mountain today." The assistant understood that he did not want a hard ride, so it found three routes and ranked them by how flat they were. The first was a small loop by the river, about five miles. Arthur chose that one. The assistant read the turns out loud, and he rode slowly, enjoying the trees. At the end he was a little tired, but he was glad he had gone.

They want to know what events are happening on their street this weekend.
Any local events?
What's on this weekend near me?
Something happening a step from my door?
Show me the community events for Saturday and Sunday.
Tell me about the street fair, and turn on a reminder for it.
Are there any medium sized events nearby, like a market or a concert in the park?
Find the events near my house this weekend and let me know which ones are free.
Could you please check the neighborhood board and tell me about the events, and also tell me if there is any noise warning for the weekend?

A car needs a little care to run well. Fuel and tyre pressure are the two things most people check. When a tyre feels soft, you add air; when a tyre cap is loose, you tighten it. Many people ask their assistant, "how much fuel is left?" or "are my tyres okay?" My grandfather used to say a car you can afford is one you can keep clean and check each week. Warming up the car on a cold morning is also common, so people say, "start the car in five minutes" or "warm it up to twenty degrees." Some ask, "where did I park?" and the car replies with the street.

Writing is how we put ideas on a page. A first draft is just a rough try, and editing is what you do later to fix it. Kids at school write stories, and grown-ups write emails and notes. People often ask a helper to check spelling, count the words, or make a sentence shorter. They might say, "how do you spell necessary?" or "how many words is this?" or "make this sound more polite." When a kid is stuck, they might click on a spelling tool to see the right word. It is pretty normal to change a sentence many times. Most good writing comes from drafting, reading it out loud, and fixing it again.

Kim came out of the hospital after a long night shift, feeling empty. A light rain fell on the forest of trees by the bus stop. She took out her phone and said, "Order dinner." The assistant asked, "From which place?" Kim said, "The usual." The assistant understood that she meant the noodle shop on Forest Road, where she ordered several times a week. It ordered her regular noodles and told her they would arrive in thirty minutes. Kim said, "Call me when it's close." The assistant said it would send a call when the driver was near. She sat on the bus and finally relaxed.

Person: I need to pay the electric bill.
Assistant: I can help with that. Which bill is it, and how much is it?
Person: Twenty-five dollars. I'm very tired after work, so please be quick.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't pay bills. But I can remind you of the date and the amount.
Person: That's fine. It's due on the tenth. I just bought some pork on the way home, and I forgot the date. Can you zoom in on the bill photo so I can read it?
Assistant: Yes, I zoomed in. It is due on the tenth. Should I remind you the day before?
Person: Yes, please. I got a message saying it was late, but that was a false alarm.
Assistant: Good. I'll remind you on the ninth.

name: bake_timer
does: Works out when to start each step of a bake and sets a timer, so bread and cakes come out kind and soft.
inputs: what you are baking, the oven temperature, and what time you want it ready
people say:
- When should the bread go in so it's done by six?
- My dough is ready. How long do I let it rise?
- Set a timer for the cookies, they burn if I forget.
- I think my mixer belt is slipping, so how long should I knead by hand?
- Tell me when the cake needs to come out.

Many people park their cars on a street and forget where they left them. A car helper can remember the place for you. On a street north of the market, for example, every car looks the same in the evening. People ask, "where is my car?" or "show me where I parked." The same helper can tell you if the car needs fuel or is covered in dust. You might say, "is it dirty?" or "remind me to wash it on Saturday." Some people also ask it to warm up the engine before they leave, or to tell them when the tyre pressure is low.

name: write_email_draft
does: Writes a first draft of an email in the tone you want, and can send a blind copy to people you choose.
inputs: who the email is for, what it should say, and the tone, like warm or formal
people say:
- Write a note to my boss saying I'll be late.
- Make it sound warm, not stiff.
- Send this to the team but hide everyone's addresses.
- Tell Anna thanks for the dinner, keep it short.
- Can you help me sound polite? I need to say no to a meeting.

name: pet_walk_planner
does: Plans a dog walk by picking a time and a route, and tells you how long the walk will take.
inputs: the pet's name, how long you want to walk, and the time of day
people say:
- Rex needs a walk this morning, but it might rain.
- Where can my dog swim near here?
- Plan a short walk, only twenty minutes.
- Pick a quiet route for my shy dog.
- Show me several places where dogs can run free.

Ravi owns a shop on the corner, and his hands were full of boxes. His pulse was fast from rushing around. He said to his phone, fast and in lowercase, "chekc off ordr stock and move paint to monday." The assistant understood that he had typed fast. It marked the stock order as done on his to-do list, and moved the paint task to Monday. The list felt strange to Ravi, because it was so short now. He asked the assistant to change the first item to top priority, and it did. Ravi smiled, picked up another box, and went to open the door for his first customer.

Amy was new to the city and lived on the north side. She sat on the porch with her baby, who was finally asleep. "Remind me to feed the baby at six," she said to the phone. The assistant set a reminder for six o'clock. Then Amy said, "No, wait, half past six. She ate late today." The assistant understood that she had changed her mind. It deleted the first reminder and set a new one for six thirty. Amy also asked when the baby's last nap had started, and the assistant told her it was at two. She put the phone down and watched the quiet street.

Person: Join the meeting.
Assistant: Which meeting do you mean? You have two today.
Person: The monthly one with Pat.
Assistant: Okay, joining the monthly meeting with Pat now.
Person: I can't hear well. Make it twice as loud.
Assistant: I made the sound louder. Is that better?
Person: Yes. Oh, sorry, I was eating lunch with a fork and my voice cracked.
Assistant: That's okay. Do you want me to share your screen too?
Person: Not yet, maybe later.

They want a reminder about their homework due date.
Remind me about homework.
Tell me when my work is due.
Can you ping me tomorrow at seven about the maths sheet?
I need a temporary reminder for Friday morning, just for the history essay.
After I bathe the dog tomorrow morning, tell me what homework is left.
What is due this week, and when?
Would you please remind me the night before my science project is due?
Could you please set a reminder for tomorrow morning at eight so I remember to hand in my book report before class?

Tony was a cook, and his left hand was covered in flour. His phone buzzed on the counter with a warning that the battery was low. He said, "Don't turn off the ringer, just make the screen dimmer." The assistant understood that he did not want the ringer silent, since he was waiting for a call from the delivery driver. It lowered the screen brightness and kept the ringer on. Tony asked it to speak the battery percentage, and it said, "Fifteen percent." He plugged the phone in next to the bags of rice on the shelf, high above the stove, at a height he could reach. Then he went back to making dough.

Person: Call Mary.
Assistant: Which Mary? You have Mary Smith and Mary from the clinic.
Person: My daughter.
Assistant: Mary Smith, then. Calling her now.
Person: Wait. Can you lend me your voice so I can say hello to my grandson in the grade school choir?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't lend my voice to other people. But I can send him a short message from you. What should it say?
Person: Tell him I'm proud of him. And that his tiny singing voice is the best.
Assistant: I'll send that to him.

They want the steps to make pancakes.
Pancake steps.
How do I make pancakes?
Tell me the recipe and the cooking time.
Show me how to cook pancakes, and read the steps out loud.
My cousin is coming over. What do I do first for pancakes, and how fast can I make them?
It's snowing outside and I want warm pancakes. Where do I start?
What's the quickest way to make a stack, and how hot should the pan be?
Could you please walk me through the recipe step by step, and tell me when to flip each one?

name: power_cut_helper
does: Tells you what to do during a power cut and finds out when the electricity will come back.
inputs: your street or address, and how long the power has been out
people say:
- All the lights went out. What is going on?
- When will the power be back on?
- Is the whole street dark, or just us?
- The fridge is warm. How long is the food safe?
- Tell the electric company that we have no power. My band has a show tonight, and we need the stage lights, which is a pretty big problem.
- Can someone visit and check the box outside?

Mrs. Lopez was a retired teacher who still liked to be organized. Her flight to the coast was in the afternoon. She sat at the kitchen table and asked the assistant, "Is my plane more than an hour late?" The assistant understood that she wanted to know if the flight was delayed. It looked up the flight times and said it was only twenty minutes late, which was less than an hour. Her neighbor would look after the dog, so she was not worried. She asked if the gate had changed, and the assistant said it was still gate twelve. She packed a bag of salty nuts, put a warm coat on, and waited for the taxi. On the plane, she would not freeze.

Hobbies like painting, knitting, and drawing give people a quiet way to enjoy their time. A young person might build a model plane, and an older person might knit a scarf. Many people use a helper to keep track of their craft. They might say, "set a timer for the paint to dry," "remind me to finish my sweater by Friday," or "text my friend a picture of my drawing." Some people do a little of their hobby right after finishing their homework. Others use a list to remember what colors or wool they need to buy. The best part is how good it feels to finish something with your own hands.

Mr. Hale, a retired teacher, stood in his hallway and looked at the dusty floor. "Hey phone," he said, "I do not want the big loud vacuum today. Send the little robot, and skip the bedroom." The assistant understood three things: use the smart robot vacuum, leave the bedroom alone, and keep the noise low. It sent the robot to the hallway, the kitchen and the living room, and it marked the bedroom as a room to avoid. Then Mr. Hale added, "Tell me when the bin is full. I may need to buy new filters." The assistant said it would send a message when the bin was full, and it put filters on his shopping list so he would not forget. Mr. Hale smiled, made a cup of tea and listened to the robot hum along the floor.

Grandpa Ron sat at the kitchen table with his tablet. He was a careful man, and the water bill had been on his mind all week. He typed quickly, with one finger: "when is my watr bill due". The assistant understood that he was asking about the water bill and looked up the date. "Your water bill is due on the twelfth," it said. "It is forty dollars." Ron wanted to stretch his money until the end of the month, so he typed again: "update my reminder to two days before". The assistant changed the reminder from the twelfth to the tenth and told him plainly that the old reminder was gone and the new one was set. Ron nodded. "Good," he said. "No more late fees." Then he finished his tea.

I want my parcel to be delivered at a different time.
Can you move my parcel to tomorrow at seven?
Deliver it later, please.
Not the usual time, make it after work.
Fix a new slot for my package, say Friday at noon.
My parcel was due on the third of April, but I will be out, so could it come the day after?
Reschedule the delivery.
Could you ask the courier to come later this week instead, since nobody is home before evening?
Push it back a day.
Hold the box until Monday morning and bring it then.

I want to send back something I ordered.
Return my shoes.
Send the blue jacket back.
Can I get my money back for the kettle?
I'm sorry to bother you, but the gas heater I ordered came with a broken knob, so could you please start a return and tell me where to drop it off?
Start a refund for order number 4471.
Rank the return choices for me, quickest first.
It doesn't fit, so I need to swap it for a bigger size.
Please take this back to the shop for me, I'm sorry, I just can't use it.

Mina owns a small shop that sells camping gear. On Friday morning she stood between the tents, holding a steel bowl she wanted to put on sale. A customer was planning a trip to the hills and asked what the weather would be. Mina did not want to walk to the back office, so she spoke to her phone. "Hills weather," she said. The assistant understood that she wanted the current weather in the hills north of town. It answered: cloudy now, ten degrees, with rain after four o'clock. Mina passed the news to the customer, who decided to leave early on Saturday. Then she said, "Rain jackets," and the assistant showed the jackets in her shop, with the number left in stock. Mina moved the three that were left to the front, next to the bowls.

Person: I want to post the video from my granddaughter's party.
Assistant: Which video do you mean? I found three from last weekend.
Person: The one where she sings her favourite song.
Assistant: Got it. Where should I post it, the family group or just one person?
Person: The family group, please. Is it long?
Assistant: It is twenty-five seconds long. Shall I post it now?
Person: Yes. And remind me about my doctor's appointment, I always forget.
Assistant: I posted the video to the family group. What day is the appointment?

A news feed is a short list of stories that your phone or speaker reads out each day. It is there so you can catch up in a few minutes while you sit with your breakfast. People change it to fit their day. If there are too many sports stories, they say, "Show less sport and more local news." If they only have a minute, they say, "Read just the headlines." Some people like to hear about a new movie on Fridays, so they say, "Add film news on Friday." To drop a topic, they say, "Stop showing weather in my news." Many people also change the time, with words like "Read me the news at seven" or "Send it later."

Priya got home after a night shift with heavy eyes and a weak voice. She dropped her bag by the door and said to her phone, "Anything in my email?" The assistant explained that she had a dozen unread messages and that three of them came from the hospital. It read the three aloud. One was from her manager about a change on Friday. "Tell her I will answer tomorrow at seven," Priya said, "and remind me then." The assistant did not send anything. It set a reminder for seven tomorrow morning and saved a short draft that said she would reply after her sleep. "Thank you," Priya said. She put the phone on the table and went to bed.

A table booking keeps a seat for you at a time you choose. It is useful because small restaurants fill up fast, and a Saturday night can be tight. Say you booked a table at the Busy Bee Cafe for four people. Later your plans change, so you ask for changes in plain words. You can say, "Make it five people." You can say, "Move it to eight o'clock," or "Can we sit outside?" If you want to cancel, you say, "Cancel my booking." On a phone you can just click the booking and pick a new time. Some people also ask for the menu or the hours, with words like "Are you open on Sunday?"

name: weekly_dinner_planner
does: Plans a week of dinners that fit what the family likes, and makes a shopping list for them.
inputs: how many people are eating, any foods to avoid, and how much time there is to cook
people say:
- What should we eat this week?
- My girl won't touch fish, so no fish dinners.
- It's foggy and cold, so plan warm meals for Monday to Wednesday.
- I need something quick on school nights, nothing over thirty minutes.
- Translate my wish for lighter food into a menu for five days.
- Fix me a dinner list for four people that doesn't cost much.

A bill is a request to pay for something you used, like electricity, water or rent. It has an amount and a due date, and paying late can cost extra. People change a few things about their bills. They set a reminder, move the due date, or choose to pay by the week instead of the month. Some banks round each payment up to the next dollar and save the difference, a little cushion like a soft pillow for the budget. To ask for these changes, people say things like, "Remind me three days before the rent is due," "Pay the water bill on the first," or "Round up my payments." If a bill is late, they say, "Pay it today."

Sun cream protects your skin from the sun at the beach. It is for the hours when you swim and play, and the sun is strongest at midday. Most people buy it at the pharmacy, and the number on the bottle tells how strong it is. A good rule is to put it on twenty minutes before you go out and again after you swim. People ask their phones to calculate the time. They say, "Remind me to put on sun cream every two hours," or "Tell me when the tide comes in." They also check the water: "How warm is the sea today?" Even a tiny change in the weather matters, so people say, "Check the sun strength again at noon."

I want to pay my yearly insurance bill early.
Pay the yearly insurance now.
While I brush my teeth, pay that insurance bill, and play a song when it's done.
Settle the annual insurance today instead of next month.
Can you take care of the insurance payment for this year before the due date?
Send the money for the one that comes once a year.
I'd like to pay it early, please, so I do not have to think about it later.
Pay it from my savings. Sorry, I mean from my checking account.
Do it now, no, wait, make it Friday.

Person: Cut the lawn shorter this time.
Assistant: How short? The mower is set to four centimetres now.
Person: Half of that, please.
Assistant: Two centimetres. Do you want me to start now?
Person: Yes, but keep the mower away from the flower beds. A little girl from next door left her toys there, and I want to hold off on that corner.
Assistant: I will skip the flower beds and the corner by the fence.
Person: Lovely. Can you also make the grass grow faster?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't do that. I can only cut it, but I can set the mower to run every three days instead of every week.
Person: Do that.

A smart speaker is a small box that listens for your voice and does what you ask. It is there to play music, answer questions and control things around the house. Most speakers use one account, but families can add more voices so the speaker knows who is talking. People change the volume all day. They say, "Turn it down," "Louder in the kitchen," or "Pull the volume back to low." They can group speakers with words like, "Play this in every room." A speaker is not the place to handle anything dangerous, like a fire or a bad fall. For that, people use the emergency number on a phone.

I want my coffee a little stronger.
Stronger, please.
Make my favorite coffee with two shots.
What happens if you use more beans? Do that.
Make it strong and put it on the bill.
Make it a bit stronger. No, wait, I mean tea, not coffee.
Less water in the cup so it is bolder.
Could you make it stronger and a little less sweet? Actually, keep the sugar the same.

Tom owns a wine shop with a small lawn behind it. On Tuesday morning he looked out of the window and said to his phone, "Start the sprinklers for twenty minutes." The assistant understood that he wanted the back lawn watered and set a twenty-minute timer. A minute later, Tom saw that the grass was still soft and wet from the night rain. "No, wait," he said. "Don't water today. Stop the sprinklers and try again on Friday." The assistant stopped the timer before the water started, then made a new one for Friday at the same time. It told Tom that nothing would run today and that the sprinklers were set for Friday morning. Tom thanked it and opened the shop.

Person: Hi, I just moved here and my wifi is slow. Can you switch me to the faster network?
Assistant: Sure. There are two networks, Home and Home Fast. Which one do you want?
Person: Home Fast. Sorry, no, wait, I think the guest one is the fast one. I'm not sure.
Assistant: The guest network is slow. Home Fast is the faster one. Should I switch to it?
Person: Yes. I have an online exam tonight and I can't be late.
Assistant: Done, you are on Home Fast now. Do you want me to check the speed again in an hour?
Person: Please do.

I want a longer bedtime story for my child.
Make the story longer.
One more story, please.
Double the length of tonight's story.
Download the one about the sour lemon so we have it in the car.
Can you forward the new story to Grandma's phone?
Keep going, we're not done yet.
Tell a story that lasts half an hour instead of ten minutes.

Rosa came in from the garden with dirt on her hands. The dishwasher had stopped again, and its little screen showed an error in German. "Translate this message," she said to her phone, and held the camera up. The assistant read the words and told her plainly that the filter was blocked. It said this problem is frequent when a dishwasher is used after muddy gardening gloves. Rosa laughed. She cleaned the filter, then said, "Run the dishwasher tomorrow at seven." The assistant set a timer so the dishwasher would start at seven in the morning, and it said so out loud. Rosa went back out to her tomatoes.

name: light_scene_manager
does: Saves, applies or deletes a named lighting scene, such as a dim movie setting.
inputs: the scene name, what to do with it, and which room
people say:
- Set up the laundry light so I can see while I load the washer.
- Delete the party colours from the living room.
- Turn the bedroom to full brightness for cleaning.
- Save this soft glow and call it reading time.
- Get rid of my old movie night lights.
- Put the lights back the way they were last night.

Ben, a student, was on the bus with his wireless headphones in and his eyes tired from a long night of reading. He typed in a hurry: "make the text biger and read my notes aloud". The assistant understood both parts. It raised the text size on his phone and began to read his notes in a clear voice through the headphones. A bush outside the window waved as the bus went round the corner, and Ben looked up. "Slower," he said. The assistant slowed the voice a little and kept reading from where it had stopped. Ben closed his eyes and listened until his stop.

I want the speaker to be louder.
Louder.
It's freezing on the porch and I can't hear, so turn it up.
Volume up a bit. No, sorry, I meant the kitchen speaker.
The ice machine is so loud that I can't hear the music, please raise the volume.
Keep turning it up until I say stop, and let the light on top flash when you can't go any higher.
Turn it up, but not that much, bring it back down two steps.

Sam, a student, was babysitting for the evening. At eight the baby was getting sleepy, but the blender was working loudly in the kitchen. Sam typed to the speaker in a hurry: "close the nusery blinds and start a nap timer for 40 minutes". The assistant understood that Sam wanted the blinds in the baby's room shut and a timer set for forty minutes. It closed the blinds, started the timer and said it would tell Sam when the nap was over. Sam turned off the blender, and the whole house went quiet.

Jess, a teenager, was learning to cook noodles while texting her friends. Her phone showed twenty-five missed calls, all from her grandmother. That was strange, so she said, "Call Grandma back on speaker." The assistant understood that she wanted to ring her grandmother and use the speakerphone so her hands stayed free. The call started. Grandma was in the attic, looking through old boxes on a cloudy afternoon, and her phone had been on silent. "I found your dad's baby photos," she said, laughing. Jess turned down the heat under the pot, read a quick message from a friend, and asked Grandma to hold up the pictures. The assistant kept the call going on speaker the whole time.

Dana finished her night shift and hung her coat on the hook by the door. Her friend Lee, a teacher, wanted to meet for dinner, but Dana was too tired to look for a place. She typed to her phone in a hurry: "book a tabel for two at the thai place tonight at 7". The assistant understood that she wanted a table for two people at the Thai restaurant she often visits, at seven in the evening. It checked and found the table free, booked it and told her the booking was for seven. It also said the kitchen stays open late, in case they ran behind. Dana sent Lee a quick message and slept on the sofa for an hour.

Omar was at his desk when he remembered that his mother, who lives alone, takes her pills at noon. "Mum's pills," he said quietly to his phone. The assistant understood that he wanted to know if she had taken them today. It checked her pill reminder and said she had confirmed the morning pills but not the noon ones. "Call her," said Omar. The assistant rang his mother. She had just come back from the garden and was making pancakes for the neighbour's children, and she took her pills while they talked. Before the call ended, Omar asked the assistant to set up a video call for Sunday, the kind they zoom on every week, so he could see her face.

Person: I want to read for half an hour every day.
Assistant: Sure. What time should I remind you?
Person: Tomorrow at seven, after dinner. Hold on, I'm slicing a cucumber for the salad right now.
Assistant: No problem. I set a daily reminder for seven in the evening, starting tomorrow. Is every day right?
Person: Yes. And charge my e-reader before then.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't charge it. I can remind you to plug it in at six, though.
Person: Do that, thanks.

I want to know when my food will arrive.
When is my dinner coming?
How long until the driver gets here?
It is thirty degrees outside and my ice cream may melt, so how many minutes are left?
Draw the driver's route on the map.
I'm sorry to bother you, but my phone battery is low and I have to leave soon, so could you please tell me how long the delivery will take?
Is it close yet?

name: next_bus_finder
does: Finds the next buses or trains from a stop and says how late they are running.
inputs: the stop or station, and the line if the person knows it
people say:
- When does the next bus come?
- Is the 8:15 train on time? I'm thirsty and want to buy a drink first.
- Translate this timetable into just the next three trains.
- I have no internet at home, how long will I wait at the corner stop?
- What time is the last tram tonight?
- Is my line running late?

Person: Make my letter shorter.
Assistant: By how much? It is about 400 words now.
Person: Make it half.
Assistant: I'll cut it to about 200 words. Do you want to keep the last paragraph?
Person: Yes, that is my favourite part. I've worked on this for an hour and I need a break.
Assistant: Done, it is shorter now. Do you want me to read it back to you?
Person: Not now. Can you send it to my boss?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send it without an address. Who should get it?

Homework is work from school that students finish at home. It is for practice, and every task has a due date. Late work can make a teacher angry, so many students keep a planner on their phone or in a notebook. People change a planner all the time. They move a due date, add a new task or mark one as finished. They say things like, "Remind me to finish maths on Thursday," "Move the history essay to Friday," or "Close the science task, it's done." Parents use similar words: "What homework is due tomorrow?" Students who want to nail every deadline often ask the planner to remind them the night before.

Zoe was studying at her desk when the lights went out. The room was dark, the street was dark, and her phone battery was nearly empty. She was not scared, only worried about her laptop. "Power cut?" she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted to know if the whole street had lost power. It opened the power company website and read out the notice: a cable had broken on her street and the power would be back in about two hours. "Please be patient," it added. Zoe thanked it. She saved her essay, turned on the phone light, and set an alarm for when the power was due back.

Carlos drives a delivery van, and on Saturday he was moving house. On Thursday night he stood among the boxes and said to his phone, "Don't book the big truck. I do not need two movers, just one." The assistant understood that he wanted a small van and a single mover. It cancelled the big truck and booked one mover for Saturday at nine. The dust from the old boxes made Carlos sneeze, and he asked about the weather. The assistant said it would be mild, about fifteen degrees, with no rain. Carlos put the last box in the back of his van. "Good," he said.

A bike ride tracker shows where you went, how far, and how fast. It is for people who want to see their progress, or plan a route before they leave. After a hot afternoon ride, many people fill the kettle and look at the numbers over tea. People change the settings in small ways. They say, "Plan a flat route of twenty kilometres," "Show my speed in miles," or "Avoid the busy road." They also say, "Tell me when I reach ten kilometres," so the phone speaks during the ride. If they get tired, they say, "Shorten the ride," and the route gets shorter.

Mrs. Ford, a retired teacher, stood in the garage with a bicycle that had a weak brake. She needed two new brake pads and was serious about spending no more than she must. The shop sold one pad for fourteen dollars. "What is twice fourteen?" she asked her speaker, and then, "And is that more or less than thirty?" The assistant understood that she wanted to double the number and compare it to thirty. It said that two times fourteen is twenty-eight, which is less than thirty by two dollars. Mrs. Ford started to smile. She wrote the number on the box lid, ordered the pads, and wheeled the bicycle back to the wall.

Nia had just moved to the city and knew no one. She spoke to her phone, politely: "Excuse me, I am new here and my legs feel weak after sitting at a desk all day, so could you please plan a medium workout for tonight? I would like something gentle that I can do at home." The assistant understood that she wanted a gentle, medium-level workout for home. It made a plan with three sets of ten squats, a short march on the spot and some stretching, with rests in between. Nia asked it to stream some music, and she did her first set on the carpet. Before bed she found a smooth stone in her pocket from the park near her new street, and put it on the shelf.

Leo, a student, sat in the cafe with a black coffee and checked his money. He typed in a hurry: "update my budget, spent 40 on bikee repair this week". The assistant understood that he wanted to record forty dollars for the bike repair under transport in his monthly budget. It made the update and then told him plainly that he had 120 dollars left to spend this month. It also said that this week was ten dollars more than last week. Leo sighed, finished his coffee and decided to walk home instead of taking the bus.

Hana was kneeling in the vegetable garden when she remembered her medicine. Her hands were muddy, so she did not want to touch her phone. "Pill time?" she said. The assistant understood that she was asking when her next pill was due. It answered that the next dose was at noon, in twenty minutes. Hana had been away from the kitchen since breakfast, and the pills were in her bag. "Make a note," she said. The assistant wrote down that she felt fine today and had not missed a dose this week. Her next task was to pick the beans, so she finished the row, washed her hands at the tap and took her pill at noon.

Voicemail is a place where a caller can leave a message when you cannot answer. It is for the times you are busy, away from your phone or asleep. People change a few things about calls. At night they put the phone on quiet so it does not ring. In a meeting they say, "Mute my phone," and later, "Unmute my phone." If they want others in the room to hear, they say, "Put the call on speaker." Many people ask, "Call my teacher back" or "Who called me today?" The phone can read out the missed calls and play each voicemail.

I want to pause my study timer for a while.
Pause the timer.
Hold on, I'm getting some ice for my drink.
It's rare for me to need a break, but I do now, so stop the clock for ten minutes.
Stop the study timer. No, make that fifteen minutes, then resume.
Resume the timer once I say I'm back.
Freeze my homework clock until I come back from lunch.
Could you stop counting? I'll tell you when to start again.

Ken works in an office with one big window. By two o'clock the sun was shining straight on his screen, and he could not read his list of payments. "Close blinds," he said to the speaker on his desk. The assistant understood that he wanted the blinds beside his desk shut, and it closed them halfway. It told him plainly that they were half closed and asked nothing more. Ken had eaten a grilled cheese sandwich for lunch, and now he checked the last payment on his list. It had to go out before five. The room was cooler and the screen was easy to read, so he finished the list by four.

I want to know when my flight leaves.
When does my plane take off?
Departure time?
Is my flight on time? It should be leaving in twenty-five minutes, I think.
What gate do I go to for the plane to Lisbon?
I want to win some time at the shops, so tell me how long before boarding starts.
Tell me if there is an extra delay.
Could you please check the board for me and read out the new time?
Will it leave later than planned?

Mia had worked all night and now wanted her hair done. Her friend had won a half price voucher for a salon, and it ended on Friday. "Book me a haircut," Mia said to her phone, "and I want pink at the tips." The assistant understood that she wanted a haircut with pink colour on the ends. It looked up the salon's opening hours and found a free place on Thursday afternoon at three. Because of the voucher, it said, the price would be half of the usual, about thirty dollars less. Mia said yes, and the assistant booked the visit and added it to her calendar. Then she texted her friend a thank you and went to sleep.

I want to see how much electricity I used.
Show me my power use for this week. No, I mean this month.
How much power did we burn today?
Give me the word on my energy use.
Deliver a short report of my electricity every Monday.
Tell me how much power the solar panels made. I paid a lot for them, so I want to know if they're worth it.
Is the house using less than last month?
Sorry, I meant yesterday, not today: what was the usage?

A contact is a card in your phone with a person's name and details. It is for finding people fast, so you do not have to remember every number. A contact can hold phone numbers, an address, a birthday and a short note. People change contacts all the time. They say, "Add Jo's new number," "Change Mum's address," or "Save this number as the plumber." They also say, "Remind me of Sam's birthday," and "Add a note to Dan: kind man, feeds my hamster when I travel." When a friend moves, you push the new address into the card, and the old one is gone.

Aziz, a cook at a small cafe, was ready for the morning rush. His tablet sat on its charging cable next to the digital scale. "Start twenty cups of strong tea," he said. Then he stopped. "No, wait. Make it coffee, not tea. The cafe sells more coffee on Mondays." The assistant understood the change. It dropped the tea order and started the coffee machine for twenty cups, strong, with no sugar. It said plainly: tea cancelled, coffee started. Aziz weighed the beans on the scale and put out the cups.

I want to know if the house has a leak.
Is there a leak anywhere?
Check the pipes for me.
There is water on the driveway up to the tire of my car, and I am afraid of a flood, so please check the water meter and tell me whether it keeps running.
Is water running when nobody is using it?
Shut off the water if you find something.
Is the water flow stronger than usual tonight?
I'm sorry, but I've been away all week and I'm worried, so could you please look at the water use and see if anything looks strange?

Mr. Okafor, a retired teacher, stood at the open fridge making lunch. "Excuse me," he said to his speaker in a soft voice, "would you please stop reading the sports stories? My grandson is asleep in the next room, and I would like only the local news, a little quieter." The assistant understood that he wanted fewer sports items, only local headlines and a lower volume. It stopped the sports, lowered its voice and read three local headlines: a new bus stop, a bake sale, and road repairs on Elm Street. Mr. Okafor nodded, took the cheese from the fridge and listened while he cut his bread.

Start reading my messages and raise the volume a bit.
Read me my Monday emails. Actually, not all of them, only the ones from my sister.
I can't look at the screen right now, would you mind reading it for me?

Priya got home from her night shift at the hospital, tired and hungry. She still wore her work belt with the little scissors on it. She wanted to cook the soup her mother makes on a daily basis, but the recipe was for eight people and she was only cooking for four. She said to the kitchen speaker, 'This soup is for eight, but I only need half. Can you cut it down?' The speaker understood that she wanted the recipe scaled to half. It read out the new amounts: three cups of broth instead of six, one onion instead of two, and one spoon of salt instead of two. Then it reminded her to stir the pot every few minutes. Priya smiled, thanked it, and began chopping, glad she did not have to do the maths with such a sleepy head.

The person wants ideas for a birthday present for a friend.
Gift ideas for my friend?

I have only a few days left and no clue what to buy, can you help?
Suggest something more unusual than a candle or a mug.
Would you please give me three gift ideas for my dad, who loves coffee, maybe something for his drip machine?

Person: My sink is leaking. Can you get someone to fix it?
Assistant: I'm sorry about the leak. Which day would you like the repair person to come?
Person: Tomorrow, please. Wait, no, my dad is at work tomorrow. Make it Saturday.
Assistant: Okay, Saturday. Is it the kitchen sink or the bathroom sink?
Person: The kitchen one. Mom was washing a raw onion and the water started dripping under it.
Assistant: Thank you. What time on Saturday?
Person: In the morning. I love mornings.
Assistant: Great. I'll ask for a repair visit on Saturday morning for the kitchen sink. Is that right?
Person: Yes. Thank you!

Tom rode his bicycle to the office and sat down at his desk. His tooth had been aching for a whole week, and he kept pressing his cheek. He took out his phone and said, 'My tooth is killing me, but I can't miss work again.' The phone understood that he needed a dentist and that he wanted a time outside of his busy hours. It looked at the dentists near the office and found one that opens at eight in the morning. It said there was a free spot on Thursday at eight fifteen. Tom said that sounded good, so the phone booked the visit, added it to his calendar, and set a reminder for the night before. Tom felt better already and went back to his emails.

The person wants to book a haircut.
Book me a haircut.
I need a trim, can I get a slot on Friday?
Is there a free spot at the barber this week?
Find a salon that isn't too far from home and book a cut for Saturday.
Please fill in a time for my haircut and tell me the shop's opening hours.
Can you check if the barber has an hour block free tomorrow afternoon?
My hair is a mess, get me in somewhere soon.
Would you be so kind as to make an appointment with my usual hairdresser and send me a reminder the day before?

Email is a way to send a message to someone far away and get an answer back when they have time. Your inbox is where new messages arrive. Most people change a few things about it. They mark mail as read or unread, move old mail into folders, and attach photos or files to a new message. When you ask an assistant for help, you can say, 'Write an email to my boss,' or 'Show me the unread mail,' or 'Attach that photo and send it.' It is smart to be careful with the name in the address box, so the right person gets it. You can also say, 'Delete the old ones' or 'Read my newest message to me.'

Omar had just moved to a new city, and most of his things were still in boxes in the closet. He found his running shoes and wanted to try the park nearby. He said to his phone, 'Find me a running route of five kilometres, and keep it flat.' The phone understood that he wanted a flat loop of about five kilometres starting from his flat, and it showed him a path around the lake. Then Omar remembered his meeting. 'No, wait, make it three kilometres. I can't skip breakfast and I'm late.' The phone changed the route to a shorter loop of three kilometres and said the maximum hill on it was very small. It also said the run would take about twenty minutes. Omar tied his laces and went out.

Feed the dog.
Give Max his dinner, please.
Time for the dog's food.
Put out a scoop of dry food for Max.
Wait, he's had a long day, so make it two scoops instead.
He's staring at his bowl, so I think he wants his dinner.
Fill the bowl, but no corn, it upsets his tummy.
Could you please start the feeder? I'm stuck in traffic and he's been alone since morning.

Luis parked his delivery truck at a rest stop and took a break. He opened his phone and said, 'Show me what my sister posted today, but do not show me any ads.' The phone understood that he wanted to read only his sister's new posts and not the ads in between. It opened her page and read out the latest one: a photo of a woman at her bakery, holding a sweet cake with lemon on top. Luis laughed. 'Like it, and tell her I'll join the family dinner on Sunday.' The phone pressed the like button and sent a short reply saying Luis would join the dinner. Then it asked if he wanted to hear the next post. 'No, that's enough,' said Luis, and he started the truck.

Dana was packing lunches when the wifi stopped being fun. The kids' tablets were still on, and she needed them put away for just one more minute. She picked up her phone and typed in a hurry: 'turn of the internet on the kids tablets for an hour'. She had spelled 'off' wrong, but the assistant understood anyway. It figured she wanted the internet paused on the two tablets for sixty minutes, and nothing else. The router light flashed once, and the tablets showed a small message that the internet was paused. The assistant told her it would come back on at nine o'clock. Dana said that was fine, and went back to cutting the sandwiches.

An appointment is a time you keep for someone, like a haircut, a dentist, or a doctor. It is for making sure the person is ready for you, so you do not wait in a long line. People often change appointments. They move them to another day, or they skip one when they are sick and cancel it. When they ask an assistant, they might say, 'Book me a haircut on Friday,' or 'Push my dentist to next week,' or 'What time does the shop open?' A loud alarm or a reminder message the day before helps people remember. A skirt that needs fixing, for example, can be taken to the tailor at a booked time.

A car needs a little care to run well. Fuel is what makes it go, and tyre pressure is how much air is in the wheels. For some people, looking after a car is a hobby, but for most it is just a chore. People often change small things: they fill up the tank, add air to the tyres, or warm up the car on a cold morning. If the car makes a strange noise, you should have it checked. When asking an assistant, people say things like 'How much fuel is left?', 'Are my tyres okay?', 'Start the car, it's freezing,' or 'Where did I park?' You can also scroll through the car screen to see the numbers yourself.

Person: Hello, I hope you can help me. I am buying an iron fence for the north side of my garden, and I need to know the price after the discount, so I can tell my wife before we go to the shop.
Assistant: Happy to help. What is the full price, and how much is the discount?
Person: The fence costs 240 dollars, and the discount is 15 percent.
Assistant: Fifteen percent of 240 is 36, so the fence will cost 204 dollars.
Person: Wonderful. And what would four of them cost?
Assistant: Four times 204 is 816 dollars.
Person: Thank you, that is very kind of you.

Maya worked in an office and had to plan lunch for her team. She said to her phone, 'Find a place for six people near work, but not the Italian place, we went there last week.' The phone understood she wanted a lunch table for six, and not at that restaurant. It read out a few options and sorted them by how close they were. The closest was a noodle shop. Maya added, 'One of us is bringing a child, so I need a high chair.' The phone asked the shop for a table at the exact time Maya wanted, twelve thirty. The shop had a table with a high chair free. The phone booked it and told Maya the address.

Ben was nine years old, and he had just fixed the wheel on his bike. He wanted to get stronger so he could ride faster. He asked the speaker in the living room, 'Can you wake me up tomorrow at seven and show me an exercise?' The speaker understood that he wanted an alarm for seven in the morning and a simple workout. It set the alarm and said, 'Tomorrow at seven, I'll tell you how to do ten jumping jacks and five push-ups.' Ben said that sounded fun. Then he asked if the park gym was open, and the speaker said it was closed until the weekend, so they could use the backyard instead. Ben smiled and went to bed.

A cup of coffee or tea is a small break in the day. The drink is made to taste the way you like, so people change how strong it is, how sweet, and how big. Some like a weak tea with no sugar, and others want a strong coffee with two spoons of sugar. When an assistant helps, you can say, 'Make it stronger,' 'Less sweet, please,' or 'Fill it up.' If your cup is empty, you can ask for another. On pizza night, many families make a big jug of lemonade, and children look forward to it all week. You can even ask for it by saying, 'Make the lemonade a little sweeter.'

Mrs. Alvarez was a retired teacher who liked to read in the evening, but the light in her living room was too bright. She said to the speaker, 'Excuse me, my eyes get tired when I read, and the ceiling light is very bright. Would you please make it softer, and a little warmer, so I can finish my book?' The assistant understood that she wanted the living room light dimmer and in a warmer colour. It lowered the brightness to about thirty percent and chose a warm yellow. She sat down with her black cat and a cup of tea, with a fork and a slice of cake on the table. The bulb gave off no heat, but the colour made the room feel warm.
