- The soup recipe is too small to read, read it to me
- Say the page slowly

Grandpa Joe was not good with technology. He stood in the laundry room holding yesterday's newspaper and a pile of dirty towels. He had tried for years to fix the old washer himself, but it was too hard. 'Start the washing machine with a double rinse and tell me when it's done,' he said to the little speaker. The speaker understood two things: he wanted the towel cycle with an extra rinse, and he wanted to be told at the end. It started the machine and said it would take fifty minutes. Joe sat down with his newspaper. When the machine finished, the speaker said, 'Your towels are done.' 'Well I never,' said Joe.

Sometimes people have to do things away from home, like go to the post office or the bank. These errands are for sending a letter, paying a bill, or picking up a parcel. People change when they go, because shops have opening hours and the line may be long. If you need to ship a package before a deadline, you must get there before closing. When asking an assistant for help, people say, 'When does the post office close?', 'Remind me to go to the bank at noon,' 'How far away is the closest branch?', or 'Move my errands to Saturday.'

A meeting at work is a time when people talk about the same thing. Before it starts, someone writes an agenda, which is a short list of what to talk about. People join by a link on a call, and then they share their screen so everyone can see the same slides. Some people take notes with a pen, while others type. A day full of meetings can be tiring, so people ask to move or shorten them. They say, 'Join my ten o'clock call,' 'Share my screen,' 'Push this meeting back an hour,' or 'Sweep my afternoon clear.'

Rosa owned a small shop. Her workers had spent all week building a new window display, and she wanted to thank them with dinner. While she listened to an audiobook in the back room, she paused it and said to her phone, 'Book a table for twenty-five on Friday at seven, somewhere with a big room.' The phone understood that she wanted a restaurant with a large space for twenty-five people. It found one with a long room that it only used for temporary parties. The restaurant said yes, and the phone booked the table and sent Rosa the address. Rosa started her audiobook again, happy that dinner was done.

Lena was a student waiting at a bus stop on a sunny afternoon. Her phone buzzed, and she saw the bus was late. She did not feel like typing, so she just said, 'Next bus?' The phone understood that she meant the next bus at her stop, and it said bus 12 would come in seven minutes. Lena wanted to pick up her pills at the pharmacy before class. She said, 'Track it,' and the phone began to follow the bus on the map. When the bus was two minutes away, it buzzed again. Lena looked up and saw the bus turn the corner.

Time management means using your day so the important things get done. A focus timer is a simple tool: you work for twenty-five minutes, then you take a short break. Routines help too, like a morning list so the day does not feel messy. People who stick to a plan often feel they win back their evenings. They change the timer or the break, and ask an assistant, 'Start a focus timer,' 'Make my breaks longer,' or 'Remind me to stretch at three.' Someone making breakfast with butter and toast can even set a ten-minute timer to get out the door on time.

does: Moves the morning alarm to a new time so you wake up well rested.
inputs: the new time, and which days it should ring
people say:
- Swap my alarm to six thirty
- I want to sleep in tomorrow
- Wake me half an hour later
- I need to be up earlier for the train
- I'm going to the plant sale early, make it five

Grandma Ruth wanted to have lunch with her friend Carol. She picked up her phone and said, 'Put lunch with Carol on Wednesday at noon.' The phone understood she wanted a new event on her calendar and added it. Then Ruth remembered that Carol's plane doesn't land until Wednesday night. 'Oh, no, I mean Thursday.' She asked the phone to compare her free times on Wednesday and Thursday, and it said she was free at noon on Thursday. The phone moved the event to Thursday at noon. Ruth added, 'Put a note on it: no raw fish for lunch, Carol doesn't like it.' The phone saved the note and gave her a thumbs up.

Close the blinds.
Shut the curtains.
Blinds down, please.
It's too bright in here, I can't see the TV.
The sun is in my eyes.
The sun is fading all my toys, shut it out.
Close the blinds I labelled bedroom, and do it straight away.
It's so bright in this room that I can't take a nap, would you mind doing something about it?

Assistant: How about twenty-one degrees?
Person: Yes, good. My dinner was cooked an hour ago and it's already cold, and the window is wet. I'll wipe it later.
Assistant: Sounds good. I have set the bedroom heating to twenty-one degrees.

Mr. Evans had a new smart speaker, but he was not good with technology. He sat in his armchair, tired after a long day at his job. He looked at the speaker and said, 'It's a bit quiet in here, I can't hear the fancy music my daughter sent me.' The speaker understood that he wanted the music louder. It raised the volume a little and asked, 'Is that better?' Mr. Evans did not know how to drag a slider on the phone, but he did not have to. He just said, 'Still too quiet,' and the speaker made it louder again. This time he smiled and closed his eyes.

Chen had just moved to a new city and did not know a single restaurant. His neighbour had told him about a place with good dumplings. He said to his phone, 'Excuse me, I would like to find a small restaurant that makes dumplings, because my mother is visiting this weekend and I want to treat her to something nice. Could you please book us a table for two on Saturday evening?' The phone understood that he wanted a dumpling restaurant and a table for two. It found a place near his flat that makes fresh dumplings daily and booked seven o'clock. Chen thanked it. He still had to mop the floors and shave before she arrived.

I'm going to chill on the couch, so just tell me when someone scores.
Did the Reds win by more than twenty-five points? Wait, I mean the Blues.

Lights help us see, read and feel comfortable at home. A lamp is easy to move, but a ceiling light lights the whole room. Smart bulbs let you change the brightness and the colour without getting up. In the evening, people like a warm, soft light, but to read or cook they want it clear and bright. A museum puts a spotlight on a painting so it is clear to see, and at home you can do the same thing with a lamp. People say, 'Make it brighter,' 'Dim the lights,' 'Turn off the lamp,' or 'Change the bulb to blue.'

Sam the cook was making dinner when the cat began to meow at his feet. The cat's seat by the window was empty, and her bowl was empty too. Sam's hands were covered in flour, so he just said, 'Feed Whiskers.' The speaker understood that he meant to give the cat her food now, and it told the automatic feeder to put out a scoop. The cat ate happily. 'Strange,' Sam thought, 'she's usually not hungry until six.' He also asked the speaker to text his wife that the cat was eating early. The speaker sent the message and Sam went back to his dough.

Food delivery brings a meal to your door. You pick the food on a phone, say where you are, and a driver brings it, sometimes across a river or through the rain. People change the address, the time, or the tip. A polite tip is a few dollars, and many people add more when the weather is bad. When asking an assistant for help, people say, 'Order me a burger,' 'Make the tip three dollars,' 'Send it to my office instead,' or 'How long until it comes?' The assistant can also tell you when the driver is close.

Person: Can you heat the pool for the kids?
Assistant: Sure. What temperature would you like?
Person: Thirty degrees. Wait, that's too hot. Make it twenty-eight.
Assistant: Twenty-eight degrees, got it. When should it be ready?
Person: By four o'clock. It might rain this afternoon, though.
Assistant: Should I close the cover if it starts to rain?
Person: Yes, please. And keep the water clear. Did you add the salt?
Assistant: I can't check the salt, I'm sorry. I can only set the heat and the cover.

Mr. Park owned a small shop and was about to leave for the evening. He wanted to make it safer. He said to his phone, 'Show me the back door camera, and I have an idea: make the motion alarm more sensitive tonight, double what it is now.' The phone understood that he wanted to see the camera on the display and raise the alarm setting to twice the level. It showed the back door, where nothing was moving, and doubled the motion setting. Then it said the alarm would arm itself soon after he locked the front door, in about ten minutes. Mr. Park nodded, picked up his coat and turned off the lights.

- It's half time, who is ahead?
- Count up our points
- Give Mia five more
- Who's winning the game?
- Start us all from zero again

A front door keeps your home safe, and a lock decides who can come in. Some locks use keys, and some use a code or a phone. A garage door opens to let in the car. People change a lot of things: they lock up at night, let a friend in, or check who is at the door. When asking an assistant, they say things like 'Lock the front door,' 'Did I shut the garage?', 'Who's out there?', or 'Open up for my sister.' A lamp by the door and a yellow light on the porch help people see who is there, and a locked door helps you win a good night's sleep.

A recipe tells you how much of each thing to use. It is written for a set number of servings, like four people. When more or fewer people will eat, you scale it up or down. If a man is cooking for eight, he doubles everything. Cups and spoons are the usual tools, and a loose measure like a pinch is fine for salt, but measure flour carefully. People say, 'Make this for two,' 'Double the recipe,' or 'How many tablespoons are in a cup?' You can also ask the assistant to draw up a shopping list for the dish.

Arithmetic is the plain maths we use every day: adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing. We use it when we pay a bill, split a cost, or double a recipe. People use words like 'plus', 'minus', 'times' and 'divided by'. They also say, 'What is 20 plus 10?', 'Take 5 from 30,' 'Share 12 among 3 people,' or 'How much are 4 of these at 6 dollars each?' A computer does it fast, but it is smart to be careful with the numbers you give it. You can let a hot drink cool while you work out the tip.

Person: I need a room for next weekend.
Assistant: Happy to help. Which city?
Person: Lisbon. I don't want a hostel, I want a real hotel.
Assistant: Got it. How many nights, and how many guests?
Person: Two nights, just me. I read the news that it will freeze at night, so I want heating.
Assistant: Which dates?
Person: Friday and Saturday.
Assistant: Okay. I'll look for hotels in Lisbon with heating and recent good reviews, for one guest, Friday and Saturday.

Person: Please send the invitations for our office party.
Assistant: Happy to. Which day is the party?
Person: Next Friday at six. We will set up tomorrow at seven.
Assistant: Got it. Who should get the invitation?
Person: Everyone on the team list. Add a note that we will roast chicken and vegetables, so it will be delicious.
Assistant: Done. I sent the invitation to the team list for Friday at six, with your note about the roast.
Person: Can you also find my lost ring? I think I dropped it at the last party.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't find lost things. You could ask the place where the party was if they have it.

Sam is a student who shares a flat, and the power bill had been too high. He picked up his phone and said, "Show me how much electricity we used this week, but I don't want the whole year, just the last seven days." The assistant understood that he wanted a short report, not a long one. It opened the energy app and showed a small chart. Sam saw that the heater used the most power. He said, "Turn the heater down to eighteen, and don't touch the lights." The assistant lowered the heater and left the lights as they were. Sam gave a little wave to his flatmate on the sofa and said the room would be cooler now. Then he asked the phone to remind him on Sunday to move some money from his bank account to pay the bill. The assistant set a reminder for Sunday evening and said it was done.

- How long until the next bus at Park Street?
- Tell me if the bus is running late.
- I'm sitting by the socket in the station cafe. How long until the 8 bus is outside?

Someone wants to book a haircut.
Haircut, please.
Book me a trim.
I need my hair cut this week.
Can you count me in for a haircut on Saturday morning?
Is there a slot open for a medium trim, about half an hour?
Find me a barber with more free times than the last one.

Lena was running late and her bus left in five minutes. She grabbed her bag and called out to the smart speaker, "Turn off the kitchen lights and dim the hall lamp to the least bright setting, please." The speaker understood both things. It switched off the kitchen lights and set the hall lamp to ten percent. Lena wanted her dog to feel calm while she was out, so she added, "And play soft music in the living room." The assistant started a quiet playlist. Just then the old bulb in the bedroom gave a small crack and went dark. Lena sighed. "Remind me to buy a new bulb tonight," she said. The assistant set the reminder for seven in the evening and told her it was saved. Lena ran out the door and caught her bus with a minute to spare.

A trip to the post office is a common errand. People go there to send parcels, buy stamps, or pick up something that was left when they were out. If you carry a suitcase or a big box, you may need a bigger label. Before you leave, you can ask your assistant to find the nearest post office, or to check when it opens. People say things like "Where can I post this?" or "Is the post office open now?" If the address on a parcel is wrong, you can ask the shop to fix it before it goes. You might also say "Move my pickup to Friday" when you can't be home. Small changes like the day, the time or the place are easy to ask for, as long as you say them plainly.

name: delivery_tracker
does: Shows where an order is and when it will arrive, even if the delivery has stretched past the first date.
inputs: the order number or the name of the shop
people say:
- Where is my order?
- When will the bike arrive?
- Has my parcel left the shop yet?
- Can you see if my favourite jacket has been sent?
- How long until my delivery gets here?

Babies like a steady day. Feeding times and nap times help them feel safe, and they help parents plan. A baby may eat every three hours, and a nap may last from thirty minutes to two hours. The length of a nap changes as the baby grows. Parents often change the plan with a few simple words: "Move the next feed to six," "Make the nap shorter," or "Tell me when the baby wakes up." A baby monitor helps too. On a foggy morning, when the baby sleeps late, a parent might say, "Don't wake her yet." While the parent fries eggs in the kitchen, the monitor sends a quiet sound to the phone. People ask for small changes in plain words, like earlier, later, longer or shorter.

Someone wants to move a meeting to a later time.
Push my meeting back an hour.
Move the two o'clock to three.
Can we do it later today?
Make my meeting later.
Shift the team call to tomorrow, please.
I'd like to move my meeting with the guest speaker to Thursday.
Please change my Monday meeting to the afternoon, because I will lose the morning to a rare doctor visit that I could not book on any other day.
Could you kindly move the meeting to next week? A rare chance to see my grandmother came up, and I do not want to lose it.

Restarting a computer is one of the easiest fixes. When a screen freezes or a program is slow, you turn the computer off and start it again. This clears small problems and makes the computer quick again. Before you restart, save your files in a folder so you don't lose them. Ben's wife was happy when her old laptop worked again after a restart. People ask in many ways: "Restart my computer," "Turn it off and on," or "Start it fresh in five minutes." They also change the screen: "Make the screen brighter," "Dim it," or "Turn on battery saver." The words are simple, and the computer does what it was told.

name: gift_idea_finder
does: Suggests a few gifts for a person, based on what they like and how much you want to spend.
inputs: who the gift is for, what they enjoy, and a price limit
people say:
- What should I get my dad for his birthday?
- I need a present for my niece. She loves riding her bicycle, and I can spend about twenty dollars.
- Any ideas for a coworker? Something polite and not too personal.
- My friend is turning thirty and I have no idea what to give.
- Something small for my aunt, but no flowers, because she sneezes all the time.

Priya, an office worker, sat down at home after a long day and found the internet very slow. It was a foggy evening and the router light blinked orange. She said to her phone, "Why is the wifi so slow? Explain it to me." The assistant checked and said that six devices were using the connection, which was twice as many as usual. Priya said, "Pause the tablet and the game console." The assistant paused both, and the speed went up to nearly double. Her video call with her brother worked fine after that. On the screen she could see his picture, a yellow duck, and she laughed. Then she asked the assistant to keep the tablet paused until nine. It said that it would.

Dan was a busy parent with sticky honey on his fingers, and he was late for the school pickup. He picked up the phone with his elbow and typed, "call jenny on speakerphoen". The assistant saw the small typo and understood that he meant speakerphone. It called Jenny, who was Dan's sister, and turned on the speaker. Dan said, "Can you get Max today? I'm running late." Jenny said yes, and said they could split the week, with her taking Monday and Tuesday. After the call, Dan said, "Save a note to call Jenny back about the week." The assistant saved the note and told him it was done. Dan washed his hands and ran out to the car.

Someone wants an alarm to wake them up.
Wake me at seven.
Set an alarm for six thirty tomorrow.
I'm taking a nap, so buzz me in twenty-five minutes.
I need to get up early. My room is messy and I have to tidy it before work.
Can you set a soft alarm, one that filters in slowly instead of a loud ring?
Please make sure I am awake by eight, because I need to buy one last ingredient for the cake before the shop closes.
Alarm, seven, weekdays.

Someone wants to call back a number that just called them.
Call them back.
Ring Tom, he just called me.
Who called me? Please call them back.
I missed a call from my brother, could you call him back for me?
I'm saving data this month, so call that number back over wifi.
Call the library on their public number and remember to leave a message if nobody answers.
Call the last number that rang, and tell me who it was.
Would you mind calling the number that missed me earlier? If nobody picks up, please leave a voicemail.

Rosa was a busy parent, and her phone kept saying that the storage was full. She had only a few minutes before school. She said, "Phone, my storage is full. Upload my photos to the cloud, but only the ones from last year." The assistant said the phone was not connected to wifi, so it connected to the home network first. Then it began to upload. "How much room will that give me?" Rosa asked. The assistant said about twenty-five gigabytes. Rosa nodded and said, "Also turn on do not disturb until noon, I have a meeting." The assistant did it. Rosa packed the lunch boxes while the photos went up. When she left the house, the screen showed that the upload was finished.

Omar was a driver who had just finished a long shift. Sitting in his truck, he typed fast: "set the round hot tub to 38 degress and start the pump". The assistant read the small typo as degrees and sent both orders to the controller at home. The tub began to heat, and the pump turned on. A moment later the assistant said the water was at 31 and would reach 38 in about forty minutes. Omar said, "Call my sister." She was a nurse and had the same long hours. When she answered, he said, "Come over after your shift, the tub will be warm soon." She said she would be there at nine.

At home, the router sends wifi to your phones and computers. Each device joins with a password. The router often hangs on a hook on the wall, and a pink sticker on it may show the wifi name and password. Some routers let you filter which devices can go online, or block certain websites for children. People ask for changes in plain words: "Change the wifi password," "Block the tablet at night," or "Restart the router." If the connection is slow, people say, "The internet is slow today," and the assistant can restart the router or tell them which device is using the most.

Wifi sometimes does not reach outside the house. If the signal is weak in the garden, people say, "The internet is bad out here." Do not put the router next to the kitchen sink or behind a thick wall, because the signal gets weaker there. When friends visit, you welcome them and give them the wifi name and password. Many routers have a guest network, which is separate from your own, so visitors can go online without seeing your files. People ask for it in simple words: "Turn on the guest wifi," "Give me a new guest password," or "Turn the guest wifi off tonight."

After a family roast dinner, Mara found a big stain on her husband's orange shirt, where he had spilled beer. She was holding the baby, so she said to the kitchen speaker, "Start the washing machine on the stain cycle, and use half the usual soap. It's only one shirt." The assistant understood that she wanted the stain cycle with less soap. It started the machine and said the cycle would take fifty minutes. "Make it warmer than usual," Mara added. The assistant raised the temperature from thirty to forty degrees. Later, Mara asked it to tell her when the wash was done. The assistant sent a message to her phone right on time, and she hung the shirt up to dry.

Joe the gardener was done for the day. His hoodie was wet and he wanted to go home, but he did not remember where he had parked the car. He shouted across the garden to his phone, "Where is my car, and is it ready to go with enough fuel?" The assistant opened the car app. It said the car was on Elm Street, two minutes away on foot, and that the tank was half full. Joe said, "Start the engine and warm it up." The assistant sent the command. When Joe walked to the car, the heater was already on and the windows were clear. He took off his wet hoodie and put it on the back seat.

name: account_balance_check
does: Gives a smart, short answer about how much money is in one of your accounts, so you can double-check before you spend.
inputs: which account you mean
people say:
- How much money do I have?
- What's in my savings?
- Is my account low? I need to pay the rent.
- Does my card have enough before I buy this?
- I'm at the cash machine in my neighborhood. What is left in my account?

A washing machine cleans clothes with water, soap and spinning. People pick a cycle, like cotton, delicate or quick. A dryer then warms the clothes until they are dry. On a cloudy day, drying outside is slow, so many people use the dryer. A small light on the machine may blink when the wash is done or when something is wrong. After drying, folded clothes can go into a vacuum bag for winter storage. People ask for changes in simple words: "Start a quick wash," "Make it warmer," "Add ten more minutes to the dryer," or "Tell me when it's done."

Person: print 20 copies of the movie night poster plese

Assistant: I can print twenty copies in colour. The thick paper tray is empty, though. Can you fill it, or should I use normal paper?

Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send faxes. I can email him a scan if you give me his address.
Person: no worries. the weather is mild this week so i think we will get a crowd
Assistant: That sounds nice. The prints are ready.

name: break_timer
does: Starts a timer for your work and tells you when to take a short rest, so you can enjoy a tasty snack or stretch your legs.

people say:
- Remind me to take a break in an hour.
- Work for twenty-five minutes, then tell me to stop.
- I want a focus timer.
- Give me a rest every half hour so I can drink a glass of water.
- Tell me when to stand up. I want to finish this before I plant the beans.

A navigation app shows you the way from one place to another. It uses maps and live traffic to tell you how long a drive will take. Your phone may upload its position every few seconds, so the app can warn you about a jam ahead. People change the plan in simple words: "Take the fastest route," "Avoid the highway," "Add a stop for fuel," or "How long until I get there?" If you want to celebrate a friend's birthday and must arrive on time, you might ask, "Will I get there by six?" or "Do I have enough time to stop for a gift?"

name: drive_time_estimate
does: Uses the internet to find how long a drive will take with today's traffic, so you can leave on time and enjoy the trip.
inputs: the place you start and the place you want to go, and a constant internet connection for live traffic
people say:
- How long to get to work?
- Is there a lot of traffic on the way to grandma's?
- What time should I leave to reach the lake by noon?
- How far is the beach?
- Will the drive take longer than usual this morning?

Nina had just woken up on Sunday morning. Her eyes were still closed when she said to the phone by her bed, "Find me a bike route of about twenty-five kilometres, and not too hilly." The assistant understood that she wanted a flat ride of that length. It showed a route along the river and said it would take about ninety minutes at a normal speed. "Switch to the quiet roads," said Nina, "I don't like cars." The assistant changed the route to a path with fewer cars. Nina said, "A dozen of us are meeting at the bridge at nine. Remind me at eight." The assistant saved the route and set the reminder for eight.

Someone wants the car warmed up before they leave.
Warm up the car.
Start the engine, I'm leaving in ten minutes.
Get the car warm, it's freezing.
Please turn on the heater in my car, because my mom is coming with me and she gets cold easily.
Increase the heat a bit, the morning air is sharp.
Start the car in five minutes. No, make that ten.
Start the engine at seven. Actually, make it seven thirty.
Could you please warm up the car for me before I come out?

Someone wants the front door locked for the night.
Lock up.
Good night, lock the front door, please.
Lock the front door and turn off the porch light.
It's bedtime, so please lock the doors.
Is the door locked? If not, lock it.
I'm heading to bed, so lock the front door and check the garage too.
Can you make sure everything is locked before I join the kids upstairs?

Someone wants the lights to come on at a certain time.
Lights on at seven.
Turn the kitchen lamp on tomorrow at seven.
Switch on the porch light when it gets dark.
I will be home at six, so have the hall light on by then.
I am not well tonight, so please keep the bedroom light on until nine.
Please note that I'm planting seeds early tomorrow, so turn on the garden light at five thirty.
Make the bedroom lights come on slowly in the morning.

Ali had moved to the city in February and still did not know where anything was. On Friday evening he dusted off his good coat and asked his phone, "What movies are on tonight near me? Nothing longer than two hours." The assistant looked up the nearby cinemas. It found three films, and the shortest one ran for ninety minutes. It read out the times, and said the cinema was ten minutes away by bus. Ali chose the one with the pale blue poster, a comedy, and said, "Show me the trailer first." The assistant played the trailer. Ali laughed and said, "Okay, the half past eight one." The assistant showed him the way and said the bus left in five minutes.

Twenty plus ten?

Add twenty and ten for me.
How much is ten more than twenty?
Quick, I'm in bed and can't do sums. What do twenty and ten make?
Zoom through this for me: twenty plus ten.
I'm in a silent library, so show it on the screen: twenty plus ten.

Carlos was a gardener with dirty hands and a tight schedule. He knelt by the roses and said to his phone, "Could you please play the next chapter of my audiobook and make it a little faster? My hands are covered in soil, so I can't unlock the screen myself, and I want to finish this chapter before I have to pay the water bill at noon." The assistant heard his voice, unlocked the phone, found the book where he had stopped, and started chapter nine at one and a quarter speed. Carlos kept digging while the story played. At eleven thirty he said, "Pause it now, please." The assistant paused it and saved his place.

Watering is the main job in a garden. Plants need water, sun and time. A sprinkler connects to a hose and sprays water over the grass. Many people set a timer so it waters early in the morning, when the sun is low. Too much water is bad for most plants, and too little is bad too. People change things in simple words: "Water the tomatoes less," "Run the sprinkler for ten minutes," "Skip today, it's raining," or "Move watering to six." If you have an appointment in the morning, you might say, "Water after I leave."

Person: Remind me about my history homework.
Assistant: Sure. When should I remind you?
Person: Not tonight. I don't want to think about it until tomorrow.
Assistant: Okay. What time tomorrow?
Person: After school, around four. Can you also explain the homework to me? I'm sitting on the rug and I don't get it.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't see your homework, so I can't explain it. If you read me the question, I can try to help. I set the reminder for four tomorrow.
Person: Can you make that reminder permanent, every day?
Assistant: Yes, I will repeat it every school day.

name: lost_pet_notice

inputs: the pet's name, a photo, and where it was last seen
people say:

- Our dog ran out of the gate, can you let everyone know?
- Post a notice, Max is missing.
- We just came back from a trip and the rabbit is not in its cage. Ask the street to look.
- Tell everyone nearby to watch for a small grey cat.

Maya woke up with a cough and a heavy head. She did not remember what day it was, so she said to her speaker, "Is it bin day today? I don't want the garden waste, only the recycling." The assistant checked the calendar for her street and said the recycling truck would come at eight, and the garden waste was next week. Maya asked, "What goes in the blue bin again?" The assistant said paper, cans and clean plastic. Maya said, "Print the bin days for the month so I can put them on the fridge." The assistant sent the page to the printer. Maya dragged the bin to the road, happy that she had made it in time.

A calendar helps you remember what happens and when. You put events on it: meetings, birthdays, trips. Some events repeat every week, like a class on Sunday. A calendar can be private or public, and a public one can be seen by many people, like a school's calendar. People change events often: "Move my meeting to Tuesday," "What am I doing on Friday?" "Cancel lunch," or "Make the dentist an hour earlier." You can also write small tasks, like "buy milk," with a reminder. When two events happen at the same time, the calendar shows a warning.

Phones make it easy to record video. You press a button, film for a while, and stop. Many people film small things: a child at a birthday party, ice cream starting to melt in the sun, or a cooking clip of an apple pie. You can watch the clip, cut off the start, share it with a friend, or save it. People change settings too: "Record in wide mode," "Make the clip shorter," "Turn the sound off," or "Send it to Mum." Long videos use more storage, so people often ask, "How much space is left?"

A smoke alarm listens for smoke and makes a loud sound to wake people up. Some alarms are connected to the house wire, and others use a small battery that needs changing once a year. If the power goes out, people look for a torch and keep the fridge shut, because raw food and milk can go bad after a few hours. In an emergency, people say, "Call for help," "Call the fire service," or "Turn on the torch." They can also adjust things, like "Make the alarm quieter after the test" or "Remind me to change the battery in spring."

Someone wants to play the next episode of a podcast.

Carry on with my podcast.
Keep going from where I stopped.
Play the episode about the north of England, the one about the summer heat.
I plan to listen on the train tomorrow at seven, so get the next episode ready.
Please could you start the following episode of my podcast? I have a long drive tomorrow at seven and I want it ready.

- Time in New York right now?

Ruth was a retired teacher who sat by the window playing her guitar. Her old dog, Bruno, sat by his empty bowl and looked at her. Ruth put the guitar down and said to the smart speaker, "Ask the feeder to give Bruno his dinner straight away, but no treats tonight. The vet said he's had too many." The assistant understood that she wanted one normal meal and no treats. It told the feeder to fill the bowl, and it said the portion was one cup. "Good," said Ruth. "And don't let me forget his walk. Remind me at six." The assistant set a reminder for six. Bruno ate his dinner, and Ruth picked up her guitar again.

name: door_lock_timer
does: Locks a door at the time you choose, which reduces the chance of leaving it open.

people say:

- I'm silly and always forget, so lock up for me.
- Make sure the back door is locked when I go out on Saturday morning.
- Lock up for the night at eleven.
- Don't let the door stay open after I leave.

Finding a film to watch is easy. People look at what is on television or on the cinema list. They ask things like "What's on tonight?" "Show me comedies," or "When is the film at the cinema?" A trailer is a short video that shows a little of the film. If you want to watch later, you can download a film to your phone before a trip. Be patient, because a big film may take a while on slow wifi. People change their plans in simple words: "Play it from the start," "Show something shorter," or "Find a film for kids."

Yuki was new to the city and wanted to know what was going on. While the kitchen tap dripped, she said to her phone, "Tell me the local news, but I don't want sports or the weather. Keep it short." The assistant understood that she wanted only town news, in a short summary. It read three headlines: a new bus line, a street market on Saturday, and a road that would be closed. Yuki said, "I didn't hear the last one, say it again." The assistant repeated it. She said, "Tell me the news every morning at seven." The assistant set a daily short news update for seven. Yuki smiled and went to fix the tap.

Person: Hello, could you please book someone to fix my dishwasher? It leaks every time I run it, and I have guests coming on Saturday, so I would really like it working by then.
Assistant: Of course. Which day and what time of day can someone come to the house?
Person: I have to talk to my boss on Friday morning, so the afternoon is better. My toddler also dropped a banana into the filter, and I think that is what broke it.
Assistant: Thank you, that helps. I can book a repair person for Friday at two. Is that all right?
Person: Yes, please. Can they also look at the washing machine?
Assistant: I can ask for that. It will make a double visit of about two hours. Should I go ahead?
Person: Yes, go ahead.

Dana was a busy parent with a crying baby and a long list of things to do. She called out to the kitchen speaker, "Could you please play the local news station on the radio? My husband is outside trying to mow the lawn, and I want to know if this windy weather is going to turn into rain, because the washing is still on the line. I would be so grateful." The speaker understood that she wanted the news radio and a weather report. It tuned in to the local news station and turned the volume up a little. After a minute it read out the forecast: windy all afternoon, with rain after six. Dana wrote a note to take the kids to the cinema on Sunday instead, and then she thanked the speaker.

Leo was nine, and his birthday party was on Saturday. He held his mom's tablet with a steady hand and said, "Make a guest list for my party, but I don't want Max on it." The assistant made a list of six friends and left Max out. Leo looked at it for a while and changed his mind. "Undo that," he said. "Max can come. I just don't want him near my cake." The assistant put Max back on the list and wrote a small note: keep Max away from the cake. Then Leo asked it to remind him at four to hang the paper stars on the wall. The assistant set the reminder for four o'clock and told him the guest list now had seven names.

Priya had just moved to the city, and she had no idea where to ride her bike. On her first morning, after a quick shower and a cup of coffee, she opened the map app on her phone and typed two words: bike routes. The assistant understood that she wanted cycling paths near her new home. It showed her three routes. One was a gentle ride along the river, five kilometers long, with no big hills. Another went through the park, and a third went past the market. Priya picked the river one. The assistant started the directions and told her that the first turn was left at the corner by the bakery. She smiled, put on her helmet and rolled out into the morning.

People measure things every day: how long a table is, how heavy a bag is, how hot the oven should be. Different places use different units, so people often ask to change one kind of unit into another. A baker may need grams instead of cups. A traveler may want miles instead of kilometers. Someone with a new camera may ask how many inches wide a photo will print. To get a perfect result, people say things like, how many ounces is this, or, give me that in centimeters, or, what is seventy degrees in Celsius. Even a small switch matters when you celebrate with a cake that has to rise just right. The words are simple: how much is it in, or, change it to.

A washing machine cleans clothes with water, soap and spinning. Most families use it daily or every few days, so they care about small settings. They change the temperature, the spin speed and how long the wash takes. Some people say, make it colder, so the colors do not fade. Others say, wash it longer, or, run a quick wash, or, spin it less. A dryer works in a similar way, and people ask for less heat or more time when the clothes are still damp. If a family cannot afford a new machine, they may carry their clothes to a shop with big machines. When a parcel arrives with a new shirt, many people wash it once before wearing it. They say, start the wash, or, delay it until tonight.

Nina was eight, and her cat Pepper had been missing since the morning. She spoke to her mom's phone: "Can you tell the neighbors my cat is lost? She is orange and has half a tail." The assistant understood that Nina wanted a lost pet message sent to the neighborhood group. It wrote a short post with Pepper's color, the half tail and Nina's street, and it asked Nina if the words were right. Nina said yes, and the post went out. Soon a neighbor wrote back that she had seen a cat near the old factory, eating stale bread. Nina's hopes began to rise. She asked the assistant to make the post twice as big so more people would see it. The assistant made the text larger and posted it again.

Hector was kneeling in the garden with dirt on his hands when he remembered the tomatoes. He grabbed his phone and typed fast, in lowercase: remind me to water the tomatos at six. The assistant understood the small typo and knew he meant tomatoes. It set a reminder for six that evening and told him so. Hector then asked it to remind him to bring the iron stakes in from the shed, and to double the first reminder so he got one at half past five and one at six. The weather was fine, and he wanted the plants to be ready. The assistant set both reminders and read them back to him, and Hector went back to his digging.

say hello in Spanish

A smoke alarm is a small box on the ceiling. It is there to wake people up if there is smoke in the house. When it senses smoke, it starts to buzz very loudly. Most people test it once a month by pressing a button, and they change the battery once a year. If the alarm buzzes by mistake, for example when the toast burns, people open a window and press the hush button. In a power cut, people look for a flashlight, and in a freezing winter they find extra blankets. A child might hold a toy duck to feel safe. People say, test the alarm, or, remind me to change the battery, or, call for help.

Sam ran out of the bathroom with his shoes in his hand. The floor was wet, and the water bill had been strange lately. He typed to the assistant: is there a leek in my house. The assistant understood that he meant a leak, and it checked the water meter. It said that the water use overnight was much higher than normal, which usually means a leak, and that his account balance was fine. It also noticed that the purple light on the water filter was on, so it reminded him to change the filter this week. Then it offered to book a plumber. Sam said yes, grabbed his bag and ran for the bus.

Zoe was lying on the couch with her knee up, texting the smart speaker from her phone. She wrote: turn the volume down and play my swim playlist. The speaker understood two things in one sentence. First it lowered the volume a little, and then it started the playlist she uses before swim practice. The first song was a happy one. Zoe's brother walked in making a sour face and said it was still too loud, so she wrote: quieter please. The speaker lowered the volume again and told her it was now at three. Her brother nodded and sat down beside her.

package status

I ordered a jar of creamy peanut butter in July and it still has not come, can you check?

could you please look up my parcel, because I need the big pot to serve dinner on Friday and I am waiting at home

Mr. Alvarez opened his flower shop early and saw dark clouds over the street. He had a big delivery to make, a long distance across town, and the bikes were already loaded. He swiped his phone open and said two words: weather now. The assistant understood that he wanted the current weather, and it gave a plain answer: cloudy, twelve degrees, and rain starting in about twenty minutes. Because it was urgent, Mr. Alvarez told his driver to leave right away. The assistant also said it would be dry again by noon, so he asked it to remind him at twelve to open the front door of the shop and put the buckets outside.

Rosa came home after a night shift, tired, with her eyes half shut. A brown envelope from the electric company was lying on the floor. She pushed it aside, sat down and said to the speaker, "How much is my electric bill, and is it more than last month?" The assistant understood both parts. It said the bill was sixty dollars, which was ten dollars more than last month, and that it was due on Wednesday. Rosa asked it to remind her on Tuesday evening so she would not forget while she slept. The assistant set the reminder, and Rosa went to bed.

A note is a quick way to keep an idea from slipping away. People write notes on paper, on a phone, or by speaking into a voice note. Maybe you are sitting on the balcony on a sunny day and you think of something to buy. You say, make a note, and your words are saved. Later you can search for the note by one word. People also change their notes. They say, put milk on my list, or, delete the last line, or, read me my notes from Monday. Some people post a copy of a note in a family chat so everyone can see it, and they say, share this note with Dad.

Person: Okay. Remind me Wednesday night to put the bin out.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you on Wednesday at eight. Stay calm, you have plenty of time.

Walter was not good with technology, but his granddaughter had set up the phone for him. The grass in the yard was getting long, and the blades of the robot mower were freshly sharp. Walter sat on the balcony with his tea and typed slowly, in lowercase: start the mowr at ten. The assistant understood that he meant the mower, and that he wanted the robot mower to start at ten. It set the schedule and wrote back a short message to say so. Walter sent a thumbs up, and the assistant answered, you are welcome, the mower will start at ten. Walter felt a little less afraid of his phone.

Kim woke up with a dry mouth and an orange from last night still on the table. She mumbled to her phone, "How many days until my sister's wedding?" The assistant said it did not know the date yet. "Oh," said Kim, "it's on the tenth of June." The assistant worked it out and said there were forty-two days to go. Then Kim rubbed her eyes. "No wait, I mean the ninth." The assistant fixed its answer: forty-one days. Kim asked for a rough estimate in weeks, and the assistant said about six weeks. Kim yawned, said thank you and finally ate her orange.

A bike ride is a simple way to get around or to stay fit. A rider usually cares about three things: how far the route is, how fast they go, and how long it takes. On a bright morning, my sister likes a long, flat route by the water. When she is in a rush, she picks a shorter way. People change a route when a road is closed, and they change their goals too. They say, find a shorter way, or, avoid the hills, or, how far have I gone, or, how fast was my last ride. A cycling app listens and shows the new path.

- Am I too late to take this lamp back?

how long for chicken
chicken cooking time
what temperature for roast chicken
how many minutes does a chicken need in the oven
how long before I turn the chicken over

A phone camera takes pictures and keeps them in an album. People take photos of food, family, and even a single apple on a table. Over a year the pictures fill up the phone, so many people pay a yearly fee for extra storage. It costs only a little, but some people choose to delete old photos instead. People change things about photos: they crop them, make them brighter, or share them with a friend. They say, share this picture with Mom, or, put these in a new album, or, delete the blurry ones. A screenshot is a photo of what is on the screen.

- My brother will laugh if we have no milk again, so please check

Mrs. Chen was not good with technology, and moving boxes were everywhere. She stood in the upstairs hall and said to her tablet, "The new house is cold and dark, and the movers come at noon." The assistant understood that she needed power turned on at the new address. It found the electric company's number and offered to send a message asking them to start service. Mrs. Chen said yes. Then she remembered that the movers had cracked a bowl last time, and she asked about a refund. The assistant wrote a short note to the moving company asking for the money back, and it read the note aloud to her before sending it.

Grandpa Joe sat in his armchair with a nearby speaker beside him. He wanted to buy a new bluetooth speaker like the one his grandson has, and he had a little money in mind. He asked the assistant, "What is half of ninety dollars?" The assistant understood it as a simple division and said, "Forty-five dollars." Grandpa said the speaker costs double that. The assistant said that meant it costs ninety dollars. Joe asked, "And if I buy two, how much then?" The assistant said one hundred eighty dollars. Grandpa Joe laughed and said he would buy only one.

A hobby is something you do for fun in your free time, like painting, knitting, drawing or building models. People work on a hobby at home, or they take it to the park on a nice day. Hobbies need supplies, so people often estimate how much yarn or paint they will need before they start. If a project is not working, they change the colors, the size or the pattern. They say, make it bigger, or, use less blue, or, start over with thinner thread. Some people also ask for help, like, show me how to draw a hand, or, how long does this model take to build.

Parking means leaving a car in a place for a while. In many cities you pay for the time. You park, type your number plate into the machine, and pay for an hour or two. A child in the back seat may get bored while you do this, and a person in jeans and a coat may stand in the rain at the machine. Many people use a phone instead and ask for small changes. They say, find a spot close to the shop, or, how much time is left, or, give me another hour, or, remind me ten minutes before my parking ends.

The news tells people what is happening nearby and far away. Many people read the headlines in the morning, and others listen while they are tired and making coffee. They choose topics like sports, weather or local news, maybe a story about the lake in their town. People change what they get. They say, show me sports only, or, give me shorter headlines, or, read the local news, or, email me the news every morning. When a story is very long, they say, just tell me the main point. A good news summary uses plain words and says what happened, where and when.

Mr. Okoye ran an old hardware shop, and he had been fixing a sink all morning. When his hands were finally dry, he touched the screen of his phone and said, "When does my brother's flight land? Not the one from Tuesday, the one today." The assistant understood that he wanted today's flight, not Tuesday's. Mr. Okoye read out the flight number, four two seven. The assistant looked it up and told him that the plane was on time and would land at 3:40 in the afternoon at gate twelve. Mr. Okoye did not want to close the shop early, so he asked it to remind him at three to leave.

Marta finished her night shift at seven and walked home slowly. She drank a glass of water and said to the bedroom speaker, "Wake me tomorrow at three in the afternoon, and keep the lights low until then." The assistant understood that she wanted an alarm at three the next afternoon and dim lights. It set the alarm and turned on the automatic dimming. Her neighbor had asked to borrow a ladder, so Marta also asked it to remind her at four to lend it. The assistant set that reminder as well and wished her a good sleep.

Eli was texting the assistant while he waited at the bus stop. His mother's glasses were ready at the shop, and he had to pick them up and then go to the post office. He typed: how late is the post office open today. The assistant answered that it closed at five thirty. Eli guessed he could make it to both places. He wrote: remind me to get the glasses first and then go to the post office in twenty-five minutes. The assistant set the reminder for twenty-five minutes later and repeated the plan: glasses first, then the post office.

A flight leaves at a set time from a gate, and the airport screens show if it is on time, late or changed. Travelers check them often because plans shift. Before you go, you may think about the size of your bag, because small bags can go in the cabin. You lock your suitcase, find your gate, and look at the board again when the weather is wet and stormy, because delays are common then. People ask, when does my flight leave, or, which gate is it, or, is it late, or, tell me if the gate changes.

Tom was fifteen and waiting for a red jacket and a music magazine he had ordered. The doorbell rang, but nobody was there. He grabbed his phone and typed two words to the assistant: track package. The assistant understood and found his order. It said the jacket was out for delivery and would reach his street by the afternoon, and the magazine was coming a day later. When the courier finally arrived, Tom greeted him at the door and carried the box inside.

Ana, an office worker, suddenly remembered that her friend's birthday was tomorrow. She whispered to her phone, "What gift can I buy for under twenty-five dollars?" She was so angry at herself for forgetting that she felt her face go hot, as if smoke would come out of her ears. The assistant understood that she needed an idea for a cheap gift. It suggested a small plant, a box of tea or a funny mug, and said all three could be bought nearby. Ana chose the tea and asked it to remind her to buy a card at lunch. The assistant set the reminder for noon.

Greta had been in the garden since dawn. She stood up to stretch her back and smell the roses. Then she remembered her front door camera. "Check the camera," she said to her phone. "Did anyone come to the gate?" The assistant understood and showed the last recordings. It said the camera saw a fox three times, a frequent visitor at night, and nobody else. Greta asked it to turn on the motion alarm for the next twenty-five minutes while she worked in the back. The assistant switched the alarm on and said it would tell her if anything moved.

Mr. Bell had a full day of planting and a trip to make to the bank. He sat on a bucket, wiped his hands and said, "Could you please tell me when the bank closes today? I want to finish the roses first, and I would hate to arrive after the doors click shut." The assistant understood that he wanted the closing time and a plan. It said the bank closed at four. It also looked up the price of the stamps he needed at the post office next door and told him it was one dollar. Mr. Bell said thank you and asked for a reminder at three.

When you book a ride, you tell the app where you are and where you want to go. A driver accepts, and the app shows a pickup point and a time. The cost is shown before you go, and a new driver may warn you if a road is closed. People change things about a ride: the pickup point, the time or the destination. They say, pick me up at the main gate, or, make it ten minutes later, or, take me to the station instead, or, how long until the car arrives.

It was a snowy Tuesday and Rita was packing lunches when she remembered the dentist. "Hey, can you move Leo's dentist visit?" she asked the kitchen speaker. "I don't want Friday, and not the morning either. There is too much snow on the roads and I can't drive in it." The assistant looked at the calendar. Leo's visit was on Friday at nine. It asked if next Monday afternoon was fine. Rita said yes, as long as it was after school. The assistant moved the visit to Monday at four, told her the dentist's office had the new time, and set a reminder for the morning of the visit. Rita zipped the lunch bag, said thanks, and called the kids to the door.

Walter stood in the hall and looked at the little screen on the wall. It had many numbers and he did not know which button to press. So he picked up his phone and said, "Make the house a bit warmer. Maybe two degrees more." The assistant checked the heating. It was set to nineteen degrees. It raised it to twenty-one and said the living room would be warm in about twenty minutes. Walter tried to zoom in on the screen to read the numbers, but his fingers were clumsy, so he asked the assistant to say them out loud. It said the living room was set to twenty-one, and the bedroom was still at nineteen. Walter smiled, put on his coat, and went out to close the garden gate.

A computer keeps your work in files, and folders are like drawers that hold them. When a file is in the wrong drawer, people say "move it to the school folder" or "put this in my documents." The screen is another thing people change. If the words look tiny, they ask for bigger text, and in a dark room they say "make it dim." Sometimes a computer gets slow or a window freezes. A friendly helper will say "try restarting it." Then the computer closes everything and starts again. If the battery falls to ten percent, you might say "save my work" so nothing is lost when the power goes out.

Many machines have a filter that catches dust or dirt. A bakery oven has one in its fan, and at home the kitchen hood and the water jug have them too. When a filter gets old, the air can smell sour or the water can taste odd. People change filters every few months. To ask for help, they say "remind me to swap the filter," "the fridge smells sour," or "book someone to fix the heater." A repair person picks a day that suits you, and you can say "not Monday" or "any morning next week." If a part is broken, they order it first and come back. After the job, you can ask "when is the next check?" and the date is saved for you.

Sam woke up in the dark and mumbled to the bedroom speaker, "Turn on the front porch camera, I want to see if my guest is here. No wait, I mean the back door camera." His cousin was coming at six, but Sam had heard a noise outside. The assistant said, "Okay, I changed it. The back door camera is on." The picture came up on the little screen. Sam pulled the warm blanket up to his chin and looked. He saw only a deep shadow near the fence and a cat walking by. The assistant said it could not see any people and that the motion sensor had not gone off. Sam yawned and went back to sleep.

Sports apps tell you the score, the time of the next game and how your team is doing. The lock screen on a phone can show a score without opening anything. People change which team they follow and say "switch to the other team" or "follow the city club." They also ask "what's the score?", "when is the next match?" or "tell me when they score." After a sweet win, fans may ask for the highlights, and after a loss they say "don't show me the results." Training works the same way. A runner can say "start my timer" or "how far did I go?" A good assistant keeps your teams in a list and answers short questions quickly.

inputs: who to send it to, and whether the paper has one page or many
people say:
- Scan this letter and send it to my sister.
- Send my fishing license to the club office as a PDF.
- Put that form on the glass and mail the picture to Dad.
- I put the wrong page in, so do it again.
- Take all three pages and send them together.

Dana was late for school pickup and had gone around the block twice. The lot by the library was full, even though the sign said the price was low. She tapped her phone and typed fast: "any open parkign spot near the school". The assistant looked at the map and said there was a street spot two blocks away and a small garage across the road with five free places. Dana asked how to pay. It said the meter took a mix of coins and cards, but she could also pay in the app. She chose the garage. The assistant paid for one hour, saved the receipt, and set a reminder for four thirty. Dana watched the upload bar finish, then ran to the gate.

Priya had a flat afternoon with nothing planned, and she needed quiet time to dig into her report. "Block two to four tomorrow for focus time and move my team meeting to Thursday," she told her laptop. The assistant made a two-hour block on her calendar for the next day. Then it moved the team meeting from Wednesday at ten to Thursday at ten and sent the new time to everyone invited. It told her that one person had already said no for Thursday. Priya said that was fine. Her goal was to finish the report before Friday, and now she had the time to do it.

Mara got home after a twelve-hour night shift with her eyes half closed. The grass was long. "Start the robot mower at nine," she told her phone. Then she yawned. "No, sorry, make it noon. I need to sleep first." The assistant said it had changed the start time to noon. It also saw that the current forecast showed rain at two, so it asked if she wanted the mower to stop early. She said yes, finish by one. Outside, a bucket sat by the shed and a bird began to fly over the fence as the mower's light blinked once. Mara went to bed and fell asleep in a minute.
