An appointment is a time you keep for a person, like the dentist or the barber. The shop learns your name, the day and how long you need. People change appointments all the time. They say "move it to Friday," "make it earlier" or "cancel my haircut." They also ask "when does the clinic open?" or "what time do you close?" Opening hours matter because the last slot of the day often fills first. If the office is up the stairs and you need a room on the ground floor, you can say so when you book. After you book, a reminder usually comes the day before.

Jonas had just moved to the city, and his flat had a printer he had never used. He needed to print his rental form before the office closed. "Print the form from my email, but not in color, and don't print the last page," he told his phone. The assistant opened the current file and found four pages. It sent only three to the printer, in black and white. The printer woke from sleep and began to hum. Jonas picked up the pages, still warm, and slid them into a peach folder. The assistant also told him the ink was low and offered to put new ink on his shopping list. Jonas said yes.

Lena closed her shop late and drove home in the dark. She buckled her seatbelt and sighed. "The delivery truck comes at six tomorrow and I'll never hear it. I'm so tired I could sleep through a storm." The assistant in the car understood that she wanted to be woken up early. It said it would set an alarm for five thirty, so she would have time for a coffee. Then it asked if she wanted a soft sound or a loud one. Lena said loud. The assistant also offered to play quiet rain sounds to listen to as she fell asleep. She said that would be the first nice thing all day.

A note is a small piece of writing you keep so you will not forget something. People write notes for shopping, ideas, phone numbers, or a thought on a sad day. You can speak a voice note when your hands are busy, like when you are cooking over the heat. To find an old note, people say "show my notes about the trip" or "what did I write on Tuesday?" To change one, they say "add milk to the list," "delete the last line" or "make this note a reminder." You can also say "note that the key is under the pot" and the assistant writes it down for you.

Person: I'm at the trailhead and the sun is going down. It's going to be a cold night out here.
Assistant: Do you want me to check the weather in the hills tonight?
Person: Yes. And unlock the car boot, I need my jacket.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't unlock your car from here. But I can tell you the weather. Which trail are you on?
Person: The lake trail. I also brought a present for my daughter, so I need a personal packing list for her tent.
Assistant: Tonight it will drop to two degrees with a light wind. For her tent, I'd pack a warm sleeping bag, a hat, a torch and a snack.

Person: I'm baking cookies for the book club tomorrow at seven. Can you make the recipe bigger?
Assistant: Sure. How many people are coming?
Person: Twelve. The recipe says it makes six.
Assistant: Then I'll double everything. That is two cups of flour, one cup of brown sugar and two eggs.
Person: It also says to fold in the chocolate. My kitten keeps jumping on the counter, so I need to be quick!
Assistant: Fold in two cups of chocolate chips with a spoon, slowly.
Person: Can you order the chocolate and bring it by noon?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't order groceries. I can add chocolate to your shopping list.

name: set_blinds_position
does: Opens or closes blinds, curtains or shutters by the amount you choose.
inputs: which room or window, and how open it should be
people say:
- Let some light into the living room.
- The sun is in my eyes.
- Close the main bedroom curtains halfway.
- The cat wants to watch the birds, so open the low blind.
- I'm going to eat breakfast, so open the kitchen shutters all the way.
- Make it dark for the movie.

Nia had moved to the city a month ago and did not know many people yet. "Remind me tomorrow at seven to buy a card for Ben's birthday," she said to her phone. "And what can I get him? Something small and nice." The assistant set the reminder for seven tomorrow evening. Then it gave her three gift ideas: a plant, a weekly planner, or a mug with a fun design. Nia liked the planner. The assistant found a shop near her office and said there was free parking behind it. It added the shop's closing time to the reminder, so she would not be late.

When you order something online, the shop packs it and a delivery person brings it to your door. Tracking tells you where the parcel is, and some apps update the position hourly. People often change an order. They say "make it a medium," "send it to my work" or "cancel the second one." Sizes can be confusing, so they ask "what size is a large in this brand?" If something arrives broken, like a camping tent with a crack in a pole, they say "I want to return this." The shop sends a label, and you take the parcel back. Returns usually need the box and the receipt.

Mrs. Hale did not trust her new phone. Her son had told her it could call a taxi. She held it close to her face and said, "Get me a car to the hospital, the main door, and I don't want the pickup at the side gate." The screen showed a map. She tried to zoom with two fingers, but it only moved the picture around. The assistant understood that she wanted a ride to the main entrance of the hospital, and it booked the only car nearby. It said the driver would arrive in six minutes and told her the color of the car. It offered to open a message channel with the driver, but she said she would just wave from the door.

Mr. Bell stood in his kitchen with a pot of icy water and a mountain of potatoes. He had taught history for forty years, but he had never learned to cook. "How long do I boil these potatoes, and how hot should the oven be for the roast?" he asked the tablet on the counter. The assistant understood that he wanted two answers. It said to boil cut potatoes for about twenty-five minutes and to set the oven to one hundred eighty degrees. Mr. Bell said he liked Fahrenheit better, so the assistant said three fifty. He asked it to set a timer, and it did.

Grandpa Leo wanted a picture of his granddaughter for the fridge. "Print the photo of Ana on the beach," he told the printer app. Then he paused. "No, wait. The one from her birthday, with the cake." The assistant found the birthday photo and asked how many copies he wanted. "One for each of my children, so three." It built a small page with the photo and printed three copies on glossy paper. The woman next door, Mrs. Cho, came by to borrow sugar and admired each one. Leo gave her a copy too, and the assistant added more paper to his shopping list.

Tom stayed at his desk past five, planning the office party. "Remind me tomorrow at seven to order the decorations," he told his phone, "and sort my party list by who is bringing food." The assistant set the reminder for seven the next morning. Then it sorted the list into two groups: people bringing food and people who had not answered yet. Tom said he wanted plain paper cups and not the fancy ones, so the assistant added that to the order note. He had a sweet tooth, and asked it to put a cake on the list as well. It did.

The router is the small box that sends wifi around your home. It has a name and a password. When a guest comes, people say "give them the password" or "make a guest network." If the internet is slow, people ask "why is it so slow?" Walls and even a big tree outside can make the signal weaker. A serious slowdown often goes away when you restart the router. The lights go off, and after a minute they return to green. People also say "change the wifi password" or "turn off the wifi for the kids at nine," and the router does what they ask.

Grandma Rosa shuffled out to the garden in her slippers. The tomatoes looked dry, and the old wire fence leaned close to the plants. "Water the tomatoes for twenty-five minutes," she told her speaker, "the sprinkler by the fence." The assistant turned on the sprinkler on the fence side and set a timer for twenty-five minutes. Rosa added, "And don't water the roses. They get too much." The assistant left the rose sprinkler off and said so. Rosa sat on her bench, watched the water fall on the leaves, and was glad she did not have to carry the hose.

Mr. Ruiz was cooking dinner from a recipe in an old book from the public library. It said to use eight ounces of butter, but his kitchen scale only showed grams. "How many grams is eight ounces?" he asked his phone. "I don't want an exact number, just close." The assistant understood that he wanted ounces turned into grams. It said it was about two hundred twenty-seven grams, so two hundred twenty-five was fine. Then Mr. Ruiz said he planned to travel to England and asked what twenty degrees was in Fahrenheit. The assistant said sixty-eight. He wrote both numbers on the recipe.

A delivery has a few parts: the order, the shipping and the arrival. Many shops send a message with a code, or a key, to open a parcel locker. People say "where is my order?", "send it to my neighbor" or "leave it at the front door." If the shop says the delivery is late, you can reply, "ask them to come on Friday." A weak box may get crushed on the way, and then people say "I want my money back" or "send me a new one." Most shops keep your orders in a list, so you can ask "what did I order last week?"

Grandpa Joe wanted the lawn to look nice for Sunday's picnic. "Give the grass a cut tomorrow at seven," he told his tablet. "The wireless mower is in the shed." The assistant started the robot mower for seven the next morning and said it would be done by about nine. It also told him the edges by the fence would still need a hand trim. Joe laughed and said he would do those with his old scissors. The assistant added a reminder for Saturday to put out the picnic chairs.

Kai was running out the door with his bag half open and his desk messy. "Put bake the cake on my list for today, but don't put it before the dentist, I'll never make it," he said to his phone. "And tell me what's left." The assistant added "bake the cake" to the end of the list, after the dentist visit. Then it read out the three things still to do: buy eggs, call his friend Jo about her party, and pick up the mail. Kai nodded, locked the door, and ran for the bus.

Ray was driving the van and stopped at a red light. "Add Mia Torres as a favorite," he said to the car. "Her number is five five five, oh one nine two. And mute the group chat until tomorrow at seven." The assistant saved a new contact called Mia Torres and put her at the top of his favorite list. Then it turned off sounds from the group chat until seven the next morning. It told him both things were done in one short sentence. The light turned green and Ray drove on, with a quiet phone.

The person wants to know how many steps they have taken today.
Step count?
My steps
How far have I walked?
Tell me how many steps I've done since this morning
I'm sleepy and want to know if I've walked enough today.
Did my sandals earn me ten thousand steps yet?
Show today's walk
I went for a long walk, so could you pick out the step number and tell me?

Max was texting his friends while walking home. Then he spoke to his phone. "Save Grandma Ruth's new number. It's five five five, zero one two three." The assistant saved the number under her name and replaced the old one. Max said he couldn't afford a big gift for his young cousin, so he wanted to send her a card. "What's the address of her house?" he asked. The assistant read out the address that was saved under his aunt's name. Max typed it into the card app, and the assistant told him the old number was still in the history, in case he needed it.

A hobby is something you do for fun in your free time, like knitting, painting or building models. Each hobby has tools and a plan. People change the plan. They ask for a bigger canvas, another color of yarn or ten more minutes on a model. They also say "remind me to paint on Sunday," "find a pattern for a scarf" or "where can I buy glue?" Many people like to do their hobby at the usual time each week, like after dinner or on the bus ride home when they knit. An assistant can keep a list of supplies and tell you what to buy next.

name: remind_bill_due
does: Keeps a list of bills and tells you before each one is due.
inputs: the bill name, the amount, and the due date
people say:
- When is the water bill due?
- Don't let me forget rent on the first.
- Tell me about any extra fees this month.
- Remind me three days before the power bill is due.
- Invite my roommate to see the shared bills list.

Nora checked her phone on a damp, gray lunch break. A photo of her sitting on a stone wall had some comments she did not like. "Delete my last post," she said to her phone, "but don't delete the whole album." The assistant understood that she wanted one photo gone and the rest kept. It deleted the post with the wall photo, left the album as it was, and told her that twelve comments went with it. Nora put her phone away and finished her sandwich.

Person: where is my pacakge
Assistant: I can check. Which one? I see two, one from a book shop and one from a pharmacy.
Person: the one for my sore tooth, the pharmacy
Assistant: That parcel is out for delivery today. It should arrive between two and four.
Person: my doorbell got disconnected, so tell the driver to knock
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send a message to the driver. But I can add a note to the order. Do you want that?
Person: yes please

Eli woke up on party day with a long list in his head and a dry mouth. His friend, a doctor, was coming straight from work, and the other guests would arrive at eight. He looked around the living room and said to the speaker, "It's way too quiet in here for a party." The assistant understood that he wanted music. It played the dance list at low volume and said it was three hours long. Eli walked to the kitchen, opened the fridge, and told the assistant to turn the music up a little. It did.

Person: Excuse me, dear. I'm taking my grandson to the lake on Saturday and the car has been making a funny noise, so could you please tell me what the tyre pressure should be?
Assistant: Happy to. Which car is it, the blue one or the white one?
Person: The blue one.
Assistant: For the blue car, the front tyres should be thirty-two and the back ones thirty-four.
Person: Thank you. Please set a reminder for Friday morning to check them. And can you rank the petrol stations by price?
Assistant: I'll set the reminder for Friday morning. I'm sorry, I can't rank the stations by price. I can show you the closest ones.

name: make_guest_wifi
does: Creates a temporary wifi network for visitors with its own password.
inputs: how long it should last, and a name for the network
people say:
- My friends are coming and they'll want the internet.
- Can the picnic guests use the wifi without my main password?
- Set up a visitor network until tomorrow.
- What should I answer when guests ask for the password? Make them a new one.
- Call the network Creamy Latte.

The person wants to check if there is a water leak in the house.
Any leaks?
Is water running somewhere it shouldn't be?
The pipe over the hamster cage is wet. Is it leaking?
Look at the water meter and tell me if it moves when everything is off.
I hear a loud drip somewhere, so please check the pipes.
Run a leak test for twenty-five minutes with all the taps closed.
Invite a plumber if you find a leak.
Has my bill gone up because of a hidden leak?

Hana came in from the garden with muddy hands and dirt on her sleeves. She typed with one thumb: "print the seed record for the new beds, 2 copies, plese". The assistant understood that she wanted her seed record printed twice. It found the file called Seed Record, sent two copies to the printer, and said the paper tray was nearly empty. Hana was lucky, because there were just enough sheets. She wanted one copy for her neighbor, who would join her at the garden club on Saturday.

A password is a secret word that keeps your things private. Most phones and apps ask for one, and the best ones are long and different for every account. People change a password when they think someone has seen it, or just once in a while. They say things like, change my password, make it stronger, or lock my phone after one minute. A phone can also hide messages on the lock screen, so a person at your lunch table cannot read them. Some people slice the risk in half by turning on a second check, like a code sent by text. At a minimum, use a screen lock. You can also ask, who can see my photos, and the assistant shows the sharing list.

Priya was a student, and the wifi in her flat kept dropping. A big storm had just passed, and the router light was blinking red. She sat at her desk, on the chair with the broken wheel, and said to her phone, 'Restart router.' The assistant understood that she meant the router in the hall. It sent the restart command and told her it would take about two minutes. Priya needed to send her essay to her teacher, so she waited. When the light turned green, she said, 'Email my essay to Mr. Dale.' The assistant found the file called essay final, attached it, and sent the email. It told her the message had gone out. Priya smiled and went back to studying.

name: wind_down_timer
does: Starts a calm bedtime routine that dims the lights, plays soft sounds, and stops them when the person falls asleep.
inputs: the time the person wants to be asleep and the kind of sound they like
people say:
- I want to be asleep by ten thirty
- help me relax, my head is full of thoughts
- it's still bright outside, make my room dark for bed
- I just had a shower, now I need to calm down
- play rain sounds until I drift off
- I put my paper book down, time to sleep

Mrs. Alvarez was a retired teacher who read one long novel every July. One evening she sat in her chair with a cup of lemon tea that tasted too sour. 'I don't want the next chapter tonight,' she said to the smart speaker, 'and please don't read it out loud. Just keep my place.' The assistant understood that she wanted to save her spot and not play the audiobook. It put a bookmark at page 212, the end of chapter nine, and said the bookmark would carry over to her phone as well. Mrs. Alvarez nodded. She finished her tea, turned off the light, and the speaker stayed quiet all night.

Tom had just moved to the city with his two kids. After a long day standing at the school gate in the cold March wind, his feet were sore. That evening he told the family tablet, 'Give the kids half an hour less screen time on school nights.' The assistant understood that he wanted the nightly limit to be shorter by thirty minutes. The old limit was ninety minutes, so it changed it to sixty. It told Tom the new limit was one hour and that it would start tonight. Tom said that was fine, and he also asked it to read the kids a bedtime story if they finished early. The assistant said yes and set the story for eight o'clock.

Luis drove a school bus, and on a rainy morning he sat in the parking lot with a wool scarf around his neck, waiting for the first stop. It had snowed last week, and the roads were still slick. He spoke to his phone: 'Excuse me, could you please remind me tonight at eight about my daughter's science project, because it is due on Friday and last time I forgot and she was very upset?' The assistant understood that Luis wanted one reminder, tonight at eight, about the science project. It made the reminder, wrote science project, due Friday, and told him it was set. Luis thanked it and started the engine.

Finding a film to watch is easy now. A phone or TV can list what is on at the cinema near you, show trailers, and tell you the times. People use it to pick a movie before they leave home. You can change the day, the place, or the kind of film. They say, show me something funny for tonight, or what's on Saturday afternoon. If the first choice is not right for the kids, they say, replace that one with a cartoon. At home, some people switch off the lamp so the room is dark before the trailer starts. Families also ask for a safe film for young children, and the assistant looks at the age rating.

Nina was nine, and the air in her room felt dry and smelly. Her neighbor was burning leaves in the yard, and the smoke was drifting in. She stood by her bed and said, 'Can you turn on the humidifier and close the north window?' The assistant understood that she wanted two things done: the humidifier on, and the window shut. It switched on the humidifier in her room, and it asked the smart window to close. Nina asked if it could help the air get clean faster, so the assistant also started the purifier on its high setting. After a few minutes the room smelled fresh again. Nina said thank you and went back to her drawing.

name: gift_idea_finder
does: Suggests gift ideas for a person based on their age, hobbies and how much money you want to spend.
inputs: who the gift is for, what they like, and the budget
people say:
- what should I get my brother for his birthday
- my aunt is turning sixty and I'm out of ideas
- something under twenty dollars for a friend who loves anything blue
- my dad likes burgers and grilling, got any present ideas
- I need a gift for my cousin who lives far away

Sam was ten, and he wanted to show his friends his new dog. The dog, Biscuit, weighed forty pound and was chilling on the sofa in the sun. Sam took a picture and told the family tablet, 'Post this on our page tomorrow at seven.' The assistant understood that he wanted the photo shared, but not right now. It said that seven in the morning was a busy time on the page, so more people might see it. Sam said that was good. The assistant set the post for tomorrow at seven and told Sam it would show him the likes when they came in. Sam gave Biscuit a pat.

Meal planning means deciding what to eat for the week before you go shopping. It is a job that many families share. People use it to save money, eat better, and stop asking what's for dinner every night. You can change a plan whenever you like. Say, swap Tuesday's dinner for pasta, no fish this week, or make Friday bigger because we invite friends over. A rare treat, like pizza, can go on the weekend. Packed lunches are part of the plan too, so a parent might say, give the kids something cold for school on Monday. At the end, the plan turns into a shopping list.

A bill is a request for money for something you used, like electricity, water or rent. Each bill has an amount and a due date. The power bill may come in a purple envelope, or as a message on your phone. People change when and how they pay. They say, pay the water bill on the first, remind me three days before the rent is due, or take the electric bill off autopay. If a bill looks high, they ask how much they used last month. An old fridge plugged into the outlet in the garage can take a lot of power, so people sometimes find the reason this way. Paying on time keeps things simple.

Maya was late for work and grabbing her keys. The pollen count was high, and she had already taken her allergy dose that morning. As she hurried to the door she said, 'Run the purifier on full until tomorrow at seven, and cool the bedroom a little.' The assistant understood that she wanted the tall purifier in the hall set to its strongest level until seven the next morning. It also lowered the bedroom heat by two degrees. It told her both things were done. Maya said thanks over her shoulder and ran for the bus. When she came home that evening, the air in the flat felt fresh and clear.

Dana got home after a rough night shift. Her dog Pepper sat by an empty bowl, whining. The kitchen lamp was glaring in her tired eyes. 'It's way too bright in here, and Pepper's tummy is growling,' she mumbled. She needed a boost of sleep more than coffee. The assistant understood the hints. It dimmed the lamp to a soft glow, and it told the pet feeder to give Pepper his usual breakfast, one cup of food. It said both things out loud so Dana knew. Pepper ate happily, and Dana dropped onto the sofa. The assistant added that it would keep the house quiet until noon.

Hector was a gardener, and he loved the garden at night. He wanted to record a short video of the first star over the roses. 'Dim the porch light and start recording tomorrow at seven in the evening,' he told his phone. The assistant understood that two things were needed: the porch light should be lowered, and the camera should start filming at seven. The light was already dim, so it only lowered it a little more. It scheduled the recording for tomorrow at seven, and said the clip would save to Hector's video folder. Hector went inside for dinner, happy that the plan was ready.

Rosa was a cook, and her kitchen was loud. The washer was running in the back room, and her hands were covered in flour. She typed with one thumb: 'remind me my sisters birtday is close, find gift'. The assistant saw the small typo and understood what she meant. Her sister's birthday was in four days. It made a reminder for the day before, and it showed three gift ideas: a cookbook, a scarf, and a pack of fancy tea. Rosa said she liked the cookbook. The assistant added it to her shopping list and told her it would remind her to wrap it. Rosa wiped her hands and went back to the stove.

Omar owned a furniture shop that sold beds, and on Saturday he wanted to follow the football. 'Show me the score of the Hawks game,' he said to his phone. Then he stopped. 'No, sorry, I mean the Eagles game.' The assistant understood that he had changed his mind, so it dropped the Hawks and looked up the Eagles. It told him the Eagles were winning two to one at halftime. It was getting dark outside, and Omar still had to close up. He asked it to tell him the final score before he started to leave the shop. The assistant said it would send a message when the game ended.

A focus timer helps you work hard for a short time and then rest. A common plan is twenty-five minutes of work and then a five-minute break. During the break you stand up, stretch, and let your eyes rest, especially if they feel sore from the screen. Some people open a window or sit near a vent to get fresh air, or they blow on a hot cup of tea. People change the timer by saying, make it thirty minutes, give me a longer break, or start my morning routine at six. You can also ask for a gentle sound when time is up instead of a loud one. A good routine keeps the day calm and the work moving.

Ben was late for the airport, and his bag was half packed. His grandmother was coming to visit, and he could not remember how long he had left to get ready. 'Days until Sunday,' he said to his phone. The assistant understood that he wanted to know how many days remained before Sunday. It counted from today and said there were three days left. Ben nodded. He had thought tomorrow was the day, and he had paid for an expensive taxi for nothing. He canceled the taxi with a quick word to the assistant, and then he sat down to finish his packing in peace.

Mr. Okafor was a retired teacher, and on cold evenings he liked to sit in his cozy chair by the window. 'Would you please record the evening news on the third channel tonight and save it for me,' he said to the TV, 'because I will be at choir practice and my wife would like to see it later?' The assistant understood that he wanted the news on channel three recorded and kept. It set the recording for six o'clock, said it would track the show even if it started late, and told him where the video would be saved. Mr. Okafor thanked it and went to find his coat.

Lina owned a flower shop, and she had a call with her supplier at ten. She sat at the counter with her laptop and said, 'Join my ten o'clock call, and make the shared window twice as big.' The assistant understood the two parts. It opened the meeting link and made the shared window double its size so Lina could see the order list. When the sound was bad, the supplier said sorry for the noise. Lina asked the assistant for half the volume, and it turned the speaker down. She still did not understand one number on the list, so she asked the assistant to read it again, slowly. It did.

A drink can be made many ways, and most people like it a certain way. Coffee can be strong or weak, tea can be hot or iced, and a smoothie can be thick or thin. A student might pack a flask of gentle green tea for class, while a runner wants a sweet fruit smoothie. When people want a change, they say, make it stronger, less sugar, half sweet, or no ice. The machine or the assistant then changes the amount of coffee, milk or honey. It is for making a drink that tastes right, without starting over every time. Some people also ask for a smaller cup in the afternoon.

Jake was late, and the hiking trip started in an hour. He threw his boots into the car and told his phone, 'Make my packing list for two nights, and bring twice as much water as last time.' The assistant understood that he wanted the usual list, but with the water doubled. It listed a tent, a sleeping bag, snacks, and six bottles of water instead of three. His job was to carry the food, so it added a bag for that too. As he drove, the phone flashed a weather alert: sunny all weekend. The assistant told him to add sunscreen to the list, and Jake said yes.

They want to see a doctor tomorrow.
Visit doctor tomorrow
Can I see a doctor tomorrow at seven?
Book me in with Dr. Lee for tomorrow morning, please.
My throat is sore and vinegar tea did not help, so I want to visit the clinic tomorrow at seven.
Is there a free slot tomorrow around seven for a check-up?
I would like the earliest time tomorrow, and I'm not sure it is safe to wait longer.
Could you please find me an appointment at the health center for tomorrow at seven in the morning?
Get me a doctor, tomorrow, seven.
I know it is short notice, but is anyone free to see me tomorrow at seven?

Person: hey how much is it if i go west next winter
Assistant: Do you mean the price of a trip, or what your money is worth in another country?
Person: my money. i have 200 dollars and im going to ireland
Assistant: Got it. When do you want to exchange it? Rates change a little every day.
Person: tomorrow at seven, before i climb on the bus to the airport
Assistant: I can't know tomorrow's rate yet, but today's rate would give you about 185 euros. I can check again tomorrow morning.
Person: ok do that

A smart speaker is a small box that can hear you and answer. It plays music, tells the weather, sets timers and controls lights. Each person in the house can have a voice profile, so the speaker knows who is talking. If one speaker is not enough, you can group speakers so the same song plays in the kitchen and the living room. People change the volume by saying, turn it up, a bit quieter, or louder please. They ask what the speaker can do, and it lists its skills. If a person is hungry, they can ask for a recipe. Say, stop, and the speaker goes quiet. It listens closely only after it hears its wake word.

They want to know when the food will arrive.
Where's my food?
How long until the pizza is here?
Is the driver back at the restaurant or on the way to me?
My guests are about to be welcomed in, so is dinner nearly here?
Will it take more than twenty-five minutes?
Can you check the delivery and tell me the time it will get to my door?
I've been waiting a while. What's the new arrival time on my order?
Please let me know as soon as the delivery person is close, I'm starving.

Walter was not good with technology. His grandson had set up the email on a tablet that sat by the coat hook in the hall. One morning Walter wiped his dirty glasses on his sleeve and said, 'Unread mail?' The assistant understood that he wanted to know about new emails. It said there were four messages, and it read the names of the people who sent them. One was from the water company. Walter said, 'Label that one bills.' The assistant put a bills label on the email and moved it to a folder with the same name. Walter was pleased that it had been so easy, and he went to make toast.

Grace was not good with technology, and she did not like the clinic website, where she had tried to change her visit three times. So she pressed the button on her speaker and said, 'Move my dentist visit to Friday and tell me what is on Thursday.' The assistant understood both parts. It moved the visit from Wednesday to Friday at the same time, and it read out Thursday's plans: lunch with her sister at noon and a walk in the east park at four. Grace was surprised that two things had happened at once. She thanked the speaker, and the assistant said that she could ask for more changes any time.

Kofi had just moved to the city, and he felt silly asking a phone what to eat. But he had no plan and not much money. 'Plan dinners for the week,' he said, 'but no meat and nothing spicy.' The assistant understood that he wanted five dinners without meat and without hot peppers. It suggested rice with beans, vegetable soup, and a pasta bake. It said half of the recipes made enough for two meals, so he could stretch his budget by eating the rest the next day. Kofi liked that idea. He asked the assistant to turn the plan into a shopping list, and it did.

name: pantry_check
does: Tells you which foods at home are running low and puts them on the shopping list so the order can be sent with one click.
inputs: the name of the food, and any direction about which store to buy it from
people say:

Scaling a recipe means making more or less of a dish than the card says. My grandma makes a soup that serves four, but if you have eight guests, you need double. Cups, spoons and servings all change together. People say, make it for six, cut it in half, or I only need enough for one. The numbers change: two cups of rice become four, and a half spoon of salt becomes a whole one. Some people also say, wake me up when the soup is ready, and set a timer. It helps when the recipe uses cups but your measuring tool uses spoons, because the helper can change one to the other.

Joy was a nurse, and she had just finished a long night shift. She sat in her car and said, 'Scan the clinic website for the least busy day next week and remind me to take my afternoon dose at noon.' The assistant understood that there were two requests. It looked at the clinic page and saw that Tuesday had the fewest visits, so it offered Tuesday morning. It also set a reminder for noon with the words, take afternoon dose. Joy said to book Tuesday, and the assistant did. She drove home, glad that she did not have to remember anything herself.

They want to book a haircut.
Haircut, please.
I don't want a morning slot. Book a haircut after lunch.
Can you fit me in for a trim sometime this week, a total of an hour at most?
My current barber is booked up, so find another one nearby, but not downtown.
I need to plan a haircut before the wedding on Saturday, any open times?
Get me anything tomorrow, except the early hours.
I would be grateful if you could find a free time at the salon this week, and please do not choose a day when it rains.
When is the next free spot at the hair place?

A lawn needs cutting and water to stay healthy. Many yards now have a robot mower that goes over the grass by itself and a sprinkler that comes on at set times. The mower rests in its dock when it is done or when rain starts, because wet grass is hard to cut. People change the plan by saying, cut the grass shorter, skip tomorrow's watering, or mow only the front. If the ground is still damp, they ask to wait a day. Someone who bought a broken mower may ask the shop for a refund. Edges are trimmed with a small tool along paths and flower beds. A little care each week keeps grass green and thick.

people say:

- small hills only, about ten miles
- cancel Saturday's ride, it's going to rain

They want to hear today's top headlines.
News.

If I'm lucky there's some good news today, so read me what you have.
Could you give me a quick summary of what happened this morning, please?

They want to know how much electricity the house is using.
Power use?
Energy now.

Sync the meter reading with my phone and show me what we used today.
We were away on holiday, did the house use much power?
The house is quiet and nobody is home, so why is the meter still running?
Could you tell me, as simply as you can, how our energy use compares with last week?
Show me my usage since this morning.

Amir had just moved to the city and was in his first apartment. He had cooked pasta, packed lunch for the next day, and turned down the brightness on his phone because his eyes were tired. Then he remembered that rent was coming. 'Move fifty dollars from savings to checking tomorrow at seven,' he said. The assistant understood that he wanted a transfer between his own two accounts at seven the next morning. It checked that savings had enough money, scheduled the move, and read the plan back to him. Amir said that was right. The assistant told him the transfer would show up in checking within a few minutes of seven.

Call Mia.

Get Mia on the line.
Please call my friend Joe and put him on speakerphone so everyone can hear.

Elena had just woken up, and her head was still full of sleep. She needed to board the early train, and she had installed a ride app last week. She mumbled to her phone, 'Book a ride to the station tomorrow at seven.' The assistant understood that she wanted a car for the next morning, not right now. It asked where to pick her up, and she said the usual place at the front door. It booked the ride and said the driver would arrive at ten to seven. Elena was glad. She pulled the blanket back over her head and went back to sleep for a little longer.

Leo was a student, and he sat on a bench in the sun with his headphones on. A woman beside him was laughing at something on her phone, and Leo remembered that his audiobook was funny too. 'Next chapter,' he said to his phone. The assistant understood that he was done with this chapter and wanted to hear the one after it. It skipped from chapter six to chapter seven and began to play. It also told him how long the new chapter was: twenty minutes. Leo smiled and leaned back, because that was just enough time before class.

Mia was eight, and she had a sore throat. She sat in bed with an electric blanket up to her chin. 'Please keep a note for Mom to take me to the doctor tomorrow at seven,' she told the family tablet. The assistant understood that Mia wanted a reminder for her mom about a doctor visit the next morning. It wrote the note and sent it to Mom's phone. Then it showed the route to the clinic on the screen, so Mom could see how long the drive would take. Mia said thank you in a small voice, and the assistant told her to drink some warm water and get some rest.

Person: Play podcast.

A smart lock lets a front door open without a key. It can open with a code, a phone, or your voice. It is for keeping the home safe and for letting people in when you are not there. People change who can come in. They say, give my neighbor a code for today, lock the garage door, or tell me when the door opens. A camera at the door can upload a short video each time someone rings, so you see who is there. A person ironing in the back room can still see the visitor on a phone screen. The lock works well when the battery is fresh, so many locks warn you when it is low.

Sports are games with teams, scores and times. People follow a match to know who is winning and when the next one starts. An assistant can tell you the score, show the league table, or remind you when your team plays. People change what they follow by saying, add my son's team, tell me when the game starts, or stop alerts for hockey. If the match does not go well, a fan may ask where the team stands now. Training is part of sports too: a runner can ask for a new running direction, or a plan for ten minutes of stretching. Go with whatever team you love, and the updates will come to you.

Chen had just moved to the city and was ordering pastries for a small party. He wanted to be sure the price was right and the total was safe to pay. 'What is twelve times four?' he asked his phone. Then he frowned. 'No, wait, I mean twelve times five.' The assistant understood that he had fixed the number and answered the new question: sixty. Chen said that was the number of pastries he needed for his guests. He asked what the price would be at two dollars each. The assistant multiplied sixty by two and said one hundred twenty dollars. Chen sighed, then placed the order anyway.

News is a short list of the things that happened today. It can be about the world, your town, or your favorite team. People use it to stay informed without reading every paper. They change what they get by saying, only local news, no sports, or read me the headlines in the morning. If a story is long, they ask for a short version. Some stories make your head spin, so people ask for good news only. A weather story may say it will be cold tonight. Say, tell me more about that one, and the assistant reads the whole story. You can ask it to stop at any time, even before you blink.

Person: its freezing in here
Assistant: I can warm it up. Which room are you in?
Person: my room upstairs. the snow outside is knee depth lol
Assistant: Okay. How warm do you want it? Twenty-one degrees is cozy for most people.

Assistant: Good idea. I've set your room to twenty degrees. It should be warm in about fifteen minutes.

Person: Please start the wash and remind me to move it to the dryer when it ends.

Assistant: Quick wash with warm water. Should I start it now?
Person: Yes, now. The baby will sleep for an hour and I want the machine done before she wakes up.
Assistant: Started. A quick wash takes thirty minutes, so I will remind you at ten past nine.

Someone wants the garden watered right now.
water the garden
the lawn looks dry, can you give it a drink?
turn on the sprinklers
my tomatos are thirsty, pls start the water
The soil is as hard as a coin, so could you get the hose going?
Run the sprinklers for ten minutes, the grass smells sour and dry.
Give the roses a good soak.
If you could wave a magic wand and water the front beds, that would be lovely.
Could you please water the back garden? I will be away all afternoon and the flowers need a drink.

A television is for watching shows, news and films. Most people keep it on a desk or a stand and control it with a remote. Every day people change a few things: the channel, the volume and the subtitles. They say things like turn it down, put on the subtitles, or go back ten seconds when they miss a line. If a baby is asleep, they say mute the tv. If a spicy cooking show is on and the kitchen is noisy, they might say make it louder. Streaming apps let you pick a show from a list, and you can pause it whenever you need a break.

Mr. Brandt, a retired teacher, put his bag on the back seat of the car. The garage was dim, so he spoke up when he talked to his phone. 'Please notify me tomorrow at seven to check the tyre pressure,' he said. 'The back left one looks soft.' The assistant understood that he wanted a reminder for tomorrow at seven in the morning about his tyres. It set the reminder and read it back to him: 'Reminder set for tomorrow at seven: check the tyre pressure.' Mr. Brandt nodded and went inside for supper. The next morning the phone buzzed right on time, and he went out with the pump and filled the soft tyre until the gauge showed thirty-two.

Rosa is not good with technology, and her phone often confuses her. Today she wondered how to say thank you in Italian, because her new neighbour had brought her a cake. 'I don't want to type anything,' she told the phone. 'And please don't show me a long list. Just say it.' The assistant understood that she wanted one short phrase, spoken aloud. It said, Grazie mille, and then said it again slowly. Rosa tried it twice. 'Say it double slow,' she asked, and the assistant said it again, very slowly. Then she asked it to save her neighbour's number as a new contact called Marco. The assistant did that and told her it was saved.

Mrs. Dube owns a small shop that sells fruit and vegetables. One morning a new farmer gave her his phone number on a scrap of paper, along with a box of potatoes. 'Save this number as Farmer Ali and clear the old number for Mr. Park,' she told her phone, 'because he doesn't sell bitter melon any more.' The assistant understood that there were two jobs in one sentence. It added a new contact called Farmer Ali with the number she read out, and it deleted the contact called Mr. Park. Then it said both things were done. Mrs. Dube said thank you and went back to weighing potatoes.

Dana the cook stood by the stove on a windy morning, sipping a cup of tea. She had a cold coming on. She pointed at the clock on the wall and spoke to her phone. 'Remind me to take half a tablet of my cold medicine at noon. The doctor said half, not a whole one.' The assistant understood that she wanted a reminder at twelve o'clock about half a tablet. It set the reminder and repeated it: 'Noon today, take half a tablet of cold medicine.' At noon the phone chimed. Dana washed her hands, took half a tablet with another cup of tea, and went back to her soup.

Assistant: A post can't go to just one person, but I can send the photo to her in a private message. Would you like that?
Person: Oh yes, that is better.
Assistant: Done. I sent the photo of the shelf to your sister in a private message.

Priya got home after a night shift, tired and in a sour mood. She dropped her motorcycle helmet by the door and spoke to the assistant. 'Pause the wifi on the kids' tablets until noon.' She yawned. 'No wait, make it two o'clock. I want to sleep until then.' The assistant understood that she had changed the time. It paused the internet on the two tablets and said, 'The tablets are paused. I will resume the connection at two o'clock.' Priya said thank you, closed the curtains and went to bed.

A bill is a note from a company that says how much you owe for things like electricity, water or rent, and by what day you must pay. That day is called the due date. People often change how or when they pay. They say pay the electric bill on the first, move the rent reminder to Friday, or remind me three days before it is due. Many people set up automatic payments, which is perfect for anyone who forgets. If a bank card is locked, you may need to unlock it before a payment goes through. Some people still keep paper bills in a box by the door, next to a jacket.

Someone wants to see how much electricity the house used this month.
How much power have we used so far?
Show my electricity use.
Did we use more or less than last month?
What does the meter say?
Does this month's bill still fit under fifty dollars?
Is the house using half as much power as it did in winter?
Tell me how often the heater has been running, please.

A table booking is a way to tell a restaurant that you are coming, so a seat is ready for you. You give a name, a day, a time and how many people will eat. Most people change a booking at least once. They say make it for four instead of two, move it to eight o'clock, or cancel my table. Restaurants usually hold a table for about fifteen minutes, so people watch the clock. On a cloudy day some places close their outdoor seats, and some hide the full menu until you ask, so it helps to say if you want to sit inside or outside.

Someone wants the alarm turned on because they are leaving the house.
I'm heading out.

Lock the place up for me.

I will return at nine, so please keep the alarm on until then.
We're off on holiday, and I want to know the house is protected.
Please switch on the alarm. I have the weight of the whole week on me and I don't want to worry about the doors.
The last one out should turn on the sensors.

Mrs. Quill, a retired teacher, had to pick up some medicine from a pharmacy across town. She worried about the traffic. 'How long will it take to drive to the pharmacy on Elm Street?' she asked her phone. 'And is that faster than going by the river road?' The assistant understood that she wanted the drive time and a comparison of two routes. It said the main road would take twenty minutes, five minutes less than the river road. Mrs. Quill chose the main road. At the final turn the assistant told her to go left, and she arrived with time to spare.

Leo, a teenager, was texting his friends while a bowl of cookie dough sat on the counter. He said to the kitchen assistant, 'Preheat the oven to 200 so I can bake these.' A moment later he added, 'sry i mean 180, 200 is too hot.' The assistant understood that he had fixed the number. It changed the oven from 200 to 180 degrees and said, 'The oven is heating to 180. I will tell you when it is ready.' Leo put a note on the calendar on his phone about his mom's birthday on Sunday, and soon the oven beeped.

Mrs. Hale, a retired teacher, sat in her dim living room with her phone beside her. An alert buzzed on the table. It was a missed call from her cousin Ben. She picked up the phone and said, 'Call Ben.' The assistant understood that she wanted to ring her cousin back. It found Ben in her contacts and started the call. After a few rings he answered, and they talked for half an hour about the garden. When they were done, Mrs. Hale said, 'Hang up,' and the assistant ended the call.

Double the recipe.

When you shop, sizes tell you if something will fit. Clothes have small, medium and large, and furniture is measured in centimeters, like how wide a table is. When you order something online, it has to travel from a shop to your home, which can take a few days. People change things about an order all the time. They say send it to my work, make it a size bigger, or return this one. Some shops set a maximum number of days for a return, so people ask when is the last day to send it back. Delivery apps show where your package is.

It should be heard from the street, even from the cinema next door.

Set the siren to the top level.

Units are the names we give to measurements. We use them for lengths, weights and temperatures. A tv is measured in inches, a train goes sixty miles an hour, and a bag of raw flour weighs a kilogram. Different places use different units, so people often need to change from one to another. They say how many ounces are in a cup, how far is ten miles in kilometers, or what is twenty degrees Celsius in Fahrenheit. This matters most when you cook or travel. A recipe from another country may use grams, while your scale shows ounces.

Assistant: Locking the front door now, and opening the left garage door. Do you know if you want it open all day?

Assistant: I will close it in ten minutes.

When a pet goes missing, neighbours often help each other. A lost pet notice is simple. You type the pet's name, what it looks like, where it was last seen and a phone number. Then you send it to the neighbourhood group or put it on a local board. People change the notice when they have news. They say add a photo, change the number, or take it down because he's home. Children often help look and may even scrape a knee while running around the park. When the pet is found, a short message to say thank you means a lot.

Sam, a driver, was on a break in the silent parking lot behind the depot. The team had said the wifi was slow again. 'Scan the network and tell me which devices are on it,' he said to his phone. 'I don't want to change any passwords or reset anything. I just want to know who is connected.' The assistant understood that he wanted a list of devices and no changes. It scanned the wifi and said there were nine devices, including two phones and a printer it didn't know. Sam thanked it, wrote the names down and told the team.

Person: Oh, of course. Please post it, then.

Ana, an office worker, sat down in the dim office on a Monday morning and her nose began to itch. The highway outside was busy and the air smelled like smoke. She began to speak to her assistant. 'Turn on the air purifier and close the window by my desk,' she said, 'because I can't breathe well.' The assistant understood that she wanted two things in one go. It switched on the purifier at a medium speed and shut the smart window beside her desk. Then it said, 'The purifier is running. I closed the window.' After a few minutes the air felt fresh and Ana began her work.

Mia, a student, wanted a quiet place to study before her exams. She spoke to her phone while she packed her black jacket. 'Book me a room at the Lakeside Hotel for two nights, starting Friday.' She stopped and then said, 'Sorry, three nights, I want to stay until Monday.' The assistant understood that she had fixed the length of the stay. It changed the booking to three nights, from Friday to Monday, and told her the check-in time was three o'clock. Mia said thanks and zipped up her bag.

Tom, a driver, waited outside the airport with a pot of hot coffee in the cup holder. His sister was flying in from far away. 'When does Flight 482 land?' he asked his phone. 'Is it late?' The assistant understood that he wanted the arrival time and any delay. It said, 'Flight 482 is delayed by twenty-five minutes and will land at ten past six.' Tom finished his coffee, said thanks, and moved the car to the waiting area. He asked the assistant to alert him when the plane had landed, and it did.

Mrs. Ellis, a retired teacher, sat at her kitchen table with a cart of groceries still unpacked by the door. She felt scared of making a mistake with her money. 'Excuse me,' she said to her phone, 'could you kindly move fifty dollars from my savings account to my checking account? I need to pull some cash out later to pay the gardener, and I would like to be sure it is there.' The assistant understood that she wanted a transfer between her own accounts. It moved fifty dollars and said her checking account now held two hundred and ten dollars. Mrs. Ellis smiled and unpacked the cart.

Assistant: No, I can't move boxes. Please put them aside before seven.

Jun, an office worker, stood in the loud lobby of her building, a parcel under her arm. She had designed the poster for a film night at the cinema across the road, and now she had to mail the prints. She said to her phone, 'I'm all out of stamps and this parcel needs to go today.' The assistant understood that she needed a place to buy stamps and send a parcel. It found the post office two streets away, told her it closed at five thirty, and showed the way. Jun thanked it and set off.

This is top priority for me, so could you please ask the clinic to find a slot closer to today?
Let my family group know that I am going in earlier.

Noor had just woken up and her eyes were still half closed. 'Tell me my balance and email me last month's statement,' she mumbled to her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted two things at once. It said her main account had three hundred and forty dollars. Then it sent an email with the statement to her address. 'Do you want me to tag the big rent payment so you can find it later?' it asked. Noor smiled. Her savings were still far from her goal, but she was glad to see the number. She said yes and went to make breakfast.

A birthday is a day each year when people celebrate being born. Friends and family give cards and gifts, and many people blow out candles on a cake, even when the wind comes in through the window. A good gift is something the person likes, and many people set a minimum and a maximum price. People use an assistant to remember dates and to find ideas. They say save the date of Dad's birthday, remind me a week before, or suggest a gift for a ten-year-old who likes drawing. Some change the date, saying move the party to Saturday.

name: scan_front_door_camera
does: Looks at the front door camera and tells you what or who is there.
inputs: which camera, and how far back in time to look
people say:
- Who is at the door?
- Is there a package on the step?
- Check the top of the stairs camera for me
- Any idea who rang the bell ten minutes ago?
- Has anyone been on the porch since lunch?

Mr. Ferris, a retired teacher, was careful about locking up at night. He sat down with a document from the alarm company beside his tea and spoke to the smart lock. 'Lock the front door every night at ten, starting tomorrow at seven in the evening,' he said, 'and increase the volume on the doorbell, please. I can't hear it from the garden.' The assistant understood that he wanted a nightly lock time and a louder bell. It set the door to lock at ten each night and turned the doorbell volume up by two steps. Then it read the plan back to him.

A flight is a trip by plane, and a flight time is the hour it leaves or lands. At the airport, a board shows each flight, its gate and whether it is on time or delayed. Gates can change, so people check often. Someone running late might jog to the gate. When they get on the plane they take a deep breath and relax. People ask for changes or news in simple words, like is my plane late, which gate is it, or tell me when it lands. If a family member is waiting at home, they ask the same thing.

Person: whats for dinner this week
Assistant: I can make a plan. Do you want five dinners or seven?
Person: 5. no wait, 6, my brother's home sunday
Assistant: Six dinners. Any food you don't eat?
Person: no fish. its snowy and cold so soup is good
Assistant: Great. I will put soup on two nights, and add pasta, rice and chicken. Should I also make a shopping list?
Person: yes, and tell me when the oven is done on tuesday. i walk in at six
Assistant: I can't read the oven sensor from here, but I can remind you at six. Shall I do that?
Person: ok

On a hot day, a fan or an air conditioner helps keep a room cool. The fan moves the air around, and the air conditioner takes the heat out of it. Most people set a number for the room, and an average choice is about twenty-two degrees. They change it with simple words, like make it cooler, turn it down two degrees, or let the fan run all night. Some people say it is too stuffy when they want fresh air. On Thursday evenings, when the heat peaks, many people start the cooling early so the room is ready when they get home.

Mrs. Wells is not good with technology, so she did not know how to book a taxi. She was staying inside because of the rain. 'I need a car to the dentist tomorrow at seven in the morning,' she said to her phone. 'And I have to print the form first, so please make it early enough.' The assistant understood she needed a ride at seven tomorrow. It booked a taxi to pick her up at her front door and said the driver would round the corner at five to seven. Mrs. Wells printed the form on her old printer and put it in her bag.

Someone wants a bike route that is about twenty-five kilometres long.
Plan a ride that is around twenty-five kilometres.
I want to ride for about an hour and a half.
Show me a loop that gets me back home after a good long ride.
I hate hills, so keep it flat, and about the same length as last Saturday.
It's a crispy cold morning and I want a ride that fills the time before lunch.
Give me a number of kilometres that is not too short and not too long.
Could you please suggest a route of about twenty-five kilometres? I want to get ready for the charity ride next month.

In many homes, children have rules about screen time, which means how long they can use a tablet or a tv. Some digital tools help parents set limits. A parent might say stop the tablet at six, give her ten more minutes, or only allow homework apps until dinner. When the time is up, the screen goes dark, and the child can move on to a game or a bedtime story. Parents also change chores and school runs. They say move the pickup to four o'clock, remind Sam about the trash, or tell me when homework is done.

Rosa came home from the hospital at seven in the morning. The flat was cold, and the bucket by the door held a thin skin of ice from the leaky window she kept meaning to fix. Her fingers felt ready to freeze. She dropped her bag and said, "Make the living room warmer, please. Twenty-five degrees would be nice." The assistant understood that she wanted the heating turned up, so it set the living room thermostat to twenty-five. It told her the radiator near the sofa would take about ten minutes to get warm. Rosa thanked it, sat down in her coat, and waited. Soon the room felt soft and cozy, and she fell asleep before her tea was ready.

name: restart_printer
does: Turns a stuck or silent printer off and on again so it can print.
inputs: which printer to restart, and the minimum number of seconds to wait before it comes back on
people say:
- the printer is frozen again
- turn my printer off and on
- nothing comes out when I press print
- it jammed, I pulled the paper out with a glove on, and now it will not answer
- give the printer a fresh start

They want to know when their plane takes off.
When do I fly?
Plane time?
Hey, when does my flight go tomorrow at seven or is that just the gate time?
Can you check what time my flight over the sea leaves?
I'm upstairs packing, so tell me when I have to be at the airport.
I can't stream the airport board from here, so what time is boarding?
Please tell me the departure time for my flight, because I want to leave home early.
Is my plane still set for tomorrow at seven, or did that change?
Which hour does my flight leave on Friday?

Person: I have to hurry. Move some money to my savings account.
Assistant: Sure. How much would you like to move?
Person: Fifty dollars. No wait, make it sixty.
Assistant: Sixty dollars, from checking to savings. Is that right?
Person: Yes. My daughter is sick and I have to get her to the doctor. I even left my tea on the table.
Assistant: Done. Sixty dollars is now in your savings. I hope she feels better soon.
Person: Thanks.

Leo was eight, and the family speaker sat on the kitchen shelf. His sister said it was rude to shout at it, so Leo pulled a chair close and spoke softly. "Please make the music quieter and tell me what you can do," he said. The speaker understood two things. First, it lowered the volume from eight to four. Then it listed a few of its jobs: playing songs, setting timers, telling the weather, and joining the other speaker in the hall. Leo liked the list. He asked it to play the same song in the hall too, and the speaker linked the two together. Soon the whole family could hear the song, and Leo danced across the kitchen.

They want to know what to do for a small burn.
Burn help
My hand touched a hot pan, what now?
How do I treat a burn?
I got an ugly red mark from the oven at the cafe, what should I do?
What helps a burn on my arm?
We were snowed in and I burned my hand on the stove, so tell me what to do first.
Do I put cold water on a burn?
Is a burn like this bad enough that I should call for help?

When a family moves house, the address changes, and many other things have to change with it. People tell the post office, the bank and the power company where they live now. A grandfather may need help with this, and younger relatives often welcome the job. Packing is work too. Heavy boxes can be dangerous to carry, so people write the room on each box and let the movers lift them. To ask for changes, people say things like change my address, move my power to the new house, or tell my bank I live somewhere new. A phone can also remind them to book the movers for Saturday, so the big day goes smoothly.

They want to skip the song that is playing.
Skip.
Next one.
I don't like this song, play something else.
Not this one, please.
My ears are sore from this loud track, so change it.
This slow song drips like a tap, and I don't want it, so next please.
I was cooking rice and this song is ruining it, can you skip ahead?
Could you please play the next song? I do not want to hear this one anymore.

Ana had just moved to a big city, and the air in her small flat felt heavy. A yellow dust sat on the window sill. She stretched her arms, yawned, and said to her phone, "The air in here smells stale. Can you run the purifier for twenty-five minutes?" The phone understood that she wanted cleaner air, so it turned on the purifier in the bedroom and set a timer for twenty-five minutes. It also told her that the filter was almost full and she should change it soon. Ana thanked the phone and opened the window a little to let in fresh air too. When the timer ended, the purifier turned itself off and the room smelled much better.

A smart bulb is a light you can change without touching the switch. People use lights to read, to cook, to relax, or to sleep. Most bulbs can be brighter or dimmer, and some can change colour from warm yellow to cool white. When someone is sick in bed, a soft light is easier on the eyes. To change a light, people say make it brighter, turn it down a little, or I want a warmer colour. They can also say turn the lamp off in ten minutes, and the lamp counts the minutes by itself and switches off when the time is up.

Person: Radio on.
Assistant: Which station should I play?
Person: The one with the morning news.
Assistant: There are two news stations here. Do you want the city one or the national one?
Person: The city one. I tried to swipe through the stations on my tablet, but it is difficult when I am this tired.
Assistant: No problem. I will play the city news. Would you like it quiet?
Person: Yes, a bit lower, please.
Assistant: Done. The volume is lower now.

Walt was getting ready for the winter holiday. He sat in his chair with his tablet and said, "Remind me to hang the lights on Saturday. Oh, no, I mean Sunday. The grandchildren come on Saturday." The assistant understood the correction, dropped Saturday, and set the reminder for Sunday morning. Then Walt asked it to disconnect the old speaker in the living room so the new one could play holiday songs. The assistant did that and started a song on the new speaker. Walt looked at the empty box where the lights used to live and smiled. He told the assistant to put a note on his list: read one chapter of the holiday book to the children on Saturday night. The assistant saved the note.

A notes app is a place to write down things you do not want to forget. You can type a note, or you can talk and let the phone write it for you, which is called a voice note. A shopping list, a sore knee you want to tell the doctor about, or how many miles you walked can all go in a note. Later, you can search for a word to find an old note. People say write this down, make a note about the trip, find my note about the doctor, put this in my shopping note, or delete the last note.

name: move_blinds
does: Moves blinds, curtains or shutters to the place you ask for, such as fully open, half open or closed.
inputs: which window or room, and how far to open it, like a regular half-open setting
people say:
- the sun is in my eyes
- let some light into the bedroom
- I put the kettle on and want the kitchen curtains closed for privacy
- open the living room curtains so I can show my guests the garden
- put the shutters on the regular night setting

A to-do list is a short list of jobs you want to finish. It helps you remember things and see what is left. Next to each job there is a small square, and you tick it when the job is done. Jobs can be small, like fix the dripping tap, or bigger, like buy a kilogram of rice and cook dinner. People change the list all the time. They say put this one first, move it to tomorrow, tick off the laundry, or take that job off my list. Some jobs matter more than others, so people also ask what is most important today.

name: show_due_homework
does: Lists the homework and projects that are due soon, with the earliest one first.
inputs: the school subject, if there is one, and how many days ahead to look
people say:
- what homework do I have
- anything due tomorrow
- I have an ugly pile of maths sheets, which one is due first
- what do I have to hand in this week
- lock in my science project, when is it due
- will there be time to study in the sunshine this weekend or is too much due

Tom wore his coat all morning because the office was cold. Only the desks by the door felt warm, and the cold air seemed to divide the room into a warm half and a cold half. He took off his cap, rubbed his hands, and said, "The heating is not working well. Please make the office twenty-two degrees." The assistant understood that Tom wanted the room warmer, so it raised the thermostat from eighteen to twenty-two. It told him the change would take about twenty minutes. Tom thanked it and went back to his emails. By lunch time, the whole office felt comfortable, and he finally hung his coat on the chair.

Mrs. Dara opened her bookshop at nine. A student who worked on weekends was shivering behind the till. "Turn on the heater by the door and set the shop to twenty degrees," said Mrs. Dara, still holding her keys. The assistant understood two jobs in one sentence. It switched on the heater, and it set the thermostat to twenty. It read the label on the thermostat to check that the number was correct, and said the shop would be warm in about fifteen minutes. The student smiled and put the kettle on. By ten o'clock, the first customers had taken off their scarves and started looking at the shelves.

Person: I want to go to the beach after my shift. Will the water be warm enough?
Assistant: Which beach are you going to?
Person: Sandy Cove. My husband says it was colder yesterday.
Assistant: Today the water at Sandy Cove is about two degrees warmer than yesterday. The tide will shift around five, so the water gets deeper later.
Person: Good. I burn fast, so I need more sun cream than last time. My nose was crispy.
Assistant: I can't buy sun cream for you, but I can put it on your shopping list.
Person: Yes, please do that.

The kids had to practice piano before dinner, and Mara was stirring a pot with one hand. "Play something quick and happy, and turn it up a little," she said to the speaker. The speaker understood two requests in one sentence. It picked a cheerful playlist with fast songs, and it raised the volume from four to five. Her youngest asked what the name of the song was. Mara did not know the answer, so she asked the speaker. It told her the title and the singer. The kids laughed, finished their piano, and ate dinner while the music played.

A video meeting lets people at work talk and see each other from different places. Before it starts, you open the link you were sent. Once you are in, you can mute yourself, turn your camera on, or share your screen so others can see your slides. An agenda is a short list of what the meeting will talk about, and people often post it in the chat. Sometimes a person has a picture of a butterfly or a beach behind them. To ask for these things, people say join my meeting, share my screen, mute me, or show me the agenda.

Mr. Green was a retired teacher, and on Thursdays he looked after his granddaughter. She stood by the door, where her boots stood in a row, and he said to the phone, "Could you please tell me when her spelling test is? I want to have her practice a little each day so she feels ready, and I would like to pair the hard words with easy ones." The phone understood that he wanted the date of the test and a plan for studying. It said the test was on Friday, and it set a reminder for four o'clock each afternoon. Mr. Green wrote the word list on the fridge. His granddaughter put on her boots and ran outside, ready for the walk.

name: find_radio_station

- put on the news
