- is this the correct station for traffic reports
- what station plays the football game tonight

They want a reminder to do something at a certain time.
remind me
remind me to buy a carrot cake on the way hmoe
Don't let me forget the meeting.
I've had a rough week, so please nudge me to take out the trash tonight.
Ping me at noon to water the plants so they grow.
Set a reminder to pick up the kids at three thirty.
Could you kindly remind me tomorrow morning to call the dentist?

Mr. Ortiz opened his shop early on a Monday. The huge room felt empty, and the only sound was the fridge humming. He was typing the first receipt of the day when he sighed and said, "It's so quiet in here." The assistant understood that he did not want to ask for anything in particular, but it guessed he wanted some company. It turned on the radio in the shop and tuned in to the local news and music station he liked. Then it set the volume low, at the height he usually kept it, so the customers could still talk. Mr. Ortiz nodded and kept typing, and soon he was humming along.

They want money back for an order.
Refund please.
I want my money back for the food box.
This order is urgent to fix, I spent forty dollars and half of it was broken.
Can I get half of the money back? The cups came smashed.
The wrong thing arrived, so I would like to return it.
How do I get a refund? I paid more than I should have.
Could you please help me send the parcel back and get my money, because the food was spoiled?

They want to know what to buy at the shop.
What do we need?
Check the list.
Tell me what's missing, I don't want to open every cupboard.
I don't need the whole list, just the things we ran out of.
Keep it neat and short, only what is gone from the fridge.
What is running low? It would make me smile to skip checking the floor of the pantry.
Could you please tell me what to buy, but don't include things I bought last week?

They want a workout plan for tomorrow.
Workout tomorrow?
What should I do at the gym tomorrow at seven?
Give me a plan for tomorrow morning.
I want to dig into some squats tomorrow at six, what sets should I do?
What exercises are good for keeping my back straight, for tomorrow after work?
After I wash the pan tonight, I will plan a workout, so what should I do on Thursday?
Could you please tell me what exercises I should do tomorrow at seven, and how many sets?

Person: Open my recipe file and make the text bigger.
Assistant: Which file? You have two, one for bread and one for cake.
Person: The cake one. I want to bake it tonight and it needs a cup of sugar, but the words are too small.
Assistant: Done. The cake file is open and the text is larger.
Person: Great. Can you also turn the oven up high?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't control your oven from the computer. You will need to do that yourself.
Person: No problem, I'll do it.

They want a haircut booked.
I need a haircut.
Book a haircut for Tuesday and tell me what time the salon closes.
My girl needs a trim, so find a time on Saturday and tell me how long it takes.
After the flood on our street I haven't had time for a cut, so find me a slot this week and check if they're open late.
Can you reserve a kind of early slot at the barber and send me the address?
Please find a free time for a haircut tomorrow and remind me an hour before.

Sam lay in bed with the blanket up to his chin. He looked at the window and saw frost on the glass. "It's freezing out there, and I have to leave in ten minutes," he mumbled to his phone. The assistant understood that he did not want a cold car, so it started the car and turned on the heater and the window warmer. A sudden beep told Sam it was working. The phone also said that the fuel was at a fraction of a tank, about a quarter, so he should stop for gas on the way. Sam sighed, got up, and found his shoes.

They want a table at a restaurant for tonight.
Table for two?
We're starving and there's no food at home.
Find me a place for dinner with a view of the sea.
I can't weigh all these menus, just book somewhere good at the bottom of the hill.
It's date night and we haven't decided where to eat.
Is there somewhere quiet to eat around seven?
Could you please find a restaurant near me with a free table for four, because my family is hungry?

Ben had just moved to the city and wanted to cook soup for four friends. His recipe made eight bowls. He stood in the tiny kitchen and said, "Make this recipe for four, and don't give me cups, because I only have a scale." The assistant understood that he wanted half the amounts in grams. It cut every number in half and wrote them in grams, not cups. It said the maximum he could cook in his small pot was about six bowls, so four would fit. Ben put a plate under the pot to catch drips, and he let the soup simmer. His friends said it was the best soup they had eaten in months.

name: sleep_timer
does: Plays quiet music or sounds and stops them after a set time.
inputs: the kind of sound, like rain or soft songs, and how long it should play
people say:
- stop the music when I fall asleep
- play quiet rain, nothing loud
- put on something calm for the baby until he sleeps
- I'm on a ladder painting, turn the music off in half an hour
- help me sleep with a slow song

Mrs. Lee, a retired teacher, sat at the kitchen table with a pile of bills. She said to her tablet, "Tell me how much I have spent this month, and remind me to pay the electric bill tomorrow at noon." The assistant added up her spending and said it was nine hundred dollars, with the largest part going to her grandson's drum lessons. It then set a reminder for tomorrow at noon. Mrs. Lee frowned at first, but then she smiled. "It's true," she said, "he plays very well, and I like to pay for it." She put the bills into a neat stack and went to make some tea.

A mailbox is a small box where letters and parcels are left for you. Many hang on a wall or a gate with a few screws. Letters fit inside, but a larger parcel may need a signature, so the delivery person might ask you to swipe the screen of their phone with your finger. If nobody is home, they leave a card and try again, or they take the parcel to a shop nearby. People change when and where things arrive. They say hold my mail while I'm away, send it to my work, or leave it with the neighbour. The mailbox should be open and empty on the day you expect something.

Nina stood in the hall with a basket of laundry and a baby asleep in the next room. "Could you please read me the new message from my cousin? My hands are full, and I want to keep it quiet because the baby is sleeping," she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted the text read aloud in a soft voice. It dimmed the screen, turned the volume down, and read the message. Her cousin asked if Nina wanted strong coffee or tea on Saturday. Nina asked the phone to reply that she would like coffee, and the phone sent the text.

Cooling a room means taking away heat so people feel comfortable. An air conditioner does this, and a fan moves the air around so it feels fresher. Many are connected to a phone, so people can change them from the sofa. Some old fans and cooling units have a printed document with instructions, but most things now have a simple app. To make changes, people say it is too hot in here, make it cooler, set it to twenty-four, turn on the fan, or turn it off at midnight. A cool room helps people sleep and keeps food and pets from getting too warm.

A camping trip needs a plan for the weather, the trail and what to pack. People bring a tent, a warm jacket and a map, and they keep small things like keys in a pocket. A yellow rain coat is easy to see if the hills turn misty. Before they go, people check the forecast. They often text a friend where they will walk and when they plan to be back. To ask for these things, people say what is the weather on the hill tomorrow, make me a packing list for two nights, or send my friend a message that I will be back by six.

Priya stood at the bus stop with a stroller and two bags. She said to her phone, "I don't want a bus with a change, and I need a ticket for me and my son." The phone asked her to spell the name of the stop she wanted. She spelled it out, and the phone said that was the correct stop. It found a bus that went straight there, leaving in eight minutes. It also showed the price of a ticket for one adult and one child. Priya paid with her phone, and the bus pulled in right on time.

They want the house alarm to turn on later.
Alarm on tonight.
Turn on the alarm tomorrow at seven when we leave.
Arm the house at ten tonight, I'm going to bed.
I keep forgetting, so can you start the alarm every day when the sky gets dark?
Wait until the kids are out the door tomorrow morning, then lock everything up.
What if I get it wrong? Please set the alarm for eleven tonight and tell me if a door is open.
Could you switch on the cameras and the alarm at nine on Friday, because we're travelling?

Chef Ana was planning meals for the week. She dimmed the light over her stove, sat down, and said to her phone, "Plan five dinners that use half as much meat as last week, and nothing too spicy." The assistant understood that she wanted less meat in each meal. It made a list of five dinners, with beans, eggs and vegetables in place of some meat. Ana asked it to make Tuesday's meal red, with tomatoes and peppers, and it did. Then it gave her a shopping list. She made a quick call to her friend to share the plan, and she felt proud of the week.

Mr. Hughes did not like new phones, but his granddaughter had set one up for him. He held it with both hands and said, "Could you please call my daughter? I would like to tell her I saw a huge spider in the shed, and I want to practice using the speaker so I can keep my hands free." The phone understood that he wanted to call his daughter and talk on speakerphone. It called her and turned on the speaker. His daughter answered, and Mr. Hughes was so excited that he laughed. He told her about the spider while he sat comfortably with the phone on his knee.

Person: Play some music for the garden.
Assistant: What kind of music would you like?
Person: Something slow with a deep sound.
Assistant: I can play slow songs with deep drums. How long should I play them?
Person: Twenty minutes. And can you tell me the difference between jazz and blues?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can only play music, not explain it. I can play one song of each if you want to hear the difference.
Person: Good idea. Do that, and close the music when I say stop.
Assistant: I will.

Grandma Rose had been sick for a week, and her daughter lived far away. She sat by the window with her phone and said, "Could you please set my pills for eight each morning and eight each night, because I forget them when I feel tired? And please make the writing larger, as the size is too small for my eyes." The assistant understood that she wanted pill reminders and bigger text. It set two reminders and made the letters larger. Then it offered to filter her calls so only family would ring through. Rose said yes, and she felt calm.

They want a lamp to turn on while they are away.
Lamp on
Lights on at dusk
I'm away until Friday, so tell the hall light to come on at dusk.
Make it look like someone is home tonight.
Could you put the living room lamp on a schedule, from seven to eleven?
Tell the lights to go on when it gets dark, please.
Please turn the porch light on every evening this week, because I'm away from home.

Person: Add a new contact for Dan.
Assistant: Sure. What is Dan's phone number?
Person: He lives at number twenty-five Oak Street. I'll find the phone number in a minute, my hands are wet from the garden.
Assistant: I saved Dan with the address twenty-five Oak Street. I will wait for the phone number.
Person: The text size on my screen is small, I can't read the number. Can you unmute the phone first?
Assistant: I've unmuted it. I can also make the text larger if you'd like.
Person: Yes, please.

Mrs. Moreno stood among the roses with her phone in her hand. "Could you please take a picture of this rose and share it with my sister, because it won a prize at the garden show and she will want to see it?" she asked. The phone understood that she wanted a photo taken and sent. It took the picture and showed her the result. The rose looked tiny in the frame, so Mrs. Moreno stepped closer, near a peeling branch. The phone took a second picture, and she liked it better. It sent that one to her sister, and a happy reply came back within a minute.

Person: Start a timer for the bread and increase the oven heat.
Assistant: How long should the timer be? And how much hotter do you want the oven?
Person: Thirty-five minutes. Make it twenty degrees hotter.
Assistant: I can set the timer. I'm sorry, I can't change the oven, but I can remind you to turn it up.
Person: Okay, remind me. I'm tired after my night shift. Also, play a podcast while I wait.
Assistant: Timer set for thirty-five minutes. Which podcast would you like?
Person: Anything temporary for the kitchen, the news is fine.
Assistant: Playing the news podcast now.

Mei had just moved to the city with her new baby. At night she felt unsure, and she said to her phone, "Tell me when the baby's next feeding is, and turn on the baby monitor." The assistant understood two requests in one sentence. It looked at the feeding log and said the next one was at two in the morning. Then it switched on the monitor in the nursery. Mei noticed that the baby's skin looked a little red, and she asked what could happen if it did not go away. The assistant said that it was only a guess, and it suggested she ask a doctor in the morning.

Leo felt sick, so he stayed in bed with his phone. He wondered if he could still send a letter to his aunt in Spain that day. First he typed two words: post office. The assistant understood he wanted the nearest post office and told him it was ten minutes away and closed at five. Then Leo typed three words: stamp price Spain. The assistant said a letter to Spain cost about two euros. Leo wrote back: bank open? The assistant checked and said the bank near the post office closed at four thirty. Leo sighed. He asked his big sister to go for him, and the assistant set a reminder for her to leave at three. Leo put the phone down and fell asleep.

Booking a haircut or a dentist visit means picking a day and a time the shop has free. The booking is there so you and the shop both know when you will arrive. People often change a booking. They move it to another day, make it earlier, or cancel it. They say things like, can you push my haircut to Friday, or I can't come on Monday, please cancel. Opening hours matter too, because it is true that no shop can take you when it is closed. So people ask, when do you open on Saturday? If you come by car, ask where to park. Some waiting rooms even have a small purifier to keep the air fresh while you wait.

Omar drove a delivery van all day, and by evening his ears were tired of engine noise. He sat down by the dryer, waiting for his socks, and spoke to the smart speaker on the shelf. Search for something funny to listen to, but not the news and not music, he said. The assistant understood that he wanted a comedy show with talking only. It found a short funny podcast about a cat that ran a shop, and it started playing it. After a minute Omar said, not so loud, please. The speaker turned the volume down from seven to four. Omar laughed at the cat joke and listened until the dryer buzzed.

Headlines are the short lines at the top of news stories. They tell you in a few words what happened, so you can decide what to read. A news app or a smart speaker can read them out each morning. People change the topic a lot. They say, give me sports instead, or only local news please, or fewer stories today. Local news might tell you that a truck broke down on the main road, or that a new bakery is selling a delicious pie. Some people like calm news, so they ask for good news only and chill with a cup of tea. You can stop the headlines at any time by saying, that's enough.

Person: Hello, can you get a room for me and my mom?
Assistant: Yes, I can help. Which night do you want to stay?
Person: We get there tomorrow at seven.
Assistant: Good. How many nights will you stay?
Person: Two nights. Mom says the room must be warm. Can you heat it before we come?
Assistant: I can't control the heat in the room, but I can ask the hotel to turn it on. Is that okay?
Person: Yes please. And does it have a network for the tablet?
Assistant: Yes, the hotel has a free wifi network. Breakfast is healthy and starts at eight.
Person: Great, thank you!

Rosa came home after a night shift at the hospital. She was tired, but she wanted to work on a hand painted invitation for her sister's party. She said to her phone, find me a good painting class this Tuesday. The assistant found a class at six in the evening. Rosa thought about it and said, no wait, Wednesday, I work Tuesday. The assistant understood she wanted to change the day, so it looked again and found a Wednesday class at the same time. Then Rosa asked it to reduce the brightness of her screen so it would not hurt her eyes. The assistant did that and saved the class in her calendar. Rosa smiled and went to bed.

name: spell_word
does: Shows the correct spelling of a single word and says it out loud, one letter at a time.
inputs: the word, and the language if it is not English
people say:
- How do I write hat in Spanish?
- How do you spell paint in French?
- Spell that last word for me, slowly.
- I always get this one wrong, can you check it?
- What letters are in the French word for apple?

Nina was late. She grabbed a plate of toast, and zoomed around the kitchen looking for her keys. The train station was twenty-five minutes away, and she was going to meet a friend from Paris. At the open door she shouted to her phone, how do I say where is the train station in French? The assistant understood she needed a short phrase to say out loud. It answered with the French words and said them slowly so she could hear them. Nina repeated them twice. Then she said, save that for later, and the assistant put the phrase in her notes. Nina ate her toast on the walk and ran for the train.

Sam drove a bus in the early shift, and he got home in the afternoon with a bad headache. The sun came right through the living room window. His mother was resting in the next room, so he did not want to shout. He grabbed his phone and typed in a hurry: close the blnds a bit. The assistant understood that he meant the blinds in the living room and that he wanted them only partly closed. It lowered them about halfway and told him so. Sam felt better. When his mother answered a call from his aunt in the other room, he asked the assistant to open the blinds in her room for fresh air. It did that too.

Maria was a cook, and she had a long day at the restaurant ahead. In the morning she told the smart garden helper, run the sprinklers for ten minutes. The assistant said okay and got ready to start. Then Maria looked at the grass. It was October, and the lawn was not very dry. No wait, make it five minutes, she said. The assistant understood that she had changed her mind, so it set the time to five minutes and said it would only water the inside part of the lawn, near the house. Maria welcomed the shorter time. She also asked it to stop the sprinklers when it started to rain, and the assistant said it would.

Person: I want to put my pancake breakfast on the calendar.
Assistant: Sure. What day and what time?
Person: Oh, I don't know how you say it. Tomorrow at nine, I think.
Assistant: Tomorrow at nine in the morning. Who is coming?
Person: Just my neighbor. Is it true you can send her a note?
Assistant: I can't send notes, but I can set a reminder for you to call her. Would that help?
Person: Yes, that is good. And a reminder to slice the fruit.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you tomorrow at eight to slice the fruit.

Mina had just moved to the city, and her phone battery was always low. One evening she said, my battery is almost dead and I'm far from home, where is a charging spot near me? The assistant understood she needed a place to charge. It found a cafe two streets away and told her the way. Then Mina said, also turn on do not disturb tomorrow at seven, because she wanted a quiet morning. The assistant set it for seven in the morning. She was carrying her guitar, so she could not type. She asked the assistant to dim the screen, and it did. At the cafe she fed her phone to the charger and ordered a tea.

Tom was a gardener, and he wore grey gloves all day. In his lunch break he sat on a bench and spoke to his phone. Show me only the unread emails, he said. The assistant understood that he wanted to skip the old ones, so it listed just five unread emails. One of them said a package was on its way, but the sender wanted to push the date back. Tom said, read that one, and the assistant read it out loud. Then he said, tell Dana the package will come half an hour later, and the assistant wrote a short email to Dana and asked, shall I send it? Tom said yes. The assistant sent the email, and Tom went back to his roses.

Person: I need to order an iron.
Assistant: Okay. Do you want a small travel iron or a big one for home?
Person: A travel one. I sleep in my truck a few nights a week and my shirts get wrinkled.
Assistant: Good idea. Where should I send it?
Person: I don't have a house address. Can you send it to my work?
Assistant: I can send it to a delivery locker or a shop near your work. Which one do you want?
Person: The locker is better. It has to come in twenty-five days at most, or I will finish my trip first.
Assistant: Delivery will take five days, so it will be early. I will order it now.

A water bill tells you how much water your home used and how much money you must pay. It comes once a month or every few months. The main body of the bill shows the amount, and the due date is near the top. People like to get their bills on time, so they stay calm and avoid late fees. When something changes, they use simple words. They say, move my due date to the first of the month, or send the bill by email instead of by post, or pay it every month by itself. If the amount looks too high, they say, why is it more than last time? A helper can find the answer or check the number for you.

Person: whats the watr temperature at the beach?
Assistant: I can look that up. Which beach do you mean?
Person: the big one near the pier, im new here
Assistant: Near the pier the water is about sixty-eight degrees today. It is a little cold.
Person: ok. is there a party there tonight?
Assistant: I don't know about parties. I can only tell you about the sun, the tides and the water.
Person: no problem. will i get cooked by the sun at noon?
Assistant: The sun is strong at noon today, so wear sun cream. Do you want a reminder to put it on?
Person: yes, and remind me to charge my phone

Going to the post office is a common errand. You walk through the door, take a number, and wait in line. It is for sending letters, picking up parcels and paying small bills. Waiting can hurt your feet, so many people ask for the quiet times. They say, when is it least busy? Others ask, is the post office open on Saturday? If you have an old parcel waiting for you, you might say, remind me to pick up my parcel on Friday. Some people want a different place, so they ask, where is the nearest pickup point? Then the helper finds a place and gives you the hours and the way.

name: ink_deal_helper
does: Looks for a discount on ink and paper that fit the user's printer and tells where to buy them.
inputs: the printer model, and what the person wants to buy
people say:
- My printer is out of black ink, and I'm in a hurry, what's the cheapest place?
- Is there a sale on paper this week?
- Find me a coupon for color cartridges.
- Write a polite note to the shop asking if they can match a lower price.
- I need ink for my old printer today, nothing too fancy.

A navigation app tells you how to get from one place to another and how long it will take. At night the app often shows quieter roads and fewer cars, so a trip may be faster. People can change the route as they drive. They say, avoid the highway, take the shortest way, or find a way with no tolls. They also ask, how long will it take if I leave at eight? Some drivers want to stay on big, well lit roads after dark. They say, use main roads only. When a driver gets hungry, they might say, find a tasty place to eat on the way. The app then changes the route and adds a short stop.

Traffic on a map is shown with colors. Green means the road is open, and purple or dark red means cars are moving very slowly. The map is there to help you pick the best road before you leave. When weather is bad, like heavy rain or lightning, roads get slow, and the map updates to show it. People who love a smooth trip ask for changes. They say, show me another way, or is there a faster road right now? If they are late, they say, how long until I get there? And if they want to leave early to miss the rush, they say, tell me the best time to go.

When you book a hotel room, you choose the day you arrive, the number of nights and the number of guests. The hotel keeps the room for you. Check-in is the time when you can get your key, and check-out is when you must leave. People often change a booking. They say, make it three nights instead of two, or add one more guest, or can we check in earlier? Some people want a room with a nice view, so they ask for a room that looks outside at the garden. Others ask about breakfast, and whether it has fresh bread and carrots in the salad. Guests who run in the morning can ask where the park is.

Ben woke up slowly, with blurry eyes. His phone was on the cold floor next to the bed, and he picked it up with a sleepy hand. The words on the screen looked too tiny to read, and a message from his boss said something about the notice board at work. Ben said, I can't see anything on this thing. The assistant understood that he did not mean the phone was broken, but that the text was too small. It made the letters bigger and asked, is this better? Ben said yes. Then the screen started to freeze for a second, so Ben asked the assistant to read the message to him out loud, and it did.

A step counter is a small tool in your phone or on your wrist. It counts every step you take and shows how far you have walked. People use it to make a daily goal, like eight thousand steps. They change things all the time. They say, set my goal to ten thousand, or show me how far I ran this week, or what was my pace today? If they stop the counter by mistake, they say, undo that. Many walkers like a quiet park or a calm road, so they also say, find me a quiet route for a short walk. The helper then picks a way and tells them the distance.

They want to know the Spanish word for grilled chicken.
What's chicken in Spanish?
Say grilled chicken in Spanish, please.
How would a waiter in Madrid call grilled chicken?
I need the exact word for it on a menu.
Tell me the Spanish for grilled chicken, and say it at half speed.
I have twenty-five seconds before I order, what do I say?
Could you please tell me the word, because I do not want to point at the picture again?
Spanish for grilled chicken, thanks.

Kofi had just moved to the city, and he wanted to find a team to cheer for. One cloudy Saturday, he made a cup of tea and asked his phone, who plays today? The assistant understood he wanted the matches in town. It told him two teams played at three, and a smaller game started at six. Kofi asked, which one has more fans? The assistant said the three o'clock game was twice as big. He said, okay, tell me when it starts, so the assistant set a reminder for half past two. Later he asked for the score. The assistant said it was one to zero, and Kofi cheered loudly in his kitchen.

An alarm wakes you up at a time you choose. A timer counts down from a time you pick, like ten minutes for pasta. People use alarms often, and sometimes more than one, because they can sleep through the first. They change them all the time. They say, wake me at six thirty instead of seven, or move my alarm one hour later, or turn off my Monday alarm. When a timer rings, people say, snooze for five minutes or add two more minutes. Some people say, set a timer so I don't pay the parking fee when my time runs out. Others set one before the beach, so they don't forget their sunglasses.

Priya owned a small shop, and a customer had asked her to deliver a box of tea across town. She was in a hurry, so she typed to her phone with one thumb: hwo long to drive to elm street. The assistant understood the typo and knew she meant the drive to Elm Street. It said the trip would take twenty minutes. Priya typed, skip the highway, there is a thin lane near it, and the assistant found a way with small roads that took twenty-five minutes. She did not like to climb stairs with heavy boxes, so she asked if there was parking near the building. The assistant found one two blocks away.

Jun was a student, and his friends were coming over for a small party in twenty minutes. The flat was too quiet and a bit sad. He said, it's so quiet in here. The assistant understood that he did not just describe the room, but that he wanted some music, so it played a happy playlist at a low volume. Jun saw dirty spots on the floor and had to mop quickly. He asked the assistant to set a ten minute timer, and he was patient with the old mop. Then the pizza man arrived, and Jun asked how to do the payment. The assistant opened the app, and Jun tapped to pay.

name: sun_glare_blinds
does: Tilts the blinds to the right angle so the sun does not shine in the eyes or fade the furniture.
inputs: which room, and how much light the person wants
people say:
- The sun is right in my eyes.
- My red sofa is losing its color, can you do something?
- I hope you can make the room less bright.
- Block the afternoon light in the kitchen.
- It's too sunny to watch my show.

name: watch_party_planner
does: Picks a show, sets a start time and sends an invite to friends so they can watch together.
inputs: the show, the time, and who to invite
people say:
- Let's watch the game with Ana and Luis tonight.
- Invite my cousins to see the new show at eight.
- Can you set up a movie night with friends? Popcorn bucket is ready.
- Tell everyone we start the series on Friday.
- I want my friends inside the same stream as me.

A lawn mower or a robot mower cuts the grass so that it stays short and tidy. In September the grass grows more slowly, so many people cut it less often. A robot mower can move around the garden by itself and go back to its base when it is done. People change how it works. They say, mow the lawn on Thursday instead of Wednesday, or cut the grass a little shorter, or skip today because it is wet. They also like smooth edges, so they say, trim the edge of the lawn along the path. If the mower gets stuck, they say, stop mowing and come home.

Chen was in a hurry to leave the house, but the rooms were cold. He said to the thermostat, set the heat to twenty-two degrees. Then he thought about the cost of heating a house. It was expensive in winter, and his office was a long distance away, so he would be gone all day. No, make it twenty, he said. The assistant understood that he wanted to fix the number, so it changed the temperature to twenty degrees. Chen also did not want the heat to run all day. He asked it to turn the heating off at eight, and to pick it up again at five. The assistant set both times. Then Chen picked up his bag and went out.

They want the plants in the garden to get water.
Water the plants.
Give the flowers a drink.
Turn on the sprinklers for a bit.
Can you shift the watering to the evening?
The water in the can is stale, so please use fresh water from the tap for the tomatoes.
It hasn't rained all week, so would you please start the garden hose?
I have homework tonight and won't be home until late, so could you kindly water the plants for me at six?
My plants look thirsty.

name: cinema_time_finder
does: Finds the times a film is on at the cinemas near the person and says which ones still have seats.
inputs: the film or the kind of film, the day, and the town
people say:
- What's on tonight after the gym?
- When can I see that new space film?
- I'm ironing my shirt, tell me what time the comedy starts.
- Any extra shows late on Saturday?
- Where is the cheapest ticket for a family film?

name: pause_show_timer
does: Pauses the show for a set time and starts it again by itself when the time is up.
inputs: how long to wait
people say:
- Hold on, I'm thirsty and need a drink.
- Stop it for five minutes, someone is at the door.
- Wait, I have to answer the phone, pause until I come back.
- Don't miss the scene with the factory, pause for two minutes.
- Freeze the show and start it again at nine.

Lara was new in the city and in a new school. At night she wanted to check her work, so she typed in a hurry: whens my scince homework due. The assistant understood the typo and knew she meant science. It looked at her list and said the science homework was due on Thursday. Lara typed, what is it about? The assistant said it was about the water cycle and a short page about speed. She wanted to study in silence, so she said, turn on a silent timer for thirty minutes. The assistant started a timer with no sound and only a small light when it was done.

Person: It's freezing in this empty flat.
Assistant: I'm sorry it's cold. Do you want me to turn up the heat?
Person: Yes please. Daily I come here after my shift and it's always cold.
Assistant: Which room should I warm up? The living room or the bedroom?
Person: Bedroom. The dust from the boxes makes me sneeze, too.
Assistant: I can't clean the dust, but I can start the air filter if the room has one.
Person: It has. Do that, and put the heat to twenty. I will pack my last bottle of water now.
Assistant: Done. The bedroom will be warm in about ten minutes.

Dani was a teenager, and she typed to her phone while eating a slice of delicious cake. Dim the lights and tell me how many days until my birthday, she wrote. The assistant understood that there were two things. First it made the lights in her room softer. Then it counted the days and said her birthday was in twenty-two days. Dani smiled and wrote, ask the bakery what size the cake is for ten people. The assistant said it would send a message. Dani put her fork down, because she was already thinking about the party and the candles.

After a long night at the hospital, Hana sat down at her desk to draw. She loved to draw a storm with lightning and a bowl of juicy peaches on the table. She said to her tablet, select the thick pencil. The assistant chose the thick pencil tool. Hana thought for a moment and said, no, the thin pencil. The assistant understood that she had changed her mind, so it picked the thin pencil instead. Then she asked it to play soft rain sounds, and she started drawing. When her eyes got heavy, she told the assistant to save the picture and turn off the lamp.

Kai lay in bed, nervous about a call with his cousin in Tokyo. He had just come out of the shower and did not know if it was too late to call. He typed two words: Tokyo time? The assistant understood he wanted to know what time it was in Tokyo right now. It answered that it was seven in the morning there. Kai felt better, because his cousin would be awake. Then he typed, remind me, and the assistant asked, when? Kai said in ten minutes. The assistant set the reminder, and Kai picked up his phone to call.

name: quiet_night_mode
does: Makes the phone and speakers silent at bedtime, so no sound or light wakes the person.
inputs: the bedtime, and the time to wake up
people say:
- I want a silent night, please.
- Stop my speaker from talking after ten.
- Don't let any brand of app buzz me while I sleep.
- Go quiet until seven in the morning.
- It's my bedtime, switch everything to sleep.

The water heater in a house keeps water hot so you can take a warm shower or wash dishes. A leak is when water drips from a pipe or a wall. A small leak can use a lot of water, so people watch the water use. Sometimes a stain on the wall or a wet floor shows a leak. When the heater is upstairs, you may hear the water breathe in the pipes. People ask for changes. They say, make the water a bit cooler, or turn the water heater off while we are away, or how much water did we use this week? If they see a drip, they say, tell me if there is a leak.

Person: Can you change my ribbon to inches and tell me the weight of a flour bag in pounds?
Assistant: Yes. How long is the ribbon, and how heavy is the flour bag?
Person: The ribbon is two meters. It's for a party banner in my shop. The flour is five kilos.
Assistant: Two meters is about seventy-nine inches. Five kilos is about eleven pounds.
Person: Simple. Can you also call the party store and ask if they are in a rush this week?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't make calls. I can give you the number of the store if you like.
Person: Yes please, that is fine.

Ines was a busy parent, and the kids were shouting in the next room. She had a paper from the bakery with a good price on a birthday cake, but she wanted a copy. Scan this page, she said to the printer helper, but don't print it. The assistant understood she wanted only a file, so it scanned the page and saved it on her phone. Then Ines said, email it to my husband, and not to the whole family. The assistant sent the file to her husband only. Ines said thanks, picked up the paper, and ran to see why the kids were still shouting.

Writing starts with a draft, which is a first try. You write your ideas down, and then you go back and fix them. Editing means changing words, checking spelling and making sentences shorter. Most writing programs show a word count, so you know how long your text is. People ask for changes in simple words. They say, make this shorter, or check my spelling, or change this word to something better. At night, when tired, it is easy to spot a mistake too late, so many people say, read it back to me. A good helper reads the text aloud, and you can hear if it sounds right.

Dee came home from a night shift at the clinic with cold feet. The kitchen was empty, and she opened the cupboard. I'm out of coffee, she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she did not say what to do, but that she wanted coffee on her shopping list, so it added coffee. Then she said, order a camping chair for the weekend. The assistant found a chair with free delivery and asked, shall I order it? Dee said yes and asked to mark the order as a gift for her brother. The assistant did it. Dee made a cup of tea and went to bed.

Tim was a child who loved to walk. One evening he asked the family speaker, how many steps did I take today and what is the way to the park? The speaker understood two questions. First it said he took six thousand steps. Then it told him the park was ten minutes away. Tim worried that he would not reach his goal of eight thousand. The speaker said he only needed two thousand more, and that the park trip would be enough. Tonight he felt proud. He asked the speaker to tell his dad, and the speaker left a note for him on the fridge screen.

Person: I don't want to be cold. Can you make it warm?
Assistant: Yes. Which room do you want to warm up?
Person: My room. But I don't want the radiator to get hot, it's too hot to touch.
Assistant: Okay. I will turn the heat up a little, not a lot. Would twenty-one degrees be fine?
Person: Yes. Mom said I can swim after school, so I will need a warm room when I come back.
Assistant: Good plan. When do you come back?
Person: At four. I will play on the grass until then.
Assistant: I will warm your room at half past three.

They want the room to be warmer, but just a little.
A bit warmer, please.
Turn the heat up by one degree.
It's rainy and my desk is cold, can you raise it?
Make it a little cozier in here.
Can we have half a degree more?
Cut the chill in the living room.
I'd like it two degrees warmer than now, and not more.
Would you kindly turn the heating up a bit, since my fingers are cold when I write?

Sofia owned a small shop, and tonight she was having a party for her customers. She was hungry, but there was a lot to do. She asked her phone, how many people said yes to the invitation? The assistant knew the guest list and said twenty-five people had said yes. Sofia said, then I need twenty-five peach tarts. The assistant did not know how to bake, but it found a bakery that could make them, and it put the order in her notes. She asked it to play lively music at six. The assistant said it would start the playlist then. Sofia ate a quick snack and hung the last lights.

name: kitchen_reminder
does: Reminds a person at a chosen time to do a small kitchen job, like taking a warm salad out of the fridge, and lets them update the time later.
inputs: what the reminder is for, and the time or day
people say:
- Tell me at six to get the salad out so it isn't too cold
- Nudge me when the rice should be done
- I keep forgetting the soup, buzz me in twenty minutes
- Can you update my dinner reminder to half past seven?
- Remind me tomorrow morning to buy warm bread

Walt did not trust his phone, but his daughter had left it with him for the trip. "Find me a room in Lisbon for three nights," he told the voice assistant. It showed a long list on the screen. "I can't scroll this thing," Walt said, "read them to me." The signal was weak, so the assistant's voice cut out twice, and Walt stepped closer to the window. The assistant read out three hotels. "The second one," Walt said. Then he stopped. "Wait, no. Two nights, not three. My knees won't take more." The assistant understood that he wanted the same hotel for two nights, so it changed the request and told him the hotel was one kilometer from the station. Walt smiled. "Good. A short walk." He said yes when it asked him to confirm, and the booking was saved.

Grandma Rosa felt sleepy after lunch, but the squeaky door in the back room was driving her mad. "Assistant, please book a repair person for the door hinge on Tuesday," she said. The assistant looked for handymen near her home and found one with a free morning. Rosa was stirring her tea when she remembered her bridge club. "Oh, not Tuesday. Make it Thursday, please." The assistant understood that she wanted the same repair on Thursday instead, so it moved the booking and read it back to her: a handyman would come to fix the hinge in the back room on Thursday at nine. "Good," said Rosa. The assistant also offered to remind her the evening before, and she said yes. Then she finished her tea and took a little nap.

Coffee is the drink many people reach for first thing in the morning. What people change about it is how strong it is and how sweet. Some want a weak cup, some want it extra strong, and a few want no sugar at all. They say things like make it stronger, less milk, one sugar, or a bit sweeter. Some coffee machines connect to the internet, so you can ask for a cup while you are still in bed. A sudden wish for something cold is common too, and then people ask for iced coffee instead. Fruit drinks work the same way. You peel the banana first, and then you can say thicker, thinner, or no ice.

A playlist is a list of songs that play one after another. People use playlists for a walk, for cooking, or to lie on the sofa and relax. What do they change? Mostly the volume, the song and the mood. They say turn it up, a bit quieter, skip this one, play that last song again, or play something cool. When it rains, many people ask for slow songs, and on a sunny day they want faster ones. They can also ask for more songs by the same artist, or say they don't like the song that is playing, and the next one starts. A new playlist is easy to make: say a name, then say the songs to put in it.

A neighbourhood message board helps people who live close to each other share news. Someone has lost a cat, a street party is planned for Saturday, or a band is too loud at night. People use the board to tell the street and to hear back. What they change is who sees the message and when it goes up. They say post this for everyone on the street, send it only to my building, or take my message down, the cat came home. Some neighbours also share a short clip from a wireless doorbell camera. If you have a sore finger and can't type, you can say the message out loud and ask the assistant to post it for you.

name: next_bus_times
does: Tells a person when the next buses or trains leave from a stop and warns about delays.
inputs: the stop or station, the line or direction if there is more than one, and whether they want a round trip home
people say:
- When does the next bus to the library come?
- Is my train running late?
- I don't want to drive today, what is the quickest way downtown?
- Anything leaving Oak Street in the next ten minutes?
- How long until the number 12 gets here?
- I need to be at the airport by nine and back tonight, what should I take?

Marco was making a fruit drink for his daughter's party when he remembered the hot tub. His hands were wet, so he did not touch anything. "Pool pump?" he said to the speaker. The assistant answered that the pump was working and had been running for two hours. "Water heat?" Marco asked. The assistant said the water was thirty-one degrees, warm enough for the kids. Marco split a lemon, turned off the blender so he could hear, and said, "Cover on." The assistant understood he wanted the hot tub cover closed for now, so it closed the cover and told him it was done. It also said the pump would keep running until eight. Marco nodded and went back to his lemons.

Person: I just got home from the night shift and I'm so tired. Can you turn off the porch lights and remind me about the party?
Assistant: Sure, I'll turn off the porch lights. Which party, and what time should I remind you?
Person: The holiday party at my sister's house. Remind me at four.
Assistant: Okay, a reminder at four today for your sister's party. Do you want me to keep the tree lights on?
Person: Yes, keep them on, but I can't stand the constant blinking. Make them steady.
Assistant: I can turn the lights on or off, but I can't change how they blink. That setting is on the lights themselves. I'm sorry.
Person: Fine. Turn them off then. The sky is one big gray cloud and the room is bright enough.
Assistant: Done, the tree lights are off. Sleep well.

name: check_account_access
does: Shows the sum of devices signed in to an account and can sign out the ones the person does not know.
inputs: which account, and which devices to sign out, if any
people say:
- Who else is logged in to my email?
- How many phones are using my shopping account?
- Kick off any device I don't know
- Sign everything out except this phone
- Unpack the whole list of devices for me, I think someone is using my account

name: battery_saver
does: Turns on a mode that makes the phone last longer by dimming the screen and pausing background apps.
inputs: on or off, and optionally the battery level at which to switch on
people say:
- My phone is almost dead, help it last
- Save power please
- Turn on low power when I hit twenty percent
- I have to pick up the kids at six and I only have ten percent left, stretch it
- The smoke alarm app must stay alive all night, make the battery last
- Even with this dirty old charger I want it to hold until tomorrow

Jade was texting from her bed with paint still in her hair. She typed to her phone assistant: "find a video on how to stretch canvas and set a timer for 20 min so the paint can dry". The assistant understood that she had asked for two things. First it searched for a short video about stretching canvas over a wooden frame and opened the top result. Second, it set a timer for twenty minutes. Jade watched the video while eating a juicy orange. When the timer rang, the assistant said, "Twenty minutes are up. Your paint should be dry now." Jade typed "thx" and went back to her painting, a little braver about the canvas.

Priya got home at seven in the morning, tired after a long night on the ward. It was a cold november day and she wanted soup. "What do I have in the fridge?" she asked her kitchen speaker. The assistant listed milk, two carrots, a few eggs and half an onion. "I don't want to go out," said Priya. "And don't order anything big. Just add celery and bread to my shopping list, nothing with nuts." The assistant understood that she wanted only celery and bread on the list and nothing with nuts, so it added those two things, ordered nothing, and said so. Priya said she would enjoy her soup later, and then she went to sleep.

Dan was cooking dinner while the kids ran around the house, and the music was too loud. "Turn the music down by half," he said. The assistant lowered the volume from sixty to thirty. Then Dan said, "Play the dance playlist I saved online." The assistant found the saved playlist in his music account and started it. When the dancing got too wild, he called, "Stop the music for a minute!" and the assistant paused it. "Set a timer for ten minutes of quiet time," Dan added. The assistant set the timer and said so. When it rang, the assistant asked if he wanted the music back, and Dan said yes, at the same quiet volume.

Omar had just moved to a new city, and he did not feel comfortable with the loud beeping from the ceiling. "Excuse me, assistant, I'm very sorry to bother you, but I just moved here from the countryside and there is a beeping noise in my hallway. Could you please tell me whether it is the smoke alarm, and how I can make it stop? I don't want to wake the neighbours," he said. The assistant understood that he wanted to know the cause of the beeping and how to stop it. It said a chirp every minute usually means the alarm battery is low, and it explained how to twist the alarm off its base and put in a new battery that fit. It also offered to remind him to buy batteries before his vacation next week, and Omar said yes.

A bike computer is a small screen on the handlebars. It shows how far you have gone, how fast you are going, and the route ahead. People use it to plan a ride, whether it is a slow ride at the speed of a jog around the park or a big hill climb at the weekend. After the ride, the bike computer and the phone sync, so the ride is saved. Cyclists change the distance, the speed they want to keep, and the route. They say find me a flatter way, add five more kilometres, avoid the main road, or how far have I gone so far?

They want to know the score of the match that is on right now.
What's the score?
Who's winning?
Any goals yet?
Is my team ahead?
The snow knocked out my TV, so I have no idea what is going on with the game.
Did the red team score yet?
My phone says the match should have begun an hour ago, so how is it going?
Could you please tell me the current result of the silver cup final?

Lena ran a small kitchen, and she had just paid for a pricey jar of saffron, the most expensive spice she knew. Late at night she typed fast: "how much did i spned on food this month". The assistant understood the typo, looked at her card spending, and said she had spent 640 dollars on food, 80 dollars more than last month. Lena groaned, then typed, "set a limit of 600 for food next month". The assistant set a monthly food budget of 600 dollars and said it would warn her when she reached 500. That would cheer up her accountant, Lena said, and she turned off the light.

Sam woke up late with messy hair and stared at the dark laptop screen. "Restart the computer and open my files from yesterday," he mumbled. The assistant restarted the laptop, and once it was back on, it opened the folder called Work that he had used the day before. Sam found his document in the middle of the list. Then a message arrived from his friend Ana, who wanted to invite him on a bicycle ride at ten. Sam said, "Tell her yes, and dim the screen, it is too bright." The assistant wrote a short reply that said yes, sent it to Ana, and turned the screen brightness down. Sam rubbed his eyes and started on his coffee.

Tomás was late for class, wearing one glove and holding a stale sandwich. He typed fast: "read this page aloud pls". The assistant began to read the web page in a clear voice. Tomás could not see the small letters well on the bus, so he typed again: "make the text biger". The assistant picked the next size up and made the letters larger. Tomás said it was still too small, so the assistant made them larger once more. He ate the sandwich, listened to the page, and got off at his stop just in time.

People take photos to remember a day. A phone keeps them in an album, and an album is a group of photos, like holidays or the cat. Sharing means sending a photo to a friend. People change which photos go in an album, who can see them, and how big they are. They say put this in the family album, share it with Mum, make a copy, or delete the blurry one. A screenshot is a photo of your screen, handy for saving a thick list or a map. Some phones even listen for your voice, so you can say cheese and the picture is taken.

Person: I need to book movers for our new apartment.
Assistant: Happy to help. What day is the move?
Person: This Saturday. Actually no, my sister can't help on Saturday, so make it Sunday.
Assistant: Sunday, got it. How many rooms need to be packed?
Person: Three bedrooms and a long hallway full of boxes. The kids' teacher said they can miss school on Monday if we need it.
Assistant: Thanks. What is the new address?
Person: 14 Mill Road. We fly out to see Grandma on Tuesday, so it must be done by Monday.
Assistant: Sunday at Mill Road works. I can't pay the movers myself, but I will send the request and you can confirm the price.

They want to move a meeting to a different time without cancelling it.
Move my meeting to Friday.
Push the three o'clock to tomorrow, don't delete it.
Can we do it later instead?
I can't make Tuesday's meeting, find it a new slot.
Shift the team call, but I don't want it on a Monday.
My day is melting, so please slide the review to next week.
The meeting is going in the wrong direction on my calendar, put it after lunch, not before.
Would you mind finding a fresh time for my meeting with Ana? I don't want to cancel it, I only need a different hour.

A meal plan is a list of what you will eat each day this week. People make one so they do not stand in front of the fridge asking what is for dinner. It also helps with shopping, because you only buy what the plan needs. People change the plan for diets, for example low salt, no meat, or more fruit. They say plan my meals for the week, make Tuesday vegetarian, swap the fish for chicken, or I need a packed lunch for my son's swim class. A good assistant will understand what you like and what you don't, and will not give you the same dinner three days in a row.

They want to know what homework is due soon.
What homework do I have?
Anything due tomorrow?
What's due by Friday at noon?
Show me my assignments, please.
I need to know what to hand in this week, like the engine project for science.
Can you cast an eye over my online class page and tell me what is due next week?
Hey, did the teacher put anything new up for tonight?
Could you please tell me which assignments are still open and when each one is due?

Hassan was parked outside a clinic, waiting for his turn. His eyes were tired. A big sneeze made him jump, and then he said, "Read my last message out loud and make the text bigger." The assistant read a message from the garage: the booking for his van was confirmed for Monday at nine. Then it made the text on the phone larger. "That's the minimum I can read," Hassan said, so the assistant went up one more size. He thanked it, put the phone in the holder, and watched the clinic door.

name: door_status_check
does: Tells a person whether the front door and the garage door are locked, and can lock them from far away.
inputs: which door, and whether to lock it
people say:
- Did I lock the front door?
- Is the garage closed?
- I'm at the hotel and can't remember if I shut up the house, please check
- Lock up, we're leaving to stay at Gran's
- It's sunny, so the kids may have left the back door open, is it shut?

Ben had just moved to a new city and wanted to bake bread in his new kitchen. "How long do I bake white bread?" he asked. The assistant said forty minutes at 200 degrees. Ben looked at the stale loaf on the counter and said, "Actually, I want rolls, not a loaf." The assistant understood and changed its answer to twenty minutes for rolls. Ben turned on the oven light to watch and said, "Set a timer for twenty minutes." When the doorbell rang, he said, "Pause the timer," and the assistant paused it. When he came back, he said, "Resume," and the timer started again.

Fatima was making soup when she heard a drip in the west corner of the kitchen. "Excuse me, assistant, could you please help me? I think the pipe under the sink is leaking, and I have a big dinner to cook tonight, and the size of the crowd is forty people, so I need to know if I can still use the water," she said. The assistant understood that she wanted to check her water use for a leak. It said the water meter showed a steady flow even though no tap was on, which usually means a leak. The pot could sit on the stove while she waited. The assistant offered to book a plumber for the afternoon, Fatima said yes, and a plumber was booked for two o'clock.

A focus timer helps you work for a short time without stopping, and then rest. Many people work for twenty-five minutes and then take a five-minute break. It is useful when you have a lot to do or an appointment later and want to use your time well. People change the length of the work time and of the break. They say start a focus timer for thirty minutes, make the break shorter, skip this break, or remind me to stand up. A red light on some timers means work time, and green means break. If you need to pull away early, you can just say stop the timer.

Nia woke up in a hotel room that felt cold, and her phone said it was five in the morning. She could not remember her plan for the day. "Checkout time?" she mumbled. The assistant answered that checkout was at eleven. "Breakfast open?" she asked. The assistant said the hotel restaurant opened at six thirty. "Does that mean I can sleep more?" Nia said. The assistant said yes, and it offered to set an alarm for six. Nia said, "Yes please," and the assistant set the alarm. She pulled the blanket up to her chin and closed her eyes.

Babies eat and sleep on a rhythm, and parents try to remember it. Feeding times are when the baby gets milk, often every three hours. Nap times are when the baby sleeps in the daytime. A baby monitor lets a parent hear or see the baby from another room. Parents change the times, and they say remind me to feed him at two, move the nap to after lunch, play her favorite lullaby, or tell me if she cries. Some parents keep a file on their phone with notes about when the baby ate and slept, and they ask for it before visiting the doctor.

They want the heating turned up.
Heat up the living room.
Make it warmer, please.
Turn the heat up and switch on the radiator in the hall.
I'm bored of wearing three sweaters indoors, so raise it a few degrees.
Put the thermostat up two degrees and turn it back down at ten.
We're going to the cinema at eight, so warm the house before we get back and keep it warm until bedtime.
If the heater is still broken, call a repair person, and meanwhile just set it to twenty-two.
Could you please raise the temperature a little, and also tell me when it reaches twenty-one?

Person: Change password.
Assistant: Sure. Which account, your email or your phone?
Person: My email. I'm new to the city and my old phone number is gone.
Assistant: Okay. I can start the change, but I need to send a code to a number you have now. Can you tell me the new number?
Person: Hold on, I'm hungry and can't think. It's 555 0142.
Assistant: Thank you. I will send a code now. A good new password can be a short sentence with a number in it.
Person: Okay. Can you just tell me my old password?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't. Passwords are kept hidden, even from me. But I can set a new one as soon as you say it.

Person: Take a picture of my screen with this recipe on it and send it to my husband.
Assistant: Done, I have the picture. Should I send it as a message or by email?
Person: A message. And write "can you buy these" under it.
Assistant: Sent with that note. Anything else?
Person: Yes, put the photos from Lucy's party in a new album and share it with Grandma.
Assistant: I can make the album. Which photos, and from which day?
Person: Saturday's. The kids were calm for once.
Assistant: I found 24 photos from Saturday. I made an album called Lucy's party and sent the link to Grandma.

They want a reminder to take a break while they work.
Remind me to take a break.
Tell me when to rest in half an hour. Actually, make it forty minutes.
Buzz me every hour so I can stretch.
I've been at this desk all week and I care about my back, so nudge me to get up.
Break in 20, no wait, 25 minutes.
I don't want to be rude to the client, so ping me quietly when it's time for a pause.
Please give me a gentle reminder to step away from the screen every hour, if that's not too much trouble.
Pause time at three. No, at four.

A dishwasher cleans dirty plates and glasses while you do something else, like fold the laundry. You put the dishes in, add a tablet, close the door and choose a program. Short programs are quick and use less water, and long ones are better for pots. People change the program, the heat, and the time the machine starts. They say wash on the quick cycle, let it run tonight after ten, use the eco setting, or stop it, I forgot a cup. On a stormy night, people often let the machine run late, because power can cost less then.

Gus owned a small bookshop and was driving to see his sister for the weekend. At a red light he asked his phone, "Is the shop alarm on?" The assistant checked and said the alarm was off. "Turn it on," Gus said. "But I don't want the motion sensor in the back room on, my cat sleeps there." The assistant understood and set the alarm for the front door and the windows, and it left the back room sensor off. It asked him to say his code, and Gus gave the correct one. The assistant said the alarm was on and that it would send him a notice if the front door opened. Gus relaxed and drove on.

Tara was kneading dough with flour on both hands when her son wanted a snack. "Set a timer for one hour for the dough to rise and add yogurt to my shopping list," she called out. The assistant set the timer and put yogurt on the list, and it told her both things were done. Because the dough needed checking, she asked for a reminder each hour, and the assistant gave her an hourly nudge. When the first timer rang, her son came to join her and help shape the rolls. Tara smiled and asked the assistant how long to bake them. It said about twenty minutes.

A kettle boils water fast. You fill it, close the lid, plug it in and press the switch. It stops by itself when the water boils. People use it for tea, soup and instant noodles. What people change is the amount of water and sometimes the heat. Some kettles let you pick 80 degrees for green tea and 100 for black tea. While the water heats, you can dig a mug out of the cupboard. People say boil the kettle, heat it to eighty, keep it warm, or turn it off. A good kettle is quiet, and if it looks dirty inside, a spoon of vinegar helps.

Person: Can you turn off the power to my desk outlet at midnight?
Assistant: Yes. Do you mean every night, or only tonight?
Person: Only tonight. Tomorrow at seven I need it back on, my laptop must charge.
Assistant: Off at midnight tonight and on again tomorrow at seven. Which outlet, the one at the desk or the one by the bed?
Person: The one with the purple tape. I'm a student and my power bill is high.
Assistant: I can switch the smart plug on the desk, but I can't see which outlet has purple tape. Is it the desk plug?
Person: Yes. And can you tap into my bill and tell me what I spent?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't open the energy company's bill. I can show how much power the desk plug used this week.

- It's urgent, my guests are hungry and nothing has come yet
- Is the driver close?
- My hobby group meets at seven and the order is late, when will it arrive?
- I want to tweet about this late order, so how late is it exactly?

Mei had just arrived in the city and was holding a bottle of water when her phone rang. She missed the call. "Call back the last number and put it on speaker," she said. The assistant called the number and switched on the speakerphone. It was the landlord, who wanted to estimate the cost of a new lock. After the call Mei said, "Check my voicemail and tell me my monthly phone plan." The assistant played one voicemail from her mother and then read out her plan, which was twenty dollars monthly. Mei thanked it and took a sip of water.

Mr. Hall was not good with technology. He stood by his front door with a bill in one hand and an iron in the other, because the postman was ringing. "Open the door, but do not unlock the back door!" he told the speaker. He felt sad that he had never learned to use the app. The assistant understood that he wanted only the front door unlocked. It unlocked the front door, kept the back door locked, and said so out loud. Mr. Hall took the parcel and said, "Lock it again, please." The assistant locked the front door, and Mr. Hall went back to his ironing.

They want to know when to take their next dose of medicine.
Next dose?
Pill time?
When do I take my medicine?
How long until my next tablet?
I don't want to spend the evening wondering, so tell me when the next dose is due.
My throat feels better after the cherry syrup, when can I have more?
What is the current plan for my pills today?
Please let me know when my next medicine is due, I keep forgetting.

Carl spent his mornings driving a delivery van. Last night he said to his phone, "Tomorrow at seven, tune the radio to the morning news." The assistant understood that he wanted the news station on at seven the next day, and it said it would set that up. The next morning at seven the radio came on. The news said a train had stopped on the bridge and the roads were slow. Carl was glad, because he did not want to pay for a monthly music plan and the radio was free. He took the long way round and arrived in time.

Kai was texting from the sofa when he opened the fridge and found only a jar of mustard. He typed to his phone assistant: "the fridge is empty again lol". The assistant understood that he might want a shopping list, so it asked, "Do you want me to start a list?" Kai said yes: milk, eggs and bread. His mum had left a receipt from the shop on the east side, so he asked the assistant to remind him to visit it after school. The assistant added the three items to the list and set a reminder for four o'clock.

- Start the bedtime routine at eight
- Tell Mia it's time to bathe and brush her teeth
- Read a short story to the little one
- Play quiet songs on the radio until she falls asleep
- Make bedtime half an hour earlier on school nights

Zoe was texting on the bus: "table for 4 tomorrow at seven at luigi's pls". The assistant understood that she wanted a table for four people at Luigi's tomorrow evening at seven, and it made the booking. Then Zoe asked, "do they have fast takeaway too?" The assistant said Luigi's did takeaway and that most orders took about fifteen minutes. Her friends wanted something to chill with, so she asked about cold drinks. The assistant said the menu had juice and soda, and a liter of lemonade for the table. Zoe sent a thumbs up and put her phone away.

A clock tells you what time it is where you are. A world clock tells you the time in other places, which is useful when you call a friend far away. When you travel, the time zone changes, and so the clock changes too. Some people pick the time zone by hand, and others let the phone do it. People change the city, the way the time is shown, and whether it is twelve or twenty-four hour time. They say what time is it in Tokyo, show me London time, or switch to the twenty-four hour clock. A pencil mark on a paper chart can help, but the phone's setting is permanent until you change it.

Rosa was kneeling by the tomatoes when a cold wind blew across the garden. Her hands were full of soil, so she spoke to the speaker on the porch. "Rain today?" she asked. The assistant understood that she wanted to know if it would rain in her town that day. It checked the forecast and said that light rain would start after lunch and stop by evening. Rosa nodded. A gardener has to learn the weather's habits, and a weekly look at the sky is never enough. "Frost tonight?" she added. The assistant said no, the night would stay above five degrees. Rosa smiled and thanked it. Her grandson had lost a tooth in the dirt last week, and she joked that the garden had kept it. Then she covered the seedlings anyway, just in case the rain came early.

Theo woke up, rubbed his eyes, and reached for his phone. "Hey, show me my new followers from this week," he mumbled. The assistant opened his social media app and began to list the new followers. "No wait, I mean likes, not followers," Theo said. The assistant understood the fix, stopped the list, and read out the likes instead. A huge number had come in overnight, because a friend had shared his photo of the lake from last July. Theo sat up in bed, surprised. The assistant said there were two hundred and forty new likes on that one photo. "Wow," he said. He asked it to turn on notifications for that post only, and the assistant did. Then Theo finally got up to make breakfast.

Nina woke up and remembered the bread dough rising in the closed cupboard, where it had been since last night. Her brother had sent her a recipe card from his trip, and it was written in Italian. She could not read a word of it. "Translate this," she said, holding the card up to her phone's camera. The assistant understood that she wanted the words changed into English. It read the card and told her the dough should rest one more hour, then bake for thirty minutes. "Timer, one hour," she said. The assistant set a timer for one hour. Nina smiled, pulled her blanket back over her legs, and waited. When the timer rang, she turned on the oven, and soon the whole kitchen smelled like warm bread.

Someone wants to know what to pack for a weekend camping trip.
what do i pack for camping
camping list
wat goes in the bag for a night in a tent
I want a packing list for two nights in the hills.
What do people bring when they sleep outdoors?
Tell me what to buy at the pharmacy and what else to put in my bag for the trail.
Is this the correct gear for a cold night by the lake: tent, sleeping bag, stove and torch?
Could you please help me get ready for our camping weekend by listing everything we need?

Max was seven, and he wanted to visit his gran, who lived downstairs from his aunt on the other side of town. He found the tablet and said, "Show me how to get to Gran's house." The assistant already knew the address. It said the bus took twenty minutes and the walk took forty. "Is the bus faster?" Max asked. The assistant said yes, the bus was twice as fast as walking. "How many stops?" Max asked. The assistant said there were six stops, and the last one was right by the park. Max wrote the number six on his hand with a pen so he would not forget it. Then he ran to ask his mum if she would say yes to the trip.

- I want dinner ideas, and please no dark chocolate this time.

Someone wants an alarm to wake them up gently tomorrow morning.
Wake me at six.
No loud beeps, just a soft sound at six thirty.
I have choir practice early, so get me up by half past six.
I don't want to sleep in again, I have a run before work.
Could you set my alarm for seven, but please don't use the harsh ring?
The paid parking starts at eight, so I must be out of bed by seven.
Please make sure I'm awake at dawn without a siren sound.
My ride comes soon, so can you ring a bell at six forty?

Someone wants to be reminded to give an elderly parent the evening medicine.
Pills at eight, please.
Mum always wins the argument about skipping her tablets, so please nudge me tonight.
I keep forgetting Dad's evening dose.
Her humidifier needs water and her tablet is due, so don't let me forget either one.
Make it a fast reminder, Grandpa's medicine is due soon.
I'll be out late, so make sure my phone pings me about the heart pills.
Could you please remind me at eight o'clock to help Grandma take her medicine?
If I don't answer the first time, ask me again.

name: bin_day_helper
does: Tells you which bin to put out on which day for your street, and what goes inside it.
inputs: your street or town, and the kind of waste
people say:
- Which day do the bins go out on the south side?
- Can my watch tell me when to put out the green bin?
- Is it paper day tomorrow?
- Where does a greasy pizza box go?
- I never remember the collection day.
- What can I put in the blue bin?

Dana was packing lunch boxes when she remembered her father. "Remind me to call Dad tomorrow at nine," she said to her phone. A second later she added, "No, make it eight. He leaves for the clinic at ten, and I want to catch him before." The assistant said it had moved the reminder to eight in the morning. Dana's father had needed constant care since his fall last spring, and she often wished she lived closer to him. The assistant then asked if she also wanted a reminder about his pills. Dana said yes, every evening at six. It set both reminders and read them back so she could check. She zipped the lunch boxes into the bags, a little less worried, and ran for the door because the school bus was already honking.

A podcast app keeps your place in every show, so you can stop in the middle of an episode and come back later. People change a few things about it. They change the playback speed when they want a story faster or slower, and they skip ahead thirty seconds when there is an advert. They say things like "go back a bit," "play it faster," or "start the next chapter." On a phone you can drag the line at the bottom to jump to another spot, and a voice assistant does the same when you say "jump to the middle." Some people listen while they cook something crispy in the oven, others while they walk to the store. The app remembers where you left off either way.

Person: Halve it.
Assistant: Happy to. Which recipe do you want me to halve?
Person: The lentil soup. It feeds the whole family, and today I'm only cooking for me.
Assistant: The soup uses four cups of lentils, so half is two cups. Should I halve the other amounts too?
Person: Yes, all of it. Most of the spices too.
Assistant: Done. That is two cups of lentils, three cups of stock and half a spoon of cumin. You can reduce the cooking time by a few minutes.
Person: Thanks. I'm so tired.
Assistant: Rest well after your shift. I can set a timer when you start cooking.

When you order something online, you pick the item, the size and how many you want, and then you choose how it will be delivered. People often change an order before it ships. They say "make it two," "switch to a larger size," or "send it to my office instead." A big box can weigh a lot, so the shop may charge more for delivery, while a small item like an umbrella ships cheaply. If something arrives and looks strange or does not fit, you can send it back. People then ask "how do I return this?" or "when will my money come back?" Keeping the receipt makes everything easier.
