inputs: your town, and the hours you want to look at
people say:
- Should I take a coat out with me?
- Will it pour this afternoon?
- Is the sky going to open up before the first bus?
- Is the picnic safe on Sunday?
- Do I need an umbrella?

Someone wants to switch the television to channel twenty-five.
Channel twenty-five, please.
Put on twenty-five.
Go to the channel after twenty-four.
It's a rainy Sunday and I want the old film on twenty-five.
My hands are in the soup pot, stirring, so could you change the channel to twenty-five?
Can you take me to the car show? The one with the horn sound at the start, I think it's twenty-five.
Would you mind switching over to twenty-five? The cooking show is boring.

First aid is the quick help you give someone before a doctor comes. For a small burn, the first step is to hold the skin under cool running water. A gentle stream for about ten minutes is usually right, and people ask "how long should I keep it under the water?" For a cut, you press a clean cloth on it until the bleeding stops. If someone is badly hurt, you call for help straight away. People ask a phone assistant to "call an ambulance," "show me what to do for a bee sting," or "set a ten minute timer." Half the job is staying calm. A first aid kit with working scissors and clean bandages makes everything easier.

Drafting means writing something rough first and fixing it later. A word count tells you how long your piece is, and many people have a limit, like five hundred words for a school essay. Editing means changing words, fixing spelling, and cutting parts that do not help. People say "how many words is this?" "check my spelling," "make this shorter," or "cancel that last change." Even a short note can use a good edit. A letter asking a shop for a refund should be clear and polite, while a cozy story for children can be slower and longer. The goal is always the same: say what you mean in simple words.

Lena had just moved to the city, and she did not know many people. She asked her phone, "Help me find a gift for my neighbour, she turns forty on Saturday." The assistant suggested a plant, some tea and a book. Lena said, "Sorry, not forty, she's turning fifty." The assistant understood the fix and offered a few gifts for someone turning fifty, like a soft scarf. Lena did not want to forget the date, so she asked for a reminder on Friday night. The assistant added it. Her neighbour had been home with a fever that week, so Lena also asked for a short card message. It wrote one line: "Happy birthday, get well soon, and thank you for making me feel welcome." Lena smiled and copied it onto a card.

Someone wants a workout to do today.
Quick workout.
Give me ten minutes of exercise.
I need something easy, and I don't have a gym.
What can I do to stretch and wake up my body?
Help me move a bit, my back is stiff.
Please track my sets while I do push-ups.
Is there a good workout for the shallow end of the pool?
Could you suggest a short routine that I can do at home before dinner, with a rest day built in?

Priya sat at her desk at the office and looked at the calendar on the wall. "How many days until the holiday on the twentieth?" she asked her phone. The assistant counted and said there were nine days left. Then Priya said, "Oh, I meant the twenty-fifth." The assistant counted again and said fourteen days. Priya gave a weak smile and sighed. In the next room, a coworker started to shout about the printer, and someone had left a cup in the sink in the kitchen. Priya laughed. Fourteen days was a long time, so she asked the assistant to remind her one week before. It set the reminder and told her the exact date, so she could stop counting and get back to work.

Person: heat the hot tub for tomorrow at seven
Assistant: Sure. What temperature should it be?
Person: the usual
Assistant: I don't know what your usual is yet. Most people pick thirty-eight degrees. Do you want that?
Person: yes pls. and can you buy more chlorine at the pharmacy
Assistant: Sorry, I can't buy things from a shop. I can put chlorine on your shopping list, though.
Person: ok do that. my sister will draw a smiley on the list lol
Assistant: Done. The hot tub will be at thirty-eight degrees by seven tomorrow, and chlorine is on the list. The total list has four items.

Sam was late for his train, and his coffee machine was still off. He grabbed his phone and said, "Could you please make my coffee strong and with no sugar, because I have a long meeting and I need to stay awake?" The assistant understood that he wanted a strong coffee with no sugar, and it started the machine. While it brewed, Sam read an article on his phone about a private cafe near the station and tried to follow the tips in it. The assistant said the coffee would be ready in two minutes. Sam put on his coat, filled his travel cup, and thanked it. He made the train with one minute to spare.

A washing machine cleans clothes with water and soap, then spins them nearly dry. Most machines have programs: a short wash for a few clothes, a long one for towels, and a cold one for delicate things. People change the temperature, the spin speed and the time. They say "wash it cold," "make it shorter," or "do an extra rinse." A dryer finishes the job, but on a warm day many people hang clothes outside, so they ask about the weather first. Do not pack the drum too full, or the clothes will not get clean. Stains are easier to remove when you treat them early.

A meeting call lets people talk at a set time even when they are in different places. You join with a link, and you can share your screen so others see what you see. An agenda is a short list of what the meeting will cover. People ask for things like "join my ten o'clock call," "share my screen," "mute me," or "send everyone the agenda." Before sharing, close what you do not need so your screen looks clean. In a dark room, the light from a laptop can glow on your face, so turn on a lamp. If you are on the way to work, you can even join from the train station with your phone.

Mr. Okafor sat in his armchair with a book, but the page was hard to read. "It's too dark in here for these old eyes," he said to the speaker. The assistant understood that he wanted more light, and it made the lamp by his chair brighter. "Still a little dim," he said, and it raised the brightness again. Then the assistant asked if he wanted the colour warmer, because the bulb was blue at the moment. He said yes, and the light turned soft and yellow. From the hall he heard the dryer buzz, because the last load of towels was done. He would fold them later. For now, the retired teacher turned the page, happy to read in peace.

Jo was in the kitchen when she spotted the bill for the internet cable on the table. "How much is in my savings account?" she asked the assistant. It said there was four hundred dollars. "Move half of that to my checking account," she said. The assistant understood that she wanted two hundred dollars moved between her own accounts. It did it, then read back the new balances. Her daughter ran in holding a shiny coin from her piggy bank and asked what was going on. Jo laughed and asked, "Is checking more than the cable bill now?" The assistant said yes, checking now had more than the bill, which was eighty dollars. Jo paid it and went back to the dishes.

A clock tells you the time where you are. The world is split into time zones, so when it is noon in one city it may be night in another. People look at a watch or ask a phone, "What time is it in Tokyo?" or "Is it too late to call my sister?" Many people hate waking someone by mistake, so they check first. They also ask a clock to change: "set the clock back an hour" when the seasons change, or "show me two clocks." If you are lucky, your phone updates by itself when you travel to a new place.

A text message is a short note sent from one phone to another. A group chat lets many people read and answer the same conversation. People ask an assistant to write and read texts for them: "text Mum I'm late," "read my new messages," "reply yes," or "tell the group I'll be there at six." It helps to say who the message is for and what it should say. You can ask to change it before it is sent, like "say sorry too." A friend might text to ask if you want to see a show at the theater. Quick replies earn you a name as a good friend.

Ivy woke up to a strange scraping noise outside her window. She was still half asleep, and her room faced the ocean, so she was not used to loud mornings. "The street is making a racket at this hour," she mumbled to her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted to know what the noise was. It looked at the neighbourhood news and found a post saying workers were fixing the road early, before the heat of the day. It also said they would finish by noon. Ivy pulled her pillow over her head. The assistant offered to start the fan and play soft rain sounds until then. She said yes, and soon the room felt calm again.

Kai sat in the corner of the library with a pile of notes. "I don't want a long summary, just the due dates," he told his phone. The assistant understood that he wanted only the dates for his assignments. It said the history essay was due Friday and the science quiz was on Monday. "Not the math, I did that already," Kai said. The assistant left the math out. Kai's science project was about iron nails and rust, and he still had to finish the pictures. He asked for a reminder on Thursday evening. The assistant set it. Kai felt calmer, so he rewarded himself with something sweet from his bag and kept studying.

name: fridge_stock_check
does: Tells you what food is running low in your fridge and puts it on your shopping list.
inputs: the name of the food, and how much is left
people say:
- Are we out of milk again?
- Do we still have eggs?
- The juice level is getting low, put it on the list.
- It's silly, but I never remember if we have butter.
- Did I use up the soap for washing dishes?
- What do we need from the shop?

name: screen_time_limit
does: Sets how many minutes a child can use a tablet each day and locks it when the time is up.
inputs: the child's name, the number of minutes, and the day
people say:
- Only one hour of games for Sam today.
- Unlock the tablet after homework, please.
- Give him extra time, his grade went up.
- Maximum two hours on weekends.
- Stop the tablet when it's bedtime.

A smart lock opens and closes your front door without a key. It is for keeping your home safe and for letting the right people in. People ask "lock the door," "is the garage closed?" "who is at the door?" or "let my neighbour in for an hour." When you travel, you can check from far away that everything is shut, which helps if you feel nervous about leaving home. A camera at the door shows who is there, whether it is a delivery person or just a cat climbing a tree. You can also change who has a code, like the person who walks your dog, and remove it later.

Making coffee or tea is a small daily thing, and the details are what people change: how strong, how sweet, how hot, how big. A strong coffee uses more grounds, and a weak tea steeps for less time. People say "a bit less sugar," "make it stronger," "extra milk," or "half a cup." In the morning there is traffic and little time to worry about the details, so a machine started by voice helps a lot. A hungry person might want a smoothie instead, which needs fruit, milk and ice. They say "make it thicker" or "no banana."

When you order food for delivery, a restaurant cooks it and a driver brings it to your door. The app shows how long it will take, and you can add a tip for the driver. People change the order before it is sent: "no onions," "add a drink," or "leave it at the back door." Later they ask "where is my food?" or "how long now?" If it is late, there may be bad traffic or news of a closed road. When it arrives, you unpack the bag and check that everything is there. Some drivers leave a personal note, like "enjoy your dinner."

Ben leaned back in his office chair after a long morning. "Play something calm," he told the speaker, "and wake me with the same playlist tomorrow at seven." The assistant understood both parts. It started a calm playlist and set an alarm for seven the next morning that would play the same songs. Then a coworker walked by and sneezed twice, and Ben's phone buzzed with an urgent message from his boss. "Quieter, please," he said, and the assistant lowered the volume. Ben answered the message, then asked it to bring the music back up a little. The assistant did, and Ben went on with his afternoon.

Someone wants to be reminded when the baby's next feeding is due.
When is the next feed?
I'm at the mall, so tell me when the baby is hungry again and set an alarm for it.
Remind me to make a fresh bottle at three.
Baby eats at four, right? Ping me before.
I'm about to zoom into a work call, so please remind me about the feeding in an hour.
How long since she ate, and when should she eat again?
Could you please let me know a little before the baby's next bottle so I can warm it up?
Nudge me at feeding time, and tell me when the nap starts.

Marta came home hot and tired. "Don't turn the heat on, I want the living room cool," she told the assistant. It understood that she wanted the room cooled and nothing warmer. It tried the air conditioner, but the air conditioner was offline, so it said so. Then it started the fan in the living room instead. Marta saw a loose screw on the fan's stand and tightened it with a coin. Her son wanted to swipe the screen of the tablet to change the speed, but she said, "No, leave it, the speed is fine." The assistant kept it on medium. A cool breeze slowly filled the room, and Marta finally sat down.

Omar had just moved to a new city, and he was nervous about missing things. He said to his phone, "Could you please remind me to call my sister when I get to the train station tomorrow, because she is expecting news about my new job and she will worry if I forget?" The assistant understood that he wanted a reminder tied to a place, not a time. It set the reminder for when he arrived at the train station and told him so. Omar felt relieved. His sister had been waiting for a serious talk about his plans, and he wanted to be sure he called her. In the morning, the phone buzzed right when he walked onto the platform.

Medicine reminders help older people take pills at the right time. A reminder rings at the same hour each day and says which pill to take. People change the time or ask for it to repeat: "remind me every morning at eight," "move it later," or "call my son if I don't answer." If the usual routine breaks, like a day out, they can ask for a different time. For emergencies, a button or a spoken "I need help" can send a call to a nearby family member. Reminders can also be small things, like a neighbour's invitation to tea at four.

Person: Find me a funny film and tell me when it's on tonight.
Assistant: Which cinema should I check?
Person: The Grand, near my restaurant. It's for my gram, she loves comedies.
Assistant: There are two comedies tonight at the Grand, at seven and at nine thirty.
Person: Seven. I'm too busy to type, so please also buy two tickets.
Assistant: Sorry, I can't buy tickets. I can set a reminder to book them, or open the cinema's page.
Person: Remind me at four, then.
Assistant: Done. I'll remind you at four to book two tickets for the seven o'clock comedy.

A robot vacuum is a small, round machine that cleans the floor by itself. It is low in height, so it can slide under a chair, but it cannot climb stairs, so it needs a flat floor. People set a cleaning schedule, like every morning at nine, and ask for a different power, such as low, medium or strong. They say "start cleaning," "clean the kitchen only," "stop, I have guests," or "go back to your base." It is a good idea to tidy cables and toys first. When you invite friends over, you might ask it to do a quick extra round before they arrive.

Zoe looked at her calendar and groaned. Too many blue boxes, which meant too many study sessions. "Move football to later, and decrease my study time from two hours to one," she told her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted two changes. It moved football to five in the evening and cut the study block to one hour. "Add more free time on Friday," she said. The assistant made Friday afternoon free. Zoe was meeting some people from her group project on Saturday, and she asked if they were all free. The assistant checked and said four people were free at noon. Zoe sent the time to the group chat and went to find her shoes.

Person: stop the water, small leak under the sink pls, ther is water everywhere
Assistant: Do you mean the whole house, or only the kitchen water?
Person: only kitchen
Assistant: I can't turn off a valve by myself, but I can show you where it usually is. Look under the sink for a small tap on the pipe and turn it to the right.
Person: found it. kids brought sand in too, what a mess
Assistant: Good. Turn it all the way off. Should I remind you to call a plumber tomorrow morning?
Person: yes at 8

name: chore_swapper
does: Moves a chore from one child to another and updates the daily chart on the fridge screen.
inputs: the chore, the two children, and the day
people say:
- Sweeping the corner by the door is Mia's job now.
- Can Leo and Ana swap dish duty?
- Put Sam on the trash this week.
- It's Tom's turn to feed the dog.
- Take bed-making off Lily today, she has a cold.

Mrs. Hale sat in her chair with a cup of tea. "Would you be so kind as to turn the robot vacuum on in the living room," she said to the speaker, "because my son and my dad are visiting this afternoon, and the floor is full of crumbs?" The assistant understood that she wanted the robot vacuum to start in the living room. It turned it on and told her it would take about twenty minutes. "Please keep it out of the kitchen," she added. "The stove is hot, and I don't want the machine near it." The assistant told the vacuum to skip the kitchen. Mrs. Hale thanked it and went to set out the cups for her visitors.

Luca stood in his kitchen holding a bottle of wine, getting ready to cook dinner. He thought of his sister, who lived in Sydney. "I wonder if my sister is still up right now," he said to the speaker. The assistant understood that he wanted to know the time in Sydney. It said the local time there was nine in the morning, so she was surely awake. Luca had hoped to call her, but he did not want to miss his cooking, so he asked the assistant to remind him at seven to ring her. It set the reminder. Luca smiled and poured the wine into the pot.

Ana sat on the dirty sofa with a pile of books, and her brain hurt. "I've been studying all day, there must be something fun to see," she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted a film to watch. It found a movie about a girl who loved to travel, showing at the cinema near her house tonight at eight. It also gave the trailer. Ana watched it and liked it. She asked the assistant to save the time, and it added the show to her calendar. She stuffed some candy in her bag, shut her books, and went to wash her face.

name: walk_pace_coach
does: Tells you how fast you are walking or running, and shares a short summary of your trip with a friend.
inputs: the start and end of your walk, and who to send the summary to
people say:
- How fast was I going on that last mile?
- Tweet my distance when I finish.
- Show my pace on the mirror screen in the hall.
- Am I slower than yesterday?
- I only have time for a short route, what's my best loop?

A reminder is a small note that rings at a time or a place. You can say "remind me to water the plants at six" or "remind me when I get home." People use reminders for things they might forget, like wash the cups in the sink or call a friend at seven sharp. They change a reminder when plans move: "push it back an hour," "reset it for tomorrow," or "do it every Monday." Some reminders repeat, and some happen once and then go away. A good reminder says what to do and when, so you know right away.

Grandpa Leo sat in his quiet kitchen with the tablet in front of him. Autumn had come, and he needed a warm coat. Last week he had ordered one online, but it turned out to be too small. 'Return coat,' he said to the tablet. The assistant understood that he wanted to send back the coat from last week's order. It opened the order and asked if he wanted his money back or a bigger size. 'Swap it,' said Leo. The assistant picked the next size up in the same blue color and set up the exchange. It printed a return label and told him the new coat would come in four days. Leo smiled. He put the old coat in the box and set it by the door, ready for the driver to pick up in the morning.

Mr. Okafor ran a small kitchen shop on Pine Street. Between customers, he said to his phone, 'Please call my supplier and read me my new messages.' The assistant understood two things: it should call the supplier saved in his contacts, and it should read out his unread messages. It started the call, and while the phone rang, it read two messages aloud. One was from a polite customer asking if the red blender was back in stock. The other was about a late delivery. Then the supplier picked up, and the assistant turned on the speaker. Soon a bell rang at the front door, so Mr. Okafor paused the call and the messages. When the customer left, he told the phone to resume, and it read the rest of the messages. He wrote the new delivery day on a notepad.

They want to know what time their flight leaves.
When do I take off?
Departure time?
What time is my flight tomorrow?
Is my flight earlier or later than half past nine?
I got my ticket in a big sale, so can you check when the plane leaves?
I'm putting the grill away before I go, so how many hours do I have until takeoff?
Could you please tell me the departure time? I have a large bag to check, and I want to leave home early enough.

A contact is a small card in your phone with a name, a phone number, and sometimes an address or a birthday. It is for finding people fast, so you never have to remember every number. People change their contacts all the time. They add a new friend, fix a wrong number, or add a birthday so the phone can remind them. When Tom met a new neighbor named Honey Park, he said, 'Add Honey to my contacts with this number.' Later he said, 'Change her number to the new one' and 'Put her birthday on March ninth.' If you point out a wrong number, you can say, 'That one is old, fix it.' You can also say 'remove' when someone is no longer needed. Most people are glad when the phone just does it.

name: share_daily_agenda
does: Folds the notes people send into one agenda for the day and shares it with everyone in the meeting.
inputs: the meeting, and who should get the agenda
people say:
- Send everyone what we're talking about today.
- Can you email the plan for the meeting to the team?
- The new artist on our team hasn't seen the list of topics yet, can she get it?
- Put all our notes together and show them to the group.
- Who is going to talk about what at ten o'clock? Send it around.

Person: I want to start a model of an old train station. Can you find me a plan?
Assistant: Of course. Would you like a big model or a small one?
Person: A small one. I am busy with other projects, so something easy.
Assistant: Do you want a kit made of wood blocks or of paper?
Person: Wood blocks, please. About twenty-five pieces.
Assistant: I found a wooden station kit with twenty-six blocks. Should I put it on your shopping list?
Person: Yes, please. Can you also bake the glue so it dries faster?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't do that. I can set a timer for the drying time, though.
Person: Lovely idea. Set it for two hours.
Assistant: Done. I will tell you when two hours are up.

Person: wifi is slwo, make it faster
Assistant: I can restart the router for you. Do you want me to do it now?
Person: not yet. my pair of coworkers are on a call
Assistant: Okay. When should I restart it?
Person: after lunch
Assistant: What exact time should I use?
Person: 1:30
Assistant: Done. The router will restart at 1:30, and it will beep once when it is back on.

They want to know how long the drive will take.
How long to get there?
Drive time to the school?
How many minutes is the trip to my aunt's house?
Is the highway faster than the back roads, or about the same?
I have to drop off the kid and I'm hanging on to a tight schedule, so how long will the drive take?
Will it take more than half an hour to reach the dry cleaner?
Could you please tell me how much time I should plan for the drive downtown?

Rosa was cooking dinner when her phone buzzed on the counter. Her hands were covered in flour, so she could not type anything. 'Who called me?' she asked the phone. The assistant said her sister had called twice and left a voicemail. 'Don't play it on the speaker,' said Rosa. 'I do not want the whole kitchen to hear.' A spider ran across the wall, and Rosa jumped, but she stayed calm. The assistant played the voicemail quietly into her ear. Her sister said her own dinner was already cooked and asked if Rosa wanted to come over. Rosa said, 'Call her back, but don't leave a message if she doesn't answer.' The assistant dialed, and when her sister picked up, Rosa said she would come at six.

name: resume_playback
does: Finds the spot where you stopped a podcast or audiobook and starts playing again from there.
inputs: the podcast or book, if there is more than one
people say:
- Where did I stop?
- I got a call in the middle of the chapter, so take me back to it.
- Keep going from where I left off in my book.
- Pick up the show about how to grill fish where it ended.
- I'm a patient listener, but I forgot the spot, so find it for me.

Mrs. Hale, a retired teacher, burned her hand on a hot pan on a warm day in June. She had just finished eating lunch and was washing up. 'Excuse me, could you please tell me what to do for a small burn on my hand? I want to be careful, because my grandchildren are visiting this afternoon and I do not want to make it worse,' she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she had a small burn and wanted safe first aid steps. It told her to hold her hand under cool running water for ten minutes, not to use ice or butter, and to cover the burn loosely with a clean cloth. It also said that if the burn blistered or hurt a lot, she should see a doctor. Mrs. Hale said thank you, and she was glad of the strong, clear advice.

Ben was late for his first class when he remembered the package he was waiting for. He pulled out his phone and typed fast: 'wher is my sugar order from monday'. The assistant understood that he wanted to know where his order of sugar from Monday was. It looked through his shopping account, found the order, and said the package was out for delivery and would arrive before five. Ben had a bad feeling that it was lost, because the shop had sent the wrong thing once before. But the assistant also said the driver was only three stops away. Ben let out a breath. He could chill now. He put his phone away, and the assistant promised to tell him as soon as the box arrived at his door.

They want the air conditioning to come on at a certain time.
Turn on the AC at six tomorrow evening.
Start cooling the house tomorrow at seven.
Can you make the bedroom cool by ten tonight?
Have the fan going when I get home at half past five.
I'd like the living room nice and cold when the guests come, around seven on Saturday.
It's going to be hot Friday morning, so help me out and get the cooling running by eight.
The weather is mild until noon, but after that please switch the cooling on.
Please make sure the apartment is cool before I walk in, because I'm back at noon on Monday.

name: set_dough_timer
does: Sets a timer for how long bread dough should rise, then tells you when it is time to shape it or put it in the oven.
inputs: the kind of dough, and how warm the room is
people say:
- Tell me when my bread has risen enough.
- How long should I let this dough sit?
- My dough is on the couch under a blanket, so call me when it has doubled.
- The dough looks rough and lumpy, how much longer should it rest?
- Remind me when to paint the loaf with egg before it goes in.

A shopping list is a short note of what you need to buy, so you don't forget things at the store. Many people keep one on their phone and put something on it whenever it runs out. When Sam saw the fridge was empty, he said, 'Put milk and eggs on my list.' Later he said, 'Take off the eggs, I found some' and 'I need two more bananas.' Some people take a picture of the fridge and ask the assistant what is missing. If a recipe is in cups and you want it in grams, you can ask the assistant to convert it. It is funny how often a list saves a second trip. People also say 'we're out of rice' or 'we need bread' to mean the same as 'add it to the list'.

Maya had just moved to the city, and her new building had a wall of small mailboxes. She did not know which one was hers, and she had no key yet. Standing in the hall, she said to her phone, 'I wonder if my mom's parcel ever found my new address.' The assistant understood that she wanted to know where the parcel was. It found the tracking number in her email and said the package had been taken to the post office on Elm Street, in the back of the building next to the bank, after one failed delivery. It would be held for five days. Maya said she could not afford to miss it again, so the assistant set a reminder to pick it up tomorrow at nine. It also saved her new address in her account as her permanent one.

Walt never trusted gadgets. His daughter had put a voice assistant in his car, and he spoke to it as if it were deaf. 'Tell me where I parked and how much gas is left,' he shouted. The assistant understood two things: Walt wanted to know where his car was parked, and how much fuel was left in the tank. It said the car was on the third floor of the garage, near the elevator, and that the tank was a quarter full. Walt had to guess how far that would take him, so he asked, and the assistant said about sixty miles. In the glove box Walt found a parking slip with an hourly price on it. He told the assistant to remind him to pay before he left, and it said it would.

Dana woke up groggy and remembered the shelf she was building. She had lost the last screw. 'Order more screws, but not the big ones,' she mumbled to the speaker by her bed. The assistant understood that she wanted small screws, not large. It looked at her past orders and found a pack of small screws at the hardware store she had used before. It said the pack of fifty cost four dollars. 'And don't use the rush shipping,' Dana said, rubbing her eyes. The assistant chose normal shipping and said the order would follow the usual schedule and arrive on Thursday. Dana thanked it, turned over, and went back to sleep.

Priya was packing boxes while her two kids zoomed around the empty living room. Outside it was a snowy day, and the wind rattled the old window. 'The movers come tomorrow, and I wonder who tells the gas company where we're going,' she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she needed to move her utilities to the new house. It added a task to her list, 'Tell the gas and power companies the new address,' and set a reminder for eight that evening. It also read out the phone number of the gas company so she could write it on the side of a box. Priya sighed, thanked it, and went back to taping the kitchen things.

Person: It's too bright in here. My eyes hurt.
Assistant: I can dim the lights. Which room are you in?
Person: The bedroom. I just got home and I want to sleep.
Assistant: Okay. Should I make them half as bright?
Person: Less than that. A quarter.
Assistant: Done. The bedroom light is at twenty-five percent.
Person: Thanks. The light in the broom closet is on too, and I don't want to spend the day with it glowing.
Assistant: I turned it off.
Person: Also, has the slow cooker finished? My stew should be cooked by now.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't check the slow cooker. I can only control the lights.

Person: Hello, could you please set a reminder for me? I just moved here, and I keep forgetting to call my mother on Sundays because she lives so far away.
Assistant: Of course. What time on Sunday should I remind you?
Person: She lives to the east, so there is a time difference. Five in the afternoon, please.
Assistant: Okay. I'll remind you every Sunday at five. What should the reminder be called?
Person: Please name it Call Mom.
Assistant: Done. The reminder Call Mom will ring every Sunday at five.
Person: Can you also tell me when she wakes up?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't know that. You could ask her what time works best.

Person: I need a hotel room for this weekend.
Assistant: Which city, and for how many nights?
Person: Denver, two nights. Wait, make it three. We decided to stay longer.
Assistant: Three nights in Denver. How many guests?
Person: Two adults and two kids. We need a big room.
Assistant: I found a family room with two beds. Do you want me to hold it?
Person: Yes, please. Is the hotel quiet? The volume of street noise matters because of my baby.
Assistant: I can't hear the street myself, but guests say the rooms at the back are quiet.
Person: Good. I'll click on the link you send and pay there.
Assistant: I just sent it to your phone.

name: warm_room_by_time
does: Heats one room to a chosen temperature at a chosen time, and can cancel the plan if you change your mind.
inputs: which room, how warm, and what time
people say:
- Get the south bedroom cozy by seven.
- I'm cold on the sofa, so warm up the living room.
- Heat the kitchen to twenty degrees at six in the morning.
- Never mind about tonight, cancel the heating plan.
- It's chilly in here, can you do something about it?

Leo was babysitting his baby cousin while his aunt was out. He was playing a game on his computer, trying to win a level, when the baby started to cry. He typed to the assistant, 'She hasn't eaten since noon and she's really loud.' The assistant understood that he wanted to know when the baby should eat. It checked the baby log in the family app and said that the last feeding was at noon. It said she usually eats every three hours, and the minimum wait between feeds was two hours, so it was time. Leo closed the game, warmed the bottle, and fed her. The assistant then noted the new feeding time in the log, so his aunt would see it when she came home.

Nia got home from the hospital at seven in the morning, tired and hungry. She ran the neighborhood group page, and she had promised to post a photo of the block party. 'Post my block party picture to the neighborhood group tomorrow at seven,' she said to the smart speaker, and then she yawned. The assistant understood that she wanted the photo posted later, not right now. It found the newest picture, which showed a plate of burnt sausages and a lot of smiling people, and it scheduled the post for seven the next morning. It asked if she wanted comments turned on, and she said yes. The assistant said the post was ready, and Nia went to bed.

Sam woke up on the sofa and heard rain on the roof. He felt small and sleepy. He had a job interview, but he had no idea what time it was or how the roads were. 'Traffic to downtown?' he mumbled to his phone. The assistant understood that he meant how heavy the traffic was on the way to downtown. It said there was an accident on the main road, and the drive would take forty minutes instead of twenty. 'Does that mean I'm late?' he asked. The assistant said that if he left in ten minutes he would still be on time. Sam jumped up, grabbed his coat, and ran for the door.

They want the pet feeder to give the dog his dinner.
Feed the dog.
It's time for the dog's dinner.
The dog is staring at his empty bowl.
Rex keeps pacing in front of the cupboard where his food is kept.
I don't want him to beg while I tidy the kitchen, so could you give him his food?
My dog hasn't had his dinner and it's getting late.
Please fill his bowl with one cup of food. He ate a few apple slices earlier, so it can be a small dinner.

name: check_pantry_stock
does: Looks at what is in the kitchen and counts how many of each thing is left.
inputs: the food or item to check, and where it is kept if you want
people say:
- How many eggs do we have?
- Are we out of rice?
- It's midnight and I want cereal, is there any milk left?
- Count the cans of soup in the cupboard.
- I only buy olive oil yearly, so do I still have some from the last time?

A focus timer is a way to work for a short time without distractions and then take a break. It is for people who find it hard to stay on one task. A common plan is twenty-five minutes of work and five minutes of rest. People often change the plan when it doesn't fit their day. A student might say, 'Make my work time longer,' or 'Make the break shorter.' A traveler waiting at the airport, with only a narrow gap before the gate opens, might say, 'Set a timer for ten minutes so I can answer my emails.' When the timer rings, you stand up, stretch, or charge your phone. Then you start the next round.

Mr. Ito, a retired teacher, kept his front hall tidy and his door always locked. One evening he sat down in his chair and could not remember if he had locked up. 'Is the front door locked?' he asked the speaker. The assistant said it was unlocked. 'Don't open it for anybody,' said Mr. Ito. 'I only want it locked.' The assistant locked the door and said it was done. Then he asked, 'Remind me to lock it every night at nine.' The assistant set the reminder. Mr. Ito felt a great amount of worry leave him. He thanked the speaker, picked up his book, and read until bedtime.

A birthday reminder is a note that tells you when someone's birthday is coming, so you can send a card or a gift on time. It is for people who don't want to forget. People add the date when they meet someone, and they change it if it was wrong. Someone might say, 'Remind me about Grandma's birthday a week before,' or 'Put Jake's birthday on June fourth.' When they need a gift idea, they say, 'What should I get a ten-year-old who loves to dance?' or 'Find a red scarf for my sister.' Some people sit down on a Sunday and put all the dates for the month into the phone. If a date changes, they just say, 'Move it to the fifth.'

Marta owned a small cafe and wanted to make pea soup for tomorrow at noon. Her recipe fed four people, but she needed to serve twelve. 'Make this pea soup recipe for twelve,' she told her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted every amount in the recipe multiplied by three. It read out the new list: nine cups of peas, three purple onions, and twelve cups of water. Then it told her the shopping would cost about fifteen dollars. Marta said that was fine, so the assistant put the new list in her notes and set a reminder to start cooking at nine tomorrow morning.

They want to know who is winning the game.
Who's ahead?
What's the score?
Is anyone beating me right now?
Tell me the points for each player.
I think my sister has more points than me, is that right?
I'm feeling sad because I keep losing, so could you tell me how far behind I am?
In our basket toss game, which team has more points?
Please check the score in the score book and tell me if the blue team is ahead, even by a little.

Carlos was busy at his shop when he remembered that his uncle took his medicine at noon. It weighed on his mind, because his uncle was old and often forgot. Carlos typed fast on his phone: 'call my uncel and remind him to take his pills'. The assistant understood that Carlos wanted it to call his uncle and tell him about his pills. It dialed the number saved as Uncle Rafael, and when he picked up, it said in a clear voice that it was time for his noon medicine. Then it told Carlos the call was done. Carlos was glad that the personal task had taken only a few seconds, and he went back to helping a customer.

Strength and sweetness are the two things people most often change about a drink. Coffee can be strong or weak, tea can be light or dark, and a smoothie can be thick or thin. Usually a person asks for one change at a time. They say, 'Make it stronger,' 'a bit sweeter,' or 'increase the sugar by one spoon.' If it is too much, they say 'less sweet' or 'make it half as strong.' A fancy cafe may offer many choices, but at home you can also ask for 'one more scoop of coffee' when you make a pot. A can of soda is sweet already, so some people add ice instead.

Person: Call Anna, please.
Assistant: I have two Annas, Anna Lee and Anna Brooks. Which one?
Person: Anna Lee. No, wait, I mean my sister, Anna Brooks.
Assistant: Calling Anna Brooks now.
Person: Oh dear, she is staying at a hotel, and it is late there. Should I wait?
Assistant: I can wait and call her in the morning, or I can leave her a message. Which do you want?
Person: Leave a message later. The light on my phone is flashing. What does that mean?
Assistant: It probably means you have a new voicemail. Do you want me to play it?
Person: Yes, please. My eyes are foggy today, so read it to me.
Assistant: Playing it now.

Joel ran out of the house with his bag, late for work. 'Set the pool heater to twenty-eight, I'm in a hurry,' he said to his phone as he locked the door. The assistant understood that he wanted the pool water to reach twenty-eight degrees. It scanned the pool app, saw that the water was only twenty degrees, and turned the heater on. It also checked the battery of the pool robot and told him that it was low. Joel said he would charge it tonight. The assistant noted that everything worked well, and it promised to tell him when the water reached the right heat. Joel hopped into his car and drove off.

Priti stumbled into her kitchen after a long shift, still wearing her earbuds. Her coffee was stale from the morning, but she was too tired to make more. She typed to her phone: 'read my new mesages and tell mom i will call after i sleep'. The assistant understood that she wanted two things: to hear her new texts, and to send a reply to her mom. It read three messages into her earbuds, one from her friend, one from her brother, and one from her mom. Then it sent a text to her mom that said Priti would call after she slept. Priti said thanks, put the phone down, and went to bed.

Greg sat at his desk before a meeting. In front of him was a list of costs for a new office tv. 'What is three hundred twenty plus one hundred eighty, and is that more than my five hundred dollar budget?' he asked his phone. The assistant understood that he wanted two numbers added together and then compared with his budget. It said the total was five hundred, which was exactly his budget, not more. Greg said that was perfect and asked the assistant to update the total in his notes. It did, and it added a line saying the budget was now used up. Greg nodded and walked to the meeting.

Person: book a table at the pasta place for frdiay
Assistant: Sure. What time, and how many people?
Person: 7 pm, four people
Assistant: Friday at seven for four. Do you want a table inside or outside?
Person: inside. last time our table wobbled because of a loose screw
Assistant: I'll add a note asking for a steady table. Anything else?
Person: can you get us a deep booth in the corner?
Assistant: I can ask, but I can't promise a booth. I'll send the request.
Person: ok. we can't afford anything fancy, so check that it's cheap
Assistant: The pasta place has main dishes from ten to fifteen dollars.

Tom closed his shop at six, tired after a long day. He sat on the sofa with a bowl of pea soup and picked up his phone. 'Show movies,' he said. The assistant understood that he wanted to see what films were on tonight. It listed three films at the cinema near him, with their times, and it also found a simple old comedy on his streaming app. Tom picked the comedy. The assistant connected his phone to the tv and started the film. Tom put his feet up, ate his soup, and laughed the whole way through.

Harold was not good with technology, and he did not trust his new smart lock. One evening he came home with a big painting in both arms and could not use his key. 'Open the front door,' he said. Nothing happened. He said it again, twice as loud as before. The assistant answered that it had not heard him well, because he was too far from the speaker. Harold took a deep breath and spoke more slowly. This time the door unlocked with a soft click, and the assistant said it was open. Harold's smile grew. He carried the painting inside, and he thought the new lock was perfect after all.

Person: My sister's birthday is next week and I have no idea what to get her.
Assistant: I can help with that. What does she like?
Person: She talks about her dream trip to Japan all the time.
Assistant: Nice. What is your budget?
Person: Under fifty dollars. I'm about to park at home, and I'm so tired.
Assistant: Then how about a Japan travel book? I found one for thirty-five dollars.
Person: Perfect. Can you wrap it and carry it upstairs to her apartment?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't carry things. I can order it with gift wrap and send it to her address.
Person: Do that, please.

They want a recipe changed to feed more people.
Make this recipe for eight.
Double it.
Scale the cake for twelve slices and give me a new shopping list.
Make it for six and tell me which cups and spoons I need.
I'm excited to cook for the whole family, so change the recipe to serve ten and tell me how much butter to use.
We have more guests than I thought, so please make it bigger.
Cut this in half and tell me the new baking time.
I nailed this cake last time, but only for four people, so please change it for nine. I want the glaze to shine, so change that too.

They want ideas for what to eat this week.
What's for dinner?
I have no idea what to cook this week.
It's snowy outside and I'm not going to the store, so what can I make with what I have?
My fridge is nearly empty and the week is long.
I'm tired of eating the same thing every night.
I'm trying to practice a better balance of vegetables and rice, so what should I cook?
Could you please plan five easy dinners for me, and think of something for my packed lunches?

Grandma Joy sat by the pool under a clear sky, with the sun shining brightly. But the water felt cold on her toes. 'Heat pool,' she said to the speaker. The assistant understood that she wanted the pool heater turned on. It turned on the electric heater and set it to the usual temperature of thirty degrees. It told her the water would take about two hours to warm up. Joy said that was fine, because she was in no hurry. She picked up her book and read in the sun. When the time was up, the assistant told her the pool was ready.

Luis was cooking dinner for the kids. He tasted the soup with one hand and held his phone in the other. The screen looked pale and he could hardly read it, so he asked the assistant to make it brighter. Then he said, 'Turn on do not disturb tonight at eight, and keep it on until tomorrow at seven.' The assistant understood that he wanted no calls or alerts during that time. It set the schedule and asked if it should filter out calls from family. Luis said yes, because his mother might call. The assistant allowed only family and said the quiet time was set. Luis put the phone down and called the kids to the table.

Nora waited at her desk. It was going to snow, and her flight to Chicago was at four. A silver suitcase stood beside her chair, and her boarding card was in her bag. 'Flight status?' she asked her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted to know how her flight was doing. It checked and said the flight was delayed by forty minutes, so the new departure was at 4:40 from gate B12. Nora sighed, but she was glad to know. She finished one more email, closed her laptop, and walked to the elevator with her suitcase.

Hana took out the recycling and noticed a smoky smell in the air from a fire far away. When she came back in, she said to her phone, 'Run the air purifier in the kids' room tomorrow at seven, and keep it on until they leave for school.' The assistant answered that it understood: it would turn on the purifier in the kids' room at seven tomorrow and turn it off at eight. It also asked if she wanted that every school day. Hana said yes, so the assistant made it a permanent schedule for weekdays. It then told her the air outside was poor today and suggested she keep the windows closed.

Ines was minding her shop on a cold afternoon, and the old radiator was clanking in the corner. Her son Lucas had a math worksheet, but she had forgotten the date. She typed quickly on her phone: 'when is lucas homewrk due'. The assistant understood that she wanted to know when Lucas's homework was due. It looked in the school app and said the math worksheet was due on Friday. Ines was relieved. Then the assistant told her about a funny note from the teacher on the page, which said Lucas had drawn a cat in the margin. Ines laughed, watered the plant by the door, and went back to her customers.

They want to know how to say a word in another language.
How do you say dessert in Spanish?
Spanish word for cake, please
what's French for good morning
Can you translate this word into Italian for me?
I need the German words for double chocolate
How would I say the food is ready in Japanese?
Say come here in Portuguese, but make it short
What do people say in Korean when they want more rice?
I'm going to a dinner party and would love to know how to tell my host that everything looks great, so could you put that into Turkish for me?

Sam woke up late, with his hair going in every direction, and walked into the kitchen with his eyes half shut. He mumbled to the phone on the counter, "Plan dinners for the week and put the shopping list on my screen." The assistant sounded bright and calm. It said it had planned five dinners: pasta, soup, rice with beans, tacos and baked fish. It had also made a shopping list with everything those meals need. Sam asked for the list to be short, so the assistant took off things he already had at home, like salt and oil. Then Sam said he only had one hour on Sunday to cook. The assistant moved the soup and the rice to Sunday, because both could be made in an hour and kept in the fridge. It all felt smooth, almost like magic. Sam yawned, thanked the phone, and poured his coffee. The list was already waiting on his screen.

They want a good place to go cycling.
Where can I bike near here?
Find me a short loop for tonight
I want a flat route, nothing with big hills
What's a nice path for a slow ride after yoga class?
Name a few bike trails by the river, please
Give me about ten miles, easy pace
Somewhere safe for my kid to cycle
Could you please suggest a route that is not too long and has street lights, because it gets dark early now and I don't want to be out on a black road?

Dana was a busy parent with two kids and a long list of errands. Standing at the front door with her keys, she said to her phone, "Remind me to go to the post office, but don't put it before the market, because the market closes early." The assistant understood that the post office had to come after the market. It made a list of stops in that order: market, bank, post office. Dana said she did not want any stop on the list after five, since the kids needed dinner. The assistant checked the opening hours and told her the post office closed at five thirty, so she could still make it. It marked the bank as done after she said she had paid the bill online, and that left only two stops. Dana smiled, picked up her bag, and herded the kids toward the car. The reminders were set.

Luca was a cook in a small restaurant, and tonight a guest from Japan was sitting at the front table. His hands were covered in flour, so he spoke to the speaker on the shelf. "Tell me how to say welcome in Japanese and write it on a card for the table." The assistant said the word slowly, twice, so Luca could copy the sounds. Then it wrote the word on his screen in big letters. Luca also asked it to filter out the hard words and keep only easy ones, so the assistant gave him three simple phrases: thank you, please eat, and enjoy. Luca practiced while he stirred the soup. When the guest heard his greeting, she laughed with joy. Later she said the warm welcome was the best prize of her whole trip.

A contact list is a small book inside your phone. It is for finding people fast, so you do not have to remember every phone number or address. Each contact can hold a name, a number, an email, a home address and a birthday. People change their contacts all the time. When a friend moves, you say, update Ana's address, or change her number to the new one. When you meet someone new, you say, add a contact called Tom. If you want to remember a birthday, you say, put Mom's birthday on her card. On a foggy morning, a delivery driver may call you, and you can see the name instead of a strange number. Some people even dress up the list by giving each friend a small picture.

A weather forecast tells you what the sky will probably do, so you know what to wear and whether to take an umbrella. It is for small plans, like a walk, a picnic, or hanging washing on a rope outside. The forecast changes through the day. When the wind shifts, rain can come sooner than planned. People ask about it in many ways. They say, will it rain tomorrow, is it cold outside, or do I need a jacket. They can also ask for a different place, like what's the weather in Lima, or a different time, like what about Saturday. The final answer is simple: a number for the temperature and a word like sunny, windy or wet. Checking before you leave the house takes only a second.

Priya, an office worker, came home tired and saw the electric bill on the table. She was careful with money, so she spoke politely to the smart speaker. "Could you please show me how much electricity we used this week, because I think the heater uses too much and I would like to find out before the bill gets bigger?" The assistant said it understood she wanted her power use for the last seven days and a hint about the heater. It found the numbers and told her the heater had used nearly half of all the power. Priya wondered if an old wire behind the TV was wasting power too. The assistant could not see wires, but it offered to deliver a short report every Monday. Priya said yes, and then asked it to remind her to turn the heater down at ten o'clock.

Jin was an office worker, and at lunch she sat on a chair in the park with a salad she had just chopped. The sun was so bright that she could not see her phone. "I can't see anything on here," she said. The assistant understood that she wanted the screen to be brighter, so it turned the brightness up. Now she could look at her photos. "These pictures look so dark," she said. The assistant took that to mean she wanted them lighter, and it offered to fix the light on the last photo. Jin said yes. The picture of her sister's garden became clear and warm. She was glad, and she asked the assistant to send it to her sister. The assistant sent the photo and told Jin it had been delivered.

Birthdays come once a year, and it is easy to forget the date. Many people keep a list of the birthdays of friends and family, with a number for each person's age. A phone can show a small note a few days before, so you have time to buy a gift or send a card. When you want to change something, you say, remind me a week before Dad's birthday, or add Grace's birthday on March ninth. If you need an idea, you can ask, what is a good gift for a grandmother, or find me something under twenty dollars. A tiny gift with a nice note can make someone very happy. After the party, some people follow up with a thank you message.

Ben was a child with a little jar of coins and a big wish for a new toy. He asked the tablet on the table, "How much money have I got? Don't count the coins from my sister." The assistant understood that it should count only Ben's coins. It added up the money he had told it about before and said he had twelve dollars. The toy cost twenty. The assistant said he needed eight more dollars. Ben did not want to ask his parents, so he asked how he could save it. The assistant said that if he put away two dollars every week, he could have the toy in four weeks. Ben asked it to switch on a weekly reminder, and the assistant set it for Sunday morning. That night Ben could sleep well, because he had a plan.

Omar was an office worker who worked from home on Thursdays. His wifi kept dropping, and he did not want to call anyone about it. "Restart the router tomorrow at seven in the morning, before my first meeting," he said to his phone. The assistant understood that he wanted the router to switch off and on at seven the next day. It said it could do that and set the time. Omar also asked it to check the local network, and the assistant found that the signal was weak in his room. It suggested moving the router closer, or choosing a different route for the cable. Omar said he would move it tonight. The next morning at seven the router restarted by itself, and the wifi was fast again when he sat down to work.

They want to know how much power the house has used.
How much electricity did we use yesterday?
Power use this week?
What's our total for the month so far?
Show me how much energy the house burned since Monday
Was last night a good night for saving power, or did we use a lot?
Tomorrow at seven, tell me how much we used overnight
Can you give me the numbers for the last three days, please?
I just got the broom out of the closet and saw every light on, so how much power has gone to waste today?

Units are the names we give to measures, like inches, meters, pounds and degrees. Cooks use cups and spoons. A person who builds a drawer uses a tape with centimeters on it. Friends in different countries often use different units, so they need to change from one to the other. People share a recipe and say, how many grams is a cup of flour, or what is seventy degrees in Celsius. They also ask, how long is five miles in kilometers, or give that to me in inches instead. It can get noisy in a busy kitchen, so a quick answer is nice. The point of a unit is that everyone agrees how big a thing is, and that you can say it the same way twice.

A baby needs food and sleep at regular times. Parents often keep a little schedule: feed at six, nap at nine, feed again at noon. A schedule helps everyone know what is next, but it is never exactly correct, because babies do not read the clock. If the baby sleeps longer on a Tuesday, the parent moves the next feed later. People say, push the nap by thirty minutes, or let her sleep a little more. They also say, remind me when it's time to feed him, or tell me when he wakes up. A baby monitor lets parents hear or see the room while they cook or rest. When the baby cries, the monitor tells the parent right away.

They want the air in a room to feel less hot.
Turn on the fan
It feels like I'm sitting in an oven in here
I don't want it this hot, please
Cool down the bedroom, but don't make it freezing
Is it true that the living room is warmer than the kitchen? Fix that
I can't even bathe in this heat without feeling sticky, so put the air conditioner on
Could you please chill the house a bit, not too much, because the baby is napping and I don't want her to get cold?

Marco, a cook, finished the lunch rush and looked out the window. The sky was gray, and the wind was blowing hard. "I was hoping for a long ride on my bike this afternoon," he said to his phone, "but it looks like it's about to pour." The assistant understood that he wanted to know if rain was coming. It checked and said rain would start at three. Marco said, "Then I'll skip the long one." The assistant found a short route of five kilometers that he could finish before three, and it saved the route as a document in his files. Marco had planned a ride with a friend, so he asked the assistant to undo that plan. It removed the event from his calendar and sent the friend a short message. Marco put on his helmet and left for his short ride.

A calendar helps you remember what happens on which day. It holds meetings, dentist visits, birthdays, and the quiet time you keep free for yourself. You can look at one day, one week, or the whole month. Plans change a lot, so people often ask for changes. They say, move my meeting to Friday, push lunch back an hour, or cancel the dentist. To add something new, they say, put a hike up the mountain on Saturday morning, or I'm going to the doctor at four tomorrow. They can also ask, am I free on Monday, or what do I have today. A good calendar tells you when two things happen at the same time, so you do not double book.

They want to know the total of two numbers.
twenty-five plus seventeen
What's 25 and 17 together?
Add up twenty-five and seventeen for me
I bought a yellow shirt for twenty-five and a hat for seventeen, how much was that in all?
I have a discount coupon for seventeen dollars and another for twenty-five, so how much do the two give me?
Before the wind blows my receipt away, what is twenty-five plus seventeen?
Could you kindly tell me what you get when you join twenty-five to seventeen?
Seventeen and twenty-five, total?

A text message is a short note you send from your phone. People use texts when a call is too much or when the other person might be asleep. You write it, pick who gets it, and send it. A group chat lets many people read the same thread, like a family chat with your mother, your brother and your aunt. When a new message comes, the phone buzzes or wakes the screen. People say, text Sam that I'm late, read my new messages, or reply yes to Dad. If you do not have enough time to type, you can say the words and the phone writes them. If you made a mistake, you can say, change that to six o'clock.

Hana had just moved to a new city and did not know the shops yet. Her coworker's birthday was on Friday, and she wanted to give a gift. Standing at a shop window, she asked her phone, "What can I give a coworker? I don't want anything pricey or anything with flowers." The assistant understood that she needed gift ideas with a small price and no flowers. It pulled up a few: a nice mug, a box of tea, and a notebook. It also showed which shops near her were open. Hana picked the tea and asked for a card to go with it. The assistant said a paper shop was two streets away. It set a reminder for Thursday so her gift would be ready on time. Hana walked there feeling less lost.

Music on a phone or speaker works like a radio you control. You pick a song, an artist or a playlist, and it plays. A playlist is a list of songs that someone saved together. People make one for a party, for a run, or for a quiet evening. While a song plays, they change things. They say, turn it down, skip this one, play the last song again, or louder, please. In a car, a driver with a foot on the brake might ask for music, and a soft beep from the speaker shows it understood. When a favorite song starts, people are glad and ask for it again. You can also say, add this to my road trip list.
