Many older people take medicine at set times, and a reminder helps them take the correct pill at the right hour. A family member can ask a phone or speaker to remind Grandma at eight and again at noon. Some people keep a notebook by the bed with the list of pills and the doctors' numbers. Check-in calls are short calls made every day to hear that everything is fine. If something goes wrong, an emergency button can call a family member or bring help. People say, remind Dad to take his pills at nine, call Mom now, change the reminder to ten, or tell me if she did not answer. These small things give families peace of mind.

A podcast is a show you listen to, with a new episode every week. An audiobook is a book read aloud and split into chapters. Both remember where you stopped, so you can pick up again later. Many apps have an automatic setting that moves to the next episode. People listen while they cook, drive or walk, and sometimes a grandfather listens in the garden. To control it, they say, play the next episode, go back thirty seconds, or skip this chapter. If a voice is too slow, they say, play it faster, or one and a half times speed. If they swipe the wrong thing on the phone, they can say, take me back to where I was.

They want to know when their team plays.
When is the next game?
Game time?
Is there a match tonight?
When do the Tigers play next?
Does the game start tomorrow at seven?
My fingers freeze at the stadium, so what time should I get there?
What's the current schedule for my team? I want to watch before the cake comes out of the oven.
Could you please tell me when my team plays next, because I'd like to invite friends over and need to plan the food?

They want to know how many days are left until a date.
How many days until Christmas?
Days left till my trip
Count down to Friday
How many sleeps until my birthday on June third?
How many days and hours until next Monday at nine?
It's nice out and I'm cleaning the garage, so how long until the party on Saturday?
Reset my countdown and tell me how many days are left until the exam on the fifth
Could you tell me how much time remains before my sister lands on the twelfth?

name: parking_timer
does: Starts a timer for the time left on a parking spot and warns you before it runs out.
inputs: how long you paid for and the time you parked
people say:
- remind me before the meter runs out
- I parked at two for two hours, tell me when to go back
- how much time is left on my spot
- I love this shop but I always forget my car, ring me ten minutes early
- I'm wearing my apron at work and can't watch the clock, keep an eye on the meter
- I only need a medium stop, about an hour, so set a timer

Elena was a nurse who had just finished a night shift. She came home and sat by the hot tub in the yard under a grey morning sky. She put a hand in the water and said, "Brr, it's not warm at all, and I have an appointment for my sore back at noon." The assistant understood that she wanted the water to be hotter. It asked if she wanted it hot right away, and Elena said yes, but not too hot. The assistant started the heater and set it to thirty-eight degrees. It said the water would be ready in about forty minutes. Elena asked it to remind her at eleven so she would not miss the appointment, and the assistant set the reminder. She went inside to eat breakfast, and later she slid into the warm water.

Parking is about finding a safe place to leave your car and paying for the time you use. Many streets have a meter or an app. You type your plate number, pick how long to stay, and pay. Some people upload a photo of the ticket to prove they paid. In the early morning the street is silent and spots are easy to find, but at noon they are not. If you want more time, you say, add thirty minutes to my parking, or how much time is left. People also ask, where can I park near the market, or is parking free on Sundays. On a hot day, a shady spot is nice, since a car is no place to bathe in sunshine.

Kofi was a driver, and the road ahead was long and heavy with traffic. At a red light he said to the car, "Play the next episode of my cooking show, but don't start it from the beginning." The assistant understood that he wanted to continue where he left off, not start over. It found the show, said he had stopped at minute twenty-two, and began from there. A little later, the host talked about a train trip through the mountains, and Kofi laughed. When a call came in, the assistant paused the show, and when it ended he asked, "Where was I?" The assistant went back thirty seconds and played again. Kofi said he did not want the sound so loud, and the assistant lowered the volume. At a gas station he stopped to stretch his legs, and the assistant kept the show paused.

Rosa owned a flower shop. She stood on a ladder hanging a sign when her phone buzzed. Her sister was flying in that afternoon. "Check if my sister's flight is on time and text her that I will pick her up," Rosa said to the assistant, without climbing down. The assistant understood two things: look up the flight, and send a message. It told Rosa the plane was running twenty minutes late and would land at four forty. Then it sent the text to her sister, saying Rosa would meet her at the arrivals door. Rosa thanked it. Several customers came in, so she asked for a reminder at four to leave for the airport. The assistant set it. Rosa climbed down and went back to work, glad that she did not have to look at the airport board herself.

Notes are small pieces of writing that help you remember things. You can type them or say them as voice notes. People write a shopping list with cheese on it, an idea for a gift, or a rough estimate of what a repair will cost. A clean list is easy to read later, so people tidy their notes. To make a new note, they say, write down call the plumber, or start a note called trip ideas. To find old notes, they say, find my note about the garden. To change a note, they say, add milk to my list, or cross off eggs. If you no longer need it, you say, delete that note.

Kai was a teenager lying on the couch, texting with friends about a camping trip in the hills on Saturday. With one thumb he typed to his phone, "What's the weather like up there, and how cold will it get at night?" The assistant said the days would be about twenty degrees and the nights about five. Kai wrote, "Make me a packing list for two nights." The assistant made one: tent, sleeping bag, warm jacket, flashlight, water and snacks. Kai said his flashlight was not working, so the assistant added new batteries to the list. His friends jumped into the chat with thumbs-up. Kai asked the assistant to send the list to the whole group, and it did.

Tomas was a driver on an early run, and the cold morning made his eyes heavy. He did not want to rush, so he waited patiently at a red light and said to the car, "I am so sleepy, and I have a long road ahead." The assistant understood that he wanted something to wake him up. It found a coffee shop on the road, five minutes away, and asked if he wanted it strong. Tomas said strong, with a little sugar. The assistant sent the order ahead and told him it would be ready at the window. Tomas also asked it to remind him to buy a jar of jam for his mother on the way home, and the assistant added that to his list for the evening.

Lena was a busy parent working at her laptop while the kids watched a movie. She said to the assistant, "Create a new folder called School Forms on my desktop. No, wait, put it inside Documents." The assistant understood the correction and made the folder in Documents, not on the desktop. Then Lena asked it to move the three files about the school trip into the folder. The assistant moved them and said the folder had three files now. A moment later, the lid of the laptop was half closed and the screen went dark. The battery was low. Lena asked, "How much battery do I have left?" The assistant said twelve percent. She plugged in the charger. On the TV, the kids were watching a movie about a plane, and she smiled.

name: gift_idea_finder
does: Suggests gift ideas for a person based on their age, what they like and how much you want to spend.
inputs: who the gift is for, their interests, and a price limit
people say:
- what should I get my dad for his birthday
- I need a present for a ten-year-old who loves bikes
- something nice under thirty dollars
- my aunt is always in pain from her back, so what would show her I care
- ideas for a friend who lives near me and likes baking
- gifts for a person who has everything

Errands are the small jobs you do outside your home or desk, like mailing a letter, going to the bank or picking up a parcel. A post office or a bank is open only at certain hours, so people check before they go. A busy person plans the stops in a sensible order, with heavy things last so nothing gets in the way. People say, what time does the post office close, plan my errands for the afternoon, remind me to pick up the package, or take the bank off my list. When they finish one, they say, mark that done. Small fixes at home, like a dripping faucet, go on the list too, with a note to call someone.

They want to know where their package is.
Where's my parcel?
Track my package
Package status?
Has my order shipped yet?
Connect me to the tracking page for my order
Set an alarm for when the parcel arrives
That box is high priority for me, so tell me how far away it is
Could you tell me if the parcel I ordered last week has left the warehouse? I've been waiting a long time.

They want to divide a number into equal parts.
Split 120 by 4
What is one hundred twenty divided by four?
120 over 4 people?
How much does each person pay if four people share a large bill of 120?
Divide 120 four ways and repeat the answer slowly
If the people at dinner tonight at eight all pay the same, what is a quarter of 120?
Could you please work out what 120 comes to when it's cut into four equal shares?

They want to know what food is in the house.
Fridge check
What's in the fridge?
Do we have milk?
What have we got left to eat?
List the food in the kitchen
I'm angry at myself for forgetting, did we run out of eggs again?
Before I weigh the flour for baking, do we have enough sugar?
My son plays on the game console all day and eats everything, so what snacks are left?

Person: I'm going on a trip and I want to know if my money will go far there. How much is a hundred dollars?
Assistant: Which currency do you want to compare it with?
Person: Pounds. I'd like to show the kids what things cost.
Assistant: Today a hundred dollars is about seventy-nine pounds.
Person: That's less than I hoped. What about double that?
Assistant: Two hundred dollars is about one hundred fifty-eight pounds.
Person: Good. Can you send the money to my sister so she can mix it in with her trip money?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send money. I can only tell you the rates and keep a safe note of them.

They want to know how much longer something must stay in the oven.
How much longer for the cake?
Time left on the bake
The top is still pale, how long should it stay in?
My cookies are not set in the middle yet, when will they be done?
Tell me when the loaf is ready to come out
The cream on top is still wet, so how much more time does it need?
The kitchen smells great, but I think the cake isn't done, so when should I check it again?
I have to pack up for the party at six, so how much longer does the bread need?

They want to tell the delivery driver where to leave a parcel.
leave the parcel at the front door
ask the driver to put it by the gate
Please have them leave the box next to the recycling bins, not at the door
leave my pakage with the neighbor
I need it early, can you ask them to come before nine?
Put a note on my order: no signature, just drop it
Could you please send a note to the driver? I'm out all day and I need the box left with the doorman.

name: group_speakers
does: Joins two or more speakers so they play the same music, or splits them back into separate ones.
inputs: which speakers to join, or which group to divide
people say:
- play the music in every room
- put the kitchen and the living room together
- I want the song on the balcony speaker too
- divide the speakers back into single rooms
- keep the sad movie music in the bedroom only
- make the whole house play at once

Nina was a busy parent standing at the park while her daughter played on the swings. She was nervous, because the school nurse had called twice and she had missed both calls. She said to her phone, "Call the school back, and turn the volume up a lot more, I can't hear anything over the kids." The assistant understood she wanted to call the school and make the sound louder. It raised the volume to full and dialed. The nurse said her son had a cold and had sneezed all morning, and he needed to go home. Nina asked the assistant to put the call on speakerphone so she could carry her bag. Then she asked it to text her husband to pick up the boy, since he was closer. Her husband wrote back that he was on his way, and Nina let out a long breath.

Jo was a teenager with a sore tooth. At breakfast, with a bowl of cereal going soggy, he texted his phone, "book me a dentist this week, but not on wednesday, i have a test." The assistant understood that it should find a visit on any day except Wednesday. It checked the clinic near his house and told him there were openings on Tuesday at four and Thursday at ten. Jo said he did not want to miss school, so he chose Tuesday at four. The assistant booked it and put it in his calendar. Jo asked it to tell him the clinic's opening hours too. It said they opened at eight and closed at six. Jo sent back a thumbs-up and ate his cereal on the other side of his mouth.

Rosa was chopping green onions when she remembered last night's match. She dried her hands and spoke to the kitchen speaker. "Excuse me, could you please read me the sports results from last night? I am cooking for my whole family, and my brother will ask about the score the moment he walks in, so I would like to know it before he does." The speaker understood that she wanted last night's sports results read aloud. It found the scores and began to deliver them in a calm voice. The home team had won by two goals. Rosa smiled and her whole body relaxed, because now she could tell her brother the news first. She went back to her onions with a happy hum.

Grandpa Leo could not sleep on Saturday night. At ten o'clock he picked up his phone and said, "Wake me at seven on Sunday, and let me stay in bed a little if I am tired." The phone understood that he wanted an alarm for seven in the morning with a snooze. It set the alarm for seven and a snooze of twenty minutes, and it told him so in a clear voice. Leo's feet felt frozen, so he pulled a thick blanket over them. He thanked the phone, put it on the table and closed his eyes. A few minutes later he was asleep.

Someone wants to know if the front door is locked.
Is the front door locked?
Check my front door, please.
Did I lock up?
I left in a hurry and now my phone is all I have. Is the door shut tight?
Tell me if the back door is locked too, and check the garage twice.
I will not earn any peace of mind unless I know the house is secure.
Be careful and look at every lock for me before I go to bed.
Is the door open or closed right now?
Could you please tell me whether the front door is locked, and if it is not, lock it?

Dana was packing lunches when her phone buzzed with an urgent news alert. "Read me the headlines about the bank loan rates," she said. Then she changed her mind. "No, sorry, I meant the local news, not the money news." The assistant understood the fix. It dropped the bank headlines and gave her three local stories instead: a road was closed near the school, a fair would be held on Saturday, and a new bus line would start next month. Dana listened while she cut the sandwiches in half. When it finished, she thanked the assistant and zipped up the lunch bags.

Walter burned his hand on the stove. He did not know what to do, and he was not good with his phone. He held it up and said, "Burn help." The assistant understood that he had a burn and wanted first aid steps. It told him to hold the burn under cool running water for ten minutes. Walter had a bag of frozen peas in the freezer and wanted to put them on his hand. The assistant said not to use ice or frozen things on a burn, and to bathe the burn in cool water instead. Walter did that, and the pain slowly got better. Then the assistant asked if he wanted to call a doctor.

Someone wants to join a video call.
Join my call.
Get me into the ten o'clock meeting.
Open the team call, please.
I'm in the car park buying milk and I'm late. Can you connect me to the meeting?
Start the call link from my calendar.
Put me in the call with the sound off.
Could you please join the budget meeting for me? I am about to lock my laptop and I would like to take the call on my phone, because my pricey headset is in my bag and I cannot reach it.
I need to be in the meeting in two minutes. Dial in now.

A bike route is a path from one place to another that is good for riding. People use routes to plan a ride, and many apps design one for you. You can change a route in simple ways. You can ask for a shorter ride, a flatter ride, or one with fewer big roads. You might say, "Plan a flat ride of ten miles," or "Keep me off the busy streets." During the ride you can ask, "How far have I gone?" or "How fast am I going?" Mia keeps a pencil note on her fridge with her best times. A crispy autumn morning is her favorite time to ride.

Someone wants to move a meeting to a later time.
Push my two o'clock to three.
Move the team meeting back an hour.
Can we do the dentist visit later in the day?
I am stuck in traffic and will miss my two o'clock.
Try to find a new time for the call, and send an update to everyone.
My afternoon is a mess. Could the meeting wait until tomorrow?
If you can, make the change automatic, so that the others are told right away.
Please shift my four o'clock meeting to five, as I have another thing on.

name: filter_check
does: Tells you if the air purifier filter needs to be wiped or replaced, so the whole house keeps clean air.
inputs: which purifier or room, and how long the filter has been in use
people say:
- Is my purifier filter still good?
- The air smells stale, does the filter need changing?
- My neighbor says a filter should be changed every three months. Is mine due?
- Does the machine in the bedroom need cleaning?
- When did I last change the filter downstairs?
- Tell me if the filter has gotten too dirty.

Person: Put a task on my list.
Assistant: What should the task say?
Person: Call the wifi company about the slow connection.
Assistant: Done. Do you want a due date?
Person: Yes, Friday. Actually, make it Thursday. I have too many things to do on Friday.
Assistant: I changed it to Thursday.
Person: Can you call them for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't make phone calls. I can remind you at nine on Thursday, if you like.
Person: Yes, please get me that reminder.

inputs: how long you need, and which days to look at
people say:

- I need something to lift my week. Is there a quiet evening?
- Find me a single hour to listen to my audiobook.
- Do I have any gaps on Thursday?
- Where can I fit a long lunch with my sister?
- Show me when nothing is planned.

Person: I want to plan a dinner for the holiday.
Assistant: Which holiday, and how many people are coming?
Person: New Year's Eve. Six people. I just moved here, so I don't know anyone yet. These are my new neighbors.
Assistant: That sounds nice. Would you like a shopping list?
Person: Yes. We will make a toast at midnight, and everyone will be hungry by nine.
Assistant: I made a list with bread, cheese, juice and a cake. Anything else?
Person: Remind me tomorrow at seven to wash the good plates.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you tomorrow at seven.

Someone wants the living room to get warmer.
Warm up the living room.
Make it hotter in here.
Brr, it's cold.
Please turn the heat up to twenty-two degrees.
My toes are like ice. Can you do something about it?
Could you please warm up the living room fast? My hands hurt from the cold, and I want to sit down with a slice of melon and read.
Raise the temperature a few degrees.
I'm freezing, so get the radiator going.

name: leak_alert
does: Sends you a message when water is found where it should not be, so your home stays cozy and dry.
inputs: which room or pipe to watch, and who should get the message
people say:
- Is water leaking under the kitchen sink?
- I just got off the bus and I think the floor is wet at home.
- Something is dripping in the basement.
- Tell me right away if a pipe starts to leak.
- The ceiling has a damp spot. Is there a problem?

Priya stood by the open window, stirring soup, when her son shouted that he was hungry. She still had to make the rice. "Tell me how long to cook the rice and set a timer for it," she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted two things. First it said that white rice takes about fifteen minutes. Then it set a timer for fifteen minutes and told her it had started. Priya had borrowed her neighbor's big pot, and she wanted to give it back clean. She smiled, turned down the heat, and wiped the table while the rice cooked.

Tom's uncle was mowing the lawn outside while Tom made pasta for the final dinner of the visit. His hands were full of flour, so he spoke to his phone. "Pasta time?" he asked. The assistant understood that he wanted to know how long to cook pasta. It said that dried spaghetti takes about ten minutes, and it offered to start a timer. Tom said yes. When the timer went off, the uncle came in with a green stain on his shoes, and the two of them sat down to eat.

name: first_aid_steps
does: Reads out simple steps for a small injury, one step at a time.
inputs: what happened, and where on the body it hurts
people say:
- I fell off my scooter and my knee is bleeding.
- Read me what to do for a cut.
- My finger got stuck in the door.
- What do I do when a bandage gets wet?
- My son has a scrape on his elbow. What now?
- How do I take care of a small burn?

Gus smelled smoke from burnt toast and gave up on cooking. He was tired and wanted to rest. He picked up his phone and typed, "order my usal pizza from luigis". The assistant understood that "usal" meant "usual". It found the pizza that Gus had ordered last time, a large one with mushrooms, and it asked him to confirm. Gus pressed yes. The assistant placed the order and said it would arrive in about thirty minutes. Gus opened a window to let the smoke out and sat down to wait.

Jo, a student, needed a haircut before her interview, but she had little money. She told her phone, "Book me a haircut for Saturday, and find a place that costs half as much as my last one." The assistant understood that she wanted a cheaper salon and a Saturday time. It looked at the shops nearby and found one that charged half the price. It booked ten o'clock on Saturday and put it on her calendar. Jo was also waiting for a parcel to ship, so she asked the assistant to move the haircut to the top of her list of things to do. It did, and she felt much better.

Ben was late for the bus, with a pot of soup still cooking at home and his bag half open. He pushed in his earbuds and said, "Keep my book going, but at one and a half speed, and tell me how many chapters are left." The assistant understood two things. It started the audiobook where he had stopped and made it play faster. Then it said that there were four chapters left. Ben was happy to hear that. He listened to the body of the story all the way to work, and he only remembered the soup when he got off the bus.

Someone wants to know when the recycling is collected.
When is bin day?
Is the recycling picked up this week?
The bin is full and the smell is bitter. Is it collection day soon?
I need to sort my trash before tomorrow. When do the trucks come?
Tell me which day the blue bin goes out.
The street looks empty of bins. Did I miss the pickup?
Could you please let me know when the next recycling collection is? My old toaster and a pile of boxes are in the hall.
What day do they take the paper?

Hiro was driving to work, stuck in traffic and bored. His nine o'clock call was about to start. He said to the car, "Join my nine o'clock call, but do not turn on the video." The assistant understood that he wanted to be in the call with his camera off. It dialed in and told him that he was connected with the video off. A coworker asked how his workout had gone, and Hiro began to talk about it. The cars started to move again, and he kept his eyes on the road.

Lena, a student, jumped out of bed and saw that it was bright outside. Her fish tank sat by the window, and she wanted some personal quiet to study. "Open the blinds halfway and close the curtains on the left window," she said. The assistant understood that she wanted both things done. It opened the blinds to the middle and closed the left curtains, and then it told her it was finished. The light fell on the tank, and the fish swam around. Lena opened her book and began to read.

Sam unlocked his car and sat down. He typed fast into his phone, "play the jazz stasion on the radio". To be safe, he waited until the car was parked and still before he sent it. The assistant understood that "stasion" meant "station". It found the jazz station and started to play it through the car speakers. His favorite band was on, and Sam turned up the sound a little. When he was ready to drive, he put the phone down and pulled out onto the road.

Mara owned a small shop, and a poster of a forest hung on its wall. One morning she heard a strange noise from the heater. She sighed a deep sigh and said to her phone, "Please book someone to fix the shop heater, and I want the same person who came twenty-five days ago." The assistant understood that she wanted a repair for the heater and the same worker as before. It looked at her past bookings and found his name. Then it booked him for Tuesday at noon. Mara asked if he could lift the heavy cover too, and the assistant added a note for him.

Ana had spent the day working in the garden. She had tied up the tomato plants and her back was sore. At night she said to her phone, "Wake me at six, but do not use the loud alarm. And don't let me forget to turn off the electric blanket." The assistant understood that she wanted a soft alarm and a reminder. It set a gentle wake-up sound for six in the morning, and it set a reminder to turn off the electric blanket at ten. Ana smiled, put her phone down and fell asleep quickly.

name: pool_care_helper

people say:

- Teach me how to cover the pool for the night.
- The kids dropped a juicy peach in the water. Is it dirty now?
- I need to buy chemicals at the pool store. What do I need?
- Why is the water cloudy?
- How hot is the hot tub right now?

Person: Make me a cup of tea.
Assistant: How strong would you like it?
Person: Strong. No wait, medium. My team of grandkids says I drink it too strong.
Assistant: Medium it is. Should I start it now?
Person: Yes. Can you plug in the kettle?
Assistant: I can't plug it in myself, but if the kettle is on a smart plug, I can switch it on. Is it?
Person: Yes, it is. Most mornings I use that one.
Assistant: Then I turned it on. Your tea will be ready in a few minutes.

Someone wants a reminder to do something later.
Remind me at six.
Let me know at six to start dinner and to turn off my audiobook.
Ping me when it's time for the bread.
Make sure I remember to call mom tonight and to pay the rent.
I want to be up bright and early, so nudge me at six tomorrow.
Could you please tell me at five to take the medicine, and remind me again an hour later?
Don't let me forget the meeting at ten.
When I get home, remind me to feed the cat.

Someone wants to change a measurement from one unit to another.
How many grams is a cup of flour?
Cups to grams, please.
The bakery scale shows ounces. What is that in grams?
Half a pound is how many ounces?
My recipe says a cup, but I only have a scale.
I don't want to pay for a wrong measurement, so tell me how many centimeters are in double this twelve inches.
Could you please change twenty degrees Celsius to Fahrenheit?
What is more, a kilo or two pounds?

Your files and folders hold your work on a computer. A file is one piece of work, like a letter or a photo, and a folder is a place where files are kept together. If the computer feels slow, it may have too many programs open, and restarting it often helps. People can also tag files with a word, like "school" or "bills", to find them again fast. When they want help, they say things like, "Open my tax folder," "Make the screen brighter," or "Restart the computer." They might ask, "How much battery is left?" or "Where did I put that file?"

Maya had just woken up and her head was still foggy. Coffee was her morning fuel, but the kettle was not on yet. She looked at her phone and said, "Good morning. I am sorry to ask so early, but could you please look at my calendar and tell me what I have today? I have a new job, and I do not want to be late for my first meeting." The assistant understood that she wanted her day read to her. It began to search her calendar and found two events: a team meeting at nine and lunch with a friend at one. Maya sat up. She thanked the assistant and got out of bed.

someone wants to book a table at a restaurant.
book a table for four.
reserve me a spot for tonight at seven
i want a table outside in the fresh air, can you do that?
can you find somewhere delicious that is open late?
dont hide the menu from me, show me what they have, and book a tabel for two
get us seats at the pizza place on saturday
Could you please call the Thai restaurant and reserve a table for six people at eight tomorrow?
anything open near me with a free table now?

Kofi had just moved to the city and had little money. He sat at his kitchen table with a pile of bills. "Hello, could you please help me make a monthly budget? I just started a new job, and I have a hobby that costs a lot, so I want to see where my money goes." The assistant understood that he wanted to plan his spending. It asked how much he earned and then listed his rent, food and bills. Then it saw that the hobby took a big piece. Kofi looked at the numbers, took a deep breath, and tried to crack a smile. He felt that he could finally manage.

The news is a way to hear what is going on near you and around the world. Many people ask for headlines in the morning, or for the sports results. Some people want only local stories, and some want a certain topic, like weather, music or food. You can ask for fewer stories or for more. You can also block a topic you do not want to hear about. People say things like, "What's in the news?", "Read me the sports scores," or "Don't show me stories about celebrities." On a freezing morning, many people also ask if the roads are safe.

Mrs. Bell was not good with her phone. A message popped up that said the storage was full. She spoke to it. "Please help me. I need to make room for photos of my grandchildren." The assistant understood that she wanted to free up space. It filtered her videos to show only the old ones, and found twenty-five that she had not opened for a year. It asked if she wanted to delete them, and she said yes. One was a video of a humid summer day at the beach, but she knew she had a plan to keep the photos safe. The assistant cleared the space, and Mrs. Bell smiled.

Jun was kneading dough when he remembered the bake sale. His hands were sticky, so he typed with one finger, "how long to let bred rise". The assistant understood that he meant bread. It said that bread dough rises for about an hour in a warm place, until it has doubled in size. Jun did not blink as he set a timer for sixty minutes. The bake sale was held monthly, and this time he wanted his loaves to be the best. He covered the bowl with a cloth and went for a walk while he waited.

Someone wants to check the spelling in a letter.
Spell check.
Check spelling.
Fix my typos.
Please look for mistakes in this message.
Is there anything wrong with the words I wrote? I'm tired.
Could you please read the page on my shelf of notes and tell me which words are spelled wrong?
Make my email short and crispy, and fix any spelling too.
I can wait while you look it over for errors.

Person: Good morning. Tell me how to make eggs.
Assistant: Good morning. How would you like them, fried, boiled or scrambled?
Person: Boiled. Hmm, I'm still half asleep. Make them scrambled, please. I want something to eat before the movie tonight.
Assistant: Scrambled it is. Crack two eggs into a bowl and stir them with a fork. Cook them on low heat.
Person: They look pale. Is that okay?
Assistant: Yes. Lift them with a spoon as they cook, and take them off when they are soft and just set.

A home security system helps you feel safe when you are away or asleep. It may have cameras, door sensors and an alarm. The cameras let you see who is at the door, and a motion sensor can tell you if someone moves in a room that should be empty. The idea is simple: you set it when you leave and turn it off when you come back. People use words like, "Turn on the alarm," "Show me the front door camera," or "Let me know if anything moves tonight." Some people ask the total number of times the door opened that day.

A workout is a plan for moving your body, and it is made of exercises. Each exercise is done in sets, and each set has a number of reps. For example, ten push-ups, then a rest, then ten more is two sets. Rest days are also important, because muscles need time to grow. People change workouts by making them longer, shorter, easier or harder. They say, "Give me a short workout," "Add another set," or "Explain this exercise again." My brother likes to train early, when the sky is still dark, and he always asks what comes next.

A podcast is a show that comes in episodes, and an audiobook is a book that is read to you in chapters. Your device remembers where you left off, so you can start again later. Many people change the playback speed, so a show goes faster or slower. They say things like, "Play the next episode," "Skip back thirty seconds," or "Go back to where I was." Some people listen while they clean the carpet or while a roast cooks in the oven. If a show does not work well, you can ask to go to another one.

Kim, a student, was nervous about a call with her cousin in Tokyo. She tied her scarf around her neck and pointed at the clock on her phone. "What time is it in Tokyo, and when should I call so it is not too late for her?" she asked. The assistant understood that she wanted two things. First it said that it was three in the afternoon in Kim's town, and eight the next morning in Tokyo. Then it said that a call at seven in the evening would be a good time. Kim thanked it and felt less nervous.

Someone wants to know how long to bake a chicken.
how long for chicken in the oven
what temp for a whole chicken?
I want to win dinner tonight. How long do I roast a chicken?
when will my chiken be done?
Tell me the time and the heat for a chicken, and what to serve as a snack.
Could you please tell me how long to cook a chicken? My family only does this big meal yearly, and I want it to be right.
Give me the oven steps for a roast chicken.

Grandma Ruth came home from the store in the van and felt hot and tired. The house was freezing in winter, but in summer it was like an oven. "Turn on the fan in the living room and tell me when it is cool enough to open the windows," she said to the speaker. The assistant understood that she wanted two things. It switched on the fan, and it checked the room's temperature. When the room reached twenty-three degrees, it told her. Ruth sat down with a glass of water and let the cool air return to the room.

Grandpa Joe sat at his desk with a cup of bitter coffee. He needed to send an invoice to a customer before the meeting. "Open the video call for ten o'clock and show me my last invoice," he said to the tablet. The assistant understood that he wanted two things. It opened the call link, and it put the last invoice on the screen. Joe checked the numbers and pressed send. When the meeting began, he said thank you to everyone for joining. The call went well, and he finished his coffee.

Gus, a gardener, wanted to see a dentist. He said to his phone, "Book me with Dr. Lee on Monday at ten." Then he looked at his window and saw the rain. "No, wait, Tuesday. I have a long job on Monday." The assistant understood that he wanted to fix the day. It changed the booking to Tuesday at ten and repeated the details back to him: Dr. Lee, Tuesday, ten o'clock. Gus said that was right. He put on his boots and went out to water the plants.

Mr. Park was a retired teacher who liked to bake. He had a jog planned for the morning and wanted to make his favorite cake after. "Tell me how long the cake takes, but I don't want the recipe with nuts," he said to the speaker. The assistant understood that he wanted the baking time and a cake without nuts. It said that a plain sponge cake takes about thirty-five minutes at one hundred and eighty degrees. It did not read the nut recipe. Mr. Park said that he would take care to turn the oven on after his jog.

Nina was eight, and she was hungry. Her mom was out, and the kitchen was closed to her except for the table. She wore her old jeans and held her tablet in both hands. She typed fast, "how do i maek toast". The assistant understood that she wanted to make toast. It told her in simple steps to ask a grown-up to help with the toaster. Nina wanted to train to be a good cook one day, so she watched. Her dad came in and put the bread in. Soon it popped up, and Nina spread jam on it.

name: unread_mail_reader

people say:
- Did anyone write to me this morning?
- Read me the email from the man about the hedge.
- Do I have new mail?
- What came in while I was out?
- Show me the black marked messages first.

name: summer_playlist_maker
does: Builds a playlist of upbeat songs for a party or a backyard barbecue.
inputs: the mood or event, and how long the playlist should be
people say:
- Something happy for the cookout, please
- Put on songs for the ball game party
- I'm going to grill tonight, get me some good music
- Make a mix about two hours long, nothing too slow
- Brown Sugar has to be in there, so build it around that

name: takeaway_order_helper
does: Places a takeaway order at a restaurant and says when it will be ready.
inputs: the restaurant, the dishes, and a pickup time
people say:
- I want food to go from the noodle place
- Get me one small coffee and a sandwich to take away
- Have my usual ready at six
- Please load my last order again, same as Friday
- Order two soups for pickup in half an hour

In autumn the weather gets cooler, and many people start to care about temperature numbers. A thermometer shows how warm or cold it is, and most places use either Celsius or Fahrenheit. If you grew up with one and then visit a place that uses the other, the numbers look strange. A weather app can change the scale for you. People ask things like switch the temperature to Fahrenheit, show me degrees Celsius, or how much is sixty degrees in Celsius. The app will reply with the new number, and the setting stays that way until you change it back. A closed window and a warm coat are easier to choose when the number makes sense to you.

A kettle is for heating water fast. Some homes have an old boiler tucked in a cupboard that heats water for the whole house, but a kettle only heats what you need for a cup of tea. Most kettles let you choose a temperature, because green tea likes cooler water and coffee likes it almost boiling. People change the setting by saying make it hotter, set it to eighty degrees, or keep it warm for ten minutes. A smart kettle may also let you ask to start it from the sofa. Add a spoon of honey if you like your tea sweet, and turn the kettle off when you are done.

They want a reminder to pack the kitchen.
Remind me to pack the kitchen
Kitchen boxes, remind me please
Can you nudge me to wrap the dishes this weekend?
Post a note in the family channel so everyone remembers the kitchen still needs packing
Remind me tomorrow to wrap the plates and to throw out the stale crackers
I keep forgetting, so would you shuffle the kitchen to the top of my moving list?
It is almost moving day and the cupboards are still full, so could you please remind me on Thursday evening to start packing them?

When you shop or travel, a price may be in a different money than the one you use. An exchange rate tells you how much of your money you get for one unit of theirs. Rates move a little every day. Say you see a scooter for nine hundred euros on a website and you pay in dollars. You need the rate to know the real price. People ask how much is that in dollars, what is the rate today, or show the prices in pounds. An app can reduce the confusion by showing both prices side by side. A fast look at the rate before you pay can save you from a surprise on your card bill.

name: room_air_booster

inputs: the room, and how strong or how long
people say:
- The air in here is stuffy
- Run the purifier in the bedroom for an hour
- I'm going to tidy the garage, so clear the dust out of the air
- The kids have a piano lesson in the den, keep the air fresh in there
- Switch the new filter fan to high

Priya got home from the hospital at eight in the morning after a long night shift. Her feet hurt and her eyes were heavy. She dropped her bag by the door and said to the speaker, "Find me a funny movie for tonight and tell me when the cinema down the road opens on Saturday." The assistant understood that she wanted two things: a comedy to watch and the Saturday opening time of the nearby cinema. It named three comedies and said the cinema opens at ten. Priya said the second film sounded perfect, so the assistant saved it to her watch list. Then she made tea so strong she could almost taste the leaves, glanced at the heating meter in the hall, and fell asleep on the sofa before the kettle had cooled.

name: yarn_planner

inputs: the thing to make, its size, and your knitting speed
people say:
- How much wool do I need for a tall scarf?
- I'm making a hat for my niece, what should I buy?
- Will three balls be enough for a baby blanket?
- How long will a sweater take if I knit slowly?
- Plan something to suit my taste, soft and green

Booking a hotel room means choosing a place, the nights you will stay, and how many guests are coming. The hotel asks for a name for the booking, and you show it at check-in, usually in the afternoon. Some places near airports offer hourly rooms for a short rest, but most charge by the night. People change a booking by saying move it one night later, add a guest, or put it under my sister's name. If you would rather camp, a tent has no check-in at all, but the ground is a lot harder.

Omar was late for his sister's wedding, still holding the iron he had used on his shirt. He cleared a small cough and said to his phone, "Excuse me, would you please take a picture of the cake table and send it to my mum, because she is sick at home today and she will be so sad if she misses it?" The assistant understood that he wanted a photo of the cake table and that it should go to his mum. The room was not very light, so it turned on the flash, took the picture, and sent it to the contact named Mum. Then it told Omar the photo was sent. He smiled, put down the iron, and ran for the car.

Greta knelt in the flower bed with a garden fork stuck in the soil. Her hands were too muddy to touch anything, and she wanted to wash them before using her phone, but rain was coming. So she typed with one knuckle: "play the local nwes on the radio, im busy". The assistant understood that she wanted the radio on, tuned to the local news station. It tuned in, and the news began to play from the phone on the garden table. A voice talked about road works and a village fair. Greta dug a round hole for the new rose and listened. When the weather report came on, she was glad she had asked, because it said rain would start at noon. She finished fast and went in to wash.

Sam was already pulling on his coat when he spoke to the kitchen display. "Tell me how much water we used this week and turn the water heater down, I have to run!" The assistant understood two requests: report the weekly water use, and lower the heater's temperature. It said the house used about two thousand litres, which was good news because it was less than last week. Then it lowered the heater from sixty to fifty degrees and said it was done. Sam heard that the bill could drop by a few dollars a month, nodded, and left. The display also showed the use rise for a moment, since the dishwasher had just started.

When you order food for delivery, you pick a place, choose your dishes, and give an address. The app shows when the food should arrive, and you can follow the driver on a map. People change things by saying make the order bigger, leave off the onions, deliver it later, or add a tip for the driver. A sandwich shop might ask if you want it cut in half. Kids may sing when the doorbell rings, and everyone is glad when the food comes hot. If it is late, people say where is my order or how much longer.

They want the call link opened for a meeting tomorrow at ten.
Join my call tomorrow at ten
Open the ten o'clock meeting link
Put the team call on my screen when it starts tomorrow
Can you open tomorrow's call at ten so the young designers can join and draw on the shared board?
I need to be on that video meeting tomorrow morning, ten sharp
Get everything in order and open the link before the call tomorrow at ten
Would you please start the meeting tomorrow at ten and let me know once everyone is in?

Dana was buckling her belt after a long day when her phone buzzed. She was cooking, with a child on each leg, so she said, "Read me the new text from school, and then reply that I will pick up Mia at four-thirty." The assistant understood that she wanted the message read out loud and a short answer sent back. It read that the school's monthly newsletter was out and that Mia needed a hat for the trip. Then it sent her reply. Dana said, "Mark that one as read, and remind me in twenty-five minutes to find the hat." The assistant marked the text as read and set a reminder for twenty-five minutes later.

Person: I want to go for a bike ride tomorrow. Can you find me a route?
Assistant: Happy to help. How far would you like to ride?
Person: Not too far. Half of what I did last week.
Assistant: I don't have last week's ride in front of me. How many kilometres was it?
Person: Oh dear. About twenty, I think.
Assistant: Then I'll look for a ten kilometre route. Should it go by the lake?
Person: Yes please. Is the water frozen this week?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't tell if the lake is frozen. I can show you the route and the weather, though.
Person: That's fine. Can you share the route with my son?
Assistant: Done, I sent it to him. Take extra water.

Lena stirred the pasta with one hand and held a can of tomatoes with the other when the phone buzzed on the counter. It was her mother, who often calls at dinner time. Lena could not pick up, so she said, "Answer on speaker, and then play the voicemail from this morning." The assistant understood both parts. It answered the call on the speaker so Lena could talk while she cooked. When the call ended, it played the voicemail, which was only twenty seconds long. Her mother had said that she would visit on Sunday. Lena laughed, said she would look forward to it, and went back to the pasta.

They want a notification when it is time to start their workout.
Notify me when it is time to exercise
Workout reminder at six
I sat all day and my legs feel like wood, so I should move soon
Tell me at half past five that I'm meant to be at the front of the yoga class
I had too much melon at lunch and feel heavy, so get me up around five
Hey, ping me before the gym closes tonight
It would be great if you could notify me an hour before leg day so that I can eat something light first

Bread rises because yeast makes tiny bubbles in the dough. Bakers wait until the dough is twice as big, then put it in a hot oven. People change a recipe by asking for more time, a hotter oven, or a smaller loaf. They say things like let it rise for another half hour, bake it ten minutes longer, or set the oven to two hundred degrees. In a small flat with a cold kitchen, you may need to organize a warm spot for the dough, such as the downstairs bathroom, a place near a radiator, or a sunny balcony. A timer helps, and an assistant can set one when you say wake me when the dough is ready.

Ravi had been in the city for only two days. His hotel heater was broken and the morning was freezing, so he dressed in two jackets and stood on the corner with his phone. He typed fast in lowercase: "get me a taxi to the midle of town please". The assistant understood that he wanted a ride to the city centre. It booked a taxi, said the pickup point was the bus stop across the street, and told him the car would come in six minutes. Ravi walked to the stop, found the white car, and was warm again before he reached the middle of the old town.

Hana's daughter had a Spanish quiz, and the sun was going down while Hana peeled carrots. She said to the speaker, "Tomorrow at seven I want to wake her up in Spanish, so how do I say good morning, my love?" The assistant understood that she wanted a Spanish phrase and some practice with it. It said buenos días, mi amor, and then repeated it slowly twice so that Hana could hear how it should sound. It was patient when she got the first word wrong. Then it offered to set an alarm for tomorrow at seven, and Hana said yes.

Leo was eight, and he sat at the kitchen table while the smell of garlic filled the room. Grandma had just visited and he wanted her number saved. He typed on the tablet in a hurry: "add grandma to my contacts her numbr is 555 0142". The assistant understood that he wanted a new contact named Grandma with that phone number. It saved her and asked if it should also save her birthday. Leo said not yet. Grandma lived far away and phone calls were expensive, so he planned to send her pictures instead. The bread in the oven had started to rise, and Dad called him to wash his hands.

Ben had a cold and a sore nose, and he was rushing for the train when he remembered his hair. He lowered his voice, because the carriage was quiet, and said to his phone, "Please book a haircut at the barber on Mill Street tomorrow at four." The assistant understood that he wanted an appointment at that barber at four the next day. It checked the opening hours, found that the shop was free at that time, and booked it. It told him the haircut was set for tomorrow at four and offered to remind him an hour before. Ben said yes, since his whole week was already full.

Mr. Alvarez was a retired teacher, and hiking was his favourite hobby. On Friday morning he typed into his phone with quick fingers: "whats the wether on the top of ridge trail saturday". The assistant understood that he wanted the Saturday forecast for the ridge trail, high up. It said the wind would increase in the afternoon and that it would be cold near the top, with a small chance of rain. Mr. Alvarez wrote on his list that he would start early and pack an extra jacket. Then he asked the assistant to add a hat to his packing list, and it did.

Person: Good evening. I have been on my feet in the kitchen all day and my back is sore, so would you please turn up the heating in the living room before I sit down?
Assistant: Of course. How warm would you like it?
Person: Twenty-two degrees, please. Also, the radiator by the door leaks a little. Can you fix it?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't fix a leak. I can set a reminder to call a plumber, if you like.
Person: Yes, tomorrow morning. My purse is under that radiator, so I will move it now.
Assistant: Good idea. The heating is set to twenty-two, and the reminder is set for tomorrow at nine.

A flight has a departure time, a gate, and a flight number. The board at the airport shows them in white letters, and they can change. If a plane is delayed, the time moves later and the gate may change too. People ask when does my flight leave, which gate is it, or is it on time. Before you go through security, check your bag, because customs may ask whether you carry seeds or fruit. Follow the signs to your gate and keep watching the board. If you do not want to miss an update, ask your phone to tell you when anything changes.

Mina owned a small shop and was sleepy after a late night counting stock. In the back room, a buzzer gave a signal that the washing machine had stopped. The wet shop towels needed drying. She said just two words to the smart dryer: "Start dryer." The assistant understood that she wanted the dryer turned on with its usual towel setting. It started the dryer for forty minutes and told her so. Mina wanted to learn how to set the heat herself, so she asked about it later, and the assistant showed her where the setting was.

A note is a short piece of writing you keep so you will remember something. You can type it or speak it as a voice note. People use notes for shopping lists, ideas, and things they need to know later, like a wifi password. When they want an old note, they say find my note about the trip or show notes from last week. To change one, they say add milk to the list, delete the last line, or rename it. On a snowy day you might write a note to warm up the car and find your sweater.

Mr. Okoye ran a flower shop and had to be in town soon. He said to his phone, "I do not want the bus. Show me trains that leave soon, and pay from my travel account." The assistant understood that he wanted trains only, leaving as early as possible. It showed him the trains, and the next one left at nine-forty. It said it could pay from his travel account once he picked a ticket. Mr. Okoye did not want to spend more than ten minutes waiting, so he chose the nine-forty train and the assistant bought the ticket.

Assistant: Happy to. Which photo is it?
Person: The one with paint on his nose.
Assistant: Found it. How many copies would you like?
Person: Two, I think. My printer is old, and I can smell hot ink when it works.
Assistant: That is fine. Is the printer turned on, and does it have paper?
Person: Let me look. Please be patient with me.
Assistant: Of course, take your time.
Person: Yes, it has paper and the light is green.
Assistant: Good. Two copies are printing now.

It's quiet time in this house, you know what to do
Would you mind switching off the kids' tablets now, since dinner is ready and we want to eat together?

Mr. Bell is not good with technology. Upstairs, his puppy was asleep, and he stood in the hall and spoke slowly to the speaker. "Excuse me, assistant, I am sorry to trouble you, but could you please set a timer for twenty-five minutes, because I want to write my letters without stopping and the puppy will need a walk after?" The assistant understood that he wanted a timer for twenty-five minutes. It set the timer and told him it would ring when the time was up. Mr. Bell asked how to switch the sound off, and the assistant said he could just say stop the timer.

Nina was ten, and she waited in the car with her dad's parcel on her lap. The bank next door looked dark and the day was cold. She said to the phone, "I wonder if the post office is still open, because this box has to go today." The assistant understood that she wanted to know when the post office closes. It said the post office closes at five, and since it was half past four, there was half an hour left. Nina told her dad to jump out and be quick, and he ran inside in time.

Jess texted her phone from the sofa: "looks pretty rainy for the weekend ngl". The assistant understood that she was asking about the weather at her campsite. It said Saturday would be rainy and Sunday would be dry. Jess said she would build a fire on Sunday only, since she had one block of dry wood. The assistant offered to move the trip to Sunday, and she said yes. It changed her booking to Sunday and put a rain jacket on her packing list.

They want to book movers for Saturday morning.
Book movers for Saturday
I need a van and two people on Saturday morning
Can someone come lift my boxes and sofa this weekend?
Find me a moving crew who will tie down the sofa so it doesn't slide
I'm out of here by Sunday, so find someone to carry everything
Please book a moving company for Saturday morning, because I have to hurry out of this freezing flat before the lease ends and I can't carry the boxes alone

Theo was cleaning the vacuum cleaner for his chore money when he typed fast on his phone: "whats 15 times 12 quikc". The assistant understood that he wanted two numbers multiplied. It multiplied them and said the answer was one hundred and eighty. Theo needed the number to work out what he would earn by the end of the month, so he thanked the assistant and wrote it down. Then he walked to the shop nearby to buy a snack with some of it.

They want their unread emails read out.
Read my new emails

Put the newest twenty-five emails on the screen
My pen is out of ink and my hands are full, so could you read the unread mail aloud?
I'm back online, so what did I miss?
Has anyone written to me since lunch?
Tell me if there's new mail from my boss
Could you please go through my inbox and read me whatever is still unread?

A to-do list is a place to write what you need to do, with the most important things first. The main tasks go at the top. As you finish something you check it off, and it disappears or turns grey. People change lists by saying put it first, mark it done, move it to tomorrow, or remove it. You might install a list app that keeps your phone and laptop the same. A task like sort the album photos can sit on the list until you have time for it.

Mrs. Park was folding clothes after bathing her young son when she thought out loud: "My neighbour turns forty on Saturday, and I wish I knew how to say happy birthday in Polish." The assistant understood that this was a request for the phrase. It said the words and spelled them out slowly. Mrs. Park practised twice and got it right on the second try. She said she would see the neighbour at the monthly book club, and she wanted to surprise her. The assistant added a note to her calendar so she would remember to say it.

An appointment is a time you agree to meet someone, like for a haircut or the dentist. The place has working hours, and you can only book inside them. People change an appointment by saying move it to Friday, book me a different time, or cancel it. They also ask what time does the barber open. If you sleep badly, you might dream about missing it, so a reminder helps. An assistant can send you one the day before. After the dentist, you might stop for lettuce on the way home.

A workout is a plan of exercises, with sets and reps. A set is a group of repeats, like three sets of ten. Rest days give your muscles time to recover. People change a plan by saying do fewer reps, add a set, or skip leg day. If you have a deadline at work, your plan may get shorter, so you tap the app and ask for a ten minute workout soon. People also ask what is next, how many sets are left, or give me a rest day.

A lamp or a ceiling light has a switch, a brightness, and sometimes a colour. With smart bulbs you can mix colours, from warm yellow to cool blue. People change them by saying dim the lights, make it brighter, turn the lamp red, or set a cosy evening mood. A colleague may say the office is too bright for reading, and you can lower it with one sentence. A bulb that gets very hot can be dangerous, so it is important to use the right kind of bulb for each lamp.

Grandpa Joe sat in his small boat tied to the dock. The sky was stormy, and he was trying to fish in peace, but his phone kept ringing. He shut the cabin door and said to the phone, "Do not disturb." The assistant understood that he wanted the do not disturb mode switched on. It silenced calls and messages and told him it was on. Grandpa Joe smiled, watched the grey clouds, and waited for a fish. He asked it to turn the mode off at noon, and it did.

Person: Move meeting.
Assistant: Which meeting do you mean? You have three tomorrow.
Person: The parent meeting at the school.
Assistant: The one at ten. When should I move it to?
Person: Later. My calendar is messy this week, I can't see a free time.
Assistant: Let me calculate. You are free on Thursday from two to three.
Person: Thursday at two, please.
Assistant: Done. The parent meeting is moved to Thursday at two.

Many places ask you to book a time before you come, like the doctor. You choose a day and an hour, and sometimes you upload a form or a photo of your insurance card. Pack what you need the night before. People change an appointment with words like move it a day, make it earlier, or cancel it. Sometimes a website asks strange questions, and if you are not sure, you can call. An assistant can remind you about the time so you do not forget.

name: holiday_checklist
does: Builds a checklist of decorations, food, and tasks for a holiday or party.
inputs: the holiday, the number of guests, and the place
people say:
- What do I need to hang for the Halloween party?
- The forecast looks stormy, so make an indoor list
- Tag the things I already own so I only buy the rest

Leo was eight, and the family was going to the beach. He held his red mug of milk and said to the kitchen speaker, 'Hey, can you wake me tomorrow at seven? We travel to the sea and I want to be ready early.' The speaker said okay and set an alarm for seven in the morning. Then Leo asked, 'Do I need sun cream?' The speaker checked the weather. It said the day would be sunny and hot, so it put sun cream on the packing list on his mum's phone. Leo smiled. He finished his milk, put the mug in the sink and went to find his swimming shorts. The speaker stayed quiet until the next morning, when the alarm rang at seven sharp.

Sam woke up and rubbed his eyes. His phone was on the pillow, next to a paper ticket from last week. He mumbled, 'What's on at the cinema tonight? And find the main trailer for the space film.' The phone found three films near his flat. It said the space film starts at twenty past eight. Then it played the main trailer on the screen. Sam said, 'Make it louder, my ears are still asleep.' The phone did increase the volume a bit. Sam then asked for tickets, but the assistant said it could not buy them. It opened the cinema's page instead. The page showed twenty-five seats left. Sam sat up, picked two seats and went to make tea.

A recipe tells you what to put in a dish and how long to cook it. People often change it a little. If friends are coming, they say, 'Make this for six instead of four,' and the amounts go up. If the oven is too hot, they say, 'Lower the heat by twenty degrees.' When they want to celebrate a birthday, they might ask, 'Show me a cake with fewer steps.' Cooking times matter too. A leg of lamb takes much longer than a chicken breast. A calm cook checks the clock and asks, 'How long is left?' or 'Set a timer for ten minutes.' Words like more, less, longer and shorter are how people change a recipe.

Mr. Bell was not good with phones. He stood outside the station in the rain, holding his phone like a hot potato. A quarter of an hour went by. At last he said to it, 'Taxi, please.' The phone showed a small map and asked where he wanted to go. 'Home,' he said. It knew his home address from before. It found a car that would leave the rank in four minutes and told him the price. Mr. Bell stepped under a shallow roof by the door to stay dry. Soon the phone buzzed and said a grey car was outside. The assistant read out the car's number so he could find it. He climbed in and said thank you to the phone, which made the driver laugh.

It was a cold October morning, and Mia was bored in the back seat. Dad was driving to Gran's house. Mia leaned toward the car's voice assistant and said, 'My feet are freezing.' The assistant understood that she wanted more heat. It turned the warm air toward the back seat and raised it by two degrees. Then Mia said, 'I want Gran to see my drawing.' She asked the assistant to upload the photo of her drawing to the family album. The assistant said the photo was uploaded and that Gran would get a message. Mia felt warm and not bored anymore. She watched the grey road go by and waited for the first house on the hill.

Rosa the gardener had a seed list to print. She said to her tablet, 'Print my plant list on the usual paper, two copies.' Then she stopped and said, 'No, wait, three copies. My neighbour wants one too.' The tablet changed the number to three and sent the job to the printer in the shed. The printer was out of ink, and the tablet told her so. Rosa put on her coat and said, 'Then scan the old order form instead, and delete the scan from last week.' The tablet scanned the paper she put on the glass and saved it. It deleted last week's scan and said so. Rosa nodded. She would buy ink on the way to the market.

Omar ran a small shop that sold rugs. A man left a card on the counter, and Omar wanted to save the number. His hands were full of boxes, and the lamp over the counter was too bright. He said to his phone, 'It's glaring in here, and I need this man's number saved.' The assistant understood two things. It dimmed the shop lights to half through the smart plug, and it asked, 'What name should I save?' Omar read the name from the card. The phone saved the name and the number as a new contact. It was a simple job. Omar smiled. It felt like a dream to have help at the counter. Then he got back to his boxes.

A medicine reminder helps you take the right dose at the right time. Many people use one for pills in the morning and at night. If the doctor changes the dose, they say, 'Change my evening pill to two.' If they feel better, they might say, 'Remind me less often.' Doctor visits work in a similar way. People ask, 'Move my appointment to Saturday,' or 'Tell me when the clinic opens.' When the nurse greets you, you can say how you feel. If the waiting room is dim, you might ask your phone for more screen light to read the label. Words like earlier, later, more and less are how people change a reminder.

Grandpa Joe stood in front of the open fridge. He said to the smart speaker, 'Put tomatoes on my list. Not the big ones, I don't want the big ones, just the regular kind.' The speaker added regular tomatoes to the shopping list. Then it warned him that the milk would run out tomorrow. 'Add milk too,' said Joe. 'And don't put eggs on it, I have plenty.' The speaker left the eggs off. It read the list back to him: tomatoes and milk. Joe nodded and said it was good. He shut the fridge door and went to find his walking stick and his old green shopping bag.

Priya worked in an office in London. At lunch her sister sent a photo from Paris of a blue box from a small bakery. The tag said twenty-five euros. Priya wanted to know the price at home, so she said to her phone, 'How much is twenty-five euros in pounds?' The phone looked up today's exchange rate and said it was about twenty-one pounds. It beeped softly when it was finished. 'That is pricey for a box of cakes,' Priya said. Then she asked the phone to send her sister a message: 'Save me one chocolate one.' The phone sent the message just as she said it. Priya smiled and went back to her desk.

Bea was peeling the stickers off a new shelf when her phone buzzed at the top of the screen. The battery was low. In a hurry she typed, 'turn on battary saver and dim the screen'. The phone understood. It switched on battery saver and lowered the brightness. Then she typed, 'also no calls till noon'. The phone turned on do not disturb until twelve. A man in the shop was trying out a drill, and the noise was so loud that Bea could not have heard a call anyway. She smiled and went back to the stickers. The phone told her the battery would now last another four hours.

When you park on a busy street, you often pay for the time you stay. A parking meter or a phone app counts the minutes. If you need more time, you say, 'Add thirty minutes' or 'Extend my parking.' If you want to leave early, you say, 'Stop my parking.' People also ask, 'How long do I have left?' so they do not get a ticket. A quiet street may have free spots, but a spot near the shops can burn through your money fast. A scooter often fits in a small space by the wall, and it usually costs less than a car.

Ana owned a flower shop and looked after the small lawn behind it. One foggy evening she said to her phone, 'Remind me tomorrow at seven to cut the grass.' The phone set a reminder for seven in the morning. Then she looked at the thermostat on the wall. It was too warm in the shop. 'Turn the heat down two degrees,' she said, and the phone told the thermostat to do it. Last, she asked, 'Will it be foggy tomorrow too?' The phone said yes, until about nine. Ana changed her mind and said, 'Then remind me at ten instead.' The phone moved the reminder to ten and said it was done. Ana locked up and went home.

A focus timer helps you work for a short time and then rest. Many people use twenty-five minutes of work and five minutes of break. When they feel excited and want to keep going, they say, 'Make it forty minutes.' When they are tired, they say, 'Shorter breaks, please' or 'Count down ten minutes.' A routine is a list of things you do in the same order every day. People change it by saying, 'Move lunch earlier' or 'Skip the evening walk today.' You can count how many sessions you finished, too. A student who gets a discount at the cafe after school might ask the assistant to start her break at three.

In hot weather an air conditioner or a fan keeps a room cool. The air conditioner takes warm air out and blows cooler air in. A fan only moves the air around, which feels cooler on your skin. People change the setting often. They say, 'Make it cooler,' 'Lower it two degrees,' or 'It's stuffy in here.' Some prefer a gentle breeze, so they ask for the fan on low. It is true that a cool room helps you sleep. In spring the weather changes a lot, so people turn the cooling on in the afternoon and off at night. They may say, 'Turn it off at midnight,' or 'Keep the bedroom at twenty degrees.'

Dana had just come home from a night shift, and she was very tired. Her phone calendar still showed an old meeting at the top. She typed in a hurry, 'move tomorow's meeting to friday at ten'. The assistant understood and moved the meeting to Friday at ten. Then Dana typed, 'when am i free to watch my son's match'. The assistant looked at her week. It said she would return to work on Thursday night, so Saturday afternoon was free. It asked if she wanted to save the match as an event. Dana typed, 'yes please', and the phone put it in her calendar. Then she fell asleep with the phone on her chest.

A dishwasher cleans plates while you do other things. You load it, pick a program and press start. When it finishes, it beeps. Some people want a quicker wash, so they say, 'Use the short cycle.' Others say, 'Run it tonight when the power is cheap,' or 'Add a hot rinse.' Before a holiday, they might ask for a long, strong wash. A kettle works in a similar way: you fill it, say 'Boil the water,' and it stops by itself. Don't open the dishwasher right away. The dishes are wet and hot. Wait until the beep and let them dry.

Lena finished her night shift at the hospital just as the sun came up. She walked to the car park and could not see her car. 'I'm so tired, I have no idea where I left it,' she said to her phone. The phone understood that she needed to find her car. It showed a pin on the map, on level two near the stairs. Then Lena said, 'The meter is about to run out.' The phone said her paid time ended in ten minutes and asked if she wanted to start more time. She said yes. The parking app paid for another hour at the special price for staff. Lena found the car, sat down and thought about her son's school project at home.

Tom drove a taxi, and he liked to plan his week. On Monday night he said to his phone, 'Put my first pickup on Tuesday at six in the morning, at the airport.' The phone added it to his schedule. It was a cloudy night, and Tom asked, 'Do a quick sweep of the news and tell me if the roads will be bad.' The phone read the traffic report. It said the roads were clear, but rain would come after nine. Tom thanked it and asked it to wake him at five. The phone set the alarm and said good night. In the morning the alarm rang, the sky was grey, and Tom was on his way to the airport before the first drops fell.

A phone call lets you talk to someone far away. When you cannot answer, the caller can leave a voicemail, which is a message you listen to later. People say, 'Call Mum,' 'Call back the last number,' or 'Play my voicemail.' If your hands are busy, you say, 'Put it on speaker.' You might be eating a burger at lunch and miss a call, and then you ask, 'Who called while I was eating?' Missed calls show up in a list. The voice can stream over the internet, so a weak signal can make it break up. A rare bad call can be fixed by saying, 'Call them again.'

Hassan was a delivery driver. At red lights he talked to the car's assistant. 'My sister's birthday is on Sunday. Give me a gift idea under twenty-five pounds.' The assistant suggested a thin wool scarf, a small plant or a book. 'Where can I buy a scarf?' Hassan asked. The assistant said the Saturday market near his flat sold scarves. Hassan said he would try the market on his day off, and he asked it to remind him on Saturday morning. The assistant set the reminder. It also asked if he wanted a card, and he said yes, a blue one. The light turned green, and Hassan drove on, happy that the gift was settled.

When you buy something online, the shop sends you a tracking number. You can use it to ask where your package is. The tracker shows every step: packed, sent, on the truck, delivered. People say, 'Where is my parcel?' or 'When will it come?' If it is late, they say, 'Change the delivery to Friday' or 'Send it to my work.' If the box arrives damaged, maybe because a bottle leaked in the post, you can ask for your money back. People say, 'Refund my order' or 'Send it back.' Many shops give you a whole month to return things, so there is no need to rush.

Carl drove a bus. During his break he rubbed his forehead and said to his phone, 'I feel awful, my head is pounding.' The phone understood that he might want to check his medicine. It looked at his reminders and said he had taken a pill at eight. It could not say what to do about the pain, but it told him the next dose was not due until two. Then Carl asked, 'Where is the nearest clinic?' The phone showed the clinic's location, a short walk north of the depot. It offered to say the address out loud, and Carl said yes. Then he drank some water and sat quietly until his break was over.

Assistant: Half of thirty-five is seventeen and a half.
Person: Great. Can you send that to my friend so she can pay me back?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't send money, but I can write the amount in a message for you.

A baby does best with a steady day. Feeding times and nap times help a tiny baby know what comes next. Parents often keep a simple list: milk at seven, nap at nine, milk again at eleven. When the baby is hungry sooner, they say, 'Move the next feed earlier.' When the baby sleeps longer, they say, 'Push the nap later.' A baby monitor lets a parent hear or see the baby from another room. On a morning with thick fog, when the whole house is still, a parent might ask, 'Keep the sound low but let me hear if she cries.' Small changes are made with words like sooner, later, louder and quieter.

Nina worked in an office, and her car was a fancy one that she kept very clean. After work she hurried outside, where a shower of rain was falling. Mrs. Park was a retired teacher who liked to know what was happening on her street. One evening a neighbour's dog barked without a break, and she did not want to shout over the fence. The assistant checked again and said the fair was open on Sunday too, from ten to four.

An alarm is a sound that tells you it is time to get up or do something. A timer counts down from a number you pick, like ten minutes for pasta. Most people ask for them in simple words: 'Wake me at six,' 'Set a timer for five minutes,' or 'Snooze for ten more.' You can wear a watch that buzzes on your wrist so you do not wake others. Some alarms are automatic and ring every weekday without being asked. If you want to change one, you say, 'Make it earlier,' 'Make it quieter,' or 'Turn it off tomorrow.' When your fruit is in the oven, a short timer keeps it from burning.

Rosa runs a small flower shop and she is always tired by the evening. One night she lay in bed with the window open, because the room was hot, and she could not sleep. She was afraid she would cry from tiredness in the morning. 'Wake me up tomorrow at six,' she told her phone, 'and make the sound soft, not a loud beep.' The assistant understood that she wanted an alarm for six o'clock the next morning with a gentle ringtone. It set the alarm and said, 'Your alarm is set for tomorrow at six with a soft tone.' Rosa smiled, put the phone on the table and fell asleep a few minutes later.

Omar drives a delivery van, and at lunch he eats in the parking lot with a cup of tea from his flask. It was a slow day, so he picked up his phone and typed in a hurry: whats on at the cinma tonite near me. The assistant understood that he wanted to see the films playing at cinemas close to him that evening. It read his location and showed three cinemas with their times. One of them had a daily late show at nine thirty. Omar liked that, because he would climb into the van at six and be done by eight. He asked the assistant to save the nine thirty time, and it did.

A time zone is a part of the world where all the clocks show the same hour. When you travel, or call a friend far away, the time can be very different. A huge number of people check the clock on their phone to see what time it is in another city. The phone knows where you are and sets the time by itself, so one wrong guess cannot plant a seed of trouble, and you do not have to cough up the answer from memory. People say things like, 'What time is it in Tokyo?' or 'Is it morning for my sister in Lima?' If you move to a new place, you can say, 'Change my clock to local time.' Some people also ask for a second clock, to see home and away at once.
