People count days all the time. You might want to know how many days are left until a birthday, a holiday or the end of school. You might read the date in a newspaper, or want to know how old someone is, or how many eggs are left in the fridge. A phone can do the counting for you. You choose a start day and an end day, or you give it a thing to count. Some people hate counting by hand, and a few get angry when the number is wrong. To change the answer, people say things like, 'Count from Monday instead,' 'Leave out the weekends,' or 'Add one more day.' Then the new number appears.

Mr. Hall does not like phones. He hates all the little buttons, and his granddaughter's screen looks pricey and confusing. But she had a test on Friday, and she was staying with him. 'Can you tell me when the spelling test is?' he asked the speaker in the hall, speaking slowly. 'Remind her tomorrow at seven to look at her words.' The assistant understood that he wanted a reminder for seven o'clock the next morning, about the spelling test. It said, 'I will remind you tomorrow at seven to study the spelling words.' Then the dryer buzzed in the next room. Mr. Hall smiled. It was easier than he had thought, and he had not pressed a single button.

Dana works in an office and was bored in a long meeting. She remembered that her email password was old, so she took out her phone and said, 'Change my email password to something new.' Then she stopped. 'No wait, not the email one. I mean the work chat password.' The assistant understood her correction. It said it would not touch the email, and it opened the settings for the work chat. It asked her to type the new password herself so that nobody else would hear it. Dana wrote it down on a paper tag that she kept on her belt, then she asked the assistant to unmute the meeting and turned back to her screen.

An alarm is a sound that wakes you up or tells you that time is up. People use alarms in the morning, and they use timers in the kitchen to know when the eggs are done. Both do one thing: they count down or wait for a time, and then they ring. Some people warn the phone to be extra loud if they sleep deeply. To change an alarm, people say, 'Make it ten minutes later,' 'Snooze for five more,' 'Turn it off for the weekend' or 'Set a timer for twenty minutes.' If you use the lock screen, you can often stop the sound there. If you do not need it anymore, you can cancel it for total quiet.

name: choose_vacuum_zone
does: Tells a robot vacuum which room or part of a room to clean and when to start, and it can download a new floor map that shows each cleaned area in a different color when the house changes.
inputs: the room or area, the time to start, and how strong the cleaning should be
people say:
- The kitchen floor is a mess, can you clean it now?
- Send the little robot to the hallway.
- Don't do the bedroom today, keep the door open for the cat.
- Run the vacuum every day at noon in the living room.
- Crumbs everywhere under the table, please sort it out.

name: homework_due_alert

people say:

- Remind me about the math sheet so I don't post it too late.
- What do I still have to hand in this week?
- Tell me an hour before the English essay is due.
- I feel like I forgot something for school, take a look.
- Don't let me miss the history quiz, I'll even take a pill for my headache first.

Ben is a gardener, and one cool morning he was painting a fence when he wanted a drink. He said to the kitchen speaker, 'Make me a coffee, but I don't want any sugar and no milk, just plain and strong.' The assistant understood that he wanted a black coffee with nothing added. It sent the order to the coffee machine and said, 'One strong black coffee, no sugar, no milk.' A minute later the machine began to zoom and hum. Ben wiped the paint off his hands, and he carried the cup to a neat bench in the yard. It tasted just right.

Lena woke up with her eyes half closed, and her phone buzzed on the pillow. It was her friend Mia, asking about breakfast. 'Reply to Mia and say I'll be there at ten,' Lena said. Then, after a yawn, 'No, I mean eleven. And call her honey, she likes that.' The assistant understood the correction. It changed the time from ten to eleven in the text. Then it read the message back: 'Hi honey, I'll be there at eleven.' Lena said, 'Send it.' She could hardly hear herself, but the assistant heard her well enough. The text was sent, and her phone was working fine. She went back to sleep for ten minutes.

bigger text
make the letters larger

A budget is a plan for your money. You write down how much comes in each month, and how much goes out for rent, food, bills and fun. People use a budget so that they can save a little and not run out of money before the month ends. Some months you must be careful, like in the cold season, when heating bills grow. Your phone can scan a receipt or a bill and add it to your list. To change the plan, people say, 'Give me less for snacks,' 'Put fifty into savings,' 'Show what I spent this week' or 'Move my rent date.' Then the numbers on the page change, and you can see what is left.

name: find_parking_spot
does: Looks for a free place to park near a street or building and starts a parking meter if the person wants to begin paying.
inputs: where the person is going, how long they will stay, and how far they will walk
people say:
- Where can I leave the car near the library?
- I need a spot for two hours, nothing too expensive.
- Is there any parking left by the stadium?
- Start the meter, I'm going in for a quick run to the store.
- Find me something steady and safe for the night.

Person: Put a meeting on my calendar, please.
Assistant: Sure. What day and time should it be?
Person: Tomorrow. I don't want it early, I just woke up and the room is still dim.
Assistant: Understood, not early. Would ten o'clock work?
Person: Make it eleven. It's a moment to talk with my boss.
Assistant: Okay, a meeting tomorrow at eleven. What should I write as the title?
Person: Write 'Talk with Mr. Green'.
Assistant: Done. 'Talk with Mr. Green' is on your calendar tomorrow at eleven.

Mrs. Lopez is a retired teacher, and she burned her finger on the oven in July. Her kitchen was foggy with steam, and she felt a little shaky. 'What do I do for a burn?' she asked her phone. 'Should I put butter on it?' Before it answered she said, 'No, wait, I mean cold water. My neighbor said butter is wrong.' The assistant understood the correction. It said, 'Hold the burn under cool running water for ten minutes. Do not use butter or ice.' It also offered to call for help if the burn got worse. Mrs. Lopez held her hand under the tap, and she said, 'Thank you.' The pain got a little better.

Person: Start a timer for the game.
Assistant: Sure. How long should the timer run?
Person: Twenty-five minutes. I just got home from the night shift and I want a small game with my kids before I sleep. It is the one where we buy things at a toy market.
Assistant: Okay, a timer for twenty-five minutes. Do you want a sound at the end?
Person: Yes, a soft one. And can you tell me the score of the match last night?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't see the score of your game, because I don't know the numbers. If you tell me, I can keep them.
Person: Okay, I'll say them out loud. Clear the old score too.
Assistant: Done. The old score is cleared and the timer is running.

They want help packing warm things for a night outside.
pack list for a cold night in a tent
what should I bring, it gets chilly up there
help me pack warm for camping

Should I take a black wool hat, or is that too much? What else do I need for the hills?
My sleeping bag has a cut in the wire frame and the nights are very cold, tell me what to bring
What should I wear for a night under the stars, in October?
Could you please make a list of warm things for the weekend camping trip?

close the curtains
shut the blinds pls

the sun is in my eyes

can you pull the blinds half way down, I'm about to stretch out and eat a noodle bowl in front of a movie and dont want any glare
close them, no wait, just the left window
Could you please close all the shutters? The neighbors can see in and I would like some privacy.

A workout is a plan for exercise. It might say do ten push-ups, rest for one minute, then do ten more. Each group of the same move is called a set, and each time you do the move is a rep. Rest days matter, because your body gets stronger when you stop. Do not push too hard, since a heavy weight can be dangerous if you are tired. Some people even bring a tent to the park and train outside. To change a workout, people say, 'Make it easier,' 'Add one more set,' 'Do fewer reps,' 'Stop the timer' or 'Skip today, I need a rest day.' The plan then changes to match what you said.

Writing a letter or a story usually begins with a rough draft. You put down your ideas first, and you fix the words later. A phone or computer can do the checking for you. It can fix spelling, count the words and read the text back. Even a person with a sore tooth can write a note to the dentist this way. If an email asks for you to reply by tonight, you can do it fast. To change what you wrote, people say, 'Make it shorter,' 'Use simpler words,' 'Fix my spelling,' 'Sound more polite' or 'How many words is this?' The text then changes. You can always say, 'Go back to the first version,' and your old words return, no matter how tall the pile of drafts.

Your phone does many things in the background, and the battery is the thing most people watch. When it gets low, the phone can turn on a mode that saves power. The screen gets dimmer, and some apps stop working. You can also schedule quiet hours, so that it does not ring at night. This is called do not disturb. If you get a call while it's on, the phone stays silent. People say, 'Turn on battery saver,' 'Make the screen darker,' 'Be quiet until morning,' or 'Free up space, I have no room for photos.' It may sound windy and complicated, but it is only a few words, like fertile soil for a small garden.

Sam just moved to the city and his flat felt cold, because the heater made a strange noise. 'My heater won't work right,' he told his phone. 'Can you find someone to fix it? Half of the radiators are cold, and the other half make a loud noise. I want a repair man who comes this week and doesn't cost more than fifty dollars.' The assistant understood that he needed a repair visit for a broken heater. It looked for repair shops near him and found one that charged less than fifty. It called the number, and the phone began to ring. Sam made himself a cup of bitter coffee, and a juice for dinner, and waited for an answer.

Kim woke up late and her head was still full of sleep. She picked up her phone and typed fast: set a focus timer for 25 minuts and keep the phne silent. The assistant understood her message even with the typos. It started a focus timer for twenty-five minutes and put the phone on silent mode. It said, 'Focus timer started. Notifications are off.' Kim put her toy robot on the shelf, tapped the screen to adjust the brightness, and sat down at the desk to work. When the timer ended, the phone gave a gentle chime, and she took a short break.

First aid means the small things you do to help someone who is hurt, before a doctor can see them. For a cut, you clean it and cover it. For a small burn, you hold it under cool water. If something gets in your eye, you rinse it with water and do not rub. People ask a phone what to do when they cannot sell the problem to anyone nearby, and the phone gives steps. They say things like, 'What do I do for a burn?', 'Call for help,' 'Say the steps again slowly,' or 'Is this bad enough for a doctor?' If someone is badly hurt, go away from danger and call the emergency number right away.

Ana is a nurse, and she came home at seven in the morning, very tired after a night shift. She had to write a short note for her manager, but she did not have the speed to type it. 'Write a message to my manager,' she told her phone. 'Say that I can carry the Friday shift, but I need Saturday off. And send it tomorrow at nine, not now.' The assistant understood that she wanted a short email scheduled for the next morning. It wrote the message and read it back. It checked the spelling and said, 'Your email is ready to send tomorrow at nine.' Ana nodded and went to bed.

Jo had just finished a night shift at the hospital and her eyes hurt. At home she typed on her phone, in a hurry: print my pass ticket, the wide one, and chek the ink. The assistant understood that she wanted to print a ticket and see how much ink was left. It sent the file to the printer in the hall. Then it told her, 'The black ink is low, about ten percent.' Jo said, 'Can you spell out the name of the right ink for me?' The assistant read the label name slowly, letter by letter. A dollar was all she had in her pocket, so she added ink to her shopping list instead.

A phone call is the simplest way to talk with someone who is far away. You tap a name or say it, and the phone rings the other person. If nobody picks up, you can leave a voicemail. If you miss a call, the phone shows who it was, so you can call back. People often add a friend to the list of favorites, so that a nearby tap is all it takes. Speakerphone lets many people hear the call together, like when you share an album of photos. To change a call, people say, 'Put it on speaker,' 'Turn the volume up,' 'Call him back' or 'Mute me for a second.' Then the phone does just that.

stop the beeping
turn off the alarm

Greg works in an office and his day is always busy. On Monday he had a big meeting at nine, and he was afraid he would be late. At his desk he said to the speaker, 'Set an alarm for tomorrow at seven, and call it Meeting.' The assistant understood that he wanted a morning alarm with a name. It also noticed a timer already running, one that Greg had set for his lunch. It said, 'Your seven o'clock alarm called Meeting is set. The timer for lunch is still on.' Greg closed the zipper of his bag and went home. The next day the alarm rang right on time.

Tom was in a hurry, because his dad was waiting in the car, and he had a sick feeling that he forgot his homework. He grabbed his phone and said, 'Open my math homework. How many problems are due today?' The assistant understood that he wanted the math assignment and the number of problems. It opened the file and said, 'Your math sheet has twenty-five problems and is due today at noon.' Tom said, 'Read me the first five.' The assistant read them out in a clear voice. Tom did the first one in his head, then ran to the car with the phone still in his hand.

An estimate is a guess about what something will cost. People make one before they spend money. For example, you may estimate that groceries for a week cost about eighty dollars. A good guess keeps your mouth from watering over something you cannot afford. When you plan a budget, you write the guess next to the real number and see which is more. If you spend less than planned, the extra money goes to savings. People say, 'Estimate my bills for next month,' 'Show me what I spent on food,' 'Lower the food limit,' or 'Give me less to spend on games.' The page then shows the new total.

They want the phone to start showing alerts again after a break.
turn notifications back on
resume my alerts
start the pings again

my battery is low, but I still want to know when my sister posts

I paused everything last week, please let it all come back now
Could you turn my social alerts back on for the weekend? I missed a few messages and I felt bad about it.

A meal plan is a list of what you will eat on each day. People write one so they do not have to think about dinner every evening. It also helps you buy only what you need. On Monday you might roast a chicken, and on Tuesday you use what is left in a soup. It is smart to plan simple meals for busy days. If you want to dive into the depth of it, you can add lunches and snacks. To change the plan, people say, 'No fish this week,' 'Make it cheaper,' 'Swap Tuesday and Thursday,' 'Add a vegetable dish' or 'Something light on Friday.' Then you get a new list.

Person: Read me my new email.

Assistant: He says, the meeting is moved to Thursday. Do you want to reply?

Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't change his meeting time, but I can tell him you may be late. Should I write that?
Person: Yes, send it. That old blue logo looks ugly, by the way.
Assistant: Your note is sent.

Hank is a gardener, and his small field was a few centimeters from a flood after the rain. He wanted a break at the seaside. 'Book a room for two nights from Friday,' he told the phone. 'Wait, I mean three nights. And I want a soft bed, not a hard one.' The assistant understood the change from two nights to three. It looked for rooms near the beach and picked one with a soft bed. 'A room for three nights from Friday is ready to book,' it said. 'Do you want to miss breakfast, or add it?' Hank laughed, and said to add it.

Priya was late, and when she got into her car it was freezing. 'Brr, it's so cold in here,' she said to the dashboard. The car heard her. It understood that she wanted the heat on, so it turned the warm air on and said so. Then she added, 'And I have an invitation for lunch, so I need to know if I have enough fuel.' The assistant said the tank was half full, enough for the drive. The light on the screen was bright, so she asked it to dim the display. It did. Priya pulled out of the driveway and made it to lunch in good time.

reschedule the call to tomorrow and silence everything till then

Fred is a gardener, and he works far from the house, near the old station road. His phone showed only one bar of wifi, and the page for ship tracking kept freezing. 'Why is the internet so slow in the garden?' he asked. 'Can you make the signal twice as strong?' The assistant understood that he wanted a faster connection outside. It could not make the signal stronger itself, but it checked the router and said, 'The router is far away. Move it closer, or use the extender.' It also found that the wifi in the shallow end of the yard was weaker than in the house. Fred put the extender by the window and the page loaded.

Finding a film to watch is easy when your phone helps. You say a few words, like the name of the film, and it shows where it plays and when. If you want a certain seat, you can place an order for tickets. The best seats are usually in the middle, and they sell out first. A good cinema also shows a trailer so you can see what the film is like. People change their plans often, and they say, 'Show me something funny,' 'Only films after eight,' 'Book two seats in the middle' or 'Find a cheaper show.' If many friends want to come, you can multiply the seats, for example by asking for six instead of two.

Person: Good morning. I'm very sorry to ask so early, but my grandson is coming after school and I will be out, so could you unlock the front door for him at four?
Assistant: Of course. Do you want it to stay unlocked, or lock again after he comes in?
Person: Please lock it again after about ten minutes.
Assistant: Okay. The front door will unlock at four and lock at ten past. Do you also want to give him a code?
Person: Yes. Also, can you sell my old key to the shop on the corner?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't sell things. I can tell you which shop is closest. Would you like to open the camera channel to see the most recent visits at your door?
Person: That would be nice, thank you.

Mrs. Reed is a retired teacher who loves to bake bread on Sunday. She had a pot of tea and an apron on, and she said to her kitchen speaker, 'Could you please help me? I am afraid I will forget the dough, because my grandchildren are coming and I will be talking all morning. Would you remind me every hour to check if the dough has risen?' The assistant understood that she wanted an hourly reminder while the dough rose. It said, 'Of course. I will remind you every hour to check the dough.' It also found a leaf of her recipe, search by search, and read her the baking time. Mrs. Reed smiled and began to knead.

Jay was away on a school trip to the museum, and he was worried about his grandmother. He typed to his phone assistant: remind gran to take her blue pill at six, but don't call her and don't use a loud alarm. She hates loud noises.
The assistant understood that Jay wanted a quiet reminder only. It set a soft chime on gran's tablet for six o'clock, with a note that said, Time for your blue pill. It did not place any call, and it did not turn on the loud alarm.
Jay loved how easy it was. At six, gran tapped the note, took her pill, and sent him a smiley face.

A radio plays stations that send out news, music and talk. People use it to hear the weather in the morning or a match at night. What they change most often is the station and the volume. Someone who wants frequent news updates might say, Put on the news station, or Turn it down a little. Some small radios run on a battery, so people ask, Did you charge the radio? Many people listen while they eat breakfast and take a vitamin. Smart radios can also save favourite stations, so you can say, Play my usual station, instead of looking for the number.

A robot mower cuts the grass by itself, so nobody has to push a mower on Saturday. It stays inside a wire or a map line, and it goes back to its base when the battery is low. People change when it works, how short the grass should be, and which part of the garden it skips. They say things like, Cut the grass a bit shorter, Don't mow when it rains, or Leave the far corner alone. Sprinklers work in a similar way. You point the spray at the dry patch and say, Water the front lawn for ten minutes. If a fork or a toy is left on the grass, the mower may stop, so pick things up first.

They want to know when a film is showing at the cinema.
What time is the film on?
When does the new space movie start?

I'm making dinner and I'll heat some creamy pasta first, so tell me when the film begins.

Any good films on this weekend?
Could you check the cinema and tell me the times for the funny one with the dog?
Is there a late show?
I'd love to see something after work, so what is playing and when?

Person: I'm chopping onions in the kitchen and the music is too quiet. Turn it up.
Assistant: Which speaker should I turn up, the kitchen one or the living room one?
Person: The kitchen one. But I don't want it so loud that it hurts my ears.
Assistant: Okay. I turned the kitchen speaker up to level six.
Person: Good. Can you tell me about the traffic on my way to school? It looks stormy outside.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't check live traffic from this speaker. I can tell you the weather, though. There is heavy rain until noon.
Person: Then I'll take an umbrella. Thanks!

A smart bulb is a light you can control with your voice. It is for making a room feel right: bright for reading, soft for the evening. Most bulbs can change their brightness and their colour, so a lamp can convert from plain white to warm yellow or even blue. People say things like, Make the lamp dimmer, Turn the bedroom light to warm, or Set the hall light to silver white. After a late ride home on the bus, someone might just say, Lights on. And before bed, Turn everything off. Short words like these are all the bulb needs.

- Don't let me forget the fancy olive oil.

An air conditioner takes the warm air out of a room and blows cool air back in. People use it on hot days so they can sleep, work or just feel calm. A fan does not make the air colder, but moving air feels cooler on your skin. Many fans hang from the ceiling and have three speeds. What people change is the temperature, the speed and the time it stays on. They say, It's too hot in here, Make it a bit cooler, or Switch it off at midnight. Heat can give you a headache, even on a cloudy day, so a cool room helps.

name: outfit_weather_check

- Is that silver sky going to bring rain?

- Should I sweep the porch with the broom today or wait for the wind to stop?
- Is it warm enough for shorts in Leeds on Friday?

name: call_for_help

- Get my sister on the phone, I fell.

A phone call lets two people talk even when they are far apart. You press a name and the phone rings. If nobody picks up, you can leave a voicemail, and the person hears it later. Missed calls show up as a number on the screen. People change how loud the call is, whether it uses speakerphone, and who they call. They say, Call Dad, Put it on speaker, or Call back the last number. A rough line or a weak signal can break up the sound, so people say, Say that again, or Call me back. If you ride a bike or a horse, you may ask for speakerphone so your hands stay free.

Reading time is a few quiet minutes with a book, often before bed. A bookmark keeps your place so you can find the chapter again. Many people read a chapter a night, and some like a timer that tells them when to stop. A new book may arrive in the mailbox, and people look forward to it. What they change is the book, the page, the size of the letters and how long they read. They say, Open my book at chapter four, Read for thirty minutes, or Make the letters bigger. A safe, calm routine helps some people dream well afterward.

A workout is a set of exercises done in order, like squats, push-ups and a short run. Each exercise has sets and reps: a rep is one movement, and a set is a group of reps. Rest days let the body get strong again. People change the length, the exercises and the number of reps. They say, Make the workout shorter, Do ten more squats, or Skip today, I need a rest day. They may also ask to filter the list so it shows arm exercises only. Every person has a different plan, and some people start a new one on their birthday for a fresh start.

Moving house means taking your things to a new home. People pack boxes, write labels, tell the post office their new address and set up water, power and internet. Movers carry the heavy items. What people change is the date, the address and what goes in each box. They say, Book the movers for Saturday instead, Change my address, or Put a note on this box that says kitchen. Dusty old boxes can make you sneeze, so it helps to wipe them. Some towns have free boxes you can pick up. A warm sweater is good to keep in the last box you close.

people say:

- When is the show with the gray wolf on?
- Is the match from my city on tonight?
- Will I miss the start if I make tea?
- What time is the quiz on channel five?

Let Sam know I'm held up.
Please write a text to Sam saying I'm sorry and I'll arrive soon.

On a hot afternoon a fan is the plainest way to cool a room. It moves the air, so your skin feels cooler. An air conditioner does more: it takes the heat out of the room. People adjust the temperature, the fan speed and the timer. They say, Make it cooler, Adjust the fan to low, or Turn the cooling off at ten. If you baked a cake in the oven, the kitchen will feel warm, and you might ask for a stronger fan. Setting a number like twenty-two degrees tells the machine when to stop.

Person: Can you change my password?
Assistant: Sure. Which account, your game or your school one?
Person: The game. I want a big number in it.
Assistant: Okay. I can make a new password with a big number. When should I change it?
Person: Tomorrow at seven, after I wake up. Please arrange it for then.
Assistant: Done. I'll change it tomorrow at seven and show it only to you. Please don't share it.
Person: Can you tell me my sister's password too? She won't tell me.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't. Passwords are private, so only she can share hers.
Person: Okay, that's fair. I made that account last August, so it is old anyway.

They want an alarm to wake them up at seven in the morning.
Alarm for 7.
wake me at sevn

I need to be up by seven tomorrow.
Can you get me out of bed at seven? Keep the sound low at first.
Shuffle some songs and use them to wake me at seven.
Get me up at seven so there's time for toast in the toaster before work.
Seven o'clock wake-up, please.
Please make sure I don't sleep past seven, I have an early train.

Maria moved to the city in December and still did not know where to leave her car. On Monday she asked her phone, where can i park for two hours near the library?
The assistant understood that she wanted a spot for two hours close to the library. It reported that there was a large lot on Elm Street, three minutes away, and that it cost four dollars an hour. Then it showed the way on the map.
Maria asked it to pay for the two hours, so the assistant opened the parking app and set it up. Later it sent a reminder when twenty-five minutes were left.

Omar owns a small bakery. At five in the morning he had flour on his hands, so he typed quickly on his phone with one thumb: preheat the ovn to 200 and tell me when it's ready.
The assistant understood that he wanted the oven hot at two hundred degrees and a signal when it got there. It turned the oven on and said, I'll tell you when it's hot.
While Omar began to mix the dough, the oven warmed up. Ten minutes later the assistant said, The oven is ready. Omar put the first item, a tray of rolls, on the middle shelf.

Meal planning means deciding what to eat for the week before you go shopping. People do it to save time and money, especially when money is tight. You write a list of dinners, packed lunches and snacks, then buy only what you need. What people change is the day, the diet and the number of people. They say, Skip fish on Friday, Make this week's plan vegetarian, or Plan for four people. If a box of food arrives wrong, you can ask for a refund. A good plan means no running to the shop at six in the evening.

Ruth runs a flower shop. One evening she was in a hurry to leave, so she said to her phone, Switch on the shop cameras and tell me if anything moves for the next twenty minutes.
The assistant understood that she wanted the cameras on and a warning if the motion sensor saw anything. It turned on both cameras and said, Cameras are on.
At eight the sensor picked up a shape, and the assistant sent her a photo. It was only the neighbour, who was out to mow the grass behind the shop, seen through the thick glass door. Ruth laughed, then asked the assistant to play her evening playlist on the way home.

Person: Yes. I'm making oatmeal and the kids are asleep.
Assistant: Okay, it will stay quiet until seven.

Mr Hall, a retired teacher, heard a noise on the road outside his house. He said to his smart speaker, Turn on the porch light and show me the front camera.
The assistant understood that he wanted two things: the porch light on and the front door camera on the screen. The light began to glow, and the picture appeared on his tablet. He could see the road, the bins and a cat.
Mr Hall smiled. Since he was awake now, he asked the assistant to read the local news. It read three short stories and then stopped.

When you buy something online, a package travels from a shop to your door. The tracking page shows where it is: packed, shipped, out for delivery. People use it to know when to be home. If you click on the wrong colour with your mouse, you can often cancel before the shop closes the order. A soft parcel, like a pillow, may be left by the door. What people change is the delivery day, the address and the time. They say, Where is my package, Send it to my office, or I want a refund.

Tina runs a small cafe. She had just unplugged the old fridge to clean it, and her hands were wet and cold, so she typed in a hurry: put heavy cream and two dozen eggs on the shopping lsit, and send john a message that we are out of milk.
The assistant understood two jobs. It added heavy cream and twenty-four eggs to the shopping list. Then it sent John a message that said, We are out of milk.
It told Tina both things were done. She dried her hands and went back to the fridge.

Dana, a busy parent, put the laptop on the floor near the socket and said to it, Restart the computer and open the folder called school forms.
The assistant understood that she wanted two things: a restart, and then the folder. It restarted the laptop. After the plain blue screen came up, it opened the school forms folder and showed three files.
While Dana filled in the first form, the assistant tracked the battery and told her it was at eighty percent, so she did not need to move. She thanked it and went on with her work.

Mr Wilson was not good with technology. The remote had too many buttons. So he spoke to the television, Take me straight to channel twenty-five, please.
The assistant understood that he wanted channel twenty-five. It switched there. A show about an old train route was on, and Mr Wilson liked it.
Then he said, I don't want the grandchildren to change the channel. Can you lock it? The assistant turned on the children's lock, so the channel could only be changed with a code. It told him the code in a clear voice and said he could ask to unlock it any time.

Lily was eight. One night the smoke alarm began to beep in the hall. She said to the family speaker, Call Grandpa. Then she stopped. No, call Mom!
The assistant understood that Lily had changed her mind. It did not call Grandpa. It called Mom and said that Lily was at home and the alarm was beeping.
Mom said it was probably a low battery, and she told Lily to write a note on the fridge to buy a new one. The assistant gave one tip: if you ever smell smoke, go outside and wait. Lily wrote the note, and it was the correct thing to do.

A birthday is the day each year when a person gets one year older. People use their phones to remember dates, pick gifts and send cards. A good reminder comes weekly in the month before, so there is time to shop. People change the date, the gift idea and how much they want to spend. They say, Remind me about Ben's birthday, Find a gift under twenty dollars, or Send a card. Some gifts are food, like a cake they can eat together, and a gift card for fuel works well for a driver.

- Tell me if Mum doesn't pick up.

A robot vacuum cleans the floor by itself. People set a schedule so it runs while they are out. It goes back to its base when the battery is low. What people change is the time, the room and how strongly it cleans. They say, Clean the kitchen now, Try the bedroom first, or Don't run when I'm home. If a pile of letters from the mailbox is on the floor, pick it up first. When the dust bin is full, the robot may say so. A low hum is normal.

Priya was a busy parent with a toddler asleep on her shoulder. Very softly she said to her phone, Could you please turn off the hourly alerts from the photo app, because every buzz wakes the baby and I really need her to sleep?
The assistant understood that she wanted the hourly notifications switched off. It turned them off and said, Done. The photo app will not buzz anymore.
The last buzz had been a like on a picture of the baby in her yellow dress. Priya whispered thanks and asked it to play soft music.

Ken, an office worker, came home that evening to the smell of fresh paint from the next flat. He told his speaker, Run the air purifier tomorrow at seven, and keep it on low.
The assistant understood that Ken wanted the purifier to start at seven the next morning at a low speed. It set the schedule and said, The purifier will start tomorrow at seven on low.
Ken looked at the purifier. Its small light was dim, which meant it was waiting. He opened a window for a few minutes and went to bed.

When Leo got back, the page was waiting on the tray. The recipe serves six. Max, who was hungry, sat down by the kitchen table and waited too.

The assistant understood that she wanted the sprinkler on the left bed to run each morning while she was gone. It set it for six every morning, and it told her in plain words what it had done.
Mrs Ortiz said thank you, as if she were talking to a person.

Zoe was on a school trip, walking up a frozen path by the lake. Her feet were cold and she wanted to know how far she had gone. She typed to her phone, Count steps.
The assistant understood that she wanted her step count. It said, You have walked 4,200 steps so far, which is about three kilometres.
Zoe typed again, Watch pace. The assistant said it would watch her pace and tell her if she went too slowly to reach the bus on time. Ten minutes later it said, You are going a little slow. Zoe laughed and walked faster.

Tyre pressure is the amount of air inside each tyre. It matters because soft tyres wear out fast and use more fuel. Most cars have a number on a sticker inside the door, and drivers check it before a long run. People change the pressure when the load changes: a full car with bags and kids needs a little more air. When they ask an assistant, they might say 'remind me to check my tyres on Saturday' or 'tell me the right pressure for the back wheels'. If your back is sore from bending down, you can ask your phone to swap the reminder to the weekend. Some cars also show a warning light when one tyre is low.

Marco was a cook, and his hands were full of flour when he spoke to the speaker in his kitchen. 'Tell the robot mower to start tomorrow at seven, and keep going every Saturday.' The assistant understood two things: a first start tomorrow at seven in the morning, and a weekly mowing day. It set the mower's schedule for Saturday at seven and said so out loud. Marco then asked if the battery was full. The assistant checked and said the battery was at eighty percent, enough for one long cut. Marco nodded, wiped his hands, and went back to his dough. He wanted to practice a new bread recipe before the weekend, and now the lawn would take care of itself.

A match score is a simple thing: it tells you who is ahead. Fans use it to follow a team without sitting in front of the screen all day. Most people change what they get. They ask for scores only for their own team, or for an alert when a goal is scored. They say things like 'tell me when United scores', 'what's the score now', or 'stop the alerts'. A low score does not always mean a boring game. Many fans also share the result with friends, so they ask the phone to send the final score to the group chat. Every item in the alert list can be turned on or off. Training works the same way: a coach may ask for a reminder an hour before practice.

A sprinkler waters the lawn so the grass stays green. Most sprinklers have a timer that says when to start and how long to run. People change the timer when the weather changes: less water after rain, a little more in a hot week. When they talk to an assistant, they say things like 'water the lawn at six in the morning', 'run the sprinklers for ten minutes', or 'skip today, it rained'. A dog that likes to dig can leave holes in the grass, so some people turn the sprinkler away from that corner. Even a little water at the right time helps more than a lot at noon, when the sun dries it up fast.

A ventilation fan, or just an open window, brings fresh air into a room. It is for clearing out smells, steam and stale air. People change how strong it is: low when they are sleeping, high when they are cooking. They also change when it runs. They might say 'turn the fan up', 'run it for an hour after dinner', or 'make it quieter'. A narrow window lets in less air, so the fan has to work harder. A plant on the shelf can make a room feel fresher, but it does not replace airflow. After a trip to the market with fish or spices in the bag, many people open the kitchen window for a while.

Dana was a busy parent, and she was putting shoes on a toddler when she spoke to her phone. 'Book a haircut for Leo on Friday and remind me an hour before.' The assistant understood two requests in one sentence: a booking and a reminder. It looked at the barber shop near the front of the school and found a free time at a quarter past four. It booked that time and set the reminder for a quarter past three. Then it asked if Dana wanted to save the shop's phone number. She said yes, and the assistant saved it to her contacts. Dana smiled, picked up the toddler, and walked out the door.

When you buy something online, the shop sends you a tracking number. This number is for following the package from the warehouse to your door. People check it when they think the parcel is late. They also change things: a new delivery day, a different address, or a safe place like the back porch. A narrow delivery window, like one hour, is hard to plan around, so many people ask for a wider one. Words they use are 'where is my package', 'deliver it on Monday', or 'send it to my office instead'. If an item is wrong, like a suitcase with a broken zip, they ask for a refund and a pickup.

A motion sensor wakes up a camera or sounds an alarm when something moves near your home. It is for keeping the house safe when nobody is there. People change when it is on: armed when they leave, off when they come back. In the dark, the camera switches to night mode so you can still see the yard. Many people forget to turn the alarm on, so they ask for a reminder or a schedule. They say 'arm the house', 'I'm home, turn it off', or 'tell me if the garage door opens'. The sound of a car engine passing by can trip an old sensor, so some people make it less sensitive.

When you travel, prices in a shop may be in a different currency. The exchange rate says how much of your money one unit of theirs is worth. It is for knowing if something is cheap or fair. The rate changes every day, so people check it before they pay. They also pick a location to compare, like a trip to Japan next month. Words people use are 'how much is that in my money', 'what's the rate today', or 'is it better to wait'. On a humid day at a market stall, you might flash your phone at the seller to show the price you worked out. A small shift in the rate can change the price of a big purchase.

Ines was a cook, and she had ten minutes for a nap before the dinner rush. First she picked up her phone and typed in a hurry: 'find a wierd gift for my brother, he likes birds, under thirty dollars'. The assistant understood that she wanted gift ideas about birds that cost less than thirty dollars. It ignored the typo and showed three ideas. One was a weird teapot shaped like a parrot. Ines laughed and said she liked it. Then she typed, 'book it for delivery by friday'. The assistant ordered the teapot and set the delivery for Friday. Ines closed her eyes and fell asleep for her short nap.

A lost pet notice helps neighbours find an animal fast. Someone posts a photo and says where the pet was last seen. Neighbours then keep an eye out near the cafe, the park or the bus stop. People change the notice often: a new photo, a bigger area, a reward. Words they use are 'make the search wider', 'increase the distance to two miles', or 'post it again'. A sharp photo of the animal's face works better than a blurry one. Noise works in a similar way. If a party is loud, a neighbour might say 'could you keep it down after ten'. A polite note usually works.

Priya was an office worker, and she was walking across the big field behind her building when her phone beeped. The battery was low. 'Make the screen half as bright and turn off whatever I don't need,' she said. The assistant lowered the brightness to half and switched off background updates. Then Priya asked which app used the most power. The assistant said a map app had used more than all the others. She closed it. The sun was sinking in the west, and she still had to pack her bag for tomorrow's trip. 'Will the phone last until I get home?' she asked. The assistant said yes, about four more hours, which was enough.

Lena had just finished a night shift, and her eyes were half shut. In the car she gave a whisper to her phone: 'Take me home, but not by the highway.' The assistant understood she wanted directions home that skip the highway. It said the back roads would take ten minutes more, and asked if that was fine. Lena said it was. A white van pulled out ahead of her, and the assistant told her to turn left in two hundred metres. Before she drove off, Lena also asked for a reminder to refill the humidifier when she got home. The assistant set the reminder to go off when she reached her street.

Omar was an office worker eating lunch at his desk. He typed in a hurry: 'how much powr did the house use yesterday'. The assistant read powr as power and checked the home energy meter. It said the house used twenty-two units yesterday, which was more than the day before. Omar spilled a little coffee on his sleeve and laughed. The assistant also said the biggest use came at six in the evening, shown as a purple bar in the app. Omar remembered that his brother had parked the van in the garage with the charger plugged in all night. He decided to talk to him.

A notification is a small message from an app that tells you something new happened: a like, a comment, a new follower. It is for helping you know what is going on without opening the app all day. People change how many they get. Some want only messages from close friends. They say 'turn off the likes', 'only tell me about comments', or 'be quiet at night'. Notifications can be annoying at breakfast, when your hands are damp from washing up and your cereal is getting soggy. So many people set quiet hours.

Walter was not good with technology, and the solar panel app on his phone confused him. So he spoke to the speaker in the hall. 'Please measure how much electricity the house uses and tell me tomorrow at seven in the morning.' The assistant understood that Walter wanted a report on his electricity use at seven the next day. It said it would do that and set the report. Then Walter asked why the number never seemed to drop. The assistant said the fridge and his grandson's electric motorcycle charger drew a constant amount of power all night. Walter laughed and asked it to remind him to unplug the charger at bedtime. The assistant did.

Person: Tomorrow at nine then. My brother's plane lands at ten, so I want it done before.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you tomorrow at nine to order more cups.
Person: Great. Now I can chill for a bit.

Watering plants is about giving them enough water without drowning them. Most plants like a drink when the top of the soil feels dry. People change how often they water as the season changes: more in summer, less in winter. A smart sprinkler can warn you when rain is coming, so it skips the next watering. Words people use are 'water the tomatoes every second day', 'skip the next one', or 'change it to evening'. A small change in time can mean a lot, because evening watering loses less water to the sun.

name: start_focus_timer
does: Starts a countdown for focused work and tells you when to take a break.
inputs: how many minutes to work, and how long the break is
people say:
- give me twenty-five minutes to work, then a break
- I need to study until my father gets home, keep time for me
- flash the lights when the time is up
- I must finish this email before my cookies turn crispy, give me ten minutes
- no phone for an hour, then tell me

Margaret was not good with technology, and the thermostat on the wall had too many buttons. She sat in her soft chair and spoke to the speaker. 'I don't want the heating on all day, just in the evening when it gets cold.' The assistant understood that she wanted no heat during the day. It made a schedule: heating on from five to ten at night, and off the rest of the time. It set the temperature to twenty degrees and said the radiators would reach it in about forty minutes. Margaret asked how much the bill would drop. The assistant said it could not know exactly, but running the heating five hours instead of fifteen could cut use by a large percent.

Tomi was a child, and it was almost bedtime. The heater hummed in the corner, and the ceiling light was too bright for his eyes. First he said to the lamp, 'Dimmer, please.' The assistant understood that he wanted less light, and it turned the lamp down to thirty percent. Tomi shut his book and put it on the shelf. Then he said, 'Warm colour.' The assistant changed the bulb from white to a soft orange glow. Tomi smiled, pulled up his blanket, and said goodnight. The assistant said goodnight back and kept the light low until he fell asleep.

A filter cleans the air or the water that goes through a machine, like a heater, a fridge or a pipe. It is for keeping the machine healthy. Over time it gets dirty, so people change it every few months. They say 'remind me to change the filter in March', 'book a repair', or 'when did I last do it'. Fold the old paper filter into a bag before you throw it away. If a machine starts making a noise in the middle of the night, or a pipe leaks, it is best to call for a repair soon.

Booking a table means telling a restaurant when you are coming and how many people there are. It is for making sure you have a seat, especially on a weekend when places are full. People change a booking often: a later time, more guests, or fewer. They say 'move it to eight', 'make it for six', or 'cancel our table'. If friends drop out, they ask the restaurant to reduce the group, so the table is smaller. The total on the bill at the end depends on what you ordered, so some people also ask to see the menu before they go.

Hana owned a little shop, and the morning sun was falling on her paintings. She spoke to the assistant behind the counter: 'Could you please close the front blinds about halfway, because the sun is strong and I do not want the paintings to fade?' The assistant understood two things: close the blinds halfway, and the reason was the sun. It closed them to the middle and said so. Hana said thank you. Then she asked it to reserve a table at the cafe for noon, since a man from the factory was coming to see her. The assistant booked the table. Hana went back to opening the last box of frames.

A birthday reminder tells you a day ahead that someone's special day is near. It is for not forgetting. People keep dates in a calendar and sync it with their phone, so the reminder shows up everywhere. They change how early they want to know: a week before for a gift, a day before for a card. They say 'remind me about Dad's birthday', 'tell me a week early', or 'put the party at the park on the calendar'. If your feet are sore from shopping, you can order the gift online and have it sent instead.

Person: Hello. I am having lunch with my son's teacher in an hour, and she speaks Spanish. Could you please help me say something kind, because I would like to build a good start with her?
Assistant: Of course. What would you like to tell her?
Person: Thank you for helping him this year.
Assistant: You can say: Gracias por ayudar a mi hijo este año.
Person: Can you say it slowly? I want it to sound smooth.
Assistant: Sure: grah-see-ahs por ah-yoo-dar ah mee ee-ho es-teh an-yo. Practice it a few times on the way.
Person: Thank you, that helps a lot.

Tariq was a driver, and he was on his way home from a long shift. He spoke to his phone: 'Switch on the kettle and tell me when the oven is hot.' The assistant understood two jobs in one sentence. It started the kettle and began watching the oven. His grandma was coming for dinner, and he wanted to make her favourite cake. The assistant said the kettle was on and the oven would be ready in twelve minutes. Tariq asked it to turn on the fancy coffee machine too, because Grandma loved a good cup after dinner. The assistant said it was done.

Sam woke up with a sudden thought and reached for the phone on the bedside table. 'Could you please tell me when the post office opens today, because I need to send my tax forms before the line gets long?' The assistant understood that Sam wanted the opening hours of the nearest post office. It said the post office opened at nine and closed at five. Outside, the snow was starting to melt, and the road was wet. Sam asked the assistant to remind him at half past eight to leave. The assistant set the reminder and wished him a good morning.

Rosa was a gardener, and she cut her finger on a rose bush. She held it up and said to her phone, 'Cut finger, help.' The assistant understood it was a small cut and told her what to do. Press a clean cloth on it. Rinse it with cool water. Put on a bandage. It also said not to touch the cut with dirty gloves, because that can be dangerous. If the bleeding did not stop in ten minutes, it said, she should call for help. Rosa had planned a jog after work, but the assistant said to rest the hand first. She did as it said, and the bleeding stopped.

Grandpa Leo sat in his armchair and sniffed. The air in the living room felt dusty. It was Tuesday, and the heating had been on all morning. 'Purifier on,' he said to the speaker. The assistant understood and turned on the air purifier in the living room at medium speed. Then it said the filter looked dirty and asked if Leo wanted a reminder to change it. Leo said yes, on Saturday. The assistant set the reminder. Soon the room smelled fresh, and Leo went back to his crossword.

A packing list is a list of what you take on a camping trip: a tent, a sleeping bag, a torch, water and food. It is for making sure nothing gets left behind. People change it with the weather: warm coats for the hills, a rain jacket if rain is coming. They say 'what do I need for two nights', 'put a rain jacket on the list', or 'spell it out, I want every item'. Delicious food matters too, so many lists have a line for snacks. One family even took their kitten along in a carrier, and wrote it on the list.

name: get_sports_results
does: Gives the latest scores and results for a team or a sport.
inputs: a team or sport name, and a date if you want one
people say:
- did my team win
- what was the score of the ball game last night
- tell me how the Tigers did, their form has been low lately
- connect me to last night's basketball results
- how did the girls' league finish

Nina woke up late, and her head was still foggy. She mumbled to her phone, 'Could you please tell me how to spell engine in French, because I have an important email to send to a mechanic in Lyon, and I expect an answer today?' The assistant understood she wanted the French word for engine and how to spell it. It said the word is moteur and spelled it out slowly: m, o, t, e, u, r. Nina typed it into her email and thanked the assistant. It also offered to check the rest of her sentence, but Nina said she would manage. Then she made coffee.

Kofi woke up and saw that it was still early. He spoke softly to the speaker so he would not wake his kids. 'Could you please dim the lamp and tell me where my package is, because I think the toy I ordered for my son should come today?' The assistant understood two things: turn the light down, and track the order. It dimmed the lamp to a gentle glow. Then it said the package had left the depot at six and was out for delivery, and it should arrive by noon. Kofi thanked it and went to make tea.

Person: I need to see the dentist.
Assistant: I can help with that. Which day would you like?
Person: Thursday. I am a bit scared, so a morning please.
Assistant: There are two morning times on Thursday: nine o'clock and half past ten. Which one is better?
Person: Nine. Do I need to bring my toothbrush?
Assistant: I can't say what the dentist wants, but most do not need one. I have booked nine on Thursday for twenty minutes.
Person: Thank you, dear.

Someone wants to know if there is a leak somewhere in the house.
Is there a leak?
Is water running when it shouldn't be?
Check the pipes for me
The paint by the bathroom wall is thick with bubbles, is water getting in?
I sweep up water by the washing machine every day, where is it coming from?
I keep finding a wet patch where the hose is in contact with the floor
Could you please look at my water use overnight, because I think something is wasting water and I want to fix it before the next bill comes?

Someone wants the television to stop playing the next episode on its own.
Stop the next episode
Don't play another one
No autoplay please
I don't want the show to keep going when I fall asleep
I've got my hat on and I'm leaving, so shut off the show after this episode
My flat is small and the walls are thin, so please don't let it run all night
Set the screen to switch off after this one

Holiday lights are strings of small bulbs that people hang on a tree or a house. They are for making the home feel festive. Many people change when the lights turn on and off. Some use a light sensor that switches them on when it gets dark, so they shine only at night. They say 'turn on the lights at sunset', 'keep them on until ten', or 'boost the brightness'. A timer helps too, because nobody wants to climb a ladder in the cold to pull a plug. Some families have only one switch for the whole house.

Jun had just moved to the city, and his alarm clock was broken. His first day at the new job started early. He held his phone and said, 'Wake me, seven.' The assistant understood he wanted an alarm at seven the next morning. It set the alarm and said it would ring with a gentle sound. Jun asked it to also remind him to iron his shirt tonight. The assistant set a reminder for eight in the evening. Jun put his head on the pillow, felt a little less nervous, and fell asleep.

Leo was nine, and he was working on a school project about teeth. The lamp over his desk was very bright. "Ouch, my eyes hurt," he said to the smart speaker in the hall. The speaker understood that the light was too strong, so it dimmed the lamp to half. "That's fine now," said Leo. Then he asked, "When does Dr. Moss open on Saturday?" The assistant looked up the dentist's opening hours and said, "Dr. Moss opens at nine on Saturday." Leo wrote the time on his project, next to a drawing of a big tooth. He also asked the assistant to book a visit for his mom at ten. The assistant said the visit was booked and that it would send a reminder the evening before. Leo smiled and went back to his drawing.

They want the phone screen to be less bright.
make the screen dimmer
screen too bright
turn down the brightness
pls lower the brigthness, its blinding me
My eyes hurt when I look at my phone at night. Can you make it softer?
I'm lying in bed and the screen is like a flashlight.
The nurse told me to rest my eyes before sleep, so could you please make the screen a lot darker?
It's so bright by the pool that I can't read anything while the kids swim, so could you change the screen to suit the sun?

A campsite booking keeps a spot for your tent on the nights you choose. Before a trip, people check the dates, how many people are coming, and whether they want a flat place near the water. You usually pay a small fee when you book, and some sites ask you to pay the rest when you arrive. If plans change, people say things like "move my booking to Saturday," "make it three nights instead of two," or "cancel the booking." Many campers also ask for a spot with a table near the tent, because breakfast tastes best outside, with bacon cooked on a small stove until it is crispy.

Person: Can you book me a haircut and tell me when the salon closes today?
Assistant: Sure. Which day and what time would you like the haircut?
Person: Friday morning, around ten. Please ask for someone who is soft with the scissors, my scalp is sensitive.
Assistant: Anna has a free time at ten on Friday. I have booked it. The salon closes at six today.
Person: Thank you. I would like to invite my brother to come along. Can you send him a message?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send messages to other people. I can give you the time and the address to share with him.
Person: That's fine, I'll text him. I have to go and fix the lock on my shed first.

name: check_room_air
does: Reads the air sensor in a room and gives one smooth score from good to bad.
inputs: the name of the room
people say:
- Is the air bad in here?
- It smells stuffy in the bedroom.
- Scan the living room air, please.
- The pollen is awful this April. Is it okay to open the window?
- How clean is the air upstairs?

Many phones can read text aloud for people who find small print hard to see. It helps with long emails, signs, and books. People can change the speed, the voice, and the length of what is read at one time. They say things like "read it slower," "speak a bit quicker," or "stop after this paragraph." Others make the letters bigger by saying "make the text larger" or "I can't look at this tiny writing." Once the settings feel right, people usually leave them alone, and they only ask for a change when their eyes are tired or when the text is very long.

Marco the cook was chopping onions in a noisy kitchen when his phone buzzed. A parcel had come to the front door, but he was too busy to go. "Please tell me when the courier is near and ask him to leave the box with my neighbor," he said. The assistant understood that these were two jobs. It set an alert for the courier and wrote a change in the delivery notes: leave the parcel next door. Marco also said, "If I miss it, remind me to pick it up from the post office on Friday." The assistant said it would remind him on Friday at noon. Marco nodded and went back to his onions.

June was only six weeks old, and her mother, Dana, was new to the city and very tired. A neighbor had agreed to lend her a baby monitor, but Dana was waiting for him to knock. She grabbed her phone and typed fast, all in lowercase: "remnd me to feed june at half past two". The assistant saw the small mistake and understood the message anyway. It said it had set a reminder for two thirty to feed the baby. Then Dana typed, "and again at five". The assistant added a second reminder for five o'clock. Dana put the phone down and smiled. At last she could sit still for a minute.

Person: I'm planning a party for Saturday. Can you send out the invitations?
Assistant: Happy to. How many guests should I invite?
Person: Double the number from last year.
Assistant: Last year you invited ten people, so I will invite twenty. What time does the party start?
Person: When the moon starts to rise, around eight. The music should be perfect, not too loud.
Assistant: I will put eight o'clock on the invitations and make a quiet music list.
Person: Can you also write the names on place cards with a pen?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't write on paper. I can make a list for you to print and copy.

Nina woke up on Sunday morning with her head full of cake. It was her uncle's birthday, and she had forgotten to buy him anything. A drip from the leaking tap in the bathroom went tap, tap, tap while she rubbed her eyes. She picked up her phone and said only two words: "Gift ideas." The assistant understood that she needed a present for her uncle's birthday. It named three things: a fancy tea set, a warm scarf, and a book about boats. Nina said, "The tea set." The assistant opened a shop page and showed the price. She smiled, since the party guest list was already full and this was the last job on her list.

Sam had just moved to the city and knew nobody. After his first swim at the public pool, he sat on a bench with his phone and said, "Could you please find the audiobook I started yesterday and start it where I stopped? I want to listen on the way home, and I don't remember the chapter." The assistant understood that he wanted his last place in the book. It said, "You stopped in chapter eleven, close to the end." Then it began to play. A minute later Sam said, "Dim the screen, please, it's too bright." The assistant made the screen darker, and Sam walked home with the story in his ears.

Grandpa Walt wanted to send his granddaughter money for her birthday. She lived far away, where the winters were snowy and cold. "How many euros is fifty dollars?" he asked the tablet. Then he stopped. "No, wait, I mean sixty dollars." The assistant understood that he had changed his mind. It worked out the new amount at today's rate and said, "Sixty dollars is about fifty-five euros." Walt wanted to remember the number, so he asked the assistant to keep a note. It saved a note called "Birthday money." Then Walt said he would also buy her a paper rose, and the assistant wrote that down too.

name: top_senders
does: Lists the people who write to you most often in your inbox over a chosen time.
inputs: how many days to look back
people say:
- Who writes to me all the time?
- Show me who sent the most mail this month.
- Did my husband email me this week?
- Drop me a list of my most frequent senders.
- I'm drowning in mail, who is it from?
- Which people keep filling my inbox?

name: plan_walk_route
does: Makes a walking loop of the length you want, starting from a place you choose.
inputs: the start place, the distance, and what to avoid
people say:
- I want a short walk from the station, about two miles.
- Give me a loop that's not too hilly.
- I'm bored of the same park, find me somewhere new.
- Is there a path without snow today?
- Take me for a one hour stroll.

Priya was an office worker, and her video call was about to start. The picture kept freezing. She put one hand on her mouse and typed with the other, all in lowercase and in a hurry: "wifi so slow, can you restart the routr". The assistant understood the small typo. It said it was restarting the router and that the wifi would be back in about two minutes. Priya asked it to end the call with her friend so she could join the meeting on time. The assistant closed the call. When the router lights came back, the connection was fast again, and Priya joined the meeting with a minute to spare.

Rosa was a nurse who had just finished a night shift. It was nine in the morning, and she was too tired to think. She carried her bag through the door and the flat was cold. "Keep the heating off now, and turn it on at four this afternoon, so the rooms are warm when I wake up," she said to the thermostat. The assistant understood that she wanted to sleep without noise and then have a warm flat. It lowered the heat for several hours and set the heating to start at four. Rosa drank a glass of orange juice, put her bag on a chair, and fell asleep.

Person: How heavy is a cow?
Assistant: A grown cow weighs a lot. Do you want the weight in kilograms or in pounds?
Person: Pounds, please. Is it more than my dog?
Assistant: Yes, much more. I don't know how heavy your dog is. Can you tell me?
Person: I forgot. I think she is about fifty pounds.
Assistant: A cow is about twenty times that. It weighs around a thousand pounds.
Person: Wow. Thank you for helping me.
Assistant: You are welcome. You were very polite.

A clock tells you what time it is, and time zones tell you what time it is somewhere else. When your friend lives far away, her morning can be your evening. People use this when they schedule a call or check if someone is awake. They ask for changes with words like "show me the time in Tokyo," "what's the time at my sister's place," or "set my clock to local time." You can also get a rough idea of the time without a clock, by looking at the sun or at when the mailbox is emptied, but a phone is much easier and does not make mistakes.

Maya was a student making dinner when her hand slipped on a hot pot of beans. She had a red mark on her finger. "I think it's small," she said in a quiet voice, "but it hurts. I don't want to call an ambulance, I just want to know what to do." The assistant understood that she did not want emergency help, only advice for a small burn. It told her to hold the finger under cool running water for ten minutes and not to put on butter or ice. It also said to call for help if the skin turned white or blistered a lot. Maya followed the steps, and the pain slowly went away.

Grandma Elsa needed a new light switch for the hall. The old one had stopped working, and her grandson had helped her disconnect it. She spoke to her tablet: "Find me a plain white wall switch and have it come tomorrow at noon." The assistant found three. The first one was expensive, so it showed her a cheaper choice with the same size. "That one," said Elsa. The assistant ordered it and said it would arrive tomorrow at noon, and that she could send it back within a month. Elsa wrote the time on a card by the door and went to make tea.

Mr. Hall, a retired teacher, was expecting his grandson for the weekend. His old phone had a constant buzz of notices, and the wifi was weak. He typed quickly, all in lowercase: "make a gues network for my grandson". The assistant understood what he meant despite the typo. It set up a guest wifi with its own name and password and said that the guest network was separate from his own. Mr. Hall also asked it to ship the new router box back to the shop, since the first one was broken. The assistant started the return and said a courier would pick the box up on Monday.

They want to know how strong the sun is at the beach today.
How strong is the sun?
Do I need sun cream today?
UV level?
Will I burn if I stay out till noon?
It feels like a heater out there. Is the sun very hot?
How bad is the sun at the beach right now?
Could you please tell me how strong the sun is this afternoon, because my young daughter has pale skin and I want to know how much cream to bring?

name: feed_pet_now
does: Gives a pet one portion from the automatic feeder, and can stop it when the pet has had enough.
inputs: the pet's name and the size of the portion
people say:
- Feed Bella, please.
- Give the cat her dinner now.
- She's been in the sunshine all day, give her a snack.
- Stop the feeder, he's had enough.
- Did the dog eat the food in the bowl on the left?
- Fill up the bowl for the kitten.

They want to hear today's top news.
News?
What's happening today?
Tell me the headlines.
Read me the main stories, please.
Anything big in the news this morning?
I want an automatic summary of the top stories as soon as I wake up.
I'm waiting at the bus stop under my umbrella and have nothing to read, so could you please find the most important news from today and read it to me?

A text message is a short note that you send from your phone to another person's phone. It is useful for plans, quick questions, and little jokes. In a group chat, many people can read the same text, such as five friends planning a pizza night. People change a text before they send it, and they use words like "change the first line," "make it shorter," or "add a smiley." They also ask, "read my last text," "reply yes," or "count the total in this chat." A text should be simple, so the other person understands it fast and can answer when it suits them.

Tomas was a cook, and on Saturday he would host a big dinner. Today he was stuck in the kitchen. He had dropped his mother's necklace behind the stove, and the room was too dark to see it. "Turn on the big kitchen light, and tomorrow at seven switch it to a warm color for dinner," he said. The assistant understood. It made the ceiling light bright at once, and Tomas found the necklace. Then he asked for the robot to vacuum the floor. The assistant said it was true that the robot had not run all week, and it started it. It also set the warm light for seven tomorrow.

They want the internet connection to go faster.
The video keeps freezing.
Nothing will load.
Can you try restarting the router?
My photos won't post, the page just spins.
Less lag, please.
Everyone in the house is online and it's crawling.
I'm trying to watch a show and it takes forever to start.

Kai was a teenager sitting on the couch with his phone. His dad was outside with a hammer, fixing the frame under the new solar panels. Kai texted the home assistant: "did we use more power than last month". The assistant understood he meant the electricity use. It told him, "This month you used less, about ten percent less than last month, and the solar panels made half of your power." Kai was happy. He asked the assistant to post the numbers in the family chat. The assistant sent the message, and his mom replied with a thumbs up. Then Kai asked if the number would be double if they ran the heater all day. The assistant said it would be about double.

They want to know when the next bus comes.
Next bus?
When's the bus north?
I don't want the express, just the normal bus.
Not the five o'clock one, the one after.
The sun is shining so I'll walk to the stop, when should I leave?
I'm taking my new blender to my sister's, so when does the next bus going north come by?
Please tell me the time of the next local bus heading north, and not the train.

A video is a moving picture you record with your phone or camera. People make short clips of birthdays, trips, and their pets. A clip of a visit to the orange farm, for example, can show how the fruit hangs in the trees. After you record it, you can watch it again, make it shorter, or share it with family. People say things like "cut the first ten seconds," "send this clip to my sister," or "play it again." If someone needs a video urgently, for work or school, they often ask for it to be sent right now and in a smaller size, so it goes through quickly.

They want the latest sports scores.
Scores?
Who won the match?
How did my team do last night?
What's the score in the football game?
Who won the last round of the tennis final?
The apple pie is cooling on the counter, so while it cools could you please tell me the football score?
My friend said our team played today and I missed it. Could you please tell me the final score, since I want to know before I call him?

They want to make a recipe bigger.
Double the recipe, please.
Make it twice as much.
I need half again as much dough.
Can you make the cookies for twelve instead of six?
It's January and everyone is home, so I want to build a bigger batch than usual.
It's a quiet Sunday, but ten people are coming for cake. Can you change all the amounts so there is more for everyone?
Please scale the bread recipe up by one and a half, because I want an extra loaf to give to my neighbor.

name: night_temperature_check
does: Tells you how cold it will get at a campsite overnight, using the most recent forecast.
inputs: the campsite or place, and the date
people say:
- Will it chill down tonight in the hills?
- How cold will the tent get?
- Do I need my thick sleeping bag?
- Does the temperature fall below freezing on Saturday?
- What's the night like at the lake?

Baking turns dough or batter into bread, cake, or cookies. Heat does the work, so the time and the oven setting matter. Most recipes say to put the tray on the middle rack and to close the oven door and not open it too soon. People change how long something bakes, how warm the oven is, or how much dough they make. They say things like "bake it ten minutes longer," "make the oven hotter," or "set a timer for forty minutes." On busy days, a delivery driver may bring the flour and eggs, and the whole house smells good by evening.

Some videos are made at home with a phone, and they stay on the phone until you share them. They are for remembering things, like the kids brushing their teeth with a bright new toothbrush, or a dog that comes running when it hears the door. People change a video by cutting it, making it shorter, or turning the sound up. They say things like "trim the end," "send it to grandma," or "play my last video." A home video does not need to be perfect. What matters is that you can find it again later, so people often ask for a name to be added.

name: find_my_reservation
does: Looks up a table you booked at a restaurant and shows the time, the number of people, and the address.
inputs: the restaurant name or the date
people say:
- I lost the details of our dinner on Friday.
- Where did we book for tonight?
- What time is the table at the place on the hill?
- Do they have home delivery if we cancel?
- When is our lunch reservation?

Person: The air smells funny.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. Which room are you in?
Person: The kitchen. The oven was on a long time.
Assistant: Thank you. Do you want me to scan the air in the kitchen?
Person: Yes, please. It's late and I'm a little scared.
Assistant: The air in the kitchen is not good. The score is twenty-five out of one hundred. Please open the window and ask a grown-up to turn off the oven.
Person: Okay. Can you open the window for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't open windows. But I can turn on the fan.

name: set_bedtime_alarm
does: Sets a gentle alarm for waking up and a reminder for going to bed, based on how much sleep you want.
inputs: the wake-up time and the hours of sleep
people say:
- Wake me at six thirty tomorrow.
- I want eight hours of sleep, when should I go to bed?
- Add ten more minutes, I'm so tired.
- Remind the whole family to go to bed at nine.
- My little girl needs a tiny nap before dinner, wake her in half an hour.

A world clock shows the time in other places at once. It is useful when you want to report in to a boss far away, or when you listen to a live podcast that starts at a certain hour in another country. People keep a personal list of the cities they care about, such as where family lives. They change the list when they need to, with words like "show me the time in Lima," "put Paris on my clock," or "take Rome off." Some also ask, "is it too late to call my brother?" and the clock tells them if it is night there.

They want more packing boxes for moving.
I need more boxes.
Get me ten medium boxes.
Order twice as many as last time.
I ran out of boxes, can you send half a dozen more?
Can you teach me how many boxes a small flat needs, then order that many?
One extra large box for the lamp and another for my phone charger and cables, please.
Could you please order twenty more medium boxes for the move on Friday, because we have more books than I thought?

Email is a way to send letters over the internet. You write a message, add a name and a subject, and press send. People use it for work, bills, and plans, like a trip with friends. The inbox holds mail you get, and the unread mail is in bold. People ask for changes with words like "mark all as read," "reply to the last email," or "text me when the boss writes." A big attachment or a very long email can be expensive for slow connections, so many people send a small photo and a short note instead. They ask, "make it shorter."

They want to reserve a hotel room for two nights.
Book me a room for two nights.
I need somewhere to sleep near the train station.
A room for two on Friday and Saturday, please.
Find me a room with a nice design and book it, and tell me if breakfast is cooked fresh.
Can you find a quiet hotel for two people next weekend and check what time we can get in?
I'm coming to town with my wife, so please book a double room for the night of the tenth and send me the address.

They want to know how much money is worth in another currency.
How much is fifty euros in dollars?
What's the pound rate?
Dollars to yen right now?
I have a fever, so I can't go to the bank. What will the rate be tomorrow at nine?
I'm looking forward to my trip. Is the Mexican peso going up or down?
Are my euros ready to buy something that costs two hundred dollars?
Could you please tell me what a hundred pounds will be in euros tomorrow at nine in the morning, because I want to change my money then?

name: scale_recipe
does: Changes the amounts in a recipe so it makes more or fewer servings.
inputs: the recipe and the number of servings you want
people say:
- Make this soup for six instead of two.
- My partner is coming, so double the pasta.
- Cut the cake recipe in half.
- Walk me through how much flour I need for twelve cookies.
- I want this to be tasty for a crowd, make it for twenty.

name: move_between_my_accounts
