does: Moves money from one of your own accounts to another.
inputs: which account to take from, which to put into, and how much
people say:
- Put fifty dollars into my savings.
- I'm saving up for swim lessons, set some money aside.
- Return the money I took from my holiday account.
- Every month, send twenty pounds to my other account.
- Take a hundred out of checking and put it in my rainy day account.

Mrs. Green was a retired teacher, and she did not like to rush. She sat in the kitchen with her phone while dinner was cooked on the stove. "Would you be so kind as to move two hundred dollars from my checking to my savings?" she said. "I want to be sure the rent is safe before the month ends, and I always forget." The assistant understood that she wanted a transfer between her own accounts. It asked her to confirm the amount, and she did. Then it said the money was moved and read her the new balances. She asked it to change the setting so it would warn her when her checking was low. The assistant said it would, and she smiled. "I guess that's all."

name: pack_list_check
does: Goes through your packing list and tells you what you have not packed yet for a hike or a night out.
inputs: the trip type and the length in days
people say:
- Did I forget anything for the weekend?
- Scan my list for a two day hike.
- Do I have enough for half the trail?
- We have a wide river to cross, what else do I need?
- What's missing from my bag?

Jonas was an office worker with a long day. He said to his calendar assistant, "Put the team meeting on Tuesday at two." The assistant did. Then Jonas looked at his mug of stale coffee and said, "No, sorry, make it Wednesday, not Tuesday." The assistant moved the meeting to Wednesday at two and said so plainly. Jonas also needed to upload the slides before the meeting, so he asked for a reminder. The assistant set one for Wednesday at one. Jonas had to plug in his laptop, because the battery was low, and he got back to work. The calendar now showed only the new time.

Omar was a driver and he was hungry after a long drive. He pulled over and said, "Order me a pepperoni pizza from Luigi's, to come on Wednesday evening." The assistant began the order. Then Omar thought about his flat tire, and the long wait for a tow truck, and he said, "No, make that a mushroom pizza, and I want it tonight, not Wednesday." The assistant understood the correction. It changed the pizza to mushroom, changed the day to tonight, and said the food would arrive in thirty minutes. Omar also asked for a tip of three dollars for the rider. The assistant added it, and Omar sat back to wait.

Zoe, a teenager, was in a group chat with her friends. They were planning a surprise party for Mia, and Zoe had to be careful. She picked up her phone and said, "Write to the group, and don't mention Mia, because it's a secret." The assistant wrote, "Let's celebrate on Saturday at four, bring cake," and did not use the name Mia. Then Zoe said, "Don't send it yet. Read it to me first." The assistant read the message out loud. Zoe liked it, and said to send it. Later she scrolled to the bottom of the chat and saw her friends' answers. She wrote down the plan on a napkin, too.

Walter was not good with technology, and his phone often felt like a puzzle. His work deadline was close, the kitchen was hot, and his nephew was visiting with a tablet. Walter did not want anyone reading his messages. He held up the phone and said, "Everybody can see my screen, and I'd like to play my music in peace." The assistant thought about it. It understood that Walter wanted his messages kept private, not louder music. So it turned on the screen lock and hid message previews on the lock screen. Then it said, "Your messages are hidden now. They will only show after you unlock the phone. Shall I play your music?" Walter smiled and said, "Yes, please." The assistant played his favorite songs, and the screen stayed dark to everyone else in the room.

Priya was nine, and she wanted to buy a toy from a shop online. The price said twelve euros, but Priya only knew dollars. She looked at the picture of a cloud on the box and asked the phone, "How much is this in dollars?" The assistant understood that she wanted the price changed into her own money. It looked up today's exchange rate and told her that twelve euros was about thirteen dollars. Priya said, "Is that fine for my piggy bank? I have fifteen." The assistant said yes, she had enough, with two dollars left over. Then it asked if she wanted to select the toy and show her mom. Priya nodded and said, "Please do." The assistant saved the toy to a list for her mom to see.

Parking meters and parking apps help you pay for the time your car stays in a spot. You pick a spot, choose how long you want to stay, and pay. Many people press a button on the meter or tap a button in the app to start. If you need more time, you ask for it. You might say, "Give me another hour," or "I need a bit longer." If you leave early, you can say, "Remove the rest of my time." A quick look at the app also tells you how many minutes are left, so you can ask, "How long until my parking runs out?" and walk back before a ticket shows up on your car.

Grandpa Leo sat in his chair with his glasses on. His granddaughter worked in an office downtown and would visit on Saturday, and he wanted to take her to the cinema. He spoke to the speaker slowly. "Excuse me, would you be so kind as to find out what comedies are showing at the little cinema on Park Street this Saturday afternoon, because my granddaughter is visiting and she likes to laugh?" The assistant understood that Leo wanted comedy films and showing times at that cinema on Saturday. It found two comedies and read the times: one at two o'clock and one at four thirty. Both were showing inside the main hall. Leo said, "The two o'clock one, please." The assistant noted the film and the time in his calendar for Saturday.

A flood warning is an important message that says water may rise soon. It is for keeping people safe. Phones, radios and smart speakers can send it. People change what they hear and where. They might say, "Tell me about floods near me," or "Warn me about storms by the ocean." If the power goes out, they might say, "Read me the emergency news," or "Hold my calls until morning." A small radio with spare batteries is a good thing to keep in a drawer. It is also wise to hold a list of emergency numbers on paper. When the warning ends, people say, "Stop the alerts," and life goes back to normal.

Someone wants to know when their delivery will arrive.
Where's my stuff?
When does my package get here?
Is my order close yet?
Spell it out for me: when will the television I paid for show up?
I ordered it twenty days ago and nothing has come.
Has my parcel left the warehouse?
Could you please check the tracking and tell me the delivery day?
Any news on my order?
How much longer until the doorbell rings with my box?

Someone wants two copies of a page printed.
Print this twice.
Two copies, please.
Double the copies of this flyer.
Print my tent packing list twice and scan the receipt too.
I need one for me and one for Dad.
Could you run off a second copy of this letter?
Make a copy of the form, but keep the printer silent because the baby is asleep.
Another one of those, please.

Mara worked in an office and got home late most days. The grass in front of her house was getting long. Before the doorbell could ring, she said to her phone, "Can you organize the robot mower so it cuts half as much as last time? The grass is close to the flower beds, and I don't want it to hurt them." The assistant understood that she wanted a shorter mowing job near the flower beds. It changed the mower's plan to cut only half of the lawn and to stay a safe distance from the beds. It also moved the start time to tomorrow morning. Then it said, "The mower will cover half the lawn tomorrow at nine." Mara nodded. She was glad she did not have to push a mower herself.

Mrs. Alvarez was a retired teacher who liked to sit on her porch with a tablet. A tall hedge shaded her chair. Her hair was getting long, and she loved her hairdresser, Tina. In a hurry, because the tea was ready, she typed, "book haircut fridya at 10 with tina". The assistant understood that fridya meant Friday. It checked Tina's schedule, found that ten o'clock was free, and booked the haircut. Then it told her, "Your haircut with Tina is booked for Friday at ten in the morning. I can remind you on Thursday evening." Mrs. Alvarez typed, "yes thanks." The assistant set the reminder, and she went back to her tea.

Jonas was late for the train. He grabbed his coat and shouted at the speaker, "I'm going to forget the salad for tonight's dinner again!" The assistant understood that Jonas wanted a reminder, not a talk about food. It added a task to his to-do list: buy salad things for dinner. Because he was in a hurry, it pushed the task to the top of the list. Then it said, "Done. Buying salad things is first on your list. Do you want me to check off the other two tasks from yesterday?" Jonas said, "Sure, each one is finished." The assistant checked off each task, and Jonas ran out to catch his train.

Someone wants their coffee made stronger.
Make it stronger.
More kick, please.
This tastes wet and weak, like dishwater.
Put in two extra scoops from the coffee can.
I'm hanging by a thread this morning, so give me a stronger brew.
Could you please make my cup bolder, because I have a long day ahead?
It needs more punch.
That's too mild for me.
Double strength today, please.

First aid is what you do right away when someone gets a small injury, before a doctor can help. It is for keeping a cut, a burn or a bump from getting worse. Every March, many schools hold a first aid class, and it makes people feel ready. People change small things: how long to cool a burn, how big a bandage is, or who to call. They might ask, "How long should I hold this burn under cold water?" or "Remind me what to do for a nosebleed." If it looks serious, they say, "Call for help." A long list of steps is not needed. Stay calm, clean the spot, and ask for help if you are unsure.

Dan had just woken up, and his eyes were still closed. He wanted a bath, but then the doorbell rang. He mumbled, "Who's at the front door, and unlock it if it's my sister." The assistant understood two things: show who was outside, and open the lock only for his sister. It checked the door camera and saw Lila holding a bag. She had split the spare key with him last year, but she had left hers at home. The assistant told Dan, "It's Lila. I am unlocking the front door now." Dan said, "Thanks, and lock it behind her." The assistant did. Then Dan finally got into his bath, wide awake, and he sang for the whole time.

Someone wants to move a Tuesday meeting to another day.
My son is sick, so I can't make Tuesday.
Tuesday doesn't work anymore.
Fold Tuesday's meeting into Wednesday.
Push the meeting back a day.
Can we do this on Wednesday instead?
I'm stuck at home with the kids today, can you shift my plans?
Please reschedule the Tuesday meeting for later in the week, since my son isn't feeling well.
Move it.

Someone wants the pool cover put on.
Cover the pool.
Time to close it up.
Put the cover on the pool for the night.
pls put the pool cvoer on
Lock the cover down, it looks like rain.
The sun is gone, so please shut the pool.
Can you make the pool safe for tonight? Keep it simple, just close the cover.
Cover on, please.

Someone wants to make a party guest list shorter.
Cut the guest list.
Trim the list to twenty people.
We have too many guests, so please take some off.
Reduce the invites for the cereal brunch, but no, wait, keep my aunt on it.
Actually, make that fifteen, not twenty.
Can you remove the last five names from the online list?
I changed my mind about the big party, so please make it smaller.
Fewer people, please.

name: days_until
does: Counts how many days are left until a date that someone cares about.
inputs: the date of the event, and its name if there is one
people say:
- How many sleeps until my birthday?
- It's cloudy today, so how long until the picnic?
- Let me breathe, how many days are left before the exam?
- How many days until the school opens, so I can contact the office?
- Is it three weeks until the trip?

Lena was a busy parent, and the baby had been awake since dawn. She was holding a bottle in one hand and a spoon in the other. She said, "How long ago did Theo eat? I think he needs half again as much as last time." The assistant checked the feeding log. It understood that Lena wanted the time of the last feeding and a bigger amount. It said, "Theo last ate at ten thirty. That was four ounces. Half more would be six ounces." Lena nodded and said, "Measure out six, please." The assistant could not pour milk, so it wrote six ounces in the log and added that the total for today was twenty ounces. Lena said, "That's fine, thank you."

Person: Turn on the cameras before I drive off.
Assistant: Sure. Which cameras do you want, the front door or the back yard?
Person: The front door. No wait, the back yard too.
Assistant: Okay, both cameras are on. Should the alarm end at a certain time?
Person: Make it end at six tonight.
Assistant: Got it. The alarm will end at six.
Person: Can you pay the twelve dollar monthly fee for my plan? It's difficult to remember.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't make payments. I can remind you when the fee is due.
Person: That's fine, please do.

name: parcel_note
does: Leaves a short note for the delivery driver about where to put a package.
inputs: the spot for the package, and which delivery it is for
people say:
- Tell the courier to put the box by the back door.
- Hide my parcel behind the planter so no one takes it.
- The pale blue door is mine, so leave it there.
- Can the driver leave my box next to the milk crate?
- Write a message for tomorrow's delivery: don't ring the bell, the baby is asleep.

A recipe tells you how much of each thing to use for a certain number of servings. Sometimes you need more or less food than the recipe makes. This is called scaling. You work out new amounts for the cups and spoons. A cake for four people might become a cake for eight, so each amount doubles. People say, "Make this for six instead of four," or "Cut the recipe in half." Time does not always double, though. Baking time may stay the same, but a bigger pot takes longer to boil. A pinch of black pepper for one pot is still a pinch in a bigger one. Taste as you work, and write down your changes.

A phone call lets you talk to someone far away. If you miss a call, the phone shows who tried to reach you, and the person can leave a voicemail. People change small things about calls all the time. When their hands are full, say while stirring creamy soup, they ask, "Put it on speakerphone." Someone pushing a cart in a store may say, "Call my wife." When the sound is too loud, they say, "Turn the call down." After a missed call, they might say, "Call them back," or "Who just called me?" If they cannot guess who a number belongs to, they ask, "Whose number is that?" And when they are busy, they say, "Don't answer, let it go to voicemail."

Person: Next chapter.
Assistant: Which book are you reading right now?
Person: The one about the sea.
Assistant: I see two sea books on your shelf, the lighthouse story and the whale story. Which one?
Person: Whale.
Assistant: Okay. You finished chapter nine. Shall I read chapter ten aloud?
Person: Yes, please. I'm brushing the dog, so my hands are busy. Use only one speaker, my other ear is sore.
Assistant: I'll play it on the left speaker at a low volume. Starting chapter ten now.

Person: My hand is bleeding. I cut it on the electric hedge trimmer.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. Is the bleeding heavy, or is it a small cut?
Person: Small, I think. No, actually it's bigger than I thought.
Assistant: Press a clean cloth on it and hold it firm. If the blood does not stop in a few minutes, you should call for emergency help. Should I call now?
Person: Not yet. Rush me the number for the clinic instead.
Assistant: Here is the clinic number from your contacts. I'm reading it out now.
Person: Thanks. Keep saving my notes from today in case the doctor asks.
Assistant: I'm saving them now. Please keep pressing on the cut.

Watering is how a garden gets the water it needs to grow. A plant in a square bed may need a small drink every day, while a big tree needs a deep soak once a week. Sprinklers do the work when you are away. People change how long the water runs, which days it comes on, and which part of the yard gets it. They say, "Water the front beds for ten minutes," or "Skip tomorrow, it's raining." If the soil feels dry an inch down, they ask for more. Some people keep a small trowel in a pocket to check the soil. They also like to watch the weather and the plants, and then change the schedule. Early morning is a good time to water.

Person: I'm new to the city and I need movers.
Assistant: Welcome. Which day do you want them to come?
Person: This Saturday. My dad is busy that day, so I can't do it alone.
Assistant: I can book movers for Saturday. What time should they arrive, and what is your new address?
Person: Nine in the morning. The address is twenty-five Elm Street.
Assistant: Thank you. Where are they picking up your things?
Person: The old place, eleven Pine Road.
Assistant: Done. The movers are booked for Saturday at nine, from eleven Pine Road to twenty-five Elm Street.

Ravi was a student heading home for the holidays. He sat at the airport with a bag on his lap, and he did not want to miss his plane. Rain began to fall outside the big windows, and many people were waiting by the gates. Ravi had packed a small cooking pot for his mother, and he held the bag tight. He asked his phone, "When does my flight leave? I don't want the weather, just the time and the gate." The assistant understood that Ravi wanted two facts only: the departure time and the gate. It said, "Your flight leaves at four fifteen from gate twelve. It is on time." Ravi sighed with relief and thanked it.

name: set_room_volume
does: Makes the sound louder or softer on one speaker or on all the speakers in a home.
inputs: which room or speaker, and how much louder or softer
people say:
- Turn it down a step in the kitchen.
- Hush the speakers while I vacuum.
- It's been a rough day, so make the living room quiet.
- Too loud in here!
- Bring the bedroom speaker up a little.

Noah was eight, and he loved to walk to the park with his mom. Today he wore a bright digital watch. After the walk, his mom would cook meat and rice, so he wanted to go quickly. He asked the phone, "How many steps did I do? I want to walk double the steps of yesterday." The assistant understood that he wanted his step count for today and a goal twice as big as yesterday's. It said, "You have walked one thousand two hundred steps. Yesterday you walked two thousand, so your goal is four thousand." It set the goal. Noah took a turn around the pond, then another, and the assistant told him every time he passed one more thousand steps.

Someone wants the room to be cooler.
Make it cooler in here.
It's like an oven, I could bake a cake in this room.
Drop the temperature by two degrees.
Make it cold enough that I'd need a jacket.
Even on a rainy day this room feels stuffy, so turn on the fan.
A bit more air, please.
Could you cool the bedroom by half a degree more than before?
Run the air conditioning twice as strong.

Sam drove past a small cafe on the edge of town when a warning light flashed on the dash. He pulled up to a red light, because he was in a hurry for the news, and typed fast on the car screen: "tunr on the news on 101.5". The assistant understood that tunr meant turn and that Sam wanted the news station at 101.5. It tuned the radio and said, "101.5 is playing the news now." A voice began to read the traffic report. Sam learned that a crash had closed the middle lane of the highway ahead, so he took the next exit instead. He was glad the radio told him in time.

name: bedtime_reminder
does: Posts a gentle reminder on your phone when it is time to get ready for bed.
inputs: the time you want to wake up, and how many hours of sleep you want
people say:
- I ate spicy food, so remind me to go to bed early.
- I want eight hours, when should I go to bed?
- Split the difference and set my bedtime between ten and eleven.
- Tell me when to lie down if I wake up at six.
- Nudge me when it's time to sleep.

name: remember_parking_spot
does: Saves where the car is parked so it can be found later.
inputs: the place, and the level or row if there is one
people say:
- I always forget where I left the car.
- Mark this spot, I'm under the fancy hotel.
- Save my space, the one near the sign with the sun on it.
- Where did I park this morning?
- Remember the car is on level three, row F.

Someone wants the radio to be louder.
Turn it up.
A bit more sound, please.
Double the volume.
Raise it half a notch, this gold oldies station is too soft.
I can't hear the song over the engine.
Could you please make it louder? I'd like to reserve the quiet for the evening.
Change the sound so I can hear the news.
Bump it up some more.

Someone wants to move money from checking to savings.
Put half of my checking into savings.
Move some cash over to my other account.
I got my tax refund, so shift most of it to savings.
Keep enough in checking to ride out the week, and send the rest across.
Great, now move double that amount to savings.
Could you please transfer a quarter of my balance into the savings account?
Send a bit more to savings than last month.
Save some of it.

The news tells people what happened today. Headlines are short lines that sum up each story. A person might want sports scores, local stories, or news about one topic. Someone might say, "What's happening in town?" or "Give me the sports scores." They also change what they hear: "Skip the weather," "Block stories about celebrities," or "Only read me the top three." A fire in a tall building may be at the top of the local news, while a game result comes lower. If a story is long, people say, "Just give me the short version." Someone with a broken arm may like the news read aloud, because holding a phone is hard.

A door lock keeps a home safe. A smart lock can open with a code, a phone or a voice, so you do not need a key. People use it when they are carrying luggage and their hands are full. They say, "Unlock the door," or "Lock up, I'm leaving." They also ask, "Did I lock the front door?" and "Who is on the porch?" At night, the porch light can bathe the brown door in a soft glow, and a camera shows who is standing there. People change who may come in, such as a neighbor, and for how long: "Let my friend in until Sunday." Garage doors work in a similar way.

Someone wants to write down a quick idea.
Write this down.
Save a note: buy a new watch strap.
Jot down my idea about the garden path.
Put this in my notes.
jot down: brighten the hall, its so ugly, paitn it yellow
Could you please keep a voice note while I talk?
Start a new note called trip ideas.
Remember this for later.

Priya, an office worker, was packing up at five. The air outside was chilly, and she wanted to remember to buy a pound of coffee on the way home. She said, "Remind me to get a pound of coffee when I'm near the store on Main Street." Then she added, "And tomorrow at three, remind me to breathe and take a short break for twenty-five minutes." The assistant understood two reminders. The first would go off when she was near the store, and the second would ring tomorrow at three. It said, "Both reminders are set." Priya smiled, put on her scarf, and walked out of the building.

Maya, a teenager, was texting from her room. Her little brother had been on the tablet for hours, and the wifi signal was weak. She typed to the assistant, "Could you please limit my brother's screen time to one hour tonight? He has a test tomorrow, and Grandma will fly into town on Friday, so I want him to rest and be ready." The assistant understood that Maya wanted a one-hour limit on her brother's tablet for tonight. It set the tablet to turn off after one hour. It replied, "Done. His tablet will stop after one hour tonight. Do you want me to remind him to go to bed?" Maya typed, "yes, at nine."

name: plan_workout
does: Makes a simple workout plan for the day or the week, with sets, reps and rest days.
inputs: the goal, how many days a week, and how long each workout can be
people say:
- I had a big salad, so what should I train today?
- Text me tomorrow's exercises before I get to the gym.
- My race is near, so ease up this week.
- Give me a plan with two rest days.
- How many sets of squats should I do?

Eli had just woken up, still in his pajamas. He walked to the window and saw that the water in the pool looked green. Yesterday he had paid a man to fix the pool cleaner, and he wanted it to make the pool shine. He rubbed his eyes and said, "Start the pool cleaner and tell me the water temperature." The assistant understood two requests. It started the cleaner and checked the heater. Then it said, "The cleaner is running. The water is seventy-eight degrees." Eli yawned and said, "Good. Let me know when it's done." The assistant promised to tell him in an hour, and Eli went to make breakfast.

We measure things so that everyone agrees how big, heavy or warm something is. Lengths use inches or meters, weights use pounds or kilograms, and temperatures use degrees. People often need to change from one unit to another, especially when they visit another country. They say, "How many cups is half a liter?" or "What is seventy degrees in Celsius?" A recipe may call for grams while a kitchen scale shows ounces. A purple box of rice might list both. When the numbers are different, people ask for the other unit: "Tell me that in kilometers," or "Say it in feet." It helps to remember a few simple facts, like one kilometer being a little more than half a mile.

Someone wants the robot vacuum to start cleaning now.
Start cleaning.
start the vaccum in the kitchen
Do the floors before my guests arrive.
I'd be glad if you'd send the robot out now.
Can the robot do the garage first?
Time to tidy the floors.
Go vacuum.
Please run the cleaner, the house is a mess.

Person: Play the radio.
Assistant: Which station would you like?
Person: The kids one with the funny songs.
Assistant: Okay, playing Kids Fun Radio. Is the volume all right?
Person: Yes, it's a lovely song. What is the date of the next funny show? Can you record it tomorrow at seven?
Assistant: The next show is on Friday. I'm sorry, I can't record radio shows. I can remind you to listen tomorrow at seven.
Person: Okay, do that.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you tomorrow at seven.

Bread dough needs time to rise, which means it slowly gets bigger as tiny bubbles form inside it. Rising time is for making soft bread. In a warm kitchen, as in August, dough rises faster. In winter it may need more time. People change the baking time, the oven heat and how much they make. They say, "Bake it ten minutes longer," or "Lower the oven to three hundred and fifty." You can see when a cake is ready if it turns golden. When someone at home is sick, a plain warm roll is a nice thing to bake.

Someone wants a sentence translated into Spanish.
Translate this into Spanish.
How do you say it in Spanish?
Put the line about the dark room into Spanish.
I need this in Spanish by tomorrow at seven.
Can you turn my message into Spanish?
What's the Spanish for good morning?
Please translate this note for my neighbor, and I need it before Wednesday.
Spanish version, please.

Hana was in a hurry. She needed a new jacket for a trip, and the shop was closing soon. She said to her phone, "Order the grey jacket in medium, and send it tomorrow at seven in the morning, because I rise early and I'll be home." The assistant understood that Hana wanted the grey jacket, size medium, delivered at seven the next morning. It placed the order, picked the early delivery time, and said, "Your jacket will arrive tomorrow at seven. I will text you when the driver is near." Hana smiled. She grabbed her keys and ran out the door.

A note is a quick way to keep something you do not want to forget. You can type it or say it out loud. Voice notes are handy when your hands are busy, such as when you lift a box on the stairs or stir a hot pot. People ask, "Write this down," or "Find my note about the garden." They change notes too: "Add milk to my shopping note," "Delete the last line," or "Read me what I wrote." Old notes can be found by a word you remember, so people say, "Show me the notes with the word paint." A good note is short and clear.

name: drive_time
does: Tells how long a drive will take right now, including traffic.
inputs: where you start and where you are going
people say:
- How long to the berry farm?
- Can I afford to leave at nine, or will I be late?
- The roads are icy, so how bad is the drive to work?
- Is there a lot of traffic to the airport?
- When should I leave to get there by noon?

Mr. Alvarez, a retired teacher, sat at his kitchen table with his tablet. 'Plan my dinners for Monday to Friday,' he told the assistant. 'Start with fish on Monday, and then email the plan to my daughter.' The assistant made a five-day dinner plan and got ready to send it to his daughter Lucia. Then Mr. Alvarez remembered something. 'Wait, not fish on Monday. Make it chicken. Lucia does not like fish.' The assistant changed Monday from fish to chicken and said so out loud. It also put a big pot of vegetable soup on Wednesday, because he wanted one easy night. Mr. Alvarez said the pot was as heavy as a stone, but he liked it. The assistant said the plan was ready, and it sent the email with the new list to Lucia. He smiled. His week of meals was done.

A weather forecast tells you what the sky will probably do, so you can plan your day. Each morning, many people ask their phone or speaker for it. They can change the place, the day, or the kind of news they want. You might say, What's the weather in Leeds on Saturday? Or, Will it rain this afternoon? If you want to know what to wear, you can ask, Do I need a coat today? or How cold is it outside? Some people ask for a warning, like Tell me if it will rain, so they do not forget their umbrella. Others plan a trip and ask, Will it be sunny when I pick pears on Sunday? A forecast is only a good guess, but it gets better the closer the day comes.

Priya was waiting for the bus and texting her phone assistant. She typed, Hello, could you please tune the radio app to the local news station, because my grandfather says there is a traffic problem near our school and I want to know if the bus will be late? The assistant understood that she wanted two things: the news station, and the traffic report. It opened the radio app, found the station, and started playing it. For the first moment she heard only music. She swiped the screen to turn the sound up, and soon a man began to read the news. The assistant told her the traffic report would come at ten past the hour. Priya asked it to remind her, and it set a reminder for ten past.

Someone wants a taxi to come to their home soon.
Get me a cab.
I need a ride from my house in ten minutes.
Can a car pick me up at the corner? Not at the main door.
Send a taxi, please, but not a big van.
My dad and I need to get to the station, and we will split the cost.
Book me a ride, and do not pick the cheapest one, because the last driver was rude and bitter.
Is there a car nearby that can take me to the airport?
I would be very grateful if you could arrange a ride for half past six this evening.

Tom was a busy parent with a full day ahead. His hands were covered in cake mix for his daughter's birthday party, so he spoke to his phone. 'Call my mother on speaker. Do not leave a voicemail if she does not answer, because I will try again later.' The assistant understood. It called his mother and turned on the speaker, so Tom could keep mixing. The phone rang and rang. Tom said, 'Don't hang up too soon, she is slow to get to the phone.' The assistant let it ring a long time, but nobody answered. It told him that his mother did not pick up and that it had left no voicemail, just as he asked. Tom nodded and put the cake in the oven.

Mrs. Okafor owned a small shop, and she wanted to take her helpers out for dinner. She had heard good things about an Italian place near the shop. 'Find that restaurant and book a table for twenty-five people on Friday at seven,' she told her phone. The assistant found the restaurant and looked at the booking page. It said large groups needed a manual check by the staff, so the assistant could not book the table by itself. Instead, it sent a request for twenty-five people at seven on Friday and told Mrs. Okafor that the staff would reply soon. While she waited, she went back to the jigsaw puzzle on her counter. An hour later, the restaurant said yes, and the assistant told her the table was hers.

When you book a ride, the app needs to know where you are and where you want to go. Then it finds a driver and tells you when the car will arrive. People change the pickup point and the time a lot. They say, Pick me up at the park gate, or Come to the back door, or Make it twenty minutes later. If the car is late, they ask, Where is my driver? Someone going to the recycling center with old boxes may ask for a car with a big trunk. A good assistant should understand that Make it later and Come in ten minutes both change the pickup time. Drivers are often proud of a clean car, and riders like to know what kind of car is coming.

name: turn_on_subtitles
does: Shows words on the screen for what the actors say, and picks the language and the size of the words.
inputs: the show or screen, on or off, and the language
people say:
- I can't hear the actors, show me the words
- The baby is asleep, so keep the sound off and put the text on
- The voices are so rough and mumbly, I can't follow
- The actors whisper too much, can you show captions
- My dog's leash is in one hand and the remote is lost, put words on the screen in Spanish

Person: Morning. Move my dentist appointment to tomorrow at seven.
Assistant: Do you mean seven in the morning or seven in the evening?
Person: Evening. Sorry, my head is still foggy. It is so cold in here and the light is too bright.
Assistant: No problem. I moved the dentist to tomorrow at seven in the evening. Can I help with anything else?
Person: Is Dana free then?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can only see your calendar, not Dana's. You could send her a message to ask.
Person: Okay, I will do that after coffee. Thanks.

name: warm_up_room
does: Uses the home network to turn up the heat in one room to a chosen temperature by a chosen time.
inputs: the room, the temperature, and the time
people say:
- It's freezing in the bedroom
- I came in with wet boots and my feet are like ice
- Have the living room cozy by six
- Get the bathroom warm before my shower
- The temperature will drop tonight, so heat up the hall

Jun had just moved to the city, and it was a cold morning, so he wore his thick coat to the market. He was still learning to translate prices in his head, so he took out his phone and typed in a hurry: wat is 48 times 3, then plus 15. The assistant understood that he wanted 48 multiplied by three, and then fifteen added to the answer. It said the answer was 159. Jun was buying three scarves for his new flat, and each one cost 48, plus a small bag for 15. He thanked the assistant, paid the seller, and put the scarves in his bag. Then he walked home through the busy streets, happy that he knew the right total.

Person: clean the flor
Assistant: Which room should the robot vacuum clean, the kitchen or the living room?
Person: kitchen. a cake fell on the floor and there are crumbs everywhere
Assistant: Oh no, I'm sorry about the cake. I will send the vacuum to the kitchen now. Should it mop too?
Person: no, i don't know how that works, just vacuum
Assistant: Okay, vacuum only. It will go back to its dock and stay away from the kitchen when it is done.

A cycling app records your rides: how far you went, how fast you were, and which route you took. It is for seeing how you are getting better and for planning your next trip. People change the goal or the route as they go. They say, Update my goal to fifty kilometers this week, or Show me a flatter route. On a rare sunny day off, someone may ask for a longer loop. Others ask, How fast was I yesterday? or Stop recording, I am at the cafe. Some friends turn it into a game and compare who rode the most. After a ride, you can say, Save this trip, and the app keeps it.

Recipes, shops and roads use different units, so people often need to change one into another. A cook may find a fancy recipe from another country that lists grams, while the kitchen scale shows ounces. Someone buying rice may see kilos on the bag but want pounds. People ask, How many cups is 200 grams of rice? or Give me that in ounces, please. Others say, I like Celsius, so tell me the oven heat that way. Runners ask how many miles are in ten kilometers. The helper does the sum and says the new number with its unit, so the cook knows exactly how much to weigh out.

Water comes into your home through a pipe, and a meter counts how much you use. The water heater keeps some of it hot, so you can have a warm shower. A small leak can waste a lot of water, so people want quick news about it. They say, Tell me if the water runs all night, or Why is my water bill so high? Some people change the heat: Make the water hotter, or Turn the heater down while we are away. A grandma who loves long baths may say, Warm the tank by evening. When the pipes are fine, the helper just says nothing is wrong.

A student wants to know what homework is due tomorrow.
whats due tomorow
What homework do I have for tomorrow?
Anything due soon?
I have a cold and missed class, so tell me what I need to hand in.
List my assignments by date.
Did the teacher shift the science deadline?
I am sleepy, so just say which task I should finish first.
Could you please tell me everything I still need to turn in this week, so that I can plan my evenings?
Show me tomorrow's schoolwork.

Rosa, a gardener, came in from the garden with dirt on her hands. Her dog Pepper stood by his empty bowl and looked at her. 'Pepper looks thirsty, and his bowl is bone dry,' Rosa said to the speaker. The assistant understood that she wanted the water bowl filled. It turned on the pet fountain in the kitchen, and fresh water began to flow. Rosa also said she had to drive to the gym at six. The assistant offered to remind her to take Pepper for a walk before then, and she said yes. It set the reminder for five o'clock. Pepper drank his water, wagged his tail, and went to find his favorite ball.

Kai was in his room, texting the home assistant. 'Dude, it's too hot up here. Can you make it two degrees cooler and run the fan twice as fast?' The house had started to fill with heat after dinner, because his dad had cooked beef stew all afternoon. The assistant understood that Kai wanted the air conditioning lowered by two degrees and the fan made faster. It did both, and it told him the new setting was 22 degrees. Kai asked if that was a total of two degrees lower than before, and the assistant said yes. After ten minutes, the room felt fresh, and Kai went back to his game.

In August, the weather can change fast, so many people check it often. A forecast tells you the heat, the wind, and the chance of rain. It is meant to help you choose what to do and what to wear. You may notice a round sun symbol on a clear day and a gray cloud on a rainy one. People change the place and the time: What will it be like in Rome on Friday? or Check this weekend. They also ask for alerts, like Tell me if it will storm tonight. Or they ask about clothes: Should I take a jacket? Each answer helps them be ready.

A calendar helps you remember what you plan to do and when. You can put in meetings, birthdays, and free time. Most of the time, you ask to add, move, or remove things. Someone says, Put lunch with Sam on Thursday at noon, or Move my meeting to later, or Cancel Friday's class. Others ask, Am I free on Monday afternoon? A light week might have only one event on it. Before a trip, a person may add, Pack bags at six, and a note to buy an apple for the road. When your plans change, you just tell the calendar the new day or time, and it keeps everything in order.

A cook wants a recipe made for six people instead of four.
Make this serve six.
Scale it up for six people, but don't change the cooking time.
I'm cooking for my friend the nurse and four others, so adjust the amounts.
Bump the recipe up to six portions.
Increase everything by half.
Don't give me cups, only grams, for six people.
Please rewrite the list at the bottom of the page for six, because I want a dish to brighten up the party table and I do not want to run out.

Ben was eight, and he was baking cookies with his mom. The baking sheet was already in the oven, and he wanted to know when to take it out. He typed to the speaker in a hurry: set a timr for twelve minutes and make it sing. The assistant understood that Ben wanted a twelve-minute timer. It said it could not sing, but it could make a happy bell sound, and Ben said that was fine. It was strange to wait so quietly, so he watched the oven light. When the twelve minutes were up, the bell rang. Ben shouted, 'Cookies!' and his mom took out the sheet with big oven gloves.

Babies need food and sleep at regular times, and parents often use a digital helper to keep track. A feeding reminder tells you when the last bottle was and when the next one is due. A nap timer shows how long the baby has slept. A baby monitor lets you hear or see the room from far away. Parents change things by saying, Remind me to feed the baby at three, or Start the nap timer, or Turn the monitor up. In autumn, when evenings come early, they may say, Dim the nursery light at six. If the baby stirs, the monitor sends a message to the phone.

name: night_check
does: Looks at the cameras, doors, and windows each night and gives a short report on anything open or moving.
inputs: the time of the check, and which rooms to include
people say:
- Is the house safe before I go to bed?
- Did I lock up?
- Arrange a look at all the doors at ten
- Did anything odd happen in the middle of the night?
- Make sure the garage is shut

Person: turn on the lihgt
Assistant: Which light, the hallway, the kitchen, or the bedroom?
Person: near the door. i have to ride my bike to the market for a vegetable box
Assistant: The light near the door is on. Do you want it bright?
Person: yes full. and make it blue
Assistant: I'm sorry, that lamp only makes white light, so I can't make it blue. Shall I keep it on bright white?
Person: ok fine. thanks

Dana, a nurse, came home after a night shift, tired and sore. The hot tub on the patio looked cold and gray in the morning light. 'The hot tub is freezing and I really need to soak,' she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted warm water. It turned on the heater and set the water to 38 degrees. It told her the tub would be ready in about an hour. Dana put the kettle on the stove and made some tea while she waited. She also asked the assistant to write the filter check on her main list, so she would not forget it. The assistant added it for the weekend. An hour later, the water was warm.

A home security system watches your house when you are away. Cameras record, sensors notice when doors or windows open, and an alarm sings out loudly if something is wrong. The price depends on how many parts you want. No system is perfect, so people check on it often. They say, Is the front door locked? or Turn on the alarm, I am leaving. They ask to see a camera: Show me the back yard. Or they ask for news: Tell me if someone comes to the door. Some people need quiet after a false alarm and say, Turn it off, it was just me.

Leo woke up on Sunday morning and reached for his phone. He typed fast: what moovies are on near me tonight. The assistant understood that he wanted cinema times for films showing that evening. It found three cinemas close by and read the times out loud. There was a single showing of the dog film at eight. Leo remembered that the trailer had a dog with a red collar, and he had paused it the night before. He asked the assistant to continue the trailer where he stopped. It did, and the little dog ran across the screen again. Leo laughed, and the assistant asked if he wanted it to save the eight o'clock time. He said yes.

A coffee machine, a kettle, and an oven all do one job: they heat something. A smart kitchen helper lets you control them with your voice. People change the time or the heat. They say, Heat the oven to 180, or Boil the kettle, or Make a strong coffee. Some tasks are difficult to remember, like the dishwasher, so people say, Tell me when the dishes are done. When you bake, you can follow your nose, but a timer helps more. Some machines can email you or send a message when a job is finished, so you do not need to stand next to them.

Hector drove a bus at night and slept in the daytime. One afternoon, he lay down with a sour taste of coffee still in his mouth. 'Wake me at four,' he told the speaker. Then he thought for a moment. 'No, wait, make it five. My grandma comes at six, and I want an hour to clear the kitchen first.' The assistant understood that Hector was fixing the time. It cancelled the alarm for four and set a new one for five, and it told him plainly that it had made the change. Hector said thanks, closed his eyes, and fell asleep.

Marco, a cook, was planning a party for his sister. His hands were full of flour, so he talked to the speaker. 'Guest list,' he said. The assistant opened the party guest list and read out the twelve names. 'Sort names,' Marco said next. The assistant put the names in order from A to Z and said so. Marco wanted a calm mood in the room, so he said, 'Soft music.' The assistant played some gentle piano songs. Marco smiled, put a plant on the table, and went back to his dough. He liked that he only needed two words each time, and the assistant always understood what he meant.

Person: Did my parcel come?
Assistant: I see two parcels on the way. Which one do you mean, the books or the lamp?
Person: The books. Is it more than one box? I saw a flash of the van outside.
Assistant: Yes, the books are in two boxes, and the van stopped at your street a minute ago.
Person: Can you tell the driver to leave them on the porch? My mailbox is messy and it hasn't got enough depth for a box.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't talk to the driver or change the delivery. I can remind you when the boxes are marked as delivered.
Person: Okay, please do that.

name: read_aloud
does: Reads text from a page, a letter, or a message out loud in a clear voice at the speed you choose.
inputs: what to read, and how slow or fast
people say:
- My eyes are tired, can you read this to me?
- Say that message out loud, slowly
- I can't see the small print on the cereal box, what does it say?
- Go straight to the last paragraph and read it
- My eyes water when I look at the screen too long, so speak the page for me

Sana had just moved to the city, and her new job sent her an invoice in a language she did not know well. The page took a long time to load on her phone, and then she saw a line with words she could not read. She said to her assistant, 'Please translate minimum payment into French and show me how to spell it.' The assistant understood that she wanted two things at once: a translation and the spelling. It said the words were paiement minimum, and it spelled them out one letter at a time. Sana wrote them down in her notebook. She felt proud, because she could now find the right line on the invoice.

name: gift_idea_finder
does: Suggests gifts for a person based on their age, what they like, and how much you want to spend.
inputs: who the gift is for, what they enjoy, and a budget
people say:
- What should I get my uncle for his birthday?
- I need something fast, the party is tomorrow
- Any ideas for a ten year old who loves space?
- Help, I have twenty dollars and no clue
- Finding a present is such a hard task, so say what is popular right now

Person: Record a video.
Assistant: Sure. Which camera should I use, the one in the hallway or the one in the kitchen?
Person: Hallway. I wonder if the cat does her morning run again.
Assistant: Okay. How long should I record?
Person: Twice as long as yesterday.
Assistant: Yesterday's clip was five minutes, so I will record ten. Do you want to share it afterwards?
Person: Yes, send it to my sister. That cat is her favourite.

A bill tells you how much you owe for something like electricity, water, or rent, and when it must be paid. Paying on time avoids angry letters and extra fees. People keep track of due dates so they do not forget. They say, When is my electric bill due? or Remind me to pay rent on the first, or Pay the water bill on Friday. Bills often climb in winter, so someone may ask, Why did it go up this month? Each month, a family may set money aside, just like they buy grapes every week, so that the bills never come as a surprise.

Grandpa Joe wanted to cook his mother's soup for his young grandson. He did not know all the steps by heart, so he took out his phone and typed in a hurry: how long do i boil the potatos for soup. The assistant understood that he wanted the boiling time. It said about twenty minutes, until the potatoes are soft when you poke them with a fork. Grandpa Joe said, 'Good, now I'm saving this recipe so I never lose it.' The assistant saved the steps in his favorites list and told him where to find them. The soup smelled wonderful, and the boy ate two bowls.

name: repeat_order
does: Sets up a weekly food order that is sent by itself, so the same meal arrives at the same time each week.
inputs: the restaurant, the meal, and the day and time
people say:
- Get me pizza every Friday at six
- The kids want their usual dinner again
- Same as last time, but every week
- Write down my order for each Tuesday and don't ask me again
- Stop me from picking dinner over and over

Wind and rain depend on where you are, so a forecast always starts with a place. The south of a country is often warmer, so a trip there needs different clothes. People ask for a forecast and then change it: Show me the south coast, or Zoom in on my town, or What about next Tuesday? Before walking the dog, someone may ask, Will it rain in the next hour? Rain maps let you zoom in until you can see your own street. People also ask for more or less detail, like Just tell me hot or cold, or Give me the wind speed too.

Nina was an office worker, and she was working late on a budget for her team. Her boss wanted to raise the money for the kitchen, including a new stove. Nina looked at her numbers and said to her assistant, 'Add 340 and 275, and then tell me what half of that is.' The assistant understood that she wanted two answers in a row. First, it said the sum was 615. Then it said half of 615 was 307.5. Nina wrote both numbers in her sheet. She thanked the assistant and sent the budget to her boss before the end of the day.

Grandma Ruth sat on the porch on a chilly afternoon with a book and a blanket. She said to her tablet, 'Could you please set a timer for twenty-five minutes of reading, and then a five-minute break, because my doctor says I should rest my eyes and I always forget?' The assistant understood that she wanted a focus timer followed by a short break. It set both and told her plainly what it had done. Ruth also said she had to drive to the shop at five, and the assistant added a reminder. When the first timer rang, a woman walking by waved at her, and Ruth waved back and rested her eyes.

A washing machine cleans clothes with water, soap, and spinning. A dial or an app sets the heat, the spin, and the time. People change these things by saying, Wash on cold, or Make it quicker, or Spin it slower. A number on the machine shows how many minutes are left. Dryers spend more energy than washers, so many people dry less and hang clothes instead. If you see a weird stain, you can ask, How do I get this stain out? Some people ask for a message when the wash is done: Tell me when the laundry is finished, and then they can fold it before it wrinkles.

Omar had just moved to the city and could not work out his oven. The paper manual was a document in another language, and he did not want to read all of it. He was upstairs and the kitchen was downstairs, so he called out to the speaker, 'Make the oven hotter, by about twenty degrees.' The assistant understood that Omar wanted the heat raised. The oven was at 180, so it set it to 200 and said so. Omar decided to bake bread that night, so he asked for a timer of thirty minutes too. The assistant started it. Omar went downstairs, and the whole house soon smelled warm and good.

Mr. Chen owned a pepper and spice shop, and he was very busy. His customers called out from the counter asking about the City game. He said to his phone, 'Could you please tell me the score of the City match, and if it is not over, tell me when it ends, because I want to close early and I need enough time to get home before the crowd?' The assistant understood that he wanted the score and the end time. It said City was winning two to one with ten minutes left. Mr. Chen told his customers the news, and they cheered. The assistant told him again when the match was over.

Lena, a student, woke up when the power went out in her building. It was dark and quiet. She found her flashlight, an important item, and said to her phone, 'Excuse me, could you please tell me if there is a power cut in my area and when it will end, because my flatmates are out and my phone battery is getting low?' The assistant checked and said that there was planned work on her street. The power would come back at ten o'clock. Lena stirred her soup on the gas stove, and ate it in the light of the flashlight. She was glad that her electricity bill was already paid, and she waited for the lights to come back.

Person: Yes, do that at six.

Rosa the gardener was kneeling in the flower bed when her phone buzzed. She had her headphones on, so she pressed the button and said, 'Who is at the front door? And don't unlock it, I do not want anyone walking in.' The assistant understood two things: she wanted to know who was there, and she wanted the door to stay locked. It showed the doorbell camera on her screen. A man in a blue cap was holding a box. 'That is the plant delivery,' Rosa said. 'Tell him to leave it by the gate.' The assistant spoke through the doorbell and passed on the message. The door stayed locked the whole time. It was a sunny day, and Rosa had planned to plant tomatoes before lunch, so she went back to work.

name: water_heater_boost
does: Heats the water tank harder for a set time so there is plenty of hot water for the next use.

people say:

- Book some extra hot water for Saturday morning
- Turn the boiler up for a bit, guests are coming

Priya had ten minutes to reach the dentist and no place to park. 'Get me a parking spot near Elm Street,' she said to her phone, 'but not the garage, I do not want to pay the new price.' The assistant understood that she wanted a spot on the street and not the garage. It found a free space one block away, in front of a shop with a blue blind over the door, and it showed her the way. Priya parked in two minutes. Then she said, 'Tell me when my time runs out.' The assistant set a timer for the two hours the sign allowed and promised to speak up ten minutes before the end.

When you shop from another country, the price is shown in a different currency, like euros or yen. The exchange rate tells you how much of your own money one unit costs. Rates change a little every day, so people ask the assistant to check them. My mother likes to see prices in her own money before she buys salty snacks abroad. She says, 'How much is that in dollars?' or 'What is the rate today?' She can also ask to change her home currency, or to show prices in two currencies at once. Travelers say things like 'Tell me what I will spend in pounds' or 'Use yesterday's rate.' It helps them know what things really cost.

Person: Set a reading time for the kids tonight.
Assistant: What time should I set it for?
Person: Seven. Actually, make it half past seven. Grandpa is still mowing the lawn and he wants to join us.
Assistant: Done. Reading time is at 7:30 tonight. Which book should I open?
Person: The one we read yesterday. Does it work offline?
Assistant: Yes, that book is saved on the device, so it works offline. I will open it at chapter four, where you stopped.
Person: Great, thanks.

Many phones can read text aloud, make words bigger, or take voice commands. These tools help people who cannot see small print or who find touching a screen hard. Some people feel it is strange at first to hear their phone talk, but they soon get used to it. They change the speed of the voice, the size of the letters, and which parts are read. They say things like 'Read this page to me,' 'Make the text bigger,' or 'Slow down a little.' A cook who is roasting a chicken with soap on her hands might say, 'Read me the next step.' With voice control, no touching is needed at all.

name: dose_reminder_check
does: Checks that a medicine dose is correct for the time of day and notifies the person when the next one is due.
inputs: the name of the medicine, the dose, and the times it should be taken
people say:
- Did I take my pills this morning?
- Tell me when my uncle needs his next tablet
- Is two spoons the correct amount of cough syrup?
- Remind me about my medicine at eight
- When is my next dose?

Grandpa Leo joined a weekly call with his old team. The room was dark, and the picture on his tablet looked gray. 'I can't see anybody,' he said, 'it's too dim in here.' The assistant understood that he wanted a brighter screen, so it raised the brightness. Then Leo said, 'I can't hear him speak.' The assistant turned up the call volume. A friend on the call asked about the weather in Leo's town, and the whole group laughed about the rain. At the end, Leo asked, 'Do I need to do anything now?' The assistant said the call was over and offered to leave the meeting. He said yes, and it did.

Mrs. Patel owns a small shop, and she needed a sign about refunds. At closing time she told her phone, 'Write a short note for the door. I will print it tomorrow at nine.' The assistant understood that she wanted a draft. 'Say that refunds are given within seven days,' she added. It wrote three clear lines and counted the words: twenty-two. 'Make it more straight to the point,' she said. The assistant cut it down to fourteen words. Then she said, 'Press save.' The assistant saved the note with the name Door Sign and set a reminder for nine the next morning so she would remember to print it. She locked up and went home.

Walter does not like technology, but his electric bill was heavy this month. He sat down and said to the speaker, 'Why is my power so high? I use half as much as my neighbor.' The assistant did not argue. It looked at his use and said that he had used double last month's amount in the evenings. 'What is using it all?' he asked. It said the old heater and a fridge in the garage use the most. 'Start with the heater,' Walter said. 'Turn it off at ten every night.' The assistant made a plan to switch off the smart plug at ten. Walter did not know what a smart plug was, so it explained: a small box between the wall and the heater that it can turn on and off. He nodded.

A monthly budget is a plan for your money. It says how much comes in and how much goes out for rent, food, bills and fun. Most people keep it private and look at it when they want to know if they can afford something. They change a budget when life changes. They say 'Put fifty back into savings,' 'Lower my food limit,' or 'How much is left this month?' Some people want to translate a big bill into a small weekly cost, so they ask, 'What is my rent per week?' A budget is not a set of strict rules. It is a way to see where your money goes, and to change it before it runs out.

Nina was running for the bus when her phone rang with a number she did not know. 'My hands are full with this pink folder and this document, and I never know who keeps calling me,' she said, out of breath. The assistant understood that she could not type, and that she wanted to know who it was and to keep the number. It said the caller was not in her contacts. 'Save it as Sam from work,' Nina said. The assistant saved the number under that name. 'He joined the team last week, and his birthday is in March,' she added. It put the birthday in too. Nina made the bus with a second to spare.

It suggested a warm wash with extra soap and offered to compare two cycles: the quick wash and the cotton wash. It said the cotton wash takes longer but cleans better. 'Then use that one,' Carlos said. The assistant started the washing machine on the cotton cycle and told him it would finish in an hour and ten minutes.

Many families set rules for screen time so that kids have time to play, read and sleep. A parent can choose how many minutes a child may use a tablet each day, and which apps are allowed. Kids like to download games or draw on the screen, but the time stops when the limit is reached. Parents change the rules often. Bedtime is early on school nights, and later on the weekend. They say 'Give her thirty more minutes,' 'Turn the tablet off at eight,' or 'No videos before homework is done.' The idea is not to punish children. It is to help them have a good balance between screens and the rest of the day.

Ben woke up and heard his sister's radio playing upstairs. 'Coffee, please,' he mumbled to the kitchen speaker. The assistant started the coffee machine and said it would take four minutes. 'Quieter,' Ben added, and the assistant lowered the volume of the kitchen radio. Then Ben began to worry that he had slept too long and would miss the bus. 'What time is it?' he asked. The assistant said it was 7:40, and the bus came at eight. Ben relaxed, poured his coffee, and drank it slowly by the window.

Jade was at the beach with her friends, wearing her purple swimsuit. She typed to her phone, 'check the water temp, is it warmer than yesterday?' The assistant checked and said the water was 21 degrees, two degrees warmer than the day before. Jade typed again, 'do i need more sun cream? i have a volleyball match at three.' The assistant said the sun was strong today, so she should put on twice as much cream as usual, and again after swimming. Jade asked it to remind her at two, and it set the reminder. She ran into the waves with a big smile.

Email is a way to send letters over the internet. Your inbox is where new messages arrive, and unread ones are shown in bold. You can write an email, attach a photo or a file, and send it in a second. A spam filter gives each message a score, and mail with a high score goes to the junk folder. People change how email looks and works. Some choose dark mode for reading at night, or change the width of the message list. They say things like 'Show unread mail,' 'Attach this photo,' or 'Move this to junk.' It is a quiet way to stay in touch with people.

'the restaurant one is nice,' Leo wrote. 'tell them thanks and change the reservation to five people.' The assistant wrote a short reply with both things in it and sent it. A minute later the restaurant answered that five people was fine. Leo put his phone away and looked out of the window.

A bookmark saves your place so you can pick up a book where you left off. Phones do the same: they remember the chapter and the page. Reading time is how long you read each day, and many people set a goal, like twenty minutes. People change their goals and their places. They say 'Go to chapter five,' 'Mark this page,' or 'Remind me to read at nine.' Some people mix paper books with audiobooks, and the phone keeps both places. If you feel sorry to stop at the end of a chapter, you can say 'One more chapter,' and the timer waits. A story about the ocean can feel short even when it is long.

Holidays are days when families and friends get together, often with decorations, special food and old traditions. Planning means choosing a day, a place, a guest list and a menu. People who feed many guests count how many will come. Plans go well when there is a list, but they change often. People say 'Add two more guests,' 'Move dinner to six,' or 'Remind me to buy lights.' Traditions can be small. A child might paint a red nose on a snowman every year, and everyone looks forward to it. A holiday is about being together more than about getting everything perfect.

Maya was a student with a lawn to cut before her parents got back from the shops. 'How long will the robot mower take for half the lawn?' she asked the speaker. The assistant said it would take about forty minutes. 'Then cut the front half only,' Maya said, 'and hold the sprinklers until it is done.' The assistant started the mower on the front lawn and paused the sprinklers. It told her it would send a message when the mower finished. Her parents were due back in an hour, so there was plenty of time. Maya sat down with her homework.

Omar woke up with a heavy head and an empty wallet. 'How much money do I have until payday?' he asked his phone. The assistant said he had 85 dollars left in his account. Omar also said, 'Remind me to iron my shirt for work.' The assistant set a reminder for tonight at eight. Omar got out of bed and made himself some toast.

Bin day is the day the truck comes for your rubbish. Most homes have a bin for paper, one for plastic, and sometimes one for food scraps. The point is to keep things that can be used again out of the trash. Some things, like an old television, need a special pickup and should never go in the bin. People change the day or ask for more pickups when they have more rubbish than usual. They say 'When is bin day?', 'Which bin is for pizza boxes?', or 'Remind me the night before.' Neighbors climb the steps with heavy bags every week, so a reminder really helps.

A recipe is a list of steps for making a dish. It tells you the oven temperature and the cooking time, like a map that shows you the way to something delicious. People change recipes all the time. They ask for more servings, a lower heat, or a shorter time. They say 'Set the oven to 180,' 'Hold the timer for five minutes,' or 'What is the next step?' If a cake needs forty minutes, a timer tells you when it is ready. A good tip is to ask the assistant to read each step as you go, so your hands stay free for the cooking.

Sam smiled and kept cutting.

On social media, a post is a photo, a video or a few words that you share with your followers. People use posts to show a trip, a new baby or a big ship they saw in the harbour. Most apps let you change a lot about how they work. You can ask the assistant to turn off notifications, hide the likes or stop videos from playing by themselves. People say things like, "stop the clips from starting on their own," or "tell me only when my sister posts." If you want to know the exact number of people who follow you, you can ask for that too.

Mr. Ortiz did not like phones much, but his grandson had set up the assistant for him. A neighbour was coming for a picnic, and the grass was long. So the assistant started the mower for three o'clock and stopped the sprinklers until tomorrow.

My brother is away this week and I promised him I'd look after his tomatoes, and the whole bed looks dry." When Lena got home, her shoes were muddy. She wiped them on the mat and went to look. The tomatoes were wet, and the leaves looked happy again.

Mr. Patel owned a small shop, and on Friday it was ten years old. "Could you please make my lemon cake recipe big enough for thirty people? Priya had just come to the city and her flat was full of boxes. "I need double the tape and half as many bags," she told her phone. The assistant looked up parking near her street and found two places. Priya wanted a single bed, so she asked for shops that sold one. While she waited she began to peel the old tape off a box. The assistant sent her three shops near the flat.

Grandma Ruth stood in the garden and looked at her beans. "Oh dear, those poor beans look so thirsty," she said to the garden speaker. She did not say the word water, but the assistant understood what she meant. It turned on the drip hose by the bean row for fifteen minutes. Ruth hoped the leaves would stand up again. "And tell me when the next dry day is," she added. The assistant looked at the calendar and the weather and told her the next dry date was Thursday. Ruth smiled, and she asked it to remind her that morning to pick the beans.

Lena owned a toy shop, and the lantern festival was only days away. 'Add paper lanterns to my list and tell me if Friday will be stormy,' she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted two things: put paper lanterns on the shopping list, and check the weather for Friday. It added the lanterns and then said Friday would be stormy, with strong wind in the afternoon. Lena had planned to hang the lanterns in the yard outside the shop. She touched the screen and asked the assistant to move the plan to Saturday instead. The assistant changed her reminder to Saturday morning.

Most pets eat at the same times every day. A feeding schedule tells you when the dog or cat gets its food and how much. People use it so nobody forgets or feeds the pet twice. Families change the schedule when they go camping, when the vet says the pet is too heavy or when the weather is hot. You can ask an assistant for these changes in plain words. People say, "remind me to feed Max at six," or "give Luna a smaller dinner," or "fold the Sunday walk into the Saturday one." The main thing is to keep the times the same, so the pet knows when to expect its food.

Ben was lying in bed. His mum had told him about a toy sale on Saturday, so he said to the speaker, 'Wake me up at six so we can go to the sale.' The speaker set an alarm for six. Then Ben yawned. 'No, not six, the shop opens at nine. Make it eight.' The assistant understood that he had fixed the time, and it changed the alarm to eight. Ben wanted his room to look neat in the morning, so he asked the assistant to remind him to put his shoes away. Then he asked it to raise the volume of the lullaby a little. The assistant did, and Ben fell asleep.

When you have a party, the first thing you need is a guest list. It says who is coming and who is not. People send an email or a text to invite them, and they ask the assistant for help. They say things like, "send the invitation to everyone on my list," or "upload the photo of the cake to the party message." Later, many people change the list. They say, "add my cousin," or "take Dan off, he can't come." Some people print the invitation on thick paper and some only send it online. Either way, the assistant keeps a count of how many people said yes.

Dana was an office worker with a long list of jobs. In the morning she told her phone, "Organize my to-do list, put the report first and the phone calls after lunch." The assistant moved the report to the top and the calls to the afternoon. A moment later she changed her mind. "Sorry, not the report first, I need the order form done first." The assistant understood that she wanted the order form at the top. It moved the form up and put the report in second place. Dana felt steady again. At noon she checked off the form, and the assistant crossed it out of the list.

Person: Can you record the soup video and send it to my sister?
Assistant: Sure. Which video do you mean, the one from today or the one from last week?
Person: Today's, I'm cooking dinner right now.
Assistant: Got it. Do you want me to send it as soon as it ends?
Person: Yes, and also learn which clips I watch the most and put them in a little list for me.
Assistant: I can send the clip when it ends. I can't learn from your clips, but I can save the ones you pick into a list.
Person: Okay, that is fine.

Mrs. Boyd was a kind person who did not like new machines. On her April trip she stayed in a hotel, and the room was very dark. She stood by the bed and said, "I can hardly see in here, dear." The room assistant understood that she meant the lights were too low. It turned the lights up and said they were brighter now. Mrs. Boyd was happy. Later she said, "These towels are a mess," while she tried to fold one. The assistant understood that she wanted fresh towels, so it sent a message to the front desk. A new pile came to her door ten minutes later.

Mr. Hale was moving to a new town and was not good with phones. "I don't want the expensive movers," he said to the assistant. "And I don't want to pay for boxes I can't use again." The assistant understood that he wanted cheaper movers and no new boxes. It looked up three moving companies and sorted them by price. Then it found a shop that rents boxes, which you can return. Mr. Hale asked it to find a time for Saturday. The assistant showed him one company with a free spot on Saturday morning and wrote it on his calendar. He thanked it, a little amazed.

name: find_battery_hogs
does: Shows which apps are using the most battery on a phone or tablet and lets the person close them.
inputs: the device, and how far back to look, like today or this week
people say:
- Why is my battery dying so fast?
- Search for the app that is eating all my power.
- Which games drain the tablet the most?
- My phone died by lunch again, what did that?
- Close whatever is using the battery in the background.
- Will I make it to the next charge?

Yoga music was playing in the kitchen, but Miguel the cook found the room too bright. He began to chop peppers and said, "Dim the lights by half." The assistant lowered the ceiling lights to fifty percent. The kitchen still felt cold, so he said, "Make them warmer, more yellow." The assistant changed the bulbs to a warm yellow. Then he asked it to make the lamp over the stove twice as bright, because he needed to see the knife. The assistant raised only that lamp to full and left the rest dim. Miguel nodded and kept cooking.

They want to know when the baby is next due to eat.
Feeding time?
Next bottle?
When does she eat again?
What time did I last feed him?
I want to follow the baby's schedule today, when is the next meal?
How long since the creamy cereal at breakfast?
Can you tell me when to feed the baby next, I'm baking and I've got flour all over my hands?
Could you please let me know what time the next feed is, so I can put the baby down for a nap after?

Zoe was waiting for a package. She texted her phone, "where's my order? i need it by friday at noon." The assistant looked up the order and read the post tracking. It said the box was at the local depot and would be delivered on Thursday afternoon. That was the first good news Zoe had heard all week. She wanted to be sure, so she asked the assistant to scan her email for the delivery message. It found one and said the driver would come between two and four on Thursday. Zoe asked it to remind her at one o'clock on Thursday to be home. The assistant set the reminder.

name: scan_to_email
does: Scans a paper on the printer and sends the picture to an email address, with a friendly note if you want one.
inputs: the email address, and whether the page is in colour or in black and white
people say:

- I need a copy of this letter on my laptop
- The receipt from last year is on the glass now, can you scan it?
- Do not make me touch the screen on the printer, just scan both sides
- Can you turn this paper into a file and mail it to Dad?

Mrs. Green was a retired teacher with a big lawn. She told the garden assistant, "Please start the robot mower at ten." The assistant set it for ten o'clock. Then Mrs. Green said, "Oh, wait, my grandma is visiting at ten and sitting in the garden. Make it two o'clock instead." The assistant understood that she had changed her mind and moved the start to two. It also said the mower would cut the grass in its normal pattern and finish around four. Mrs. Green then asked it to pack the mower away in its box if it started to rain. The assistant said it could send her a message in that case, but it could not pack the mower itself.

name: tidy_contacts
does: Finds people who are saved twice in the address book and joins them into one entry.

people say:
