- Organize my address book, it's a mess.
- Sorry, I added Aunt Rita twice, can you fix that?
- Clean up the doubles in my phone numbers.
- Is Mark in there more than once?
- Give me a minute and merge the extra copies.

They want a gift idea for a friend who has a birthday soon.
Gift idea?
What should I get Sam?
I need something nice for my mum, she turns fifty.
What do you think a ten-year-old would like?
I want to see some ideas for a warm jacket or something like it.
Can you find me a present for under twenty-five dollars?
My friend lives out west and likes plants, got any thoughts?
Could you please suggest something kind and not too expensive for a coworker's birthday next week?

It was September and the first cold evening. Grandpa Joe sat in the living room and breathed on his cold hands. "Please turn the heating on and make the living room twenty degrees," he told the thermostat. The assistant turned on the radiators and set the room to twenty. Then Joe said, "And bring back the warm blanket from the bedroom, dear, if you can." The assistant said it could not carry blankets. It could, however, turn on the heater in the bedroom so the room would be warm when he went back for it. Joe laughed and said that would do.

Max was a child who loved getting letters and packages. He asked the speaker in the hall, "When will my parcel come? Mum said it's a toy." The assistant looked up the order. It said a driver would deliver the parcel tomorrow at about ten in the morning. Max looked at the sharp pencil in his hand and wrote the time on a card. Then he said, "Tell me again tomorrow at nine." The assistant made a reminder for nine o'clock. The next day, at nine, the speaker said that the parcel was close, and Max ran to the door.

Mr. Wu was not good with phones, but his daughter had put an assistant on his table. His hands were shaky and the baby upstairs was crying, so he spoke very briefly. "Pills time?" he asked. The assistant understood that he wanted to know when to take his next medicine. It said he took one pill at eight in the morning and the next was due at eight tonight. Mr. Wu was worried that it was late, but the assistant said it was still normal to wait. Then he asked it to heat the milk bottle alarm. It set a timer for the baby's milk instead and told him so.

Person: It's really hot in the room where I plan to stay next weekend.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want a room with air conditioning?
Person: Yes please. Please find something nearby the lake.
Assistant: I can look. How many nights will you stay?
Person: Three nights, from Friday.
Assistant: Thank you. I can't book a room myself, but I can search and show you hotels near the lake with air conditioning.
Person: That would be fine. My salary doesn't go far, so show the cheap ones first.
Assistant: Sure, I'll sort them by price.

name: update_mower_schedule
does: Changes the days and times when a robot mower cuts the lawn.
inputs: the mower's name, the days, and the start and end times
people say:
- Mow only on Mondays and Thursdays.
- Can you update the mower so it stops before the kids come out?
- Don't cut the grass while the toy tractor is out there.
- Start the mower an hour earlier on Saturday.
- Check online and tell me if the mower has new settings.
- I want it to rest on rainy days.

Every computer keeps your things in files, and files live in folders. A screen shows you what is open, and a battery keeps the computer going when it is not plugged in. People change a lot of small things every day. They make the screen brighter, set it to a medium size for the text or ask the computer to restart when it gets slow. You can say these things out loud to an assistant. People say, "make the text bigger," "close all the windows," or even shout, "restart the computer!" when the machine will not work. Then they wait a minute while the glass screen goes dark and comes back.

When you buy something online, the shop packs it in a bottle or a box and gives it to a delivery driver. You can follow this trip with a tracking number. It tells you where the parcel is and when it will arrive. People use this to plan their day. If the parcel is late or wrong, they ask for a refund or a new one. They say things like, "where is my order?" or "change the delivery to Friday." They may also say, "continue to send me updates," or ask for the maximum number of updates a day. Most shops give you a few days to send something back.

They want to see the emails they have not read yet.
show unread mail
unread emails?
any new mail?
what's in my inbox that i havent opened
show me the top of the inbox, the bottom can wait
I need to measure how much mail I missed, let me see the new ones.
Did anything come in while I was out marking grade papers?
Could you please open the messages I haven't read yet so I can catch up?

Hana, an office worker, came in on a freezing morning. The meeting room was cold and the heating was low. She did not want to flood the small room with heat, but she wanted it warm. "Warmer, please," she told the thermostat. The assistant understood that she wanted the temperature to go up. It raised the room from sixteen to twenty degrees and said that it would take about ten minutes. Hana put her coat on the chair and waited. When her team came in, the room was comfortable. She said, "Good," and the assistant kept the size of the heating the same.

Mrs. Lee had taught school for forty years, and now she liked to sit on her balcony with a cup of tea. One evening she said to the speaker, "Oh, it's a bit dark out here for writing, isn't it?" She did not say turn on the light, but the assistant understood. It turned on the lamp on the balcony. Mrs. Lee then said, "I wrote down a fancy word for my poem. Please keep it with my notes." The assistant opened her notes and saved the word, then asked if she wanted to read it back. She said yes, and the assistant read it out loud.

Person: hey, it's freezing in this hotel room
Assistant: Do you want me to turn the heating up?
Person: yes pls. also the room smells like oil from the kitchen
Assistant: Sorry about that. I can't change the smell, but I can ask the front desk for another room. Want me to?
Person: not now. how do i work the room tablet? i can't find the manual
Assistant: There is no paper manual, but I can read you the short guide. Do you want it?
Person: ok. then we want to dance tonight, any place near here?
Assistant: Yes, two places are close. How many people are coming?

They want to send a video clip to someone.
Send this video to Jo
Share the clip
Push that clip over to my brother
Text my mum the video I just took
Send the top video in my gallery to Tom
I filmed my dad using the drill, can you send that to my sister?
Please share the last twenty seconds of that clip with the family group, if it is not too big

Mr. Adams was a retired teacher who wanted a smaller power bill. He sat in his kitchen and said, "Find out which of my machines uses the most electricity." The assistant searched the energy report from his house. It said the old freezer used the most, followed by the dryer. Mr. Adams was friendly with his neighbour, who had solar panels, so he asked, "How much sun power did my neighbour's house make?" The assistant said it could not see other people's houses. "Oh, I mean mine," Mr. Adams said, "I have no panels, silly me." The assistant understood that he wanted only his own report, and it read out the figures for the hill-side house.

Ella was a child who loved numbers. She put her bowl of cereal on the table and said to the speaker, "What is twelve plus eight, and what comes after you take five away from that?" The assistant understood that she was asking two questions. It said that twelve plus eight is twenty, and that twenty take away five is fifteen. Ella wrote both numbers in a straight line on her paper. Then she asked, "Now double the fifteen and tell me half of it." The assistant said double is thirty and half is seven and a half. Ella clapped, finished her cereal and asked for another one.

They want a workout to do today.
Give me a workout
What should I do today?
Something quick for my legs
I plan to train for twenty minutes, what fits?
I tied a band to the post in the garden, what can I do with it?
Give me ten pushups. No wait, make it fifteen
It is raining, so I will stay inside. Could you please think of some exercises with sets and reps?

Old Mr. Cole was a gardener, and he had a lot on his mind. He stood by the shed and said, "It's a pity I'll forget the tomatoes again tomorrow." The assistant understood that he wanted a reminder, even though he did not say so. It asked, "Should I remind you in the morning?" He said yes. So it set a reminder for eight o'clock to check the tomatoes. Then Mr. Cole said, "I need a fast way to the garden shop, too." The assistant drew a route on his phone map, and the shop was only ten minutes by car. Mr. Cole thanked it and went inside.

Carla was a busy parent, and she had to get her son to the dentist. "Book me a ride to the dentist at three," she said to her phone. "But I can't afford the fancy cars, and I don't want a driver who plays loud music." The assistant understood that she wanted the cheapest ride, and a quiet one. It found a small, plain car for twelve dollars and noted that the driver liked a gentle, quiet trip. It asked her to confirm the pickup at her front door. Carla said yes, and the ride was booked for three o'clock.

A focus timer helps you work for a short time and then take a break. Many people work for twenty-five minutes, rest for five and then start again. The timer is useful because it keeps you from sitting too long. You can change the length of the work time, the break or the sound it makes. People say, "make my breaks ten minutes," or "don't ring the bell, just flash the red light." Some people skip the timer on Saturday because they want to blow off steam. Others say, "start the timer again," when they come back from lunch. It is a simple way to get a routine.

When you shop online, you choose what you want, pick a size and pay. Then the shop sends the order to your home. Many shops have a minimum amount you need to spend to get free delivery. If something does not fit, you can send it back and get your money returned. People change things all the time. They say, "change the size to medium," "deliver it to my work," or "lock the order so it cannot change." Sometimes the order is for a school project and needs to arrive by a certain day. In that case people ask, "can you get it here by Friday?"

Nina was a busy parent, and the kids were noisy in the car. She typed quickly on her phone, "play the silly song abuot the frog, then turn it up". The assistant understood that she wanted the children's song about a frog, and a louder sound. It found the song and started it, then raised the volume a little. The kids sang along. In the back, her son shouted that they should win the singing game. Nina grinned. "skip to the next one, the one from the carpet cleaner ad," she wrote. The assistant skipped ahead and played the next song.

A restaurant booking is a promise that a seat will be ready for you. You pick a day, a time and how many people are coming, and the restaurant keeps a table free. Plans change, so people often ask to move the time, add a guest or cancel. They say things like 'make it eight instead of seven' or 'we are five now, not four'. Opening hours work in a similar way. If the road is busy or the weather is cool, many people check that the kitchen is still open before they leave. A menu lets you select a dish ahead of time, and you can ask for takeaway if you would rather eat at home.

name: voice_note_finder
does: Finds a spoken note you recorded earlier and plays it back so you can hear it again.
inputs: a few words about what the note was about, and roughly when you recorded it
people say:
- Play the note I made about the chair I want to buy
- Where is that large recording from last week
- I want to hear what I said about the garden
- Find my voice memo from Monday morning
- What did I record about the dentist

Marta the gardener came in from the peach trees with muddy boots. Earlier she had seen a strange car by the gate, and now she wanted the house kept safe while she worked outside, because later she planned to invite her sister for lunch. She stood in the hallway and said, 'Lock up.' The voice assistant understood she meant the doors. It locked the front and back doors, switched on the camera by the gate and told her both doors were secure. Marta nodded. 'Alarm too,' she added. The assistant set the alarm to stay mode, so the motion sensors in the yard would not ring while she moved around. She thanked it and went back to the garden.

Fuel is what keeps a car moving. The gauge on the dashboard shows how much is left, and the manual in the glove box tells you how big the tank is, often about fifty liters. People ask for small changes to what they do next: 'remind me to fill up when it is a quarter full' or 'find the nearest station'. Tyre pressure works in a similar way. If the warning light comes on, you check the pressure and add air. On a cold morning, many people ask the car to warm up for ten minutes before they leave, so they do not have to wipe the frost off the windows by hand.

Bread dough needs time to rise. Yeast makes small bubbles that puff the dough up, and a warm spot helps. A good baker will explain that the dough should double in size before it goes in the oven. People set timers for this and change them as they go: 'give it another ten minutes' or 'bake it five minutes less'. Oven heat matters too, and every recipe says how hot to make it. One baker who used to work at a hotel on the south coast always asked for a reminder to check the loaves halfway through. When the crust is golden and sounds hollow when you tap it, the bread is done.

A robot mower cuts the grass by itself. You choose the days and the hours it works, and when the battery runs low it drives back to its station. People change the plan often. They say 'skip the mowing tomorrow, the kids are playing' or 'cut the grass a bit shorter'. Sprinklers work in a similar way. A single timer decides when the water comes on, and you can ask it to stay off when rain is coming. On warm days the grass grows fast, and weeds climb along the edges. A neat edge makes the whole lawn look better. One neighbour says the mower beeps like a microwave when it finishes, which makes everyone laugh.

Time zones exist because the sun is not overhead everywhere at once. When it is bright noon in one city, it can be dark night in another. A phone shows the time where you are, and it can show other cities too. People add a place so they know when to call. Someone with a son studying far away might say 'what time is it in Tokyo' or 'is it too late to call him'. They also change the clock when summer time starts, saying 'move the clock forward one hour'. The phone usually does this by itself when you travel, so you rarely need to know how to set it by hand.

Person: Good morning. I would be very grateful if you could make me a packing list for the weekend, because last time I forgot my torch and had a miserable night.
Assistant: Happy to help. Which nights are you going, and will you sleep in a tent?
Person: Friday and Saturday, in a small tent. Some friends from the walking club will join me.
Assistant: Lovely. How cold will it get? I can check the hill weather if you tell me the place.
Person: Near the lake at Ridgeway. And please add something for my ears, the wind there makes them ache.
Assistant: I will add a warm hat and ear covers. The list so far: tent, sleeping bag, torch, spare batteries, stove, water and a daily snack bag. Shall I send it to your phone?
Person: Yes please, thank you.
Assistant: Done. The list is on your phone now.

Knitting is a slow hobby that fits into quiet evenings. You pick your wool, say blue for a scarf, and follow a pattern row by row. People count rows so they do not lose their place, and they ask to change the count: 'add one row' or 'go back two rows'. Many knitters start a big project in February, when the days are short, and hope to finish before spring. A timer can help you take a break, and you can ask it to remind you to put the work down and rest your hands. If you want to forward a pattern to a friend, you can send it as a message with a few kind words.

Sam woke up thirsty and stumbled into the kitchen with a bowl of lettuce for the rabbits. He could barely crack his eyes open, and then he remembered that the hot tub had gone cold overnight. 'Heat the tub to one hundred and two,' he mumbled to the speaker. The assistant understood that he meant degrees and that he wanted the hot tub, not the pool. It said it would start the heater now and that the water would be ready in about forty minutes. Sam thanked it, drank a big glass of water, fed the rabbits and went back to bed for a little while.

Someone wants to know how far they rode today.
How far did I go?
Distance, please
What's the total for my ride?
My legs are dead, so how many miles was that?
I'm hungry enough to empty a whole shelf of cakes, so did I earn it? Tell me how far I rode.
Tell me how many kilometres I covered this morning.
Did I go further than yesterday?
Could you please tell me the distance of the route I designed on Sunday?

A workout plan tells you which exercises to do, how many sets and how many reps. A set is a group of reps, like ten push-ups in a row, and between sets you rest. Rest days matter because muscles grow while they recover. People change the plan all the time: 'add one more set' or 'make today lighter'. Someone who has just left the hospital, or who is scared of getting hurt, might say 'go easy for a week'. An app can find a simpler routine and set a timer for each rest. A good plan is one you can follow every week, not one that wears you out.

Someone wants to know how many steps they have taken today.
Steps?
How many steps so far?
How far have I walked, and how many steps is that?
Give me my step count.
I want to know if I'm close to ten thousand.
I spend most of the day on my feet, so what's my total?
Counting my steps is the only task I have left today, can you do it?
My shoes feel loose, so tell me how much I've walked and how fast I went.
Could you tell me my steps and my pace for this morning?

Person: It's so quiet in here. I can never work this radio thing.
Assistant: I can turn the radio on for you. Which station would you like?
Person: I don't know the names. The one with the news in the morning.
Assistant: Do you mean the local news station or the national one?
Person: The local one. My neighbour says they earn prizes for their news.
Assistant: Good. I've tuned to Local News Radio and the news is playing.
Person: It sounds a bit raw and too loud. And there's a draft coming from the vent behind me. Can you shut it?
Assistant: I lowered the volume a little. I'm sorry, I can't control the vent. I can only play the radio and change the sound.

Priya got home after a twelve-hour night shift. The bedroom felt dry and stuffy, and her eyes hurt. She dropped her bag on the chair, caught sight of herself in the hall mirror and sighed. 'Turn the humidifier on high,' she said to the speaker. Then she changed her mind. 'No, wait, low. I want a soft hum so I can sleep.' The assistant understood the correction and set the humidifier in the bedroom to low. It also told her that the air purifier was already running quietly in the corner. Priya thanked it, closed the curtains and fell asleep within minutes.

Leo had moved to the city two days ago, and his phone was almost dead. He sat on the steps in the yard of his new building and said, 'My battery is dying, make it last.' The assistant turned on battery saver and lowered the screen brightness. Leo asked it to pair his earbuds, because he wanted to call his sister. The assistant found them nearby and connected them. It told him the battery was at nine percent and that a serious drain came from the map app, which it closed. When he got home, it said, he should charge the phone for twenty minutes. Leo smiled and made his call.

A pool pump moves the water through a filter so it stays clean. At home, most people run it on a timer, perhaps eight hours a day. When leaves make the water messy, they ask for the pump to run longer. If someone is swimming, they say 'pause the pump' and later 'resume the pump'. Water temperature works the same way. A hot tub is usually kept at around thirty-eight degrees, and people say 'make it a little warmer' or 'drop it by two degrees'. A cover keeps the heat in and the leaves out, so people also remind each other to put it back on.

Rest days are part of every good fitness plan. After hard workouts your body needs time to rebuild, so a plan often has a day with no exercise at all. People with busy weeks move these days around: 'make Wednesday my rest day' or 'skip tomorrow's workout'. A timer tells you when to stop a set, and a reminder can tell you when to start. Many people like to eat toast or fruit before a morning run for energy. If you feel tired, you can say 'make this week easier', and the plan can shorten the sessions or drop a set.

Someone wants to know the score of tonight's match.
Score?
Latest score
What's the score in the game?
Who's winning?
Is my team ahead right now?
Tell me how the match is going, I'm stuck at the sink doing dishes.
I had to borrow a small radio, so I can't see the screen. What's the score?
Could you please give me the score and tell me how much time is left?

A packing list is a short note of what to take on a camping trip, so nothing important stays at home. People keep it on their phone and change it before each trip, saying things like 'add a stove so we can cook' or 'remove the big tent, we are only two'. Families who go camping on a monthly basis usually reuse the same list and change only a few lines. Many also check the weather in the hills the night before, asking 'will it be cold up there on Saturday?' A photo of the trail map is useful too, because the phone may have no signal on the trail. A monthly trip also needs a fresh look at the list, since the seasons change.

Jay was sitting on the floor among half-filled boxes, texting his friend. His mom wanted the kitchen packed by dinner, but he would much rather swim at the pool. He had a bag of crispy chips in one hand and typed to the assistant with the other: 'ugh its been two hours and theres still no truck'. The assistant understood he wanted to know when the moving truck would arrive. It checked the movers' booking, told him the truck was due at four o'clock because the driver had been stuck in traffic, and sent him the driver's phone number. Jay sighed, put the chips down and went back to the boxes.

name: delay_alert
does: Watches a bus or train line and warns you when it is late or cancelled, so a stormy morning does not cost you an hour.
inputs: the line or route, and the time you plan to travel
people say:
- Is my train going to be late tonight
- Tell me if the seven fifteen bus gets held up
- Will the storm mess up my trip to work
- Warn me before I leave if the line is down
- I have no idea whether the trains are running

Dana was packing lunches and looking for a way to get the kids out of the house. 'What's on at the cinema tomorrow at four?' she asked her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted showtimes for a family film. It found a single cartoon at four called Moon Pirates and read out the times. Saving some money was on her mind, so she asked whether there was a cheaper ticket. The assistant said children's tickets were half price before five. Dana said she would need four tickets, two for the kids and two for the grown-ups. The assistant held four seats for tomorrow at four and sent the confirmation to her phone.

Omar woke up with a worry he could not name. Then he remembered: the electricity bill. He rubbed his eyes and said to his phone, 'Bills due?' The assistant understood he wanted to know what was coming up. It said the electricity bill of sixty dollars was due on Friday and the water bill was due next week. It also reminded him that his bank balance was low. Omar groaned, then smiled, remembering the story his dad always told about paying bills the day they arrive. He asked the assistant to remind him on Thursday morning, and it did. 'Thank you,' he said, and went to make coffee.

Ines ran a small fish shop and was waiting for a box of paper bags. Between customers she looked at her phone and said, 'Parcel status?' The assistant understood she wanted tracking for her latest order. It said the parcel was out for delivery and the driver would drop it off by noon. 'Sign for it?' she asked. The assistant explained that a signature was needed, so it would send her a message when the driver was at the door. 'Total items?' she asked next. The assistant said the box held three packs of bags, total weight four kilos. Ines thanked it and went back to wrapping a salmon.

Joining a work call is simple: you click a link, or you ask the assistant to open it at the right time. Inside the call, people adjust a few things, like the microphone, the camera and the volume. If someone sits far from the microphone, they say 'turn me up' or 'mute me for a minute'. Sharing a screen shows your slides to everyone, and you can say 'stop sharing' when you finish. An agenda lists the topics so the meeting stays short, and a good one gives each topic five minutes. A meeting that drags on can feel as heavy as a pound of bricks, so people say 'end the call at three'.

Person: Tide times?
Assistant: Sure. For which day?
Person: Tomorrow.
Assistant: High tide is at ten past nine in the morning and low tide is at three in the afternoon.
Person: Neat. I want to convert that into a sign for my shop window. Can you print it?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't print. I can send the times to your phone so you can copy them onto a sign.
Person: Yes, do that. And put the beach radio on in the shop.
Assistant: Done. The times are on your phone and the radio is playing.

Person: I posted a photo of my roses. I want more people to see it.
Assistant: Do you want me to share it again, or send it to your followers directly?
Person: Share it again. Double the reach if you can.
Assistant: I can share it again on your page, but I can't control how many people see it.
Person: That's fine. It's my dream garden, and the last post got only half the likes of the one before. I nearly cry when I think of the work. A tiny bit of attention would be nice.
Assistant: I'm sorry. I've shared it again. Would you like to add a few words?
Person: Yes: My dream garden in June.
Assistant: Added and posted.

A calendar keeps your plans in one place. A single event has a day, a start time and an end time, and many people add a place too. People move events often. They say 'push the meeting to Thursday' or 'make it an hour later'. Free time shows the gaps between events, and you can ask 'when am I free this week' to design a day around them. Some families still keep a paper calendar on the fridge, but a phone calendar can remind you before an event begins, say ten minutes ahead, so nothing is missed.

Person: Quick, I'm late. Set a nap alarm for the baby, but not the loud one.
Assistant: Of course. How many minutes should the nap be?
Person: Forty. And turn the monitor on.
Assistant: The alarm is set with a soft chime, and the monitor is on.
Person: Great. Now tell me what she should wear tonight, it's a total mystery to me.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't say what she should wear, but I can check tonight's temperature. It will be fourteen degrees.
Person: Then a thick sleepsuit. Not the one with the hamster on it, that's too thin.
Assistant: Good idea. I'll remind you at seven to lay out the thick one.

Someone wants to know what films are showing at the cinema.
What's on?
Anything good at the cinema?
Show me the movie times for tonight.
I'm bored and it's Thursday, so I wonder what's playing near me.
It's a sad grey evening and I'd love to get out of the house and see a film.
Is there a cinema where I can park easily and see something tonight?
Could you please tell me what's on at the cinema this weekend?
Any new releases?

When you order something online, the shop packs it and a driver brings it to your door. You choose a size and a delivery day, and you can change them before it ships. People ask 'make it a medium' or 'send it to my work address instead'. If an item does not fit, returning it is simple: you show a code and drop the parcel at a shop. Some drivers leave parcels by the gate if no one is home, so people say 'leave it with the neighbour'. If you are sorry you bought something, you can ask for your money back within a few weeks.

name: address_change_helper
does: Tells the right places about your new address, like the bank, the post office and the electric company, so nothing gets lost.
inputs: the new address, the date you move, and which places should be told
people say:
- I'm moving next month, tell everyone my new address
- Change my mail to the new house
- Make sure the electric company knows I'm leaving on the first
- Mom needs my new address for her cards, can you send it
- Tell the pet shop where to send the cat feed
- I got the cool new flat on Oak Street, so change my address everywhere

Omar owned a bakery and drove a small van. Before the morning rush he said to his car, 'How much petrol do I have?' The assistant answered that the tank was less than a quarter full, about eleven litres. Omar's mouth went dry. He had a single stop to make before opening, but he did not want to run out. 'Find me the closest station,' he said, 'and I prefer one on my way to the shop.' The assistant found a station half a mile ahead on the same road and started the directions. Omar filled the tank and reached the bakery with time to spare.

Someone wants to know when their homework is due.
When's it due?
What homework do I have?
Tell me my assignments for this week.
Remind me about the essay.
I'm in a stormy mood about school, so just tell me what is due first.
Has my teacher set anything new?
Could you ask the speaker on my desk to read out my homework list, the one with the twenty-five questions?
Please tell me which assignment has the closest due date, because I want to start with that one.

Tom the gardener came in with muddy boots, and a rainy week had tracked dirt across the whole hall. He pulled off his boots and said to the speaker, 'Run the vacuum tomorrow at seven.' The assistant understood that he meant the robot vacuum and set it for seven in the morning. It added the job to the cleaning schedule and said the robot would do the hall first. 'Skip the bedroom,' Tom added. 'My wife sleeps late on Saturdays.' The assistant removed the bedroom from the job, and told him the robot would be finished by half past eight. Tom nodded and went to wash his hands.

Rosa ran a gift shop and had a video call with her supplier in ten minutes. She was stacking boxes when she typed to her phone: 'join the meeitng at 3'. The assistant understood what she meant in spite of the typo. It opened the link from her calendar for the supplier meeting at three and turned the microphone on. The call was about an event for new candles, and she wanted to hear the first voice message from the supplier before it started, so she asked it to play that message. She also asked it to turn the volume down a little, because less noise helps in a busy shop. The assistant did both, and Rosa joined the call on time.

Mr. Wells wanted a hotel room in a village by the sea. He held his phone a little away from his face and said, 'Book a room for two nights.' Then he frowned. 'No, three nights. My wife says three.' The assistant understood the correction. It found a small hotel in the village with a free breakfast and asked how many guests there would be. 'Two,' he said. Then he asked whether the room had a kettle, because he liked to boil his own water for tea. The assistant said yes. It booked three nights for two guests and read the check-in time out loud, which was after two in the afternoon.

In a board game, a score is a number that tells you who is winning. Players write it on paper or ask a phone to keep it. Scores change fast, so people say 'add three points for Mia' or 'take one away'. A timer is useful for word games: you set it for a minute and shout when the sand runs out. Rules can be confusing, and people ask 'how many cards do I draw'. In the middle of a game, someone might need a break, so the timer is paused. One family keeps score on the back of a shop receipt, which works well until somebody spills the juice.

Eli was eight and hungry. His mom had left dough in a tray, and he stood on a stool by the oven and said, 'How long do I bake the bread? Don't rush me, and I don't want it burnt.' The assistant understood that he wanted the baking time, and it did not rush him. It told him to bake the bread for twenty minutes at two hundred degrees and asked him to wait until the oven beeped. Then it set a timer. When it rang, the bread was warm and golden, and Eli's mom helped him take it out. 'I did it,' he said. The assistant said it smelled wonderful.

Grace finished her night shift at seven and wanted a short walk before going to sleep. The morning was chilly, and she pulled her scarf tight. 'Track a walk, about three miles,' she told her watch. Then she shook her head. 'Sorry, two miles. I'm too tired.' The assistant changed the goal to two miles and started tracking. It said it would notify her when she reached the halfway mark. On the way she passed her bank, where she had planned to ask about a loan, so she asked the assistant to remind her to call them in the afternoon. It set the reminder for two o'clock.

Someone wants to know how many words their essay has.
Word count?
How long is my essay?
How many words are in this, and how many pages?
Count the words for me.
I need to increase the length, so how many words do I have now?
A bulb went on in my head about the ending, but first tell me how many words I have so far.
My teacher is bitter about short essays, so please check my length and my spelling.
Could you please count the words in my draft so I know whether I have reached the limit?

Mr. Alvarez, a retired teacher, stood at the sink washing his hands with soap and thinking about dinner. He said to the speaker, 'Find a table for two at an Italian place tonight. I don't want anywhere noisy, and not too far.' The assistant found a quiet Italian restaurant ten minutes away and asked for a time. 'Seven is fine,' he said. The assistant booked a table for two at seven and told him there would be no wait if he arrived on time. It also showed him the menu on his phone. Mr. Alvarez dried his hands and went to find his coat.

Nina was a student with a desk covered in glue sticks and paper for a school project. Her hands were sticky, so she said, 'Text Amir that I'll be there tomorrow at seven.' The assistant understood she meant Amir from her group chat and wrote the message for her. She added, 'Tell him I'll bring the posters. His dad said he will fry rice for everyone.' The assistant added that line and read the whole message back to her. She said it was fine. It sent the text inside the group chat so everyone could see it, and Nina went back to her glue.

Someone wants to find a note they wrote last week.
Find my note from last week
Where did I put that note about the plumber?
Show notes from Tuesday
Not the shopping list, the other one about the trip.
That heavy note about the budget, can you open it?
My guests arrive soon and I need the note with the recipe link.
Could you please look through my notes for the one with the word garage in it?

Kai was nine years old, and in March his class would go on a long hike. He wanted new boots, so he asked the tablet, 'Can I get these boots in a bigger size?' The assistant understood that he meant the boots on the shopping page. At the bottom of the page it showed size three, and Kai asked for one size bigger. The assistant changed it to size four. It said the boots were half price today and that delivery would take two days. Just then his phone buzzed with a message from his mom, who said yes. The assistant placed the order.

name: burn_care_steps
does: Gives short steps for treating a small burn at home and says when to call for help, so you can avoid a pricey trip to the clinic when you do not need one.
inputs: where the burn is, how big it is, and what caused it
people say:
- I touched the hot pan, what do I do
- My hand is red and stings from the kettle
- How long should I run cold water on this
- Should I lift the cloth off the burn
- The driver of our van burned his arm on the engine, help

Mia was texting from the couch while the television murmured in the background. She was supposed to meet friends at nine, and her legs still ached from a morning jog. She typed: 'my feet are killing me and its too far to walk'. The assistant understood that she wanted a ride. It asked for the pickup point, and she wrote 'the front door'. It booked a car that would arrive in eight minutes and showed her the driver's name. She added, 'tell him not to call, im in a quiet house'. The assistant passed the note to the driver, and Mia put on her shoes.

Carla was a busy parent packing for a trip with her son. 'Book a hotel room in Lisbon for three nights,' she said while folding shirts. The assistant asked how many guests there would be. 'Three. Me, my son and my mother,' she said. It found a room with an extra bed and placed a temporary hold on it. The hold would last fifteen minutes, so she had time to check her husband's dates. A few minutes later he sent a message saying the dates were fine. Carla told the assistant to confirm, and it booked the room and sent her the details.

Someone wants the phone to read a message out loud.
Read it out
Read my messages to me
Can you say that text out loud?
I can't see the screen well, so read it.
What does the monthly bill email say?
Both my hands are covered in vinegar from cleaning, so please read the new message aloud.
Could you read me the screen? I tend to hide my glasses and can never find them.
Excuse me, I would be very thankful if you could read my new messages out loud, because my eyes are tired after a long day and the small writing gives me a headache.

The person wants the pet feeder to put less food in the dog's bowl tonight.
give rex less fod tonight pls
Half a scoop for Rex this evening
Could you cut down his dinner a little?
Rex ate too much yesterday, so make his bowl smaller
Don't fill the bowl all the way
He made a mess on the carpet, so please add only a small amount of food tonight
I'd like a lighter dinner for the dog
Would you mind asking the feeder to hold back a bit? The vet told us he is a little heavy and we should go easy.

name: loud_storm_warning
does: Tells you if thunder or loud storms are coming to a place on a certain day.
inputs: a place and a day
people say:
- Will it be loud outside on Wednesday?
- Is thunder coming this week?
- Should I replace the picnic with a movie night, or will the sky stay calm?
- Any storms near Leeds tomorrow?
- Do I need to bring the dog in before it gets rough out there?

Mara got home from the hospital at seven in the morning. She was so tired that her eyes kept closing. Yesterday she had told her son she would put up the holiday lights, and she hated the thought of lying awake worrying about it. She sat down on the couch and said to the smart speaker, 'Tree lights, please.' The speaker understood that she meant the plug for the lights on the Christmas tree in the front room. It turned the plug on and said the tree lights were on. Mara smiled. Then she asked it to turn them off at ten at night and on again at six each evening. The assistant set up that plan and said it out loud so she knew. Mara closed her eyes, and the glow of the tree stayed with her as she fell asleep.

Finding a film to watch is easy when you let an assistant help. You say what kind of movie you want, and it shows a short list. It might be a dog movie for the kids, a scary one for Friday, or something short for a train ride home. People change the list by saying things like show me only new ones, nothing too long, or skip the sad ones. If the first choice looks weak, you can say try again or give me another. You can also ask for a trailer before you decide, or for the times at the cinema near you. To change the time, you just say later tonight or what about Saturday.

When something at home breaks, an assistant can help you fix it or book someone who can. A leak in the attic, a noisy fan, or a dirty filter at the bottom of the heater can all be handled the same way. You say what is wrong and when you are free, and the assistant finds a repairer. People change the plan with short words. They say move it to Friday, make it the morning, or cancel that one. If the visit has to go earlier, they ask if someone can come sooner. For small jobs, the assistant can remind you to change a filter every three months. When the repairer is on the way, it tells you, so you know when to go to the door.

name: plant_light_check
does: Compares how much sun two spots in a garden get and says which one is better for a plant.
inputs: the name of a plant and two places in the garden
people say:
- Where should my basil go, the porch or the back fence?
- Which spot gets more sun for tomatoes?
- I grow herbs for pasta and need a bright corner.
- Compare the sunny bed with the shady one.
- Are my round pots too dark by the wall?

Walter was not good with phones, but his daughter had put a voice assistant on the kitchen table. One morning he looked in the mirror and sighed. His hair was so long it was touching his collar, and he did not want to miss the wedding on Saturday. He said, 'My hair is getting in my eyes, and the big day is very close.' The assistant understood that he needed a haircut. It asked which shop, and he said Tony's, the one he always used. It found a free time on Thursday at ten and booked it. Then it told him, 'Your haircut at Tony's is on Thursday at ten.' Walter's wife asked it to find a tailor to fix her skirt too, and it read out the shop hours.

Lena ran a small shop that sold jam and honey. Her best customer, Mr. Boyd, had a birthday coming, and she wanted to welcome him with a little gift. She asked her phone, 'What do I give a man who has everything? Find something that costs half of what I paid last year.' The assistant understood that she wanted gift ideas at about half of last year's price, which was forty dollars. It said an average gift in that range is a tin of tea or a small plant, and it listed three ideas. Lena picked the tea. Then she asked for a reminder two days before the birthday, and the assistant set it and said the reminder was saved.

Weather forecasts tell you what the sky will do, so you can plan your day. Many people think of them as just rain or sun, but they also show the heat, the wind and the chance of rain. If you are on a tight budget and want to walk instead of taking the bus, you might check whether an empty field will turn to mud. You can ask for a different place, a different day, or just the next hour. People say what about tomorrow, how cold will it be tonight, or will it rain at five. If you want less detail, you say just the short version. If you want more, you say tell me about the whole week.

The person wants to know how many days are left until a date.
How many days until June first? No wait, I meant July first.
days left till the deadline
Count the days to my sister's wedding
I'm sitting in my cozy chair planning the year, so could you tell me how long until the report is due?
Is it a lot of days until Christmas?
How long till my birthday?
Wait, not the first, I meant the fifteenth
Tell me how many sleeps until the trip

Omar drove a delivery van, and by the time he got home he only wanted to sit down. The washer was running in the back room, and his daughter was watching cartoons on a tablet downstairs. He said to the TV, 'Connect to the sports channel, but not the news. I don't want the news tonight.' The assistant understood that he wanted the football game and no news. It switched the living room TV to the sports channel and said the game was starting in ten minutes. It also asked if he wanted subtitles, and he said no. The assistant left them off and kept the volume the same. Omar put his feet up and waited for the game.

name: find_old_email
does: Searches your inbox for an old message by who sent it or what it was about.
inputs: a name or a few words from the message
people say:
- Where is that email from my aunt about the party?
- I had a dozen messages from the school, show me the last one.
- My head hurt when I read that note about the bill, find it again.
- Dig up the sad letter my friend sent me in May.
- Show me anything from Tom this week.
- Find the message with the train ticket.

name: bin_day_reminder
does: Tells you which bin to put out and on what day.
inputs: your street and the kind of bin
people say:
- Which bin goes out tomorrow?
- The man from the council said it changed, so when do they come now?
- Remind me the night before green bin day.
- Do the bright blue bags go out on Monday?
- Did I miss the pickup? I saw the truck fly by.

Knitting is a hobby many people enjoy in the evening. You use wool and two needles to make a scarf or a hat. A cat on your lap can make it harder, so keep the wool in a safe basket. When you make something, you decide on the color, the size and how soft it should be. People say make it longer, use thicker wool, or try a bigger needle. A helper can also count your rows so you do not lose your place. You can say how many rows have I done, or start again from row ten. And to remember what to make next, you can say put a hat on my list.

name: coffee_strength_setter
does: Sets how strong, how big and how hot the coffee maker makes a cup.
inputs: the strength, the size of the cup and the heat
people say:
- Make it stronger, I need fuel for the day.
- Not so bitter, please.
- Give me the exact same cup as yesterday.
- I want a slow drip coffee, medium size.
- Weaker for my mum, coffee makes her jumpy.
- Hot, but not boiling.

A packing list helps you remember what to take on a camping trip. You need a tent, a sleeping bag, water and food. Small things matter too, like a torch and a lighter. There is no microwave in the hills, so people take a small stove. A list can change every day, depending on the weather and how long you stay. People say add a rain jacket, delete the heavy boots, or move the stove to the top. The assistant can check the daily forecast for the hills and tell you if the nights will be cold. When you are done, you can say this is the list for the lake, so you can find it again next year.

Measurements tell us how big, how heavy or how hot something is. A recipe may ask for grams, but your scale shows ounces, so people ask for the other kind. They say how many cups is that, how many pounds are in a kilogram, or what is twenty degrees in Fahrenheit. The current temperature outside may be in one kind of degrees, and your friend far away uses another. Before you pack a bag for a trip, you might check the weight limit. A weather map may say a cloud is six kilometers high, and you might ask how many miles that is. People change a number by saying use the other unit, or give it in feet instead.

The person wants the wifi to work faster and stop dropping.
Wifi is slow
Fix the internet, please
The video keeps freezing, can you clear it up?
Why is my connection so bad tonight?
Make the internet smooth again
Can you restart the router for me?
We can't load anything and I think the router is stuck
Excuse me, my niece has an online swim class in five minutes and the picture keeps stopping, so could you please make the wifi stable again? She would be very grateful.

Rosa locked up her shop late on Friday and noticed the camera light was off. She had been reading an article on her phone about break-ins, and that made her worry. She typed fast, with no capital letters: turn on the back door camra and message me if it sees anything. The assistant understood that she wanted the camera at the back door switched on, with a message sent to her phone if it saw movement. It turned the camera on and said so. Rosa picked up her bag and walked home, knowing the shop would be watched all night.

name: clip_trimmer
does: Cuts a short video so only the part you want is left.
inputs: the video, where to start and where to stop
people say:
- Cut the first ten seconds off my video.
- Remove the dirty bit at the end where I dropped the phone.
- Keep only a fraction of it, just the last half minute.
- Make this clip shorter so I can send it.
- I only want the part where she blows out the candles.

name: free_time_finder
does: Looks through your calendar and finds a time when you have nothing planned.
inputs: a day or a week, and how long you need
people say:
- When am I free on Thursday?
- Find me an hour this week to pick up milk and run errands.
- Look at my calendar and tell me when I'm not busy.
- I need to be ready for a meeting, is there a gap before lunch?
- Is the afternoon open?
- Any space for a long call tomorrow?

Grandpa Joe had a letter to send, but his knees were bad and the post office was a long walk. He sat by the window with his tablet and said, 'My knees are too sore for the walk to the post office, and I can't hand in this page myself.' The assistant understood that he needed someone to deliver his letter. It found a pickup service that collected mail from homes and asked if he wanted a driver that afternoon. Joe said yes. The assistant booked a pickup for three o'clock and told him the cost. At three, a woman in a shiny red van knocked, took the page in its envelope, and drove off. Joe never had to leave his chair.

Priya had ten minutes before she had to leave, and she was still trying to dress. Her phone was on the bed, and she had no free hand. She typed with one thumb: call mom on spekaer. The assistant understood that she wanted to call her mother with the speakerphone on, so she did not need to tap the screen again. It dialed, and Mom's voice filled the room. It was the final call before the trip, and Priya asked about the bus time while she pulled on her shoes. When the call ended, the assistant said so. Priya grabbed her keys and ran out the door.

Mrs. Alvarez, a retired teacher, liked to read a bedtime story to her granddaughter on the phone every night. Tonight she also had a doctor's visit to think about, and she had to report to the clinic at eight in the morning. She said to the smart speaker, 'Excuse me, would you please wake me at six thirty tomorrow, because I have to be at the clinic by eight and the bus takes an hour?' The assistant understood that she wanted an alarm at six thirty and set it. It repeated the time to her. Then a sudden noise from the kitchen made her jump, and she asked for a ten minute timer to watch the kettle. The assistant started it.

Sam was already in the car when he remembered the garage was open. He was far from the house, and the neighbor's boy was coming to mow the lawn at noon. He said into his phone, 'Is the front door locked, and who rang the doorbell?' The assistant understood that he wanted the lock status and the doorbell history. It said the front door was locked, the garage door was open, and the doorbell had rung once, twenty minutes ago, when a courier left a box. Sam asked it to close the garage, and it did. It also showed a clip of twenty-five seconds from the camera, so he could see the box on the step.

Dee woke up on moving day with a headache. The kitchen was a mess, and the last project was packing the dishes. She mumbled, 'I need more boxes, double what I have, and what do I do with the cooked rice?' The assistant understood two things. She wanted to order boxes, twice the ten she already had, and she needed a tip for the leftovers. It ordered ten more boxes for same day delivery and said cooked rice keeps for a day in the fridge, so she could pack it in a small cooler. It also reminded her that her brother, who wanted to design the layout of the new living room, was coming at two.

Nina was a busy parent, and her phone had buzzed twenty-five times since breakfast. She stood outside the school with her toddler on her hip and said, 'Turn off post alerts for two hours, I'm going for a jog after drop off. And change my profile picture to the one from the beach.' The assistant understood two things. She wanted her social media notifications muted for two hours, and she wanted the beach photo as her new picture. It did both and told her the alerts would come back at eleven. Nina smiled, put the phone in her pocket and pushed the stroller toward the park.

Kofi came home after a night shift in November, when the mornings were still dark. She wanted to rest, but first she wanted to put away the video of her niece's school play. She said to her tablet, 'Move my school play video to the family folder, and make it half as long. There is too much extra at the start.' The assistant understood that she wanted the clip saved in the family folder and cut down to half its length, with the first part removed. It moved the video, trimmed it, and said the new clip was two minutes long. Kofi pressed play, smiled at her niece in a paper crown, and went to bed.

Nadia ran a tiny bookshop two kilometers from the bus stop. At closing time her phone showed that someone had asked to see her shop photos. She typed fast, all in lowercase: cancel the sharing on the black tablet and lcok my phone. The assistant found the black tablet in her list of devices and stopped it from sharing the photo folder. Then it locked her phone, so it needed a passcode to open. It told her that nobody else could see the folder now. Nadia put the phone in her bag and turned off the lights.

Smart lights let you change a room with your voice. A lamp can be bright when you read and soft when you want to chill. You can also change the color, like a warm yellow for dinner or a cool blue for work. People say make it dimmer, a bit brighter, or turn off the ceiling light. If you want a mood, you can say something cozy for movie night. Someone hosting a spicy food night might ask for a warm red glow. Someone reading by the window with the old bridge in view might ask for the lamp to be a little brighter. The lights simply do what the words say.

Tao was a student with an exam in the morning. He lay down on the rug in his room, but he saw that he had left his alarm unset. There were only six hours left until the exam. He had to dig his phone out from under a pile of notes. Then he said, 'Alarm, six sharp.' The assistant understood that he wanted an alarm at six in the morning and set it. It told him, 'Alarm set for six.' Tao also said, 'Sleep sounds.' The assistant started soft rain sounds and said it would stop them after an hour. Tao closed his eyes and soon he was asleep.

Grandma Ruth was moving to an apartment up north to be near her son. Her son was going to fly in on Friday to help her. She picked up the tablet and said, 'I don't want the big truck, and I don't want to pay for packing. Find me a small mover. What is the number of the one I looked at last week?' The assistant understood that she wanted a small moving service that did not pack her things. It found the company from last week, read out the phone number slowly, and offered to call it for her. Ruth said yes, and the assistant dialed. A friendly man answered on the second ring.

Mr. Haddad, a retired teacher, planned to visit his sister by the sea. He sat at the table with a slice of toast and asked his phone, 'Find me a hotel with a small room, no more than half of what I paid last time. And I want a thick curtain, because I sleep late.' The assistant understood that he wanted a hotel room for two nights at half the price of his last stay, which was two hundred dollars, so about one hundred. It added the curtain to the search. It found three places and read them out. Mr. Haddad picked the second one and asked the assistant to keep it for him.

name: return_item_helper

people say:
- This bread arrived stale, send it back.
- I want to return the cat bed, it's too small.
