- The bag is the wrong size, can I swap it?
- Get my money back for the shoes.

Person: Hello. Would you please read me the headlines? I am stuck in a long meeting and I hope to catch up before lunch.
Assistant: Sure. Which kind do you want, local news, sports or world news?
Person: Sports, please. I'm a little bored of the same stories.
Assistant: Here are two sports headlines. The city team won at home last night, and a runner broke a record at the weekend.
Person: Great. Can you tell me who will win tomorrow's game? I'll think about it on my walk to the station.
Assistant: Sorry, I can't know that. I can tell you when the game starts, if you like.

name: voice_note_saver
does: Records what you say out loud and saves it as a note.
inputs: your voice and a name for the note
people say:
- Write this down: call the neighbor about the fence.
- Jot down the idea I had in the middle of the night.
- Remember that I need to check the oven filter.
- Keep what I'm about to say.
- Save a note for the shopping trip.

Ben drove a taxi, and at the end of the day he pulled onto his street and saw a tree branch lying next to the bins. A bird began to tweet in the tree above him. He said to his phone, 'What goes in the green bin, and is this branch okay?' The assistant understood that he was asking about garden waste. It said the green bin takes branches shorter than twenty-five centimeters, and bigger ones need a special pickup. There was not enough room in the bin for the long branch, so Ben asked the assistant to book a pickup. It did, and told him the day.

Grandpa Lou always spoke very politely, even to machines. He took his morning dose of pills with tea and then said to the garden speaker, 'Excuse me, if it isn't too much trouble, could you please start the robot mower at nine tomorrow? My grandson is visiting, and I want the lawn done before the heat of the afternoon, because the grass is too long for his ball.' The assistant understood that he wanted the mower to start at nine in the morning. It set the plan and said so. The next day the little red mower rolled out right on time, and Lou watched from his chair, pleased.

Camila was a cook in a busy restaurant, and she had a note about the dentist stuck to her fridge. One morning she said to her phone, 'Excuse me, could you please book me a dentist visit on Tuesday after lunch? My back tooth hurts and I would like to go before the weekend rush at the restaurant.' The assistant understood that she wanted a dentist booked on Tuesday afternoon. Cars zoom past the window of the office. A soft voice at the dentist answered the call, and the assistant found a time at two thirty. It booked it and added it to her calendar.

The person wants to know what an amount costs in another currency.
Euros to dollars?
How much is that in dollars?
What's fifty pounds in yen?
Tell me the rate for pesos today
The shelf sensor says twenty euros, what's that in my money?
I'm creating a budget for my trip, so what is a hundred euros in Swiss francs?
Show me today's rate, it never stays constant
What would this cost me back home?

Hana drove a bus, and when she got home the house was cold. She said to the thermostat, 'Make the living room two degrees warmer, and just the radiator by the window.' The assistant understood that she wanted two more degrees in the living room, with only the window radiator. It tried, but the thermostat was offline, so it told her plainly that it could not change it yet and suggested checking the wifi. While she waited, Hana went to tidy the hall. She found the back window open by an inch and shut it. A minute later the thermostat came back, and the assistant raised the heat.

Jay was a teenager watching his baby sister while Mom was out. He ate an apple and texted the assistant: no loud alarms, just text me if the baby monitor hears crying. Snow was falling outside, and a sudden gust shook the window. The assistant understood that he wanted no sound alarm, only a text message on his phone when the monitor heard crying. It turned the sound alerts off and the text alerts on. It said, 'No loud alarms. I will text you if she cries.' Jay put the phone on the arm of the couch and watched the snow.

Translating words helps when you travel or talk to a neighbor who speaks another language. You say a word or a phrase, and the assistant says it back in the other language. At a cafe abroad, you may ask how to say one soda and a sandwich. People change it by saying say it slower, spell it, or use the polite way. A phrase can sound funny when said wrong, so people ask how to say it right. If a translation does not seem right, they say try another word. If a phone call with a friend disconnects while you practice, you can say start again from the last line.

Person: Is it going to rain?
Assistant: Where do you want the forecast for?
Person: Where my dad lives. He's on the coast.
Assistant: I don't know where your dad lives. What town is it?
Person: Hartley. And show me twice as many days, I'd like to see the whole week. Sorry, undo that, just the next two days.
Assistant: Okay, two days for Hartley. It will rain tomorrow morning and be dry after lunch.
Person: Good. Should I leave the window open for the cat?
Assistant: I'd close it before the morning.

Tess was a cook, and her hands were wet from washing pots in the sink. She said to the kitchen speaker, 'Turn the music down by half. The walls here are thin and the neighbors go to bed early. And record a note: buy more flour.' The assistant understood two things. It lowered the volume to half of what it was and saved a voice note that said buy more flour. It told her, 'Music is at half. Your note is saved.' Tess dried her hands and went back to the dishes, humming softly.

Person: Put on the show, please. I'm making tea.
Assistant: Which show? I see a few you watch.
Person: The cooking contest. The final one of the season.
Assistant: The final episode of the cooking contest. Which channel do you want?
Person: Channel twenty-five.
Assistant: Okay, it is on channel twenty-five now.
Person: Can you divide the screen so I can see the news too?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't split the screen. I can switch back to the news when the show ends.

Mia was nine, and she was supposed to be in bed by eight, but tonight there was pizza. She sat on a high stool by the window and typed to the speaker, wher is the pizza, its late. The assistant understood that she was asking when the food delivery would come. It looked up the order and said the driver was ten minutes away and was stuck behind a slow truck. It told her the delivery had been paid already, so nobody needed to find money. Mia watched the street until the headlights stopped outside and the doorbell rang.

Person: It's dripping from the ceiling again.
Assistant: Sorry to hear that. Do you want me to book a repair? Which room is it in?
Person: The kitchen, over the stove where I fried the chicken last night.
Assistant: Got it. When would you like the repairer to come?
Person: As soon as possible. Can you display the free times on the screen?
Assistant: Here are three times today. Two o'clock, four o'clock and six o'clock.
Person: Two o'clock.
Assistant: Booked for two o'clock. I'll tell you when the repairer is on the way.

Person: Turn on the fan, please. I've been in the garden all day.
Assistant: Which fan, the one in the bedroom or the one in the hallway?
Person: The hallway. Actually no, the one in the bedroom.
Assistant: Okay, the bedroom fan is on. Low or high?
Person: High. And can you replace the old electric fan in the kitchen with a new one?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't buy or install a fan. I can put one on your shopping list, if you like.
Person: Yes, please do that.

Person: I'm new here. Can you set a timer for my bread and tell me how long the dough should rise?
Assistant: Sure. What kind of dough is it?
Person: Plain white bread, in a warm kitchen. I'm leaving for work soon.
Assistant: It usually rises for about an hour. I'll set a timer for one hour. Do you also want a baking timer?
Person: Yes, please. The oven fan is noisy, so I might not hear it.
Assistant: Then I'll make the alarm loud. Forty minutes for baking?
Person: Thirty. And what jam would pair well with it?
Assistant: Strawberry is a good pair for white bread.

Mr. Alvarez, a retired teacher, spilled red wine on his best white shirt, and dinner with old friends was only two hours away. It was an urgent job. He grabbed his phone and typed fast: how long is the quik wash, i need the shirt clean. The assistant understood that he wanted to know how long the quick cycle took on his washing machine. It said the quick wash takes thirty-five minutes. Then Mr. Alvarez typed, start it and tell me when it's done. The assistant started the quick wash and set a timer to track the time. Every hour of the evening was planned, so he was glad to have a clear answer. When the machine finished, the phone chimed, and the assistant said the shirt was clean and could go in the dryer.

Rosa runs a small gift shop near the harbor. One afternoon a tourist wanted to pay for a scarf with a coin from home and a few paper notes, and Rosa was not sure what they were worth. She said to her phone, how much is twenty-five euros in dollars today? The assistant understood that she wanted the exchange rate, worked out the amount, and told her the answer in dollars. Rosa also asked it to alert her when the rate got better, because the money kept changing in constant small steps. The assistant said it would send her a message when the rate moved by a good amount. Rosa thanked the tourist, put the money in the till, and wrapped the scarf with a smile.

A playlist is a list of songs that play one after another. People use playlists when they cook, drive, clean or study. Most people change just a few things: the volume, which song plays next, and the order of the songs. To make the music louder they say, turn it up a little, or, I wish it were quieter. To skip a song they say, next one, or, skip this. Some people say something silly like, hit the brake on this song, when they only mean pause it. A good assistant knows that pause, stop and hold on mean nearly the same thing. If you want to hear a song again, you can say, play that one again, or, go back.

An air purifier cleans the air in a room by pulling it through a filter. People use one when the air feels stuffy, when there is smoke outside, or when someone at home is sick. What do people change? Mostly the fan speed, the timer and the mode. They say, make it stronger, run it quietly tonight, or, turn it off in an hour. A humidifier is a little like it: it adds water to dry air, and people ask for more or less. Cooking a big pot of soup can fill a kitchen with steam, so some people open a window or switch on the fan over the stove. If the room still feels heavy, they repeat the request: turn the purifier up, please.

The sea changes through the day. At high tide the water comes far up the sand, and at low tide it goes back out. Swimming can be difficult when the tide pulls hard, so many people check the tide times before they go. Sun cream protects your skin, and most people put it on again every two hours. People also like to know how warm the water is. They ask things like, what time is high tide, is the water cold today, or, how strong is the sun right now? After a swim, many people drink hot tea from a flask and dry off in the sun. If you want the numbers for another place, you can say, check the next beach along instead.

name: line_watcher
does: Tells how long the line is at a post office or bank branch right now.
inputs: the branch or its street, and the time the person plans to go if they have one
people say:
- how busy is the post office right now
- is there a long wait at the bank on Main Street
- give me a signal when the line gets short
- should I go out on this icy morning or will the bank be quiet later
- does the branch welcome walk-ins at lunchtime or will I be stuck waiting

Subtitles are the words at the bottom of the screen that show what people are saying. They help when a room is noisy, when a baby is asleep, or when someone cannot hear well. A family on a camping trip may watch a little show on a tablet with the sound off, and subtitles let them follow the story. People change a few things about them: they turn them on or off, make the letters bigger, or pick another language. They say, put the words on, the text is too small, or, switch the subtitles to Spanish. Sometimes people say, what does that mean, when they cannot read a word fast enough, and ask to go back ten seconds to read it again.

Tom was nine, and he wanted to cook pancakes for his sister while she worked on a puzzle at the table. The recipe made twelve pancakes, which was too many. Tom said to the kitchen speaker, make this recipe for four people. No wait, for three, it's just me, Dad and Anna. The assistant understood that Tom had changed his mind and made the recipe again for three. It said the small batch needed one cup of flour, one egg and one cup of milk, and it read the amounts slowly. Tom measured each thing and said next after every step. The assistant waited and read the next line when he asked. Soon the kitchen smelled warm and sweet, and Anna put her puzzle away.

name: arrival_tracker
does: Shows when a food order will arrive and how far away the driver is.
inputs: which order, if the person has more than one open
people say:
- where is my pizza
- how long until my dozen dumplings get here
- is the driver close yet
- the map looks weird, did the driver get lost
- does the app lie, it said ten minutes an hour ago

Most people have more than one account at a bank, for example one for daily spending and one for savings. The balance is the amount of money in an account. A transfer moves money from one of your accounts to another. People do this when a spending account is nearly empty or when they want to save more. On many apps you can even drag the money from one account to the other with a finger. They say, move fifty dollars to savings, put some money into my checking account, or, send what's left to savings. A sharp eye on the balance helps, so people often ask, how much do I have, or, what's left in checking? If a card is lost, they say, freeze my card.

Lena, a student, was packing for a weekend hike in the hills, and her train left soon, so it was urgent. She said to her phone, what will the weather be like on Saturday, and add a rain jacket to my packing list. The assistant understood two things in one sentence: she wanted the forecast for the hills, and she wanted one more item on her list. It said Saturday would be cool with light rain, and it added the rain jacket below the tent and the water bottle. Lena knew that high up in the hills she would breathe harder, so she packed extra snacks too. She had paid for the train with her student account, and the ticket was already on her phone. She locked the door and ran to the station.

Person: Good morning. I am a retired teacher, and I am moving to a smaller flat next month, so I would be very grateful if you could set a reminder for me.
Assistant: Of course. What should the reminder say?
Person: Please remind me to call the electric company, so the power is on in the new flat on the first day.
Assistant: Which day should I remind you?
Person: The third of the month, in the morning. I find that I forget things when I am busy with boxes.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you on the third at nine in the morning. Should I also remind you about the water bill?
Person: Not yet. My budget is low this month, so I will wait.
Assistant: All right. Good luck with the move.

Person: Heat pool.
Assistant: Which pool should I heat, the front one or the back one?
Person: Front. My aunt is visiting and she hates cold water.
Assistant: What temperature would you like?
Person: Eighty degrees. Don't let it drop below that.
Assistant: Okay. I will heat the front pool to eighty and keep it there. Do you want it ready by noon?
Person: Yes, please.

Marco, a cook, was writing the menu card for his little restaurant. His hands were greasy from the grill, so he talked to his phone instead of typing. Spell bruschetta, he said. The assistant spelled it letter by letter: b, r, u, s, c, h, e, t, t, a. Marco wrote it down and smiled. His next line read roasted garlic bulb on delicious grilled bread, and he wanted to know if it was too long. Word count, he said. The assistant understood that he wanted the number of words in the draft so far, and it told him there were forty-one. Marco cut a few words, asked again, and the assistant said thirty-six. The menu card was ready to print.

Brightness is how strong the light from a phone screen is. Outside in the sun, people turn it up so they can see the screen. At night they turn it down so it does not hurt their eyes. Battery saver makes the charge last longer, and do not disturb stops calls and sounds while you sleep. People say, make the screen brighter, dim it a little, or, silence my phone until morning. When a new phone comes, you peel the thin plastic sheet off the screen before you start. Joggers sometimes clip a small phone to a jacket collar, and they ask for a quiet screen so the light does not bounce around. Storage is the space for photos and apps, and people ask, how much room do I have left?

name: wash_setting_picker
does: Chooses the right washing machine setting for a kind of clothes and starts it.
inputs: the kind of clothes or fabric, and how dirty they are
people say:
- wash my wool sweaters gently
- I don't understand which setting is for towels, just pick one
- the bedsheets are really dirty, give them a strong wash
- run something quiet, the baby is asleep
- the delicates bag is in the drum, start it

Person: How many days until my tomatoes are ready?
Assistant: I can count that for you. What day did you plant them?
Person: The third of May. The seed packet said seventy days.
Assistant: Seventy days after the third of May is the twelfth of July.
Person: Wonderful. I often forget dates, so can you remind me?
Assistant: Yes. Should I remind you on the day, or a few days before?
Person: A week before. Then I can wave over the fence and offer some to my neighbors.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you on the fifth of July.

When you buy something online, the store usually sends you a tracking number. You can use it to see where your package is, and many people simply ask, where is my order, or, when will it come? If a delivery is late, people say, explain why it is delayed, or, can you tell me the new date? Sometimes the thing you get is not what you wanted, such as a lamp with less brightness than you hoped, and then you ask for a refund. Fresh food, like a creamy cheese, has to arrive cold, so people check the time and ask for a window. A refund can take a few days to come back to your card.

Jonas, a student, was planning a birthday party for his roommate, and he was bad at keeping lists in his head. He asked his phone, how many people did I invite? The assistant counted the guest list and said twenty-five. Jonas then asked how to spell congratulations for the banner he was painting, and the assistant spelled it slowly, letter by letter. He also said, play something fun, and the assistant started a party playlist at a low volume. Later, when the big game came on during the party, he asked, what's the score? The assistant understood he meant the soccer match and read the score aloud. Everyone cheered, and the night went well.

Person: I want to post a photo of my dinner, but I don't want everyone to see it.
Assistant: Who should see it? Everyone you follow, or just a small group?
Person: Just my close friends.
Assistant: Okay. Which photo should I use?
Person: The one of the pan of pasta. It looks delicious.
Assistant: I found it. Do you want to add a caption?
Person: Yes, write Sunday dinner. No hashtags, please.
Assistant: Posted to close friends with the caption Sunday dinner and no hashtags.

A bank balance is the amount of money you have in an account right now. Checking it helps you decide what you can spend, whether it is a night at the theater or a week of groceries. People check it often and ask, what's my balance, or, how much is left? A transfer moves money between your own accounts, and on many apps you can drag the money from one account to another with a finger. When a fee appears that nobody expected, people get angry and ask, why was I charged? They also ask for more or less money to be moved, using words like, put in a bit more, or, take out twenty.

Painting is a hobby where an artist puts color on paper or cloth with brushes. People paint to relax, to make a gift, or just to see what happens. They change things as they go: the color, the size of the brush, how thick the paint is, and how long to wait. They say, make it a little darker, use a bigger brush, or, I need a pair of clean brushes. Many hobbies work this way, from knitting to building models. When the paint is wet, people ask an assistant to set a timer, and they say, tell me when it's ready. Then they can come back and add the next layer.

Grandpa Joe sat at his computer with a cup of bitter coffee. He wanted to read an article about gardens, but the screen was dim and gray. He sighed and said, I can't see a thing in here. The assistant understood that he meant the screen was too dark, and it made the screen brighter. Joe squinted and muttered, these letters are so small, they look like a slice of a stamp. The assistant understood that he wanted bigger text and made the words larger. Now the article was easy to read. Joe said thank you, took another sip of his coffee, and read about tomatoes all morning.

Ordering food to your door is simple. You pick a restaurant, choose your dishes, and pay in the app. The app shows a delivery time, and a driver brings the food. A doctor on a night shift might order dinner this way, since there is no time to cook. The app may warn you when a place is very busy, and then the time gets longer. People change a few things: the address, the dishes, and the tip. They add special instructions too, like no onions or leave it at the door. They say, make that two burgers, add a bigger tip, or, change the address to my office.

They want to know how many days are left until a date.
how many dasy until my trip
How long until Friday?
What's the countdown to Christmas?
How many sleeps until the holiday?
I'd cry if I forgot our gold anniversary, so how far away is it?
I left my glasses at the shop, so please count the days until they are ready on the twentieth.
Would you be so kind as to work out how many days are left before school starts again?

Priya, a cook, worked all day in a busy kitchen, and her father lived alone on the first floor of an old building. She said to her phone, remind dad to take his pills at eight and call him at nine. The assistant understood two jobs in one sentence. It set a pill reminder for her father at eight and planned a call for nine. Priya also asked it to count how many days of pills were left in the box, and the assistant said six. The pills were expensive, so she did not want to run out by accident. The assistant offered to remind her on Friday to order more, and Priya said yes. She went back to the stove feeling calmer.

Hannah, a gardener, had just met a kind man who sold lemon trees at the market. She said to her phone, add Victor Reyes to my contacts, his number is 555-0142. Then she looked at her note and said, wait, it's 555-0124, I got the last two numbers wrong. The assistant understood that she had fixed a detail and saved the number as 555-0124. Hannah added, put his birthday as the tenth of June, because she wanted to celebrate it with a small plant. The assistant saved that too. It was a long day in the sun, and Hannah smiled as she put her phone away, glad that she would not lose his number.

Ben woke up late with a stale taste in his mouth and a meeting across town. He mumbled to his phone, how long does it take to drive to the office, and send the route to my car screen. The assistant understood two requests in one sentence. First it checked the traffic, using a city website with road works, and said the drive would take thirty-five minutes because of a closed lane. Then it sent the best route to his car screen. Ben jumped up, brushed his teeth, and grabbed his keys. He asked the assistant to message his boss that he would be ten minutes late, and it did. He got in the car and set off.

Mina woke up at three in the morning when the baby monitor crackled. She was too tired to talk much, so she whispered to the speaker, feeding time? The assistant understood that she wanted to know when the baby last ate and said the last bottle was at midnight. Mina rubbed her eyes and said, start timer. The assistant started a timer for twenty minutes so she could skip checking the clock. The baby had gas, so the simple lullaby on the speaker was not helping. Mina said, skip song, and the assistant played the next one, a slower one. Soon the room was quiet again, and Mina went back to bed.

They want a gift idea for a birthday.
Gift ideas?
What should I get my brother for his birthday?
I need a present for my mom, and something that will last.
Any great ideas for a dad who loves fishing?
Find me a gift for under fifty dollars and tell me when the shop closes.
Help, the party is on Saturday and I have nothing for my gram!
What can I give a friend who already has everything?
I would be so thankful if you could suggest something thoughtful and remind me to buy it on Thursday.

Notes help you keep your ideas safe. You can write them down, type them, or say them out loud as a voice note. A funny idea can come at night, and by morning it may fall out of your head, so people say, note this down, or, remember that for me. Each note is an item in a list, and people change them: add a line, take one away, or fix a word. Later they look for old notes by saying, find my note about the garden, or, read me my list from Monday. Short notes are the easiest to find, so many people use simple titles.

Sam, a student, burned his hand on a hot pan while cooking dinner. It hurt, so he said to his phone, my hand is burned, what should I do? The assistant understood that this was first aid and told him to cool the burn under running water for ten minutes. It sounded calm and clear. Sam asked, what's the price of burn cream at the drugstore? The assistant said it was usually a few dollars. Because it was a small burn, he did not need to call anyone. Sam then said, remind me to look at it tomorrow at seven. The assistant set the reminder and said to see a doctor if it looked worse. Sam put a clean cloth on it and kept his personal first aid kit close.

Mrs. Doyle was not good with technology, and a parcel with a new skirt was supposed to come that week. She felt nervous about it, so she spoke to the speaker in the hall. Where is my parcel, and when will it come? she said. The assistant understood two questions in one sentence. It looked up the order and said the parcel was on a truck and would come on Thursday. It also said the maximum wait was two more days. Mrs. Doyle asked it to remind her to check the mailbox in the afternoon, and the assistant said it would. She shut the mailbox, felt proud, and waited for Thursday.

Aiko was new to the city, and the bathroom in her little apartment was always chilly. One morning she saw a crack in the wall and wanted to show her landlord. She said to her phone, take a photo of the bathroom wall. The assistant opened the camera and took the picture. Then she said, create an album called New Apartment and put it in there. The assistant made the album and saved the photo. Aiko also said, remind me tomorrow at seven to send these to the landlord. The assistant set the reminder. Aiko felt better knowing that she had a plan, and she wrapped a warm scarf around her neck.

Omar woke up in the dark. The room was strangely silent, with no hum from the fridge and no light on the clock. Weak light came from the street. His body felt heavy, and his mind was still half asleep, so he said to his phone, it's pitch black in here and the fridge is silent. The assistant understood that he meant the power was out. It turned on the phone flashlight and said to keep the fridge door shut so the food would stay cold. Omar had been trying to stick to a diet, and he laughed that at least the ice cream was safe. He asked the assistant to call the power company, and it did.

Person: remind me to take my pils at noon
Assistant: Which pills should I put in the reminder?
Person: the thick white ones for my blood pressure
Assistant: Got it. Should I remind you every day, or just today?
Person: every day. the board in my shop says lunch is at noon so that works
Assistant: That sounds good. I will remind you every day at noon to take the thick white pills for your blood pressure.

Walter was not good with technology, but he wanted dinner without cooking. He pointed at his speaker and said, order pizza for four people from Tony's, same as last time. The assistant understood that he meant the order he had made before and put it in. It said the pizza would cost twenty-eight dollars and asked if he wanted to add a tip. Walter said, add a good one. The assistant added five dollars. Then Walter said, tell me when it comes. The assistant told him the driver would arrive in about thirty minutes. When the doorbell rang, he opened the door, took the tasty pizza, and thanked the driver. His grandchildren cheered.

name: box_label_maker
does: Makes labels for moving boxes and tells which room each box should go in.
inputs: what is in the box, and the room it belongs to
people say:
- put a label on the box with the light bulbs, kitchen
- write fragile on the glasses box
- the freezer bag stuff is icy cold, mark it to unpack first
- which room does the box with winter coats go to
- make a sticker for each bedroom box

Dana was new to the city and still learning her way around. When she got home, she found a slip on the door about a black parcel. She did not know what to do, so she asked her phone, there's a note about a parcel, I don't want it left outside, I want it held at the post office. The assistant understood that she did not want the parcel left on the step and asked the carrier to hold it at the nearest post office. The parcel held a new phone battery, and Dana could not afford to lose it. The assistant told her which post office had it and when it opened. She wrote down the hours and went to bed relieved.

Kai, a teenager, was lying on the couch and texting the assistant on his phone. Book a haircut for saturday and tell me when the shop closes, he typed. The assistant understood two requests in one sentence. It booked a haircut at eleven on Saturday and said the shop closed at six. Kai was young and had never booked his own haircut before, so he felt a little proud. He was saving money for new shoes, so he asked how much a cut cost. The assistant said it was fifteen dollars. Kai disconnected his earbuds, put his phone on the table, and went to find his wallet.

They want the bedroom light dimmed but not turned off.
Dim the lights, but don't turn them off.
Make it softer in here.
Not so bright, please.
Lower the lamp a bit.
I want to watch a movie, so make the room darker, but not completely dark.
The little girl is excited and can't sleep, so turn the lights down low without switching them off.
Would you mind making the light gentler, as I don't want it off, only quieter?

They want to order the same groceries again.
Reorder.
Order that again.
Same as last time, please.
Buy my usual things.
There is fog outside and I don't want to drive to the store, so can you order my usual stuff?
Arrange delivery for the same things as last week.
Could you please put in my average weekly shop and send it to the house?

They want the heating to turn on at a certain time.
Heating on at seven tomorrow.
Warm the house up before I get up tomorrow at seven.
Have it nice and warm by tomorrow at seven.
Turn on the radiators for tomorrow at seven, please.
I'd like a calm, warm room by tomorrow at seven, since the baby will be playing with her ball on the floor.
Please warn me if the heater can't reach twenty degrees by tomorrow at seven.

Grandma Rosa had baked bread all morning, and the kitchen was very hot. Her grandchildren were coming for lunch. She said to the speaker, excuse me, could you please turn the fan up to a higher level and turn on the air conditioning in the kitchen? I have been baking for hours and my grandchildren are coming, and it is too hot for them. The assistant understood that she wanted the fan on high and the air conditioning started. It told her the kitchen would feel cooler in about ten minutes. Rosa thanked it and sat down by the window. Soon many little feet ran in, and the room was fresh and cool.

Person: I'm just waking up. Give me a workout, but no running.
Assistant: Okay. How many minutes do you have?
Person: Fifteen. I did not sleep well, so I feel a little sad and slow.
Assistant: Then a gentle one with stretching and light squats. Should I start it?
Person: Yes. Just one question: can you count the sets out loud?
Assistant: Yes. I will count each set and tell you when to rest.

Frank, a gardener, came in from the yard feeling sleepy after a long morning of digging. He said to the kitchen speaker, make coffee, two cups. Then he thought again and said, actually just one, my wife is still asleep. The assistant understood that he had changed his mind and told the coffee machine to make one cup. It said the coffee would be ready in three minutes. Frank had a good idea and asked it to play soft music too. As the coffee brewed, the steam seemed to dance above the machine. He poured it, sat at the table, and looked out at his garden with a warm cup in his hands.

Grandpa Lou was eating a banana at the bus stop, and he wanted to go to the market. He asked his phone, when is the next number twelve bus? The assistant understood that he meant the bus on route twelve and said it would come in twenty-five minutes. Lou wanted his daughter to know, so he said, forward the timetable to Emma. The assistant sent it. He also asked about a weekly pass, since he rode the bus often. The assistant said a weekly pass cost eighteen dollars and could be bought on the bus. Lou finished his banana, sat down on the bench, and waited with a smile.

They want to know how far they have walked today.
How far did I walk today?
Steps so far?
Give me my step report.
Have I done ten thousand steps yet?
Tell me out loud how many miles I've gone since the fresh morning air got me out of bed.
Would you please let me know my distance so far, and shout when I pass five miles?

They want the car warmed up before they leave.
warm up my car
strt the engine, its freezing
Get the car warm, I'm leaving in a minute
Sounds like it is pretty cold out, so could you heat the car up?
Please start the car and turn the heater on, I will be out in five minutes
Could you please start the engine ten minutes before I leave, so the seats are warm?

Ivy woke up to a drip, drip, drip from the kitchen. Her knee hurt as she walked over the wet floor. Still half asleep, she said to her phone, book a plumber for the kitchen tap at nine. Then she stopped and said, no, the bathroom tap, the kitchen one is fine. The assistant understood that she had fixed a detail and booked the plumber for the bathroom tap at nine. It said the plumber would come from the east side of town. Ivy asked, what do I owe him for a visit like that? The assistant said the visit usually cost sixty dollars. Ivy put a bowl under the drip and made her tea.

Priya was late for the train and the platform was loud. She held up her phone and said, 'Could you please pick up my cooking podcast where I stopped yesterday, and play it a little faster, because I only have twelve minutes before my stop and I really want to hear the end?' The phone found the episode she had left halfway through. It said, 'I found Kitchen Talk, episode forty. You stopped at twenty-one minutes. I will start there and make the speed one and a half times faster.' Priya smiled as a smooth voice began to talk about how soda is made. She stepped onto the train, found a seat, and listened until her stop.

Someone wants to know how long the drive home will take.
Drive time?
How long till I'm home?
What does the traffic look like on the way back?
I have to sweep the bathroom before guests come, so when will I get home if I leave now?
Tell me the trip time to my house, please.
Is the road home busy right now?
How many minutes is it to my place?
Check the digital map and tell me how long I'll be on the road.
Would you mind telling me how long it will take to drive home with today's traffic?

Rosa got home from the hospital at eight in the morning, tired and hungry. She sat on the couch and said, 'Hey, where is my box of vegetables? I want it before this evening, because I have to chop a lot for soup.' The assistant checked her orders. It said, 'Your vegetable box is out for delivery. It should arrive between two and four this afternoon.' Rosa said, 'Can it come sooner? Half a day is too long to wait. And tell them to leave it at the front door.' The assistant said it could not make the truck go faster, but it added a note to leave the box at the front door. It promised to send a message when the driver was close. Rosa smiled, closed her eyes, and slept.

name: trim_video_clip
does: Cuts a short piece out of a longer video so it can be saved or shared.
inputs: the video, the time where the piece starts, and the time where it ends
people say:
- Cut out the part where the butterfly lands
- Make this video shorter, I only want the last minute
- Keep just the sharp part from ten seconds in to thirty
- I paid for this film, but I only want the first scene
- Trim it so it's easy to send to Mum

Someone wants the pool water to be warmer.
Warm the pool up.
Heat the water to twenty-eight degrees.
It snowed last night and the water feels icy, can you fix that?
I have a booking for a pool party at noon, so please get the water ready.
Turn on the heater.
I'd be lucky to find the water above twenty, so make it nicer to swim in.
It's too cold to get in, do something about it.
Could you please raise the pool temperature a few degrees before the kids come?

A text message is a short note you send from your phone to another person. People use texts when a call feels like too much, or when the other person may be asleep. A smart phone can read a new text out loud and write one when you speak. People change small things about it: who gets the message, when it is sent, and how loud the sound is. To change them they say things like, 'Text Dan that I'm ten minutes late,' 'Read my last message,' or 'Send it tomorrow morning, so it won't wake him.' Some say, 'Tell her I'm a mile away.' Group chats work the same way, but many people get the note. To quiet a noisy group, people say, 'Be quiet about this chat.'

name: warm_up_car
does: Starts the engine and heats the inside of the car before a trip.
inputs: which car, and what time you plan to leave
people say:
- I'm leaving soon, get the car ready
- It's freezing out, make the car cosy for the morning
- Start the engine at seven so I'm not cold
- I need to zoom to the vet with the puppy, heat up the car
- I'm tired of scraping ice, get the windows clear

Someone wants the news on the radio.
Put the news on.
I want to hear what's happening today.
Anything new in the world?
I haven't heard the headlines yet.
Tune to the news station, please.
While I stir this spicy soup, could you find the news?
I'm going fishing in an hour and feel out of touch with everything.
What's going on out there?
It's very quiet in here and I'd like to know what the world is up to.

name: lock_door
does: Locks a door of the house and says when it is done.
inputs: which door, and when to lock it
people say:
- Please lock the red door at the side of the house
- Lock up for the night
- Make sure nobody can get in tonight
- I forgot to lock up, can you do it for me?
- Grandpa is out in the yard to plant flowers, keep the front door shut till he's back

Marco was at the stove with flour on his hands when he looked at his list. 'My list is a mess,' he said to the kitchen speaker. 'The things I already did are still sitting at the front, and I can't see what is left.' The speaker understood that he wanted the finished tasks cleared out of the way. It said, 'I will check off the done items and move them to the bottom. Three tasks are left.' It read them out: buy flour, call Dad, and load the dishwasher. A little signal chimed when it was done. Marco nodded and kept stirring, glad that the list was short again.

Someone wants the computer to restart later.
Restart it.
Reboot the laptop tomorrow at seven.
Turn the computer off and on again at noon.
Please restart the downstairs computer after the update is installed tonight.
Can you restart this machine in an hour?
I'm going to bed, so start it fresh at six in the morning.
My gram uses the old computer downstairs, so make it fresh by eight tomorrow.
It's slow, so reboot it on Friday at nine.

A computer's battery keeps it running when it is not plugged in. When the charge gets low, the screen goes dim and a warning shows. People change a few things to make the battery last longer. They make the screen less bright, close programs they do not use, or turn on a saver mode. Some people set it by hand with a manual switch, while others let the computer decide. They say, 'Dim the screen,' 'Save my battery,' or 'How much charge is left?' Someone eating oatmeal at the breakfast table might say, 'Turn on battery saver, I want to visit my sister and I'll be on the train all day.'

name: guest_list
does: Keeps the list of people coming to a party and tells you how many have said yes.
inputs: the name of the party, and the name of the guest
people say:
- Who's coming on Saturday?
- Put Nina down as a yes
- How many people have said they'll come?
- Take Joe off, he can't make it
- Mia will bring a lamp for the garden, write that next to her name
- Tidy up the list, there are two Sams

name: boil_water
does: Heats the kettle and tells you when the water is hot.
inputs: how hot the water should be, and when to start
people say:
- I need hot water
- Get the kettle going
- Have it ready in five minutes for tea
- Is the water done yet?
- I'm walking a kilometer to the shop, so have the kettle hot when I get back
- Set it to eighty degrees, green tea is fine that way

Dana was eating lunch at her desk when she remembered the eggs at home. She typed to her phone in a hurry: 'how long do i boil eggs so thye are hard'. The assistant understood she wanted a cooking time for hard eggs. It answered, 'Put them in boiling water for ten minutes, then move them to cold water.' Dana typed again: 'text kim to turn on the vent and start the pot, the kitchen air is stale'. The assistant sent a text to Kim that said, 'Please turn on the vent and start the pot. The kitchen air is stale.' It also set a ten minute timer for Dana. She went back to her salad and felt relieved.

A radio picks up voices and music from the air. Each station has a number, and people turn a knob or press a button to find the one they like. They change the station, the volume, and sometimes save favorites so the radio can store them. When the sound is not clean and there is a hiss, people move the dial slowly until the voices come through. A slow, careful turn works best. People ask for changes in many ways. They say, 'Put on something calm,' 'Louder, please,' 'Go back to the last station,' or 'Keep this one.' In a car, someone may even say, 'I can't hear the talking,' and mean the same thing.

Someone wants to call their mother.
Call Mom.
Ring Mom.
Get my mother on the phone.
Dial Mum, please.
I want to talk to my mother.
I've shut the shop for the day, so please call my mum now.
The weather is mild and I'm on the porch, so I'd like to speak with my mother.
Could you please phone my mum and put her on speaker?

Person: Could you please put some thick bacon on my shopping list, because I'm cooking breakfast for the whole family on Sunday and we always run out?
Assistant: Of course. How many packs should I write down?
Person: Two packs. And a leg of lamb for the weekend too.
Assistant: Done. Which day will you cook the lamb?
Person: Saturday. Can you shuffle the list so the meat is at the top?
Assistant: Yes, the bacon and the lamb are now first.

Mr. Okafor, a retired teacher, stood at the window looking at his garden. 'The soil looks like a desert and the tomatoes are drooping,' he said to the speaker. A package of new seeds had come that morning, and he wanted the flat beds wet before he planted them. The assistant understood that he wanted water for the garden. It said, 'I will turn on the sprinkler for ten minutes.' Then it asked, 'Would you like me to change the schedule so it waters at six every morning?' Mr. Okafor said yes. The sprinkler began to hiss, and he went to get his gloves.

Lily, who was eight, sat on the sofa with a sad face. 'It's so quiet and boring,' she told the tablet. 'I finished my last book and the library is shut today.' The tablet understood that she wanted something to read. It said, 'I can read you a story. Do you want one about a dragon or one about a fox?' Lily said, 'The dragon, please.' The tablet began to read in a soft voice about a small dragon who was afraid of fire. Lily lay back on the cushions and listened until the story was finished. Then she asked for another.

A focus timer helps people work without stopping too often. You pick a short block of time, like twenty-five minutes, and work until it rings. Then you take a short break. People change the length of the block, the length of the break, and how many rounds to do. They also use it for small jobs at home. If bread is in the oven, a timer tells you when it is ready. When you are not sure how long a job will take, you can estimate and then change the time later. People say, 'Start a thirty minute timer,' 'Make my breaks five minutes,' or 'Give me ten more minutes.'

Someone wants ideas for decorating the house for the winter holidays.
Decoration ideas?
How should I decorate this winter?
Give me something to hang on the door.
Explain a simple way to make the house look festive.
Help me decorate.
Any weird but fun ideas for the tree?
Could you suggest a few ideas for the living room, nothing too expensive?
Tell me what I can put in the window.
The house looks so plain right now.

A medicine reminder is a gentle alert that tells an older person when to take a pill. It is for people who forget, or who take many different pills in a day. The alert can be a sound, a voice, or a message to a family member. People change the time, the name of the pill, and who gets told. They say things like, 'Remind Grandma at eight each morning,' 'Let me know when she has taken it,' or 'Call me if she doesn't answer.' In August, when families travel, someone far away may ask for a special check each evening, so they know everything is fine at home.

Jonah was lying in bed with his phone, typing fast. 'cancel my alarm for tomorrow,' he wrote. 'the roads are icy so school starts late, and my uncle's wife is driving me at ten.' The assistant understood that he wanted his morning alarm turned off. It answered, 'I cancelled your seven o'clock alarm. Do you want a new one?' Jonah typed, 'yeah wake me at nine, twenty-five min before we leave.' The assistant set the alarm for nine, and said it would sound softly and get louder. Jonah put the phone down, pulled up his blanket, and fell asleep.

Nadia, who cooked at a small cafe, sat at the kitchen table with a scarf she was knitting for her uncle. She had spilled tea near her bag, and the scarf was only half finished. 'I can't remember what comes after the third row,' she said to the speaker. 'I'm completely stuck.' The assistant understood that she wanted help with the next step of her pattern. It said, 'Your pattern says to knit two rows, then purl one. Do you want me to read the steps one at a time?' Nadia said yes, wiped the table, and picked up her needles.

Tom was a busy dad with two hungry kids and a thin wallet. At the grocery door, he told his phone, 'I hate fish, and the kids won't eat anything spicy, so no fish and no spice this week. Plan five dinners for me.' The assistant understood that he wanted a week of simple, cheap meals without those two things. It said, 'Here is a plan: pasta with tomato sauce, chicken and rice, bean tacos, vegetable soup, and baked potatoes. I left out fish and spice.' Tom said, 'Be patient with me, I may change the soup.' The assistant was patient, and said it could swap any dinner he liked.

Person: I want to send a text to my daughter, but I don't want a long one.
Assistant: Of course. What would you like it to say?
Person: Begin with hello and tell her I'm coming this winter.
Assistant: Which day should I say you are coming?
Person: Not a day yet. Just the season. My glasses are loose and I can't see the screen well, so please read it back.
Assistant: Here it is: Hello, I am coming to see you this winter. Should I send it?
Person: Yes, please send it.
Assistant: Sent to your daughter.

Kai had been playing games for hours when his stomach made a loud noise. 'There's nothing in the oven and nothing in the fridge,' he typed to his phone. 'Mom taught me never to eat chips for dinner.' The assistant understood that he wanted food brought to the house. It said, 'Do you want your regular order from Tony's Pizza, a large with cheese?' Kai typed, 'yes pls.' The assistant placed the order and said, 'It will arrive in about thirty minutes. I added a tip, as you usually do.' Kai put the phone down and went to set the table.

Carl, a driver, parked his truck and looked at his phone. 'I have more jobs than time today,' he said. The assistant checked his to-do list and found six tasks. It read them: go to the bank, fold the laundry upstairs, fix the mirror, call the garage, pick up bread, and wash the truck. Carl said, 'Do the shortest ones first, and move the laundry to tomorrow.' The assistant sorted the list so the quick jobs came first, and moved the laundry to the next day. Now only five tasks were left for today, and Carl started with the bank.

Someone wants the heating turned up and a message when the room is warm.
Warm it up.
Turn up the heat and send me a note when the room is toasty.
It's cold in here.
Raise the speed of the fan heater and shut the vent, please.
The air is so dry and chilly, please make the living room warmer.
Could you heat the bedroom and the hall, please?
I'm coming home soon, get the house cosy.
Push the thermostat up a few degrees, if you don't mind.

A robot mower cuts the grass by itself while the family does other things. It drives over the lawn in lines, turns at the edges, and goes back to its station when it needs to charge. People change how often it works, how short the grass should be, and when it should stay in. They say things like, 'Mow the lawn on Saturday,' 'Cut it a little shorter,' or 'Do not go out if it rains.' If the grass grows fast, they may say, 'Double the mowing this week.' A light rain is fine for most mowers, but a heavy storm means it should stay home.

Sam, a driver, was on his break in the freezing cold, with a hot drink in his hands. 'Tell me when my parcel comes,' he said to his phone. Then he stopped. 'Wait, not mine. It's my sister's parcel, the one with the blue scarf.' The assistant understood that he wanted a warning about his sister's delivery. It said, 'I will warn you when your sister's parcel is delivered. The price on the label is twenty dollars, and it needs a signature.' Sam said, 'Perfect, I'll be home by five.' The assistant said it would send a message at five if the parcel had not come.

Jess was late for work, with her bag half open and her keys in her hand. 'Lock the front door and the back door, and check the garage too,' she said. The assistant checked all three. It said, 'The front door and back door are now locked. The garage is open.' Jess said, 'Close it, and leave the hall light on for an hour more, because I need to pay the man who fixes the curtain rail.' The assistant closed the garage and kept the light on. Jess ran down the steps and got into her car, knowing the house was safe.

Someone wants eggs on the shopping list.
Put eggs on the list.
Twelve eggs, please.
We're out of eggs.
Write down two dozen cheap eggs, a flood of guests is coming on Sunday.
I have a ticket for the egg sale at the market, so write eggs on my list.
Don't let me forget eggs.
The fridge has no eggs left.
Could you please note that I need eggs for breakfast?

Ben was at his desk, sipping a creamy latte, when his phone buzzed again. 'This camera keeps pinging me every time a leaf moves,' he said to the assistant. 'I can't get anything done.' The assistant understood that he wanted the alerts to stop for a while. It said, 'I will mute the garden camera for one hour.' Then it asked, 'Do you want a link to the live view, in case you want to look?' Ben said yes. The assistant sent the link to his phone, and the buzzing stopped. Ben went back to his work, and the phone stayed quiet until lunch.

name: party_budget
does: Keeps a list of what you have spent on a party and shows the total so far.
inputs: what you bought, and how much it cost
people say:
- I swiped my card for the cake, put down forty dollars
- What's the total so far?
- How much have we used?
- The music was free, so take that sum off
- Write down balloons, twelve dollars
- Tell me when we pass two hundred

Jin woke up late and rubbed both eyes. 'When is the rent due?' Jin asked the speaker, still half asleep. 'No, not the rent, I mean the internet bill.' The assistant understood the correction and said the internet bill was due on the twentieth. That was close, only two days away, and it was thirty dollars. Outside, a neighbour began to shout about the gate, because a delivery man had left it open. Jin said, 'Pay it today.' The assistant answered that it would pay the thirty dollars that afternoon and send a message afterwards. Jin pulled the blanket back up.

Person: Could you please change the weight on my recipe, because I am going to jog home and shop on the way, and I need to know how much to buy?
Assistant: Sure. What does the recipe say, and what do you want it in?
Person: It says five pounds of potatoes. I want kilos.
Assistant: Five pounds is about two and a quarter kilos.
Person: Thank you. So a whole bag of two and a half kilos is enough?
Assistant: Yes, a bag of two and a half kilos will cover it.

Hana sat at her office desk, looking at the clock. 'Could you please book me a ride to the train station for six tonight?' she asked her phone. 'And I would like the car to pick me up one block away at the corner, because the front street is closed for roadwork and it is not easy for cars to get in.' The assistant understood that she needed a ride at six, with a pickup at the corner. It said, 'I booked a car for six o'clock at the corner of Pine Street. The driver is named Luis, and he will arrive in about four minutes before.' Hana smiled and kept working, sure she would catch her train.

Leo was bored of painting the kitchen when he heard a hiss. He turned and saw water begin to pour from a pipe under the sink. 'Call the plumber, quick!' he shouted at his phone. 'The pipe is leaking, I need someone in twenty minutes!' The assistant understood that this was an emergency. It said, 'I am calling Fast Fix Plumbing now. Turn off the water at the main valve, near the front door.' The plumber answered, and the assistant told him the address. He said he could come in twenty-five minutes. Leo ran to the valve and turned it, and the water slowed down to a drip.

The clock on the wall at the foot of the stairs shows the time where you live. The sun does not rise at the same moment everywhere, so a clock in another city shows a different time. People call these areas time zones. When someone travels, they adjust their watch to match the new place. Time itself keeps moving at a constant pace, but the number on the clock changes. People ask, 'What time is it in Tokyo?', 'Is it morning in London?', or 'Set my clock to local time.' It helps them call friends far away without waking them up.

Someone wants a recipe made twice as big.
Double the recipe.
Make this serve twice as many.
I have too many guests, I can't breathe, make the recipe bigger.
Two times the amounts, please.
My knee hurts and I'd rather not work it out the manual way, so change all the numbers for eight people.
How much flour do I need if I make double?
Rewrite it for twice the servings, if you don't mind.
I need more of everything, there are ten of us tonight.

name: parking_time_left
does: Tells you how long until your parking runs out and reminds you before it does.
inputs: where you parked, and the time your parking ends
people say:
- How long do I have left on the meter?
- Remind me before my parking runs out
- Do I owe more money for this space?
- Warn me ten minutes before I have to move the car
- I left my backpack in the car, how long until I must go back?
- Most places let you stay two hours, what about here?

Maria's kids sat on the loose cushions of the sofa, waiting. 'Find a movie for the kids, something with a kitten,' she said to the tv. 'No, wait, a puppy. They like puppies more.' The assistant understood the correction. It said, 'I found a film called Little Paws, about a puppy. It is ninety minutes long and good for all ages.' Maria asked, 'Is it a happy one? They grow bored fast with sad movies.' The assistant said it was funny and warm. Maria told it to start the movie. The kids cheered, and she went to make popcorn.

Lena was folding laundry when her young son ran in. 'How do you say jump and dance in Spanish?' he asked the speaker. The assistant understood that he wanted two Spanish words. It said, 'Jump is saltar. Dance is bailar.' The boy repeated them and began to jump and spin around the room. Lena laughed and said, 'Remind us tomorrow at seven to practice these words again.' The assistant set a reminder for tomorrow at seven, and said it would ask the boy to say each word out loud. Lena kept folding, and her son kept dancing.

Mrs. Hale, a retired teacher, sat on her porch with a hammer next to her. 'Remind me to feed Rex at five,' she said to her phone. 'And fill his huge water bowl, because I will mow the lawn first.' The assistant understood that she wanted two reminders for the dog. It said, 'I set a reminder at five for dinner and a bowl refill. Rex also needs his walk. Do you want a reminder for that?' Mrs. Hale said, 'Yes, twenty minutes after dinner.' The assistant added it. She picked up her hammer to fix the pet door, and then went to start the mower.

name: find_dentist_slot
does: Looks for the next free time at a dentist, books it and puts the visit in the calendar.
inputs: which dentist, and which days suit the person
people say:
- My tooth hurts, get me in as soon as you can
- I hate waiting rooms, find a time when it is quiet
- Do they have anything on Tuesday?
- Book a check-up for the kids, and mark it in peach on my calendar
- Put my visit in red so I do not miss it

Bread and cookies begin as dough, a soft mix of flour, water and other things. Baking changes the dough with heat, and it needs time to rise or rest first. A wet dough feels sticky and makes soft bread, while a dry dough makes hard cookies. Cookies are often shaped into a small round lump the size of a coin. People change the baking time, the heat of the oven, and the size of the batch. They say, 'Set a timer for twenty minutes,' 'Make the oven hotter,' or 'Cancel the timer, the bread is not ready.' They also ask, 'How long should it rise?'

A bike ride is a trip on two wheels, and many people plan it before they go. A route shows the roads and paths to take, how far it is, and how long it should take. Riders often choose public paths that cars cannot use. They change the length, the speed they want to ride at, and the hills they will pass. They say, 'Find me a flat ride of ten miles,' 'Avoid the busy roads,' or 'Block out Sunday morning for a ride.' On rainy days, some people ride an indoor bike, and they put a rug under it to keep the floor safe.

Reading text aloud is a tool for people who cannot see small words well, or who are busy with their hands. The phone reads the screen out loud in a clear voice. People change how fast it reads, how big the text is, and which voice they like. They say, 'Read this page to me,' 'Make the words bigger,' or 'Slow down.' If they are interrupted, they ask, 'Continue where you stopped.' It can read signs and labels too, like a note that says go west, or a recipe that needs one liter of milk. Voice control lets them do all this without touching the screen.
